hunches.title: Sold hospitals were already bleeding
hunches.hunch: Hospitals that changed owners since 2021 sit at 1-2 stars 36% of the time and 58% posted negative FY2023 net income, but hospitals sold AFTER their FY2023 report were already 60.5% negative on it, so the distress precedes the sale rather than following it.
hunches.join_keys: POS_OTHER.CCN (PRVDR_CTGRY_CD='01', 13,540 rows; CHOW_DT YYYYMMDD filled on 2,532) = HOSPITAL_GENERAL.CCN (5,423 of 5,432 Care Compare hospitals have a POS row; 3,181 rated); POS_OTHER.CCN = HCRIS.PROVIDER_CCN (5,736 hospitals with a 350-380 day report; HCRIS is 6,103 rows / 6,040 CCNs, longest period per CCN kept)
hunches.query_sql: with hc as (select PROVIDER_CCN ccn, try_to_number(NET_INCOME,18,2) ni, try_to_number(TOTAL_COSTS,18,2) tc, CCN_FACILITY_TYPE ft, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') fye, datediff(day, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'), try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) days, row_number() over (partition by PROVIDER_CCN order by datediff(day, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'), try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) desc) rn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HCRIS), h as (select CCN, try_to_date(nullif(trim(CHOW_DT),''),'YYYYMMDD') chow from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_POS_OTHER where PRVDR_CTGRY_CD='01') select case when chow > hc.fye then 'A_sold_AFTER_this_FY (pre-sale margin)' when chow > dateadd(year,-3,hc.fye) and chow <= hc.fye then 'B_sold_within_3y_BEFORE_FY_end (post-sale margin)' when chow <= dateadd(year,-3,hc.fye) then 'C_sold_3plus_years_before' else 'D_never' end grp, count(*) hospitals, round(100*avg(case when ni<0 then 1 else 0 end),1) pct_negative_income, round(median(ni/nullif(tc,0))*100,2) median_margin_pct_of_cost from hc join h on h.CCN=hc.ccn where rn=1 and days between 350 and 380 and tc>0 group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 5,736 hospitals with a 12-month cost report and a POS row: 86 sold after their FY end, 48 sold within 3 years before it, 1,201 sold 3+ years before, 4,401 never sold. Star leg: 118 active short-term hospitals sold since 2021, 101 rated.
hunches.first_number: 60.5% of the 86 hospitals sold after their FY2023 report year had negative net income on that report (median margin -4.69% of cost) vs 33.5% of 4,401 never-sold (median +5.21%); the 48 sold within 3 years before the FY end sit at 52.1% negative, median -0.22%. Star leg: 35.6% of 101 rated short-term hospitals sold since 2021 are 1-2 stars vs 23.1% of 1,901 never-sold (Care Compare snapshot ingested 2026-07).
hunches.hit_means: A bigger gap in the pre-sale group says buyers pick up hospitals that are already wounded; a bigger gap in the post-sale group would say new owners strip them. Pre-sale distress is the larger number here, so the story is who buys the wounded and what they do next, with a real date to anchor it.
hunches.miss_means: Flat rates across the four groups would mean an ownership change carries no financial signal and the star gap is ownership mix (43% proprietary among recent sales vs 15% never-sold).
hunches.tier_reason: CHOW_DT and FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE are both real dates, so sale-before vs sale-after the report year is a true before/after; chain holds end to end and the first number is found.
hunches.time_axis: CHOW_DT 1973-06-30 to 2026-01-01 (8-char YYYYMMDD text); HCRIS fiscal year ends 2022-12 to 2024-12 (3,534 end in 2023, 2,564 in 2024); Care Compare star is one snapshot.
traps: HCRIS called FY2023 mixes 3,534 reports ending in 2023 with 2,564 ending in 2024 and 5 in 2022, and holds 304 stub-period reports of 58-333 days; filter days between 350 and 380 and compare each hospital to its own FY end.
3,173 hospital rows carry CHOW_CNT>0 with a blank CHOW_DT; only 2,532 of 5,670 hospitals with a change count have a date.
POS_OTHER holds no HHA, hospice or ESRD rows, so this works for hospitals only.
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest are hunch 31 (hospital-owned vs independent HHAs, ownership snapshot via ASSOCIATE_ID) and hunch 11 (HCRIS negative income x Open Payments). Neither uses CHOW_DT or any dated ownership change; this is the hub's first dated sale leg.

hunches.title: Chains getting worse, then fined
hunches.hunch: Nursing-home chains whose harm-level (G-or-worse) citations per home rose most from 2023 to 2025 (Bria, Crest Healthcare Consulting, Unlimited Development, Hurlbut) also carry rising penalty counts and fine dollars in 2024-2025, while the national G+ share moved only from 5.78% to 6.18%.
hunches.join_keys: NURSINGHOME411.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN = DEFICIENCIES.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN (418,408 of 418,479 rows find a home; 310,716 carry a CHAIN_ID); NURSINGHOME411 CCN = PENALTIES.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN (16,180 penalties at 6,831 homes). CHAIN_ID filled on 10,162 of 14,713 homes, 617 chains, 301 with 10+ homes.
hunches.query_sql: with n as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN ccn, nullif(trim(CHAIN_ID),'') chain_id, CHAIN_NAME chain_name from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_NURSINGHOME411 where nullif(trim(CHAIN_ID),'') is not null), ch as (select chain_id, min(chain_name) chain_name, count(*) homes from n group by 1 having count(*)>=10), d as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN ccn, year(try_to_date(SURVEY_DATE)) y, SCOPE_SEVERITY_CODE sev from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_DEFICIENCIES where try_to_date(SURVEY_DATE) between '2023-01-01' and '2025-12-31'), agg as (select n.chain_id, d.y, count(*) defs, count(distinct d.ccn) homes_cited, sum(case when sev in ('G','H','I','J','K','L') then 1 else 0 end) gplus from d join n on n.ccn=d.ccn join ch on ch.chain_id=n.chain_id group by 1,2) select ch.chain_id, ch.chain_name, ch.homes, max(case when y=2023 then defs end) defs_2023, max(case when y=2025 then defs end) defs_2025, max(case when y=2023 then gplus end) gplus_2023, max(case when y=2025 then gplus end) gplus_2025, round(max(case when y=2025 then gplus end)/ch.homes - max(case when y=2023 then gplus end)/ch.homes,3) gplus_per_home_delta from agg join ch on ch.chain_id=agg.chain_id group by 1,2,3 order by gplus_per_home_delta desc nulls last
hunches.distinct_entities: 301 chains with 10+ homes (10,162 chained homes in all); Bria 15 homes, all 15 cited in both 2023 and 2025; Crest 13 of 13 both years.
hunches.first_number: Bria Health Services: G-or-worse citations 49 (2023) to 76 (2025) on 15 homes, 21.5% to 33.5% of its citations; penalties 30 (2023 H2), 37 (2024), 41 (2025); fines $1.52M (2024) to $2.02M (2025). Crest Healthcare Consulting: 12 to 33 G+ on 13 homes; fines $539k to $1.22M. National: G+ share 5.78% to 6.18%.
hunches.hit_means: A chain whose harm-level share doubles while its home count and homes-cited count hold steady is deteriorating in operation, not just being surveyed more; penalties following the next year say regulators saw it too.
hunches.miss_means: A riser whose homes-cited count also jumped (Wellington 7 to 13 homes cited, Hurlbut 8 to 10) is partly a coverage artifact, not decline; a chain whose fines lag its citations shows enforcement not keeping pace.
hunches.tier_reason: SURVEY_DATE and PENALTY_DATE are both real dates; two full years are compared and penalties follow in time; first number found.
traps: CHAIN_ID is a 2026 snapshot: a home bought in 2024 has its 2023 citations attributed to the current chain.
The deficiency file is a rolling three-survey-cycle window, not a series; 2019 covers 2,004 homes, 2023 10,787. No 2018-2022 chain trend exists in the warehouse.
Homes cited nationally grew 10.7% from 2023 to 2025, so a riser must clear that.
NURSINGHOME411 (617 chains, 10,162 homes) and FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME (635 chains, 10,479 homes) disagree on chain membership; say which you used.
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 2 ranked fines per home by chain as one cross-section (Bria $5.24M over 15 homes). This ranks on the 2023-to-2025 severity trend and reads penalties as the lagging leg; Bria tops both lists.

hunches.title: E-tags ignore the storms
hunches.hunch: Nursing homes in counties hit by a $10M-plus property-damage storm are cited for emergency-preparedness (E-tag) failures no more often in the 12 months after the storm than in the 12 months before, and no more often than homes in never-hit counties.
hunches.join_keys: NURSING_HOME.STATE + lpad(PROVIDER_SSA_COUNTY_CODE,3,'0') = POS_OTHER.STATE_CD + SSA_CNTY_CD -> FIPS_STATE_CD||FIPS_CNTY_CD (crosswalk 3,150 pairs, 0 conflicts; 14,663 of 14,700 homes map to 2,830 counties); FIPS = STORM.STATE_FIPS||lpad(CZ_FIPS,3,'0') where CZ_TYPE='C' (447 county events at $10M+ 2018-2025 in 278 counties with a home; 390 zone-typed events dropped); FIRE_DEFICIENCIES.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN = NURSING_HOME CCN (22,260 of 22,260 E-tag rows match)
hunches.query_sql: with xw as (select STATE_CD, SSA_CNTY_CD, min(FIPS_STATE_CD||FIPS_CNTY_CD) fips from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_POS_OTHER where nullif(trim(SSA_CNTY_CD),'') is not null and nullif(trim(FIPS_CNTY_CD),'') is not null group by 1,2), nh as (select n.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER__CCN ccn, xw.fips from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME n join xw on xw.STATE_CD=n.STATE and xw.SSA_CNTY_CD=lpad(n.PROVIDER_SSA_COUNTY_CODE,3,'0')), hit as (select STATE_FIPS||lpad(CZ_FIPS,3,'0') fips, try_to_date(BEGIN_YEARMONTH||lpad(BEGIN_DAY,2,'0'),'YYYYMMDD') d from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_STORM_EVENTS where CZ_TYPE='C' and YEAR between 2018 and 2025 and (case right(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,1) when 'K' then try_to_number(left(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,length(DAMAGE_PROPERTY)-1),18,4)*1e3 when 'M' then try_to_number(left(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,length(DAMAGE_PROPERTY)-1),18,4)*1e6 when 'B' then try_to_number(left(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,length(DAMAGE_PROPERTY)-1),18,4)*1e9 else try_to_number(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,18,4) end) >= 1e7), et as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN ccn, try_to_date(SURVEY_DATE) sd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_FIRE_DEFICIENCIES where DEFICIENCY_PREFIX='E'), pairs as (select distinct nh.ccn, hit.fips, hit.d from hit join nh on nh.fips=hit.fips) select count(*) home_event_pairs, count(distinct ccn) homes, sum(case when exists (select 1 from et where et.ccn=pairs.ccn and et.sd between dateadd(day,-365,pairs.d) and dateadd(day,-1,pairs.d)) then 1 else 0 end) etag_12m_before, sum(case when exists (select 1 from et where et.ccn=pairs.ccn and et.sd between dateadd(day,1,pairs.d) and dateadd(day,365,pairs.d)) then 1 else 0 end) etag_12m_after from pairs
hunches.distinct_entities: 4,957 distinct home-by-storm-day pairs (7,737 before collapsing same-day multi-event rows) across 3,428 homes in 278 hit counties; 6,810 homes carry any E-tag 2018-2026.
hunches.first_number: E-tag cited in the 12 months before the storm: 571 home-event pairs; in the 12 months after: 516. Homes in hit counties tagged at least once 2019-2025: 43.5% (1,490 of 3,428) vs 44.4% (4,983 of 11,235) in never-hit counties.
hunches.hit_means: More E-tags after than before would say surveyors find the plans failed when a real event tested them, or that storms expose unprepared homes.
hunches.miss_means: Equal before and after, which is what came back, says E-tag citation follows the survey calendar and paperwork audits, not disasters. Cook County's $500M flood of 2023-07-02: 78 homes tagged after, 76 before. A storm story needs evacuation or incident data that is not landed.
hunches.tier_reason: Both legs carry day-level dates and the chain holds end to end; the first number is found and it kills the claim as written.
hunches.time_axis: Storm events 2018-2025 by day from BEGIN_YEARMONTH+BEGIN_DAY; E-tag SURVEY_DATE 2018-01-04 to 2026-05-21 (301 rows in 2018, 6,091 in 2024).
traps: FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.COUNTY_FIPS is empty on all 14,700 rows; PROVIDER_SSA_COUNTY_CODE is an SSA code, converted through the POS_OTHER SSA/FIPS pair.
The storm mart's BEGIN_DATE_TIME is TIMESTAMP_NTZ and null on all 540,874 rows from 2018 on; build the date from BEGIN_YEARMONTH and BEGIN_DAY.
E-prefix (emergency preparedness) tags do not exist in the health deficiency file (0 rows); they live in FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_FIRE_DEFICIENCIES, 22,260 rows, tags 0001-0042.
DAMAGE_PROPERTY is text with K/M/B suffixes and 116,606 blank rows; CZ_TYPE 'Z' forecast-zone rows (238,845) are not counties.
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 26 used the same storm mart against USDA housing; hunches 13/30 used fire deficiencies for the shell carousel. Nobody has joined nursing homes to storms by county or used the E-tag family.

hunches.title: Top-paid hospitals, low stars
hunches.hunch: The 81 hospitals in the top Medicare inpatient pay-per-discharge decile that carry a 1- or 2-star rating are academic and safety-net centers collecting $5.89B, and once payment is divided by the beneficiary risk score the top decile becomes the best-rated, so highly paid and poorly rated is a case-mix artifact rather than extraction.
hunches.join_keys: INPATIENT.RNDRNG_PRVDR_CCN = HOSPITAL_GENERAL.CCN (2,991 of 3,044 match, 2,660 rated); INPATIENT.RNDRNG_PRVDR_CCN = HCRIS.PROVIDER_CCN (3,029 of 3,044, longest-period report per CCN)
hunches.query_sql: with inp as (select RNDRNG_PRVDR_CCN ccn, try_to_number(TOT_MDCR_PYMT_AMT,18,2) mdcr, try_to_number(TOT_DSCHRGS,18,2) dis, try_to_number(BENE_AVG_RISK_SCRE,18,6) risk from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_MEDICARE_INPATIENT_HOSPITALS_BY_PROVIDER), hg as (select CCN, try_to_number(HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING) star from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL), hc as (select PROVIDER_CCN ccn, try_to_number(NET_INCOME,18,2) ni, row_number() over (partition by PROVIDER_CCN order by datediff(day, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'), try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) desc) rn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HCRIS), b as (select inp.*, hg.star, hc.ni, mdcr/nullif(dis,0) pay_per_dis, ntile(10) over (order by mdcr/nullif(dis,0)) dec from inp left join hg on hg.CCN=inp.ccn left join hc on hc.ccn=inp.ccn and hc.rn=1 where dis>0) select dec, count(*) n, round(min(pay_per_dis)) min_ppd, round(max(pay_per_dis)) max_ppd, round(avg(risk),3) avg_risk, count(star) rated, round(avg(star),2) avg_star, sum(case when star<=2 then 1 else 0 end) n_1_2_star, round(100*avg(case when star<=2 then 1 else 0 end),1) pct_1_2_star, round(100*avg(case when ni<0 then 1 else 0 end),1) pct_neg_income, round(sum(mdcr)/1e9,2) mdcr_bn from b group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 3,044 inpatient hospitals; 304 in the top decile; 81 of those at 1-2 stars.
hunches.first_number: 81 hospitals in the top pay-per-discharge decile ($20,316 to $130,721 per discharge) with 1-2 stars, $5.888B Medicare inpatient payments (file undated, ingested 2026-07-26), 32 with negative FY2023 net income and 49 positive. Raw top decile 26.6% at 1-2 stars vs bottom decile 19.3%; risk-adjusted top decile 12.2% at 1-2 stars, avg 3.48.
hunches.hit_means: A payment-to-star gradient surviving risk adjustment would mean Medicare pays most to hospitals that harm patients most.
hunches.miss_means: The gradient vanishing under BENE_AVG_RISK_SCRE, which is what happened, means the star rating punishes case mix; the names are MUSC, UAB, Jackson Memorial, LA General, Grady, University of Iowa. Money and stars are measuring different things.
hunches.tier_reason: All three legs are single snapshots and the inpatient file has no year column; cross-section only.
hunches.time_axis: None usable: inpatient file has no year column and the registry records no vintage for it; Care Compare star is one snapshot; HCRIS FY ends 2023-2024.
traps: FED_CMS_MEDICARE_INPATIENT_HOSPITALS_BY_PROVIDER._SOURCE_RUN_ID is unique per row (3,044 distinct on 3,044) and there is no year column; every numeric is TEXT, use try_to_number(x,18,6).
HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING is 'Not Available' on 2,250 of 5,432 hospitals; try_to_number drops them silently.
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 11 crossed HCRIS margin with Open Payments; hunch 18 used the outpatient service file. Neither used inpatient BY_PROVIDER payment totals or pay per discharge against the star rating.

hunches.title: Dialysis in bad-water counties
hunches.hunch: Dialysis facilities in counties where half or more of the community-water population sat on a system with a health-based Safe Drinking Water Act violation in 2020-2024 show no higher standardized mortality or hospitalization than facilities in counties with no violating systems.
hunches.join_keys: DIALYSIS.STATE + upper(COUNTY_PARISH) = left(GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.PWSID,2) + upper(COUNTY_SERVED) where AREA_TYPE_CODE='CN' (1,710 of 1,836 dialysis counties match, 7,139 of 7,557 facilities; misses are SAINT vs ST., PRINCE GEORGES, and every Louisiana parish); GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.PWSID = PUB_WATER_SYSTEMS.PWSID (active CWS, POPULATION_SERVED_COUNT) = VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT.PWSID (IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND='Y', NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE 2020-2024: 225,508 rows, 42,979 distinct VIOLATION_IDs, 21,536 PWSIDs)
hunches.query_sql: with geo as (select distinct PWSID, left(PWSID,2) st, upper(trim(COUNTY_SERVED)) cty from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS where AREA_TYPE_CODE='CN' and nullif(trim(COUNTY_SERVED),'') is not null), dia as (select CCN, STATE st, upper(trim(COUNTY_PARISH)) cty, PROFIT_OR_NON_PROFIT pnp, try_to_number(MORTALITY_RATE_FACILITY,18,6) mort, try_to_number(HOSPITALIZATION_RATE_FACILITY,18,6) hosp, try_to_number(nullif(FIVE_STAR,''),18,6) star from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_DIALYSIS), v as (select PWSID, count(distinct VIOLATION_ID) hb_viols from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT where IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND='Y' and try_to_date(NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') between '2020-01-01' and '2024-12-31' group by 1), pw as (select PWSID, try_to_number(POPULATION_SERVED_COUNT,18,0) pop from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_PUB_WATER_SYSTEMS where PWS_ACTIVITY_CODE='A' and PWS_TYPE_CODE='CWS'), cty as (select geo.st, geo.cty, sum(case when v.hb_viols>0 then pw.pop else 0 end) pop_v, sum(pw.pop) pop from geo join pw on pw.PWSID=geo.PWSID left join v on v.PWSID=geo.PWSID group by 1,2), j as (select dia.*, cty.pop_v/nullif(cty.pop,0) share from dia join cty on cty.st=dia.st and cty.cty=dia.cty) select case when share>=0.5 then 'A_50pct_plus' when share>=0.1 then 'B_10_50pct' when share>0 then 'C_under_10pct' else 'D_none' end grp, count(*) facilities, count(distinct st||cty) counties, round(avg(mort),2) avg_mort, round(median(mort),2) med_mort, round(avg(hosp),1) avg_hosp, round(avg(star),2) avg_star from j group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 7,071 facilities in 1,691 matched counties: 785 facilities (252 counties) with 50%+ of CWS population on a violating system, 1,541 (451) at 10-50%, 3,401 (597) under 10%, 1,344 (391) none.
hunches.first_number: Standardized mortality rate 22.15 in the 785 facilities where 50%+ of the county's water population sat on a violating system vs 21.58 in under-10% counties and 21.79 where none violated; national 21.8 (SMR window 2021-2024). Hospitalization 143.1 vs 145.8. Nueces County TX: 96% on violating systems, 16 facilities, mortality 25.7.
hunches.hit_means: Higher mortality where the tap fails would point at dialysate water quality or a sicker, poorer population in neglected counties.
hunches.miss_means: Flat rates, which is what came back, say facility reverse-osmosis treatment and CMS risk adjustment wash out municipal water; Nueces is one county, not a pattern. Lifting to a per-year test needs the yearly measures in FED_CMS_MEDICARE_DIALYSIS_FACILITIES (YEAR 2021-2024).
hunches.tier_reason: SDWA violations are dated but the dialysis mortality is one 2021-2024 window per facility; cross-section only.
hunches.time_axis: SDWA NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE is MM/DD/YYYY text, filtered 2020-2024; dialysis SMR_DATE reads '01Jan2021-31Dec2024' on every row.
traps: FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT is a violation-by-enforcement long table: 225,508 rows for 42,979 distinct VIOLATION_IDs (5.2 rows each) in the health-based 2020-2024 slice; count distinct VIOLATION_ID or violations inflate 5x. IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND is null on 1,002,550 rows.

FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.STATE_SERVED is null on county (CN) rows; the state is left(PWSID,2) and ANSI_ENTITY_CODE is the 3-digit county FIPS. ZIP_CODE_SERVED exists only on the 7,155 ZC rows.
County-name join to CMS misses 126 of 1,836 dialysis counties: SAINT LOUIS, SAINT CLAIR, SAINT LUCIE (CMS spells SAINT, SDWA ST.), PRINCE GEORGES (apostrophe), and every Louisiana parish.
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 6 (rural dialysis) used dialysis x affiliation x QPP HPSA status. No prior hunch touched any SDWA table; the county bridge from dialysis to water systems is new.

hunches.title: Hospitals as hazardous-waste violators
hunches.hunch: Hospitals that EPA's RCRA program has cited three or more times since 2015 post negative FY2023 net income at 34.5% versus 24.5% for matched hospitals with no citations, with no difference in star rating, so compliance spending tracks money, not care quality.
hunches.join_keys: RCRA_NAICS.ID_NUMBER where NAICS_CODE like '62211%' (3,340 IDs) = RCRA_FACILITIES.ID_NUMBER; normalized FACILITY_NAME + upper(CITY_NAME) + STATE_CODE = normalized HOSPITAL_GENERAL.FACILITY_NAME + upper(CITY_TOWN) + STATE, multi-word names only (832 IDs to 811 CCNs: 14.9% of 5,432 hospitals, 24.9% of RCRA hospital sites); RCRA_VIOLATIONS.ID_NUMBER = matched ID (1,915 violations since 2015 at 350 CCNs, 61 never returned to compliance); HOSPITAL_GENERAL.CCN = HCRIS.PROVIDER_CCN (801 of 811)
hunches.query_sql: with rf as (select distinct n.ID_NUMBER id, trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(f.FACILITY_NAME),'[^A-Z0-9 ]',''),'\\s+',' ')) nname, upper(f.CITY_NAME) city, f.STATE_CODE st from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_RCRA_RCRA_NAICS n join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_RCRA_FACILITIES f on f.ID_NUMBER=n.ID_NUMBER where n.NAICS_CODE like '62211%'), hg as (select CCN, try_to_number(HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING) star, trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(FACILITY_NAME),'[^A-Z0-9 ]',''),'\\s+',' ')) nname, upper(CITY_TOWN) city, STATE st from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL), hc as (select PROVIDER_CCN ccn, try_to_number(NET_INCOME,18,2) ni, try_to_number(TOTAL_COSTS,18,2) tc, row_number() over (partition by PROVIDER_CCN order by datediff(day, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'), try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) desc) rn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HCRIS), m as (select distinct rf.id, hg.CCN, hg.star from rf join hg on hg.nname=rf.nname and hg.city=rf.city and hg.st=rf.st where array_size(split(rf.nname,' '))>=2), v as (select ID_NUMBER id, count(*) viols from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_RCRA_VIOLATIONS where try_to_date(DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED,'MM/DD/YYYY')>='2015-01-01' group by 1), per as (select m.CCN, max(m.star) star, sum(coalesce(v.viols,0)) viols from m left join v on v.id=m.id group by 1) select case when viols>=3 then 'A_3plus' when viols>=1 then 'B_1_2' else 'C_zero' end grp, count(*) hospitals, count(star) rated, round(avg(star),2) avg_star, round(100*avg(case when star<=2 then 1 else 0 end),1) pct_1_2_star, round(100*avg(case when hc.ni<0 then 1 else 0 end),1) pct_neg_income, round(median(hc.ni/nullif(hc.tc,0))*100,2) med_margin_pct from per left join hc on hc.ccn=per.CCN and hc.rn=1 group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 832 RCRA site IDs matched to 811 Care Compare hospitals: 252 with 3+ violations since 2015, 98 with 1-2, 461 with none.
hunches.first_number: 34.5% of the 252 hospitals with 3+ RCRA violations since 2015 had negative FY2023 net income (median margin +5.18% of cost) vs 24.5% of 461 zero-violation matched hospitals (median +7.46%); avg star 3.24 vs 3.15. Virginia Hospital Center, Arlington VA: 71 violations since 2015, 4 stars. Five sample exact pairs: DEKALB REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER (Fort Payne AL, CCN 010012), BAPTIST MEDICAL CENTER SOUTH (Montgomery AL, 010023), GADSDEN REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER (Gadsden AL, 010040), FLOWERS HOSPITAL (Dothan AL, 010055), DCH REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER (Tuscaloosa AL, 010092).
hunches.hit_means: More waste violations at thinner-margin hospitals says environmental compliance is the first budget cut; a repeat violator with an open violation and a negative margin is a facility to visit.
hunches.miss_means: Flat stars, which is what came back, say waste handling and patient outcomes are run by different shops; a 10-point margin gap on 252 vs 461 hospitals is suggestive, and the 811 matched skew to large urban hospitals that register with RCRA at all.
hunches.tier_reason: Violations are dated but star rating and HCRIS are one snapshot each; the exact-name match leaves 75% of RCRA hospital sites unmatched.
hunches.time_axis: RCRA DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED is MM/DD/YYYY text 1987-2025, filtered 2015+; ACTUAL_RTC_DATE blank on 61 matched violations; star and HCRIS are snapshots.
traps: FED_EPA_RCRA_RCRA_NAICS.NAICS_CODE mixes lengths: '62211' on 2,139 rows vs '622110' on 1,207; filtering on the 6-digit code alone loses 64% of hospital sites.
A loose first-three-words match adds 159 CCNs but pairs BAPTIST MEDICAL CENTER EAST with BAPTIST MEDICAL CENTER SOUTH in the same city; use exact normalized names.
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 29 counted TRI sites per county against hospital terminations; hunch 22 put TRI in HOLC zones. Nobody has matched EPA facility records to individual hospitals by name, and RCRA is a new table family for this hub.

hunches.title: Triple owners are the good ones
hunches.hunch: The 89 PECOS associate IDs that hold a nursing home, a home health agency and a hospice at once run better-rated, less-fined homes and better-scoring HHAs than other chain homes, so the one-owner-three-post-acute-lines shape found in the Frank case is, at scale, the integrated nonprofit system rather than the bad actor.
hunches.join_keys: SNF_ENROLLMENTS.ASSOCIATE_ID (14,425 rows, 12,218 distinct, 100% filled) = HHA_ENROLLMENTS.ASSOCIATE_ID (11,508 / 10,223) = HOSPICE_ENROLLMENTS.ASSOCIATE_ID (6,066 / 5,372): 89 IDs in all three; 58 of them also in HOSPITAL_ENROLLMENTS (9,175 / 5,280). SNF_ENROLLMENTS.CCN = NURSINGHOME411.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN (330 of 334 triple-owner homes); HHA_ENROLLMENTS.CCN = HOME_HEALTH.CCN (141 of 144); SNF CCN = PENALTIES CCN
hunches.query_sql: with tri as (select a.ASSOCIATE_ID from (select distinct ASSOCIATE_ID from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_SKILLED_NURSING_FACILITY_ENROLLMENTS where nullif(trim(ASSOCIATE_ID),'') is not null) a join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HOME_HEALTH_AGENCY_ENROLLMENTS h on h.ASSOCIATE_ID=a.ASSOCIATE_ID join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HOSPICE_ENROLLMENTS o on o.ASSOCIATE_ID=a.ASSOCIATE_ID group by 1), snf as (select distinct CCN, ASSOCIATE_ID from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_SKILLED_NURSING_FACILITY_ENROLLMENTS), nh as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN ccn, try_to_number(OVERALL_RATING,18,6) star, try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_FINES_IN_DOLLARS,18,2) fines, try_to_number(REPORTED_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_PER_DAY,18,6) hprd, nullif(trim(CHAIN_ID),'') chain_id, ABUSE_ICON abuse from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_NURSINGHOME411), g as (select nh.*, case when tri.ASSOCIATE_ID is not null then 'A_triple_owner_home' when nh.chain_id is not null then 'B_other_chain_home' else 'C_independent' end grp from nh left join snf on snf.CCN=nh.ccn left join tri on tri.ASSOCIATE_ID=snf.ASSOCIATE_ID) select grp, count(distinct ccn) homes, round(avg(star),3) avg_star, round(100*avg(case when star<=2 then 1 else 0 end),1) pct_1_2_star, round(avg(fines),0) avg_fines, round(avg(hprd),3) avg_nurse_hprd, round(100*avg(case when abuse='Y' then 1 else 0 end),2) pct_abuse_icon from g group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 89 owners holding 334 nursing homes, 144 HHAs and 106 hospices (584 facility enrollments); 58 of the 89 also hold a hospital. Largest: Evangelical Lutheran Good Samaritan Society 87/19/4, Liberty Healthcare Group 30/18/4.
hunches.first_number: Triple-owner homes (330 in NH411): avg overall star 3.30, 31.8% at 1-2 stars, $20,229 fines per home, 0.79 penalties per home 2023-06 to 2026-05; other chain homes (9,920): 2.84, 44.8%, $31,261, 1.10 penalties per home. Their 141 HHAs: star 3.42 vs 3.25, discharge-to-community 83.7 vs 80.1, preventable hospitalization 9.28 vs 10.92 (lower is better).
hunches.hit_means: Worse scores would have said vertical integration is a referral-capture machine; better scores, which is what came back, say the owners who enroll all three lines under one ID are Good Samaritan, Dignity, Presbyterian, Intermountain and county hospital districts.
hunches.miss_means: The method only sees an owner who enrolls all three lines under one PECOS associate ID. A for-profit roll-up that enrolls each facility as its own LLC never shares an ID and is invisible here, so the clean result is a bridge gap on bad actors, not an acquittal. The PECOS All Owners file would close it.
hunches.tier_reason: The claim is directly testable as written and the penalty leg is dated 2023-06 to 2026-05; ownership itself is one snapshot.
hunches.time_axis: PENALTY_DATE 2023-06-17 to 2026-05-13; enrollment, NH411 and Home Health files are 2026 snapshots.
traps: Shared ASSOCIATE_ID selects integrated systems by construction; 58 of the 89 also own a hospital.
One ID (Good Samaritan) carries 87 SNFs, so any per-owner average is that one system; report per home.
hunches.overlap_check: Hunches 1, 20 and 31 counted pairs (SNF+hospice 133, hospital+HHA 475, hospital+hospice 334). The triple, the hospital fourth leg, and the quality and penalty profile of the owners' homes and HHAs are new.

hunches.title: REH conversions after the loss
hunches.hunch: Rural hospitals that converted to Rural Emergency Hospital status in 2023-2026 were already deep in the red on their last pre-conversion cost report: 28 of 35 negative, median margin -12.25% of cost against +5.2% for hospitals nationally.
hunches.join_keys: HOSPITAL_ENROLLMENTS.REH_CONVERSION_FLAG='Y' (48 rows, 45 with REH_CONVERSION_DATE) -> split_part(CAH_OR_HOSPITAL_CCN,'|',1) predecessor CCN = HCRIS.PROVIDER_CCN (35 of 48; the unsplit join found only 21); predecessor CCN = POS_OTHER.CCN category 01 (30 of 48, 25 of them terminated); new REH CCN = HOSPITAL_GENERAL.CCN (8 of 48)
hunches.query_sql: with r as (select CCN reh_ccn, split_part(nullif(trim(CAH_OR_HOSPITAL_CCN),''),'|',1) old_ccn, try_to_date(nullif(trim(REH_CONVERSION_DATE),''),'MM/DD/YYYY') cd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_ENROLLMENTS where REH_CONVERSION_FLAG='Y'), hc as (select PROVIDER_CCN ccn, try_to_number(NET_INCOME,18,2) ni, try_to_number(TOTAL_COSTS,18,2) tc, CCN_FACILITY_TYPE ft, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') fye, row_number() over (partition by PROVIDER_CCN order by datediff(day, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'), try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) desc) rn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HCRIS) select count(*) reh_rows, count(cd) dated, min(cd) first_conv, max(cd) last_conv, count(hc.ccn) in_hcris, sum(case when hc.ni<0 then 1 else 0 end) neg_income, round(100*sum(case when hc.ni<0 then 1 else 0 end)/nullif(count(hc.ccn),0),1) pct_neg, round(median(hc.ni/nullif(hc.tc,0))*100,2) med_margin_pct, sum(case when hc.ft='CAH' then 1 else 0 end) cah, sum(case when hc.ft='STH' then 1 else 0 end) sth, sum(case when cd > hc.fye then 1 else 0 end) converted_after_fy_end from r left join hc on hc.ccn=coalesce(r.old_ccn, r.reh_ccn) and hc.rn=1
hunches.distinct_entities: 48 REH hospitals, 35 with a predecessor cost report (17 critical access, 18 short-term); 34 of the 35 converted after that report's fiscal year ended.
hunches.first_number: 28 of 35 (80%) REH converters had negative net income on their last cost report (FY ends 2023-01-31 to 2024-08-31), median margin -12.25% of cost; all short-term hospitals 33.9% negative with median +5.17%, all critical access 32.4% and +5.21%. EAMC-Lanier AL: -138% of cost, converted 2025-02-10; Sturgis Hospital MI -55%, converted 2023-08-02.
hunches.hit_means: REH is a lifeline taken by hospitals already failing, and the conversion date lets you watch what happens to a county after its inpatient beds close (terminations, transfers, the nearest hospital's volume).
hunches.miss_means: If converters looked like the national mix, REH would be a strategic choice, not a rescue; 13 of 48 have no cost report under either CCN, so 35 is a floor on the sample.
hunches.tier_reason: REH_CONVERSION_DATE and FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE are both dated and 34 of 35 reports precede the conversion; first number found; n is small at 35.
hunches.time_axis: REH_CONVERSION_DATE 2023-02-10 to 2026-03-14 (MM/DD/YYYY text, 45 of 48 filled); HCRIS FY ends 2023-01-31 to 2024-08-31.
traps: FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_ENROLLMENTS.CAH_OR_HOSPITAL_CCN holds pipe-separated multiples ('041304|04Z304', '370178|37S178|37U178'); the raw value matched 21 predecessors, split_part on '|' matched 35.
REH CCNs run in a new 0779-0801 series; only 8 of 48 appear in Care Compare and the new CCN has no cost report, so all history sits under the predecessor CCN.
hunches.overlap_check: Own idea. Nearest are hunch 29 (POS hospital terminations vs HCRIS) and hunch 12 (LTCH margins). The REH flag and its conversion date have not been used anywhere.

hunches.title: Terminations foreshadowed in cost reports
hunches.hunch: Hospitals whose Medicare participation ended in 2024-2026 were 67.6% negative on their FY2023 cost report (median -8.14% of cost) versus 33.8% for hospitals still active, while the sale-then-closure version dies: only 44 of 1,299 terminations since 2015 (3.4%) had an ownership change in the prior 24 months.
hunches.join_keys: POS_OTHER.CCN (category 01; PGM_TRMNTN_CD<>'00'; TRMNTN_EXPRTN_DT YYYYMMDD) = HCRIS.PROVIDER_CCN with a 350-380 day report (142 hospitals terminated 2024-2026 match, 7 terminated in 2023, 5,586 active); POS_OTHER.CCN = HOSPITAL_GENERAL.CCN (0 of 762 hospitals terminated 2019-2023 present, 10 of 99 terminated in 2024)
hunches.query_sql: with hc as (select PROVIDER_CCN ccn, try_to_number(NET_INCOME,18,2) ni, try_to_number(TOTAL_COSTS,18,2) tc, datediff(day, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'), try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) days, row_number() over (partition by PROVIDER_CCN order by datediff(day, try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'), try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) desc) rn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HCRIS), h as (select CCN, PGM_TRMNTN_CD term, try_to_date(nullif(trim(TRMNTN_EXPRTN_DT),''),'YYYYMMDD') term_dt from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_POS_OTHER where PRVDR_CTGRY_CD='01') select case when term<>'00' and term_dt between '2024-01-01' and '2026-12-31' then 'A_terminated_2024_2026' when term<>'00' and term_dt between '2023-01-01' and '2023-12-31' then 'B_terminated_2023' when term='00' then 'C_active' else 'D_terminated_earlier' end grp, count(*) hospitals, sum(case when ni<0 then 1 else 0 end) negative_income, round(100*avg(case when ni<0 then 1 else 0 end),1) pct_negative_income, round(median(ni/nullif(tc,0))*100,2) median_margin_pct_of_cost from hc join h on h.CCN=hc.ccn where rn=1 and days between 350 and 380 and tc>0 group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 5,736 hospitals with a 12-month cost report and a POS row: 142 terminated 2024-2026, 7 terminated 2023, 5,586 active, 1 earlier.
hunches.first_number: 96 of 142 (67.6%) hospitals terminated 2024-2026 were negative on their FY2023 cost report, median margin -8.14% of cost, vs 1,889 of 5,586 active (33.8%, median +5.32%). Worst: EAMC-Lanier AL -138.1% (terminated 2024-11-30), Hampstead Hospital NH -111.1% (2025-02-02), Western Peaks Specialty LTCH UT -103.8% (2024-04-30). CHOW within 24 months before termination: 44 of 1,299 terminations 2015-2025.
hunches.hit_means: The cost report predicts termination one to two years out, so the active hospitals below -30% of cost today are the watch list; the 3.4% CHOW figure says closures are rarely flips.
hunches.miss_means: Care Compare deletes terminated hospitals, so the last star before closure cannot be read from the snapshot; and 2023's 365 terminations (271 of them code 01 voluntary on short-term hospitals) barely appear in HCRIS (7), which is the coding-sweep signature, not a wave of closures.
hunches.tier_reason: TRMNTN_EXPRTN_DT and FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE are both dated and the report precedes the termination; first number found; the CHOW-then-terminate sub-claim was tested and is dead at 3.4%.
hunches.time_axis: TRMNTN_EXPRTN_DT 1963-05-07 to 2026-03-19 (YYYYMMDD text, filled on every non-00 row); CHOW_DT 1973-2026; HCRIS FY ends 2022-12 to 2024-12.
traps: Terminated hospitals vanish from FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL: 0 of 762 hospitals terminated 2019-2023 are present, 10 of 99 terminated in 2024. 'Last star before closure' needs an archived Care Compare release.
2023 hospital terminations: 365 vs 68-122 in other years, 271 of them PGM_TRMNTN_CD '01' on subtype 01; only 7 of the 365 filed a 12-month FY2023 cost report. Treat 2023 as a sweep.
CHOW-year cohorts are small (14 to 92 hospitals a year) so the 24-month termination rate swings 2.3% to 21.4%; never-sold hospitals terminated at 10.9% over 2012-2026.
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 29 counted POS terminations by year against TRI county density and flagged the 2023 spike. This is the first join of a termination date to that hospital's own last cost report, and the first test of sale-then-terminate.

hunches.title: Sprinkler flag yes, inspector says install
hunches.hunch: 1,500 nursing homes whose Care Compare directory says automatic sprinklers cover all required areas were cited K0351, install an approved automatic sprinkler system, in a Life Safety survey since June 2024, 458 at F-or-worse scope and 3 at immediate jeopardy.
hunches.join_keys: NURSING_HOME.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER__CCN = FIRE_DEFICIENCIES.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN (1,605 K0351 citations since 2024-06-01 at 1,504 homes; 1,500 of those homes carry the 'Yes' flag, 2 'Partial', 2 'Data Not Available')
hunches.query_sql: with k as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN ccn, count(*) cites, max(SCOPE_SEVERITY_CODE) max_sev, sum(case when upper(DEFICIENCY_CORRECTED) like '%CORRECTED%' or nullif(trim(CORRECTION_DATE),'') is not null then 1 else 0 end) corrected from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_FIRE_DEFICIENCIES where DEFICIENCY_PREFIX='K' and DEFICIENCY_TAG_NUMBER='0351' and try_to_date(SURVEY_DATE)>='2024-06-01' group by 1) select n.AUTOMATIC_SPRINKLER_SYSTEMS_IN_ALL_REQUIRED_AREAS flag, count(*) homes, count(k.ccn) homes_cited_k0351_since_2024_06, round(100*count(k.ccn)/count(*),2) pct, sum(case when k.max_sev in ('F','G','H','I','J','K','L') then 1 else 0 end) cited_F_or_worse, sum(case when k.max_sev in ('J','K','L') then 1 else 0 end) immediate_jeopardy, sum(case when k.corrected<k.cites then 1 else 0 end) some_uncorrected from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME n left join k on k.ccn=n.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER__CCN group by 1 order by 2 desc
hunches.distinct_entities: 1,504 homes cited K0351 since 2024-06-01; 1,500 of them flagged 'Yes' (10.25% of the 14,638 'Yes' homes); 34 homes in the whole directory say 'Partial'.
hunches.first_number: 1,500 of 14,638 'Yes' homes (10.25%) cited K0351 since 2024-06-01; 458 at F or worse; 3 at immediate jeopardy: Pittsburg Skilled Nursing Center CA (2025-03-06, K), The Eleanor Nursing Care Center NY (2024-09-17, L), Autumn Lake Healthcare at Norwalk CT (2024-07-23, J); 26 homes still carry an uncorrected K0351.
hunches.hit_means: The directory flag is self-reported and near-constant (99.6% Yes); the inspector's K0351 is the real sprinkler status, so each of the 1,500 is a public listing contradicted by the home's own survey record.
hunches.miss_means: K0351 also covers partial or non-approved installations, so a cited home may have sprinklers that fail a standard rather than none; but the flag cannot read 'Yes' while the tag stands, and only 34 homes ever admit 'Partial'.
hunches.tier_reason: Citations are dated; the directory flag is one 2026-05-01 snapshot with no history, so no before/after on the flag.
hunches.time_axis: Fire SURVEY_DATE 2016-07-28 to 2026-05-21; flag PROCESSING_DATE 2026-05-01 only.
traps: FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.AUTOMATIC_SPRINKLER_SYSTEMS_IN_ALL_REQUIRED_AREAS is 'Yes' on 14,638 of 14,700 rows (99.6%), a near-constant like the ownership-change flag, and 1,500 of the Yes homes were cited for no approved system.

FIRE_DEFICIENCIES.DEFICIENCY_CORRECTED has six spellings ('Deficient, Provider has date of correction' 3,657; 'Waiver has been granted' 71; 'Deficient, Provider has plan of correction' 32; 'Deficient, Provider has no plan of correction' 17; 'No revisit needed' 2; 'Past Non-Compliance' 2 on K0351 alone); CORRECTION_DATE is the safer test.
hunches.overlap_check: Own idea. Hunch 13 used fire deficiencies at G+ severity for the shell carousel; nobody has crossed the directory's self-reported sprinkler flag against the K0351 tag.

hunches.title: Administrator churn, harm rising
hunches.hunch: Nursing homes that lost two or more administrators saw harm-level (G-or-worse) citations per home rise 53% from 2023 to 2025 (0.538 to 0.825) while homes with no administrator departure rose 14% (0.293 to 0.334), about the survey-coverage growth.
hunches.join_keys: NURSING_HOME.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER__CCN = DEFICIENCIES.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN, aggregated per CCN per year first; NUMBER_OF_ADMINISTRATORS_WHO_HAVE_LEFT_THE_NURSING_HOME filled on 12,961 of 14,700 homes (7,901 zero, 3,561 one, 1,499 two or more, 1,739 blank)
hunches.query_sql: with d as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN ccn, year(try_to_date(SURVEY_DATE)) y, sum(case when SCOPE_SEVERITY_CODE in ('G','H','I','J','K','L') then 1 else 0 end) g, count(*) defs from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_DEFICIENCIES where try_to_date(SURVEY_DATE) between '2023-01-01' and '2025-12-31' group by 1,2), n as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER__CCN ccn, try_to_number(nullif(trim(NUMBER_OF_ADMINISTRATORS_WHO_HAVE_LEFT_THE_NURSING_HOME),''),18,0) adm, try_to_number(nullif(trim(TOTAL_NURSING_STAFF_TURNOVER),''),18,6) turn, try_to_number(OVERALL_RATING,18,6) star from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME), a as (select n.ccn, n.adm, n.turn, n.star, sum(case when y=2023 then g end) g23, sum(case when y=2025 then g end) g25 from n left join d on d.ccn=n.ccn group by 1,2,3,4) select case when adm is null then 'Z_blank' when adm=0 then 'A_0' when adm=1 then 'B_1' else 'C_2plus' end adm_left, count(*) homes, round(avg(turn),1) avg_nurse_turnover_pct, round(avg(star),2) avg_star, round(sum(coalesce(g23,0))/count(*),3) gplus_per_home_2023, round(sum(coalesce(g25,0))/count(*),3) gplus_per_home_2025, round(100*(sum(coalesce(g25,0))-sum(coalesce(g23,0)))/nullif(sum(coalesce(g23,0)),0),1) gplus_change_pct, count(case when g25>coalesce(g23,0) then 1 end) homes_gplus_rose from a group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 14,700 homes: 7,901 with zero administrator departures, 3,561 with one, 1,499 with two or more, 1,739 blank.
hunches.first_number: Homes with 2+ administrators gone: G+ citations per home 0.538 (2023) to 0.825 (2025), +53.3%, 445 homes rose vs 248 fell, nurse turnover 53.8%, avg star 2.31. Zero gone: 0.293 to 0.334, +14.1%, turnover 43.4%, star 3.31. One gone: +45.4%.
hunches.hit_means: Leadership churn is a leading indicator surveyors and families could act on, and it stacks with nurse turnover; the 1,499 two-plus homes are a list.
hunches.miss_means: The departures column is a single recent 12-month window with no start date in the file, so this reads 'churned lately, harm rose lately' and the direction of cause is open; the 14% floor is coverage growth (homes cited 10,787 to 11,939).
hunches.tier_reason: The deficiency leg is dated but the administrator-departure leg is one undated window; cross-section on the predictor.
hunches.time_axis: Deficiency SURVEY_DATE full years 2023 and 2025; turnover window undated, directory PROCESSING_DATE 2026-05-01.
