hubs.notes:
NUMBERING: these are hunches #32-#43 for Hub C. Five run Tier 1 with dated legs (sold hospitals, chain trend, storms/E-tags, REH, terminations) plus triple owners; four Tier 2; one Tier 3.

DEAD OR REVERSED SEEDS, with the number that killed them:
- Seed 1 HHA/hospice CHOW: 0 HHA (05), hospice (08) or ESRD rows in POS_OTHER; only categories 21/12/01/19/06 exist. Hospitals branch lives (hunch 32). HHA proxy reverses: hands-changed agencies rate 3.48-3.55 vs 3.17 owner-founded.
- Seed 2 as 2018-2025: the deficiency file covers 2,004 homes in 2019 and 10,787 in 2023; only 2023 vs 2025 is a fair trend.
- Seed 3: chain holds, result is null. E-tags 571 before vs 516 after in 4,957 home-storm pairs; hit-county homes tagged 43.5% vs 44.4% never-hit.
- Seed 4: no gradient. Top pay-per-discharge decile 26.6% at 1-2 stars vs 19.3% bottom; risk-adjusted top decile 12.2%. The 81 are academic and safety-net hospitals.
- Seed 5: null. Mortality 22.15 in worst-water counties vs 21.58 clean vs 21.8 national.
- Seed 6: margin signal only (34.5% vs 24.5% negative income), zero star signal; exact name match reaches 811 of 5,432 hospitals.
- Seed 7 reverses: triple owners' homes 3.30 stars / 31.8% low-star vs other chains 2.84 / 44.8%. The ASSOCIATE_ID bridge finds integrated nonprofits by construction; for-profit roll-ups enrolling one LLC per facility never share an ID.
- Seed 8a (last star before termination): 0 of 762 hospitals terminated 2019-2023 remain in Care Compare. Reframed to the last cost report (hunch 40). Seed 8b (sale then terminate within 24 months): 44 of 1,299 terminations since 2015 (3.4%); dead.

WISH LIST, top 5 for Hub C:
1. CMS PECOS 'All Owners' files (Hospital, SNF, HHA, Hospice ownership: owner name, role, ASSOCIATION_DATE, PE/REIT/holding flags). Rescues: hunch 38 blind spot (roll-ups under separate LLCs), hunch 23 hidden-owner DME, hunch 30 carousel (a real owner-change date instead of incorporation), hunch 2 chain attribution over time. Question: which private-equity or REIT owners' homes rose fastest in G+ citations 2023-2025 and were they bought before the rise.
2. CMS Provider of Services file, all provider types (02 SNF, 05 HHA, 08 hospice, 09 ESRD with CHOW_DT, CHOW_PRIOR_DT, PGM_TRMNTN_CD, TRMNTN_EXPRTN_DT). Rescues: seed 1 HHA/hospice (hunch 43), the nursing-home CHOW constant trap, seed 8 for HHA/hospice, dialysis terminations. Question: do HHAs and hospices sold 2021-2024 lose stars and discharge-to-community afterward, using the same pre/post design that worked for hospitals.
3. HCRIS beyond one hospital year: hospital 2552-10 FY2018-2024, SNF 2540-10, HHA 1728-94, hospice 1984-14. Rescues: hunch 28 (no SNF cost data), hunch 21 (one-year offset), hunch 11, hunches 39 and 40 become multi-year trajectories, hunch 33 gets margins next to citations. Question: how many years of losses precede a termination or REH conversion, and do chain home margins rise as harm citations rise.
4. CMS Hospice Utilization and Payment PUF by provider and year (live discharge rate, length of stay, days, dollars). Rescues: hunch 1 (hospice ghosts have no utilization), the Frank hospice thread (zero data now), hunch 38's hospice leg. Question: do owner-shared or recently re-incorporated hospices discharge patients alive at higher rates and keep them longer.
5. Care Compare archived releases 2019-2026 (Hospital General Information, Home Health, Nursing Home Provider Info by month). Rescues: hunch 32's star snapshot, seed 8a (last star of the 762 dropped hospitals), hunch 31 and 43 time axes, the sprinkler flag history (hunch 41). Question: does the star rating fall after a CHOW, and what did the 365 hospitals dropped in 2023 look like the month before.
Also: the Medicare Provider Reassignment (revalidation reassignment list) file is the org-to-person bridge Hub B needs; it is not in this hub's list but every FQHC/RHC/OTP dead hunch waits on it.

OTHER THINGS THE SYNTHESIZER MUST KNOW:
- The registry lives at LIBRARY_META.REGISTRY.SOURCE_REGISTRY and SOURCE_FRESHNESS; LIBRARY_META.CONNECT.SOURCE_REGISTRY does not exist. SOURCE_FRESHNESS has no vintage for the inpatient or hospital general files (RECENCY_KIND 'none').
- FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL and FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_COMPARE are the same 5,432 CCNs; the hash differs only because the key column is named CCN vs FACILITY_ID.
- FED_CMS_MEDICARE_DIALYSIS_FACILITIES holds per-year measures 2021-2024 (8,241 CCNs per year) and is the only dated dialysis outcome leg; hunch 36 can be lifted to Tier 1 with it.
- Every hospital CHOW/termination/REH result uses 12-month HCRIS reports only (5,799 of 6,103) and compares each hospital to its own fiscal year end because FY ends span 2023 and 2024.
- All numbers are from the Python door; every query wrapped in try/except with JSON receipts in the hubC folder (p00 through p10). No real cost number for this run: no prior identical pattern exists in the query log to price it against.

hunches.title: Flood-year drinking water violations
hunches.hunch: Counties with a FEMA IA disaster declaration in 2015-2020 log more health-based Safe Drinking Water Act violations in the year after the declaration than the year before, relative to never-declared counties.
hunches.join_keys: FEMA.FIPS (5-digit, non-null on 89% of rows since 2015, INCIDENTTYPECODE<>'B') = CENSUS.GEOID; SDWA_VIOLATIONS.PWSID = GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.PWSID (AREA_TYPE_CODE='CN'); left(PWSID,2) = CENSUS.STUSPS and lpad(ANSI_ENTITY_CODE,3,'0') = CENSUS.COUNTYFP (394,358 of 411,651 CN rows match, 95.8%, 3,192 counties; 443 PWS serve 2+ counties so a violation counts once per county served). Violations deduped on PWSID+VIOLATION_ID because the table fans out 3.5x on enforcement rows.
hunches.query_sql: with decl as (select FIPS, min(left(DECLARATIONDATE,4))::int yr, count(*) regs from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS where DECLARATIONDATE >= '2015-01-01' and DECLARATIONDATE < '2021-01-01' and INCIDENTTYPECODE <> 'B' and length(FIPS)=5 group by FIPS), hb as (select c.GEOID fips, right(v.NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE,4)::int yr, count(*) n from (select distinct PWSID, VIOLATION_ID, NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT where IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND='Y' and right(NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE,4) between '2013' and '2022') v join (select distinct PWSID, ANSI_ENTITY_CODE from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS where AREA_TYPE_CODE='CN') g on g.PWSID=v.PWSID join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY c on c.STUSPS=left(g.PWSID,2) and c.COUNTYFP=lpad(g.ANSI_ENTITY_CODE,3,'0') group by 1,2), declared as (select d.yr, count(*) counties, sum(coalesce(b.n,0)) before_n, sum(coalesce(a.n,0)) after_n from decl d left join hb b on b.fips=d.FIPS and b.yr=d.yr-1 left join hb a on a.fips=d.FIPS and a.yr=d.yr+1 group by 1), yrs as (select 2015 yr union all select 2016 union all select 2017 union all select 2018 union all select 2019 union all select 2020), control as (select y.yr, count(*) counties, sum(coalesce(b.n,0)) before_n, sum(coalesce(a.n,0)) after_n from yrs y cross join (select GEOID from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY where GEOID not in (select FIPS from decl)) c left join hb b on b.fips=c.GEOID and b.yr=y.yr-1 left join hb a on a.fips=c.GEOID and a.yr=y.yr+1 group by 1) select 'declared' grp, * from declared union all select 'control', * from control order by 1,2
hunches.distinct_entities: 1,027 declared counties 2015-2020 (889 with any health-based violation 2013-2022); 2,916 counties with health-based violations; 136,546 distinct health-based violations 2013-2022; 2,266 never-declared control counties
hunches.first_number: Declared counties: 5,059 health-based violations in year+1 vs 5,577 in year-1, ratio 0.907; cohort-weighted control ratio 0.825. The whole gap is the 2015 Oklahoma+Texas flood cohort: 154 counties, 1,819 to 2,211 (1.216). The other 873 declared counties ran 0.758, below control. Inside Oklahoma, 2015-declared counties went 667 (2014) to 882 (2016), +32%, vs +18% in non-declared Oklahoma counties; Texas +21% vs +9%. The excess is Stage 2 disinfection byproduct MCL violations (rule family 220): Oklahoma 578 in 2014 to 885 in 2016.
hunches.hit_means: A declared county's health-based violations rise after the disaster while matched counties fall: flood water pushes organics into small systems and the chlorination byproducts breach the MCL. The Oklahoma/Texas 2015 cohort is the live version of that story.
hunches.miss_means: Violations track the national decline regardless of disasters, which is what 873 of 1,027 declared counties show. Disasters do not generally break water systems in a way SDWIS records within a year, or state reporting swamps the signal.
hunches.tier_reason: Both legs carry dates (FEMA DECLARATIONDATE 2002-2026, SDWA NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE 1970s-2026) and the before/after ran. The general claim is killed by the first run; the OK/TX 2015 flood cohort survives as a specific lead.
hunches.time_axis: FEMA declarations 2015-2020 (first per county); SDWA health-based violations by begin year 2013-2022; control counties same calendar windows
traps: SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT fans out 3.5x on enforcement rows and has 1,002,550 enforcement-only rows with null VIOLATION_ID
GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.STATE_SERVED is 0% filled; state comes from left(PWSID,2)
FEMA INCIDENTTYPECODE 'B' is COVID funeral assistance, 3,127 counties in 2020
Oklahoma and Texas health-based violations rose statewide 2015-2016, so any Oklahoma-heavy cohort inherits a state trend
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 5 (FEMA debt trap: FEMA IA x HMDA rate spread). This uses FEMA IA against SDWA violations, a table pair not in any existing hunch, and adds a matched never-declared control.

hunches.title: Sewage noncompliance after storms
hunches.hunch: NPDES permittees in counties hit by a $10M+ property-damage storm show a higher share of significant-noncompliance quarters in the quarter after the storm than in their own other quarters, 2015-2024.
hunches.join_keys: STORMS: lpad(STATE_FIPS,2,'0')||lpad(CZ_FIPS,3,'0') where CZ_TYPE='C' = CENSUS.GEOID (3,106 of 3,308 county codes since 2015 match, 93.9%; misses are Connecticut 09xxx and 97xxx/99xxx codes); ICIS_FACILITIES.COUNTY_CODE 'OK063' split as STUSPS+COUNTYFP = CENSUS (3,206 of 3,232 codes match; COUNTY_CODE null on 42% of facilities); QNCR_HISTORY.NPDES_ID = ICIS_FACILITIES.NPDES_ID (616,835 of 616,835 IDs since 2015 match, 367,000 with a county); quarter index = year*4+qtr-1 on both sides
hunches.query_sql: with storms as (select distinct lpad(STATE_FIPS,2,'0')||lpad(CZ_FIPS,3,'0') fips, left(BEGIN_YEARMONTH,4)::int*4 + ceil(right(BEGIN_YEARMONTH,2)::int/3.0)::int - 1 idx from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_STORM_EVENTS where CZ_TYPE='C' and YEAR between 2015 and 2024 and (case when DAMAGE_PROPERTY like '%B' then try_to_number(replace(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,'B',''),18,6)*1e9 when DAMAGE_PROPERTY like '%M' then try_to_number(replace(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,'M',''),18,6)*1e6 when DAMAGE_PROPERTY like '%K' then try_to_number(replace(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,'K',''),18,6)*1e3 else try_to_number(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,18,6) end) >= 10000000), fac as (select f.NPDES_ID, c.GEOID fips from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_NPDES_ICIS_FACILITIES f join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY c on c.STUSPS=left(f.COUNTY_CODE,2) and c.COUNTYFP=right(f.COUNTY_CODE,3) where f.COUNTY_CODE is not null), q as (select q.NPDES_ID, fac.fips, q.YEARQTR, left(q.YEARQTR,4)::int*4 + right(q.YEARQTR,1)::int - 1 idx, q.HLRNC, case when q.HLRNC in ('E','X','T','S','D') then 1 else 0 end snc, case when trim(q.HLRNC) not in ('','U','R','P') then 1 else 0 end anync from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_NPDES_NPDES_QNCR_HISTORY q join fac on fac.NPDES_ID=q.NPDES_ID where q.YEARQTR between '20151' and '20244' and fac.fips in (select fips from storms)), tagged as (select q.*, case when s1.fips is not null then 1 else 0 end q_plus1, case when s2.fips is not null then 1 else 0 end q_plus2, case when s0.fips is not null then 1 else 0 end q_zero, case when sm.fips is not null then 1 else 0 end q_minus1 from q left join storms s1 on s1.fips=q.fips and s1.idx=q.idx-1 left join storms s2 on s2.fips=q.fips and s2.idx=q.idx-2 left join storms s0 on s0.fips=q.fips and s0.idx=q.idx left join storms sm on sm.fips=q.fips and sm.idx=q.idx+1) select case when q_plus1=1 then '1 Q+1 after storm' when q_plus2=1 then '2 Q+2' when q_zero=1 then '0 storm quarter' when q_minus1=1 then '3 Q-1 before' else '4 other quarters' end win, count(*) fac_qtrs, count(distinct NPDES_ID) facs, count(distinct fips) counties, round(avg(snc),4) snc_share, round(avg(anync),4) any_nc_share from tagged group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 502 county-quarters with a $10M+ storm across 409 counties (2015-2024); 84,144 NPDES facilities in 382 of those counties; 768,405 facility-quarters; 31,590 facility-quarters fall in a Q+1 window
hunches.first_number: Quarter after a $10M+ storm: 10.8% of facility-quarters in SNC codes and 37.6% in any noncompliance, vs 15.0% and 41.7% in the same facilities' other quarters (2015-2024). No lift. Year-matched, the one exception is 2017: Q+1 any-noncompliance 47.5% vs 22.0% (Harvey counties, 3,502 facility-quarters).
hunches.hit_means: Permittees fail effluent limits or miss DMRs in the quarter after a major storm: flooded lagoons, bypassed plants, lost records. Harvey 2017 shows that shape.
hunches.miss_means: The QNCR does not register storm damage within a quarter, or the SNC share is dominated by chronic non-reporters whose status does not move with weather. That is what the pooled 2015-2024 number says: the general claim is dead as written.
hunches.tier_reason: Both legs dated to the quarter (storm BEGIN_YEARMONTH, QNCR YEARQTR); the self-controlled before/after ran. Result kills the general claim; Harvey 2017 is the only surviving cohort.
hunches.time_axis: Storm events by begin month 2015-2024 (CZ_TYPE='C' only); QNCR quarters 20151-20244
traps: Storm mart BEGIN_DATE_TIME/END_DATE_TIME are null on all 1,780,730 rows; STATE_FIPS and CZ_FIPS are unpadded
CZ_FIPS is a county only when CZ_TYPE='C'; 714,633 'Z' rows are forecast zones
DAMAGE_PROPERTY is text with K/M/B suffixes
HLRNC SNC mapping E/X/T/S/D is my assumption from ECHO code lists, not verified against the data dictionary; 'W' (775,208 rows) is unclassified and counted as noncompliance
ICIS_FACILITIES.COUNTY_CODE null on 513,577 of 1,213,737 facilities
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 26 (storm arbitrage: storm mart x USDA MFH vacancy, one snapshot). This pairs the storm mart with NPDES QNCR history, both dated, and uses a within-facility before/after rather than a cross-section.

hunches.title: Jail-heavy counties and violent death
hunches.hunch: Counties in the top quintile of VERA 2019 jail population rate have higher CDC suicide and homicide rates in 2019 and 2024 and lower QCEW 2022 private weekly wages than bottom-quintile counties.
hunches.join_keys: VERA.COUNTY_FIPS (YEAR='2019', nullif(trim(TOTAL_JAIL_POP_RATE),'') on 2,902 of 3,049 rows) = CDC.GEOID (2,625 of 2,902 have a CDC row; non-suppressed rate on 1,213 for suicide 2019, 1,421 homicide 2019, 1,402 overdose 2019) = QCEW.AREA_FIPS (AGGLVL_CODE='71', OWN_CODE='5'; 2,902 of 2,902 match)
hunches.query_sql: with vera as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, URBANICITY, try_to_number(nullif(trim(TOTAL_JAIL_POP_RATE),''),18,6) jr from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_VERA_INCARCERATION_TRENDS where YEAR='2019'), vq as (select fips, URBANICITY, jr, ntile(5) over (order by jr) q from vera where jr is not null), cdc as (select GEOID fips, max(case when INTENT='All_Suicide' and PERIOD='2019' then r end) s19, max(case when INTENT='All_Suicide' and PERIOD='2024' then r end) s24, max(case when INTENT='All_Homicide' and PERIOD='2019' then r end) h19, max(case when INTENT='All_Homicide' and PERIOD='2024' then r end) h24, max(case when INTENT='Drug_OD' and PERIOD='2019' then r end) o19, max(case when INTENT='Drug_OD' and PERIOD='2024' then r end) o24 from (select GEOID, INTENT, PERIOD, try_to_number(RATE,18,6) r from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY where INTENT in ('All_Suicide','All_Homicide','Drug_OD') and PERIOD in ('2019','2024') and try_to_number(RATE_M,18,6)=0 and try_to_number(RATE,18,6) >= 0) group by 1), wage as (select AREA_FIPS fips, try_to_number(ANNUAL_AVG_WKLY_WAGE,18,6) w from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_BLS_QCEW where AGGLVL_CODE='71' and OWN_CODE='5') select q, count(*) counties, round(avg(jr),1) jail_rate_2019, round(avg(w.w),0) wkly_wage_2022, count(c.s19) n_s, round(avg(c.s19),2) suicide19, round(avg(c.s24),2) suicide24, count(c.h19) n_h, round(avg(c.h19),2) homicide19, round(avg(c.h24),2) homicide24, count(c.o19) n_o, round(avg(c.o19),2) od19, round(avg(c.o24),2) od24 from vq left join cdc c on c.fips=vq.fips left join wage w on w.fips=vq.fips group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 2,902 counties with a 2019 jail rate; 1,213 with an unsuppressed 2019 suicide rate; 1,421 homicide; 1,402 overdose; 359 counties carry all four suicide/homicide values in both years
hunches.first_number: Weak. Correlation of 2019 jail rate with 2019 suicide rate is -0.09, with homicide -0.03 (n up to 1,421 counties). By quintile suicide runs 10.2, 15.8, 16.2, 17.6, 14.8 per 100k (inverted U); wage falls monotonically 1,021 to 888 dollars a week. The one gradient is overdose change: top-jail-quintile counties went 14.0 (2019) to 22.5 (2024) per 100k, +61%, vs 10.4 to 11.2 in the bottom quintile.
hunches.hit_means: High-incarceration counties are also high-violent-death, low-wage counties: one deprivation cluster. The wage leg holds; the violence leg does not.
hunches.miss_means: Jail rate and violent death are not the same geography. Jail rate is high in rural southern and plains counties whose suicide and homicide counts are small and often suppressed, so the visible cohort is biased to larger counties.
hunches.tier_reason: CDC injury file carries annual PERIOD 2019-2024 (not one TTM window as previously recorded) and VERA is 1970-2026, so a trend is possible and was run; QCEW is 2022 only and stays cross-section.
hunches.time_axis: VERA 2019 (last full-coverage year, 3,049 counties); CDC 2019 and 2024; QCEW 2022 only
traps: RATE_M is text '0.000000000000000'; RATE_M='0' matched zero rows and silently emptied three hunches until fixed
RATE = -999 sentinel on 6,549 suppressed rows
COUNT_SUP is '1-9' on 1,424 of 3,143 counties for Drug_OD 2023, so half of counties have no usable rate
VERA blanks are empty strings, not nulls
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest are hunch 9 (GHGRP x QCEW x injury TTM, cross-section) and the mart JUSTICE__COUNTY_DOUBLE_BURDEN (jail x overdose top decile, one vintage). This uses suicide and homicide intents with two CDC years, which neither does.

hunches.title: Penalty deserts, reversed
hunches.hunch: Counties with the highest jail rates and highest-minority facility footprints let significant-noncompliance facilities go unpenalized more often than other counties.
hunches.join_keys: ECHO.FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS (5-digit on 2,539,755 of 3,157,891 rows, empty string on 618,136; 3,229 distinct) = VERA.COUNTY_FIPS (YEAR='2019', 2,901 quintile counties match) = CENSUS.GEOID. SNC defined as FAC_PROGRAMS_WITH_SNC > 0 (20,836 facilities) because FAC_SNC_FLG is 'N' on every row.
hunches.query_sql: with e as (select FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS fips, FRS_ID, try_to_number(FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES,18,2) pen, try_to_number(FAC_QTRS_WITH_NC,18,6) qnc, try_to_number(FAC_PERCENT_MINORITY,18,6) pmin, case when try_to_number(FAC_PROGRAMS_WITH_SNC,18,6) > 0 then 1 else 0 end snc from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_ECHO where FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS <> ''), cty as (select fips, count(*) facs, sum(snc) snc_facs, sum(case when snc=1 and coalesce(pen,0)=0 then 1 else 0 end) snc_unpen, sum(case when qnc>=9 then 1 else 0 end) chronic, sum(case when qnc>=9 and coalesce(pen,0)=0 then 1 else 0 end) chronic_unpen, avg(case when snc=1 then pmin end) snc_pmin from e group by 1), vera as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, try_to_number(nullif(trim(TOTAL_JAIL_POP_RATE),''),18,6) jr from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_VERA_INCARCERATION_TRENDS where YEAR='2019'), vq as (select fips, jr, ntile(5) over (order by jr) q from vera where jr is not null) select q, count(*) counties, round(avg(jr),1) jail_rate_2019, sum(snc_facs) snc_facs, sum(snc_unpen) snc_unpen, round(sum(snc_unpen)/nullif(sum(snc_facs),0),4) unpen_share, sum(chronic) chronic, sum(chronic_unpen) chronic_unpen, round(avg(snc_pmin),1) avg_snc_fac_pct_minority from cty join vq on vq.fips=cty.fips group by 1 order by 1; -- plus: select case when pmin>=50 then 'majority minority' when pmin>=25 then '25-50' else 'under 25' end band, sum(snc) snc_facs, sum(case when snc=1 and coalesce(pen,0)=0 then 1 else 0 end) snc_unpen, round(avg(case when snc=1 and pen>0 then pen end),0) avg_pen from e where pmin is not null group by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 17,832 SNC facilities with a county FIPS across 3,229 counties; 15,901 of them with zero penalties in the ECHO window; 33,978 facilities with 9+ noncompliant quarters, 30,596 unpenalized
hunches.first_number: 89.2% of SNC facilities (15,901 of 17,832) carry $0 in ECHO penalties, and 11,141 have no formal action at all. The share is flat across jail-rate quintiles: 91.4, 85.6, 88.8, 89.5, 89.7%. By facility minority share it runs the wrong way for the hunch: 90.9% unpenalized where minority share is under 25%, 86.9% at 25-50%, 83.0% in majority-minority tracts, and the average penalty when one exists is $1,014,015 in majority-minority tracts vs $405,639 under 25%. The true deserts are Mingo WV (82 of 82 SNC facilities unpenalized), Lewis WA (72 of 72), Boone WV (60 of 60), Benton WA (57 of 57).
hunches.hit_means: Enforcement discretion tracks who lives nearby: minority and high-incarceration counties get chronic violators without fines. The data says the opposite; penalties are, if anything, more likely near minority communities.
hunches.miss_means: Unpenalized SNC is the norm everywhere (nine in ten), and the variation is by state enforcement regime, not demographics: coal-country West Virginia and Washington state show 100% unpenalized. The story is state primacy, not environmental justice.
hunches.tier_reason: ECHO is one snapshot and FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES is a trailing five-year window; VERA gives one year of context. No before/after is possible with this table. The seed dies as written because FAC_SNC_FLG is a constant, and the reframed run reverses the demographic claim.
hunches.time_axis: none usable: ECHO snapshot (ingested 2026); penalties window 2021-2026 by FAC_DATE_LAST_PENALTY; VERA 2019
traps: FAC_SNC_FLG is 'N' on all 3,157,891 rows
FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES is a trailing five-year sum: 1,907 of 1,931 penalized SNC facilities have their last penalty dated 2021-2026
FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS empty string on 618,136 rows
The mart ENVIRONMENT__EPA_PENALTY_GAP (93,808 rows) already flags CHRONIC_NO_PENALTY and IN_MAJORITY_MINORITY_COMMUNITY at facility level
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is the mart ENVIRONMENT__EPA_PENALTY_GAP, a facility-level screen with CHRONIC_NO_PENALTY and majority-minority flags. This rolls up to county, adds the VERA jail-rate leg, and finds the minority gradient runs opposite to the mart's framing.

hunches.title: Hazardous waste and drug poisoning
hunches.hunch: Counties with more RCRA hazardous-waste violations per capita in a given year 2003-2015 have higher CDC drug-poisoning death rates in the same year.
hunches.join_keys: RCRA_VIOLATIONS.ID_NUMBER = PROGRAM_LINKS.PGM_SYS_ID where PGM_SYS_ACRNM='RCRAINFO' (147,131 of 147,240 violating IDs match a FIPS_CODE, 99.9%; one FIPS per ID, no fan-out); PROGRAM_LINKS.FIPS_CODE (numeric 5-digit for RCRAINFO) = POISONING.FIPS by year (40,827 of 40,831 county-years join)
hunches.query_sql: with links as (select PGM_SYS_ID, min(FIPS_CODE) fips from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_PROGRAM_LINKS where PGM_SYS_ACRNM='RCRAINFO' and FIPS_CODE is not null group by 1), rv as (select l.fips, right(v.DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED,4)::int yr, count(*) viols, count(distinct v.ID_NUMBER) facs from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_RCRA_VIOLATIONS v join links l on l.PGM_SYS_ID=v.ID_NUMBER where right(v.DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED,4) between '2003' and '2015' group by 1,2), pz as (select FIPS fips, YEAR::int yr, try_to_number(POPULATION,18,6) pop, case when band='>30' then 31 else (try_to_number(split_part(band,'-',1),18,6)+try_to_number(split_part(band,'-',2),18,6))/2 end mid from (select FIPS, YEAR, POPULATION, ESTIMATED_AGE_ADJUSTED_DEATH_RATE_11_CATEGORIES_IN_RANGES band from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY) where YEAR between '2003' and '2015'), j as (select pz.fips, pz.yr, pz.pop, pz.mid, coalesce(rv.viols,0) viols, coalesce(rv.viols,0)*100000.0/pz.pop vr from pz left join rv on rv.fips=pz.fips and rv.yr=pz.yr where pz.pop > 0), b as (select j.*, case when viols=0 then '0 none' when vr < 10 then '1 under 10 per 100k' when vr < 30 then '2 10-30' else '3 30+' end band from j) select band, count(*) county_years, count(distinct fips) counties, round(avg(mid),2) poison_rate_mid, round(avg(vr),1) rcra_viols_per_100k from b group by 1 order by 1; -- and: select corr(vr, mid) r_pooled, corr(ln(1+vr), mid) r_log, count(*) n from j
hunches.distinct_entities: 40,827 county-years 2003-2015 (3,140 counties); 18,392 county-years with at least one RCRA violation; 249,740 violations at 2,698 counties
hunches.first_number: Pooled correlation of RCRA violations per 100k with the drug-poisoning rate midpoint is 0.007 over 40,827 county-years (0.063 on the log). Poisoning midpoint: 9.75 per 100k in county-years with zero violations, 11.03 under 10 violations per 100k, 10.82 at 10-30, 10.23 at 30+. Change 2005-09 to 2011-15 by RCRA-change quintile: poisoning rose 5.13, 4.65, 5.18, 4.85, 4.96 in every quintile alike.
hunches.hit_means: Industrial hazardous-waste noncompliance marks the same deindustrialized counties where the opioid wave hit, so the two rise together year by year.
hunches.miss_means: The two series share nothing beyond the national opioid trend. That is the result: dead on first run, and it stays dead after a population-quartile control (the 30+ band is 8.77 in the smallest quartile, 12.93 in the largest, mirroring the zero band).
hunches.tier_reason: Both legs dated by year (RCRA determination dates 1980s-2026; poisoning 1999-2015), the same-year and change tests ran, and the result kills the hunch.
hunches.time_axis: RCRA violations by determination year 2003-2015; CDC drug poisoning 2003-2015 (file ends 2015)
traps: RCRA dates are MM/DD/YYYY text; left(x,4) gives '01/0'
Poisoning rate is a banded string like '16.1-18' or '>30', midpoint required
PROGRAM_LINKS.FIPS_CODE is numeric for RCRAINFO but 'OH155'-style for AIR and NPDES
RCRA_FACILITIES has no county column at all; the links mart or ECHO RCRA_IDS is the only route
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 8 (VERA jail 2010-2015 x poisoning x HPSA). This swaps in RCRA violations, a table no existing hunch uses, with a same-year and a change design.

hunches.title: Air violators and factory wages
hunches.hunch: Counties whose manufacturing jobs pay least carry the most Clean Air Act federally reportable violations per manufacturing worker, so pollution and low wages travel together.
hunches.join_keys: VIOLATION_HISTORY.PGM_SYS_ID = PROGRAM_LINKS.PGM_SYS_ID where PGM_SYS_ACRNM='AIR' (35,530 of 35,537 violating IDs match, 99.98%); PROGRAM_LINKS.FIPS_CODE 'OH155' split as left 2 = CENSUS.STUSPS, right 3 = CENSUS.COUNTYFP to get GEOID (a numeric join matched 0 counties); GEOID = QCEW.AREA_FIPS (AGGLVL_CODE='74', INDUSTRY_CODE='31-33', OWN_CODE='5', DISCLOSURE_CODE<>'N'; 2,877 of 2,886 mfg counties join; 1,541 have a violation)
hunches.query_sql: with links as (select l.PGM_SYS_ID, min(c.GEOID) fips from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_PROGRAM_LINKS l join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY c on c.STUSPS=left(l.FIPS_CODE,2) and c.COUNTYFP=right(l.FIPS_CODE,3) where l.PGM_SYS_ACRNM='AIR' and l.FIPS_CODE is not null group by 1), av as (select l.fips, count(*) frvs, count(distinct v.PGM_SYS_ID) facs, sum(case when v.HPV_DAYZERO_DATE is not null and v.HPV_DAYZERO_DATE<>'' then 1 else 0 end) hpvs from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_ICIS_AIR_ICIS_AIR_VIOLATION_HISTORY v join links l on l.PGM_SYS_ID=v.PGM_SYS_ID where right(v.EARLIEST_FRV_DETERM_DATE,4) in ('2021','2022','2023') group by 1), airfac as (select l.fips, count(*) air_facs from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_ICIS_AIR_ICIS_AIR_FACILITIES a join links l on l.PGM_SYS_ID=a.PGM_SYS_ID group by 1), mfg as (select AREA_FIPS fips, try_to_number(ANNUAL_AVG_EMPLVL,18,6) emp, try_to_number(ANNUAL_AVG_WKLY_WAGE,18,6) wage from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_BLS_QCEW where AGGLVL_CODE='74' and INDUSTRY_CODE='31-33' and OWN_CODE='5' and coalesce(DISCLOSURE_CODE,'') <> 'N'), tot as (select AREA_FIPS fips, try_to_number(ANNUAL_AVG_EMPLVL,18,6) emp, try_to_number(ANNUAL_AVG_WKLY_WAGE,18,6) wage from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_BLS_QCEW where AGGLVL_CODE='71' and OWN_CODE='5'), j as (select m.fips, m.emp mfg_emp, m.wage mfg_wage, t.wage tot_wage, m.emp/nullif(t.emp,0) mfg_share, coalesce(a.frvs,0) frvs, coalesce(f.air_facs,0) air_facs from mfg m join tot t on t.fips=m.fips left join av a on a.fips=m.fips left join airfac f on f.fips=m.fips where m.emp > 0 and t.emp > 0), q as (select j.*, ntile(4) over (order by mfg_wage) q from j where mfg_emp >= 500) select q, count(*) counties, round(avg(mfg_wage),0) mfg_wkly_wage, sum(frvs) frvs, sum(mfg_emp) mfg_emp, round(sum(frvs)*10000.0/sum(mfg_emp),2) frvs_per_10k_mfg_emp, round(sum(frvs)*1.0/nullif(sum(air_facs),0),3) frvs_per_air_fac from q group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 2,877 counties with 2022 private manufacturing employment; 1,541 with at least one FRV 2021-2023; 14,996 FRVs in 1,617 counties; 2,003 counties with 500+ manufacturing jobs in the wage quartiles
hunches.first_number: Counties in the bottom manufacturing-wage quartile ($926 a week, 2022) carry 14.9 federally reportable air violations per 10,000 manufacturing jobs (2021-2023) vs 9.6 in the top quartile ($1,701), a 1.55x gradient in the employment-weighted aggregate. Per county the correlation is -0.005 (n=2,003). Per air facility the rate is flat, 0.059-0.066. The heaviest counties are not factories: Contra Costa CA 944 FRVs of which 780 high-priority (refineries), Kern CA 607, Weld CO 262 across 11,089 air facilities (oil and gas wells).
hunches.hit_means: Low-wage manufacturing counties are also lax-compliance counties: the same employers cut both corners.
hunches.miss_means: Air violations are an oil, gas and refinery phenomenon that has nothing to do with the manufacturing wage; the aggregate gradient is a composition effect and the per-county correlation is zero.
hunches.tier_reason: QCEW holds one year (2022, annual rows only), so the wage leg is a single vintage; the violations leg is dated but has nothing dated to compare against.
hunches.time_axis: ICIS-AIR EARLIEST_FRV_DETERM_DATE 2021-2023 (right 4 chars of MM-DD-YYYY text); QCEW 2022 only
traps: PROGRAM_LINKS.FIPS_CODE for AIR is 'OH155' not numeric; numeric join matched 0 counties on first run
ICIS-AIR dates are MM-DD-YYYY (hyphens) while RCRA dates are MM/DD/YYYY (slashes)
QCEW DISCLOSURE_CODE 'N' rows carry 0 employment, not null (338 of 3,224 manufacturing county rows)
QCEW is YEAR 2022, QTR 'A' only; AGGLVL 71 = county total, 74 = county NAICS sector; OWN_CODE 5 = private
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest are hunch 9 (GHGRP tonnage x QCEW 2022 x injury) and hunch 21 (HCRIS salaries x QCEW NAICS 622). This is the first use of ICIS-AIR violation history against QCEW, and the first to use the manufacturing sector row.

hunches.title: Decriminalization states, emptier jails, more overdoses
hunches.hunch: Counties whose jail population rate fell most between 2019 and 2023 saw the largest rise in overdose death rates 2019 to 2024, and the effect concentrates in the two states that decriminalized drug possession in 2021, Washington (State v. Blake) and Oregon (Measure 110).
hunches.join_keys: VERA.COUNTY_FIPS self-join YEAR 2019 to YEAR 2023 (1,945 counties with a positive rate both years) = CDC.GEOID for INTENT='Drug_OD', PERIOD 2019 and 2024, RATE_M numeric 0 and RATE >= 0 (1,184 counties unsuppressed both years); 824 counties survive both filters
hunches.query_sql: with v as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, YEAR, STATE_ABBR, try_to_number(nullif(trim(TOTAL_JAIL_POP_RATE),''),18,6) jr from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_VERA_INCARCERATION_TRENDS where YEAR in ('2019','2023')), vj as (select a.fips, a.STATE_ABBR st, a.jr jr19, b.jr jr23, (b.jr - a.jr)/a.jr pct_djr from v a join v b on b.fips=a.fips and b.YEAR='2023' where a.YEAR='2019' and a.jr > 0 and b.jr is not null), od as (select GEOID fips, max(case when PERIOD='2019' then r end) od19, max(case when PERIOD='2024' then r end) od24 from (select GEOID, PERIOD, try_to_number(RATE,18,6) r from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY where INTENT='Drug_OD' and PERIOD in ('2019','2024') and try_to_number(RATE_M,18,6)=0 and try_to_number(RATE,18,6)>=0) group by 1), j as (select vj.*, od.od19, od.od24, od.od24-od.od19 dod from vj join od on od.fips=vj.fips where od.od19 is not null and od.od24 is not null) select case when st='WA' then 'WA' else 'other 49' end grp, count(*) counties, round(avg(pct_djr)*100,1) pct_change_jail, round(median(pct_djr)*100,1) med_pct_jail, round(avg(od19),2) od19, round(avg(od24),2) od24, round(avg(dod),2) d_od, round(median(dod),2) med_d_od, sum(case when dod>0 then 1 else 0 end) up, sum(case when dod<0 then 1 else 0 end) down from j group by 1 order by 1; -- national: select corr(pct_djr, dod), count(*) from j  => -0.011, 824
hunches.distinct_entities: 824 counties with a jail rate in both 2019 and 2023 and an unsuppressed overdose rate in both 2019 and 2024; 12 in Washington, 15 in Oregon, 812 elsewhere
hunches.first_number: Nationally there is no relationship: correlation of percent jail-rate change 2019-2023 with overdose-rate change 2019-2024 is -0.011 over 824 counties; the quintile that cut jail 43.9% saw overdose +2.33 per 100k (median 0.0), the quintile that grew jail 32.8% saw +0.39. Washington's 12 measurable counties: jail rate -33.2%, overdose 14.4 to 39.75 per 100k (+25.4), 12 of 12 up. Oregon's 15: jail -20.0%, overdose +16.0. The other 49 states: jail -9.4%, overdose +0.99, median 0.0. Six of the 12 largest overdose jumps among counties that cut jail 40%+ are Washington counties (Yakima +39.0, Thurston +27.1, King +24.2, Chelan +23.3, Clallam +18.0, Snohomish +13.4).
hunches.hit_means: Where possession stopped sending people to jail in 2021, jail counts fell and overdose deaths climbed far faster than the national curve. Whether that is causation or the late arrival of fentanyl on the West Coast is the reporting question; both states fit both stories.
hunches.miss_means: Jail decline and overdose change are unrelated once you leave the Pacific Northwest, which the 812-county median of 0.0 shows. The national decarceration-kills claim is dead; the two-state cluster is what survives.
hunches.tier_reason: Both legs carry years (VERA 2019 and 2023, CDC 2019 and 2024) and the change-on-change test ran; the state cluster is directly testable and dated to the 2021 policy shocks.
hunches.time_axis: VERA jail rate 2019 vs 2023 (2023 covers 2,090 counties, 1,981 with a rate); CDC Drug_OD 2019 vs 2024 (annual PERIOD rows)
traps: VERA 2023 coverage is 2,090 counties, 2024 is 1,633 and Washington falls from 39 counties (2019) to 16 (2023) and 8 (2024); the 12 WA counties are the ones VERA still tracks, skewing to larger counties
CDC overdose rate is suppressed ('1-9') on roughly 45% of counties, removing most rural counties from both sides
RATE_M is text; RATE_M='0' matches nothing, use try_to_number
National overdose deaths peaked 2022-2023 and fell in 2024, so a 2019-2024 delta understates the mid-period rise everywhere
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest are hunch 8 (jail 2010-2015 x poisoning to 2015, a window the previous sweep called dead) and the mart JUSTICE__COUNTY_DOUBLE_BURDEN (one-vintage jail x overdose top decile). This uses the 2019-2024 CDC annual series the previous sweep did not know existed, runs change-on-change, and isolates the two 2021 decriminalization states.

hunches.title: Disaster counties and overdose, killed
hunches.hunch: Counties hit hard by a non-COVID FEMA disaster in 2021-2022 saw overdose and suicide death rates rise more from 2019 to 2024 than counties with no declaration.
hunches.join_keys: FEMA.FIPS (declarations 2021-2022, INCIDENTTYPECODE<>'B', length 5; 758 counties, 3,062,288 registrations) = CDC.GEOID (Drug_OD and All_Suicide, PERIOD 2019 and 2024, unsuppressed) = DIM_COUNTY.COUNTY_FIPS for POPULATION_2020 (2,262 of 2,270 CDC counties have population; registrations per 1k residents splits heavy from light)
hunches.query_sql: with decl as (select FIPS fips, count(*) regs, count(distinct DISASTERNUMBER) disasters, sum(try_to_number(HAAMOUNT,18,2)) ha from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS where DECLARATIONDATE >= '2021-01-01' and DECLARATIONDATE < '2023-01-01' and INCIDENTTYPECODE <> 'B' and length(FIPS)=5 group by 1), anydecl as (select distinct FIPS fips from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS where DECLARATIONDATE >= '2019-01-01' and DECLARATIONDATE < '2025-01-01' and INCIDENTTYPECODE <> 'B' and length(FIPS)=5), cdc as (select GEOID fips, max(case when INTENT='Drug_OD' and PERIOD='2019' then r end) o19, max(case when INTENT='Drug_OD' and PERIOD='2024' then r end) o24, max(case when INTENT='All_Suicide' and PERIOD='2019' then r end) s19, max(case when INTENT='All_Suicide' and PERIOD='2024' then r end) s24 from (select GEOID, INTENT, PERIOD, try_to_number(RATE,18,6) r from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY where INTENT in ('Drug_OD','All_Suicide') and PERIOD in ('2019','2024') and try_to_number(RATE_M,18,6)=0 and try_to_number(RATE,18,6) >= 0) group by 1), pop as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, POPULATION_2020 p from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_COUNTY), j as (select c.fips, c.o19, c.o24, c.s19, c.s24, p.p, d.regs, case when d.fips is not null and d.regs*1000.0/nullif(p.p,0) >= 20 then '1 declared 2021-22, 20+ regs per 1k' when d.fips is not null then '2 declared 2021-22, under 20 per 1k' when a.fips is not null then '3 declared other year 2019-24' else '4 never declared 2019-24' end grp from cdc c left join decl d on d.fips=c.fips left join anydecl a on a.fips=c.fips left join pop p on p.fips=c.fips) select grp, count(*) counties, round(avg(o19),2) od19, round(avg(o24),2) od24, round(avg(o24-o19),2) d_od, round(median(o24-o19),2) med_d_od, sum(case when o24>o19 then 1 else 0 end) up, sum(case when o24<o19 then 1 else 0 end) down from j where o19 is not null and o24 is not null group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 1,184 counties with an unsuppressed overdose rate in both 2019 and 2024; 58 heavily hit (20+ registrations per 1k residents, 2021-2022), 242 lightly hit, 311 declared in another year 2019-2024, 573 never declared
hunches.first_number: Heavily hit 2021-2022 disaster counties: overdose 25.47 (2019) to 24.40 (2024) per 100k, -1.07, median -0.3, 21 up vs 30 down; suicide -0.41. Lightly hit: +2.26. Declared in another year: +4.0. Never declared: -0.75. The hardest-hit counties (Lee FL 203,361 registrations, Jefferson LA 184,821, Orleans LA 174,346, Harris TX 142,613) split both ways: Lee -6.4, Orleans +9.4, Wayne MI -11.4, East Baton Rouge +12.2.
hunches.hit_means: Displacement, lost housing and broken treatment access after a disaster push overdose and suicide up for years. The data does not show it at county scale.
hunches.miss_means: County mortality rates over five years do not register a one-season disaster; the heavy-hit group is Florida and Louisiana, whose overdose peaks came earlier than the national one. Killed on first run.
hunches.tier_reason: Both legs dated (FEMA declaration dates, CDC annual 2019-2024) and the before/after grouping ran; the result is a clean null.
hunches.time_axis: FEMA declarations 2021-2022 (and 2019-2024 for the any-declaration control); CDC Drug_OD and All_Suicide 2019 vs 2024
traps: INCIDENTTYPECODE 'B' (COVID) covers 3,127 counties in 2020 and must be excluded or every county is 'declared'
FIPS is null on 2,047,012 of 18,263,336 FEMA rows since 2015 (11%)
DIM_COUNTY in LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE is the only county population denominator in the warehouse (POPULATION_2020, 3,222 counties); XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY carries land area only
Never-declared counties are small and rural with low baseline rates, so they are a poor control without population weighting
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 5 (FEMA IA x HMDA rate spread, 2015-2017). This pairs FEMA IA with the CDC county mortality series, a pair not used anywhere, and tests health rather than credit outcomes.

hunches.title: Subsidized housing beside noncompliance
hunches.hunch: Counties with the most HUD-assisted housing units per resident also carry the most significant-noncompliance EPA facilities and health-based drinking-water violations per capita.
hunches.join_keys: HUD: left(lpad(STCTYTRT,11,'0'),5) = DIM_COUNTY.COUNTY_FIPS (2,800 of 2,811 HUD counties match; 4,933 rows needed the lpad); ECHO.FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS = COUNTY_FIPS (2,429 counties with an SNC facility); SDWA via PWSID to GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS CN to census STUSPS+COUNTYFP (2,549 counties with a 2020-2024 health-based violation); population from DIM_COUNTY.POPULATION_2020
hunches.query_sql: with hud as (select left(lpad(STCTYTRT,11,'0'),5) fips, count(*) projects, sum(try_to_number(TOTAL_UNITS,18,6)) units, avg(case when try_to_number(PCT_MINORITY,18,6) >= 0 then try_to_number(PCT_MINORITY,18,6) end) pct_minority from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJECTS where length(STCTYTRT) in (10,11) group by 1), pop as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, POPULATION_2020 p from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_COUNTY where POPULATION_2020 > 0), snc as (select FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS fips, sum(case when try_to_number(FAC_PROGRAMS_WITH_SNC,18,6)>0 then 1 else 0 end) snc_facs, sum(case when try_to_number(FAC_QTRS_WITH_NC,18,6)>=9 then 1 else 0 end) chronic from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_ECHO where FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS<>'' group by 1), hb as (select c.GEOID fips, count(*) hb_viols from (select distinct PWSID, VIOLATION_ID from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT where IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND='Y' and right(NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE,4) between '2020' and '2024') v join (select distinct PWSID, ANSI_ENTITY_CODE from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS where AREA_TYPE_CODE='CN') g on g.PWSID=v.PWSID join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY c on c.STUSPS=left(g.PWSID,2) and c.COUNTYFP=lpad(g.ANSI_ENTITY_CODE,3,'0') group by 1), j as (select p.fips, p.p, coalesce(h.units,0) units, coalesce(h.units,0)*1000.0/p.p units_per_1k, h.pct_minority, coalesce(s.snc_facs,0) snc_facs, coalesce(s.chronic,0) chronic, coalesce(b.hb_viols,0) hb_viols, coalesce(b.hb_viols,0)*100000.0/p.p hb_per_100k from pop p left join hud h on h.fips=p.fips left join snc s on s.fips=p.fips left join hb b on b.fips=p.fips), q as (select j.*, case when units=0 then 0 else ntile(4) over (partition by (units>0) order by units_per_1k) end q from j) select q, count(*) counties, round(avg(units_per_1k),1) hud_units_per_1k, round(avg(pct_minority),1) hud_pct_minority, sum(snc_facs) snc_facs, round(sum(snc_facs)*100000.0/sum(p),2) snc_per_100k, round(sum(chronic)*100000.0/sum(p),2) chronic_per_100k, sum(hb_viols) hb_viols_2020_24, round(sum(hb_viols)*100000.0/sum(p),2) hb_per_100k, round(median(hb_per_100k),2) med_hb_per_100k from q group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 3,222 counties with population; 2,797 with HUD-assisted units (3,165,501 units, 35,601 projects, quarter 31DEC2025); 2,429 with an SNC facility; 2,549 with a 2020-2024 health-based water violation
hunches.first_number: Top-quartile HUD-density counties (29.6 assisted units per 1,000 residents, tenant minority share 44.5%) carry 6.90 SNC facilities and 26.6 health-based water violations per 100,000 residents (2020-2024) vs 4.55 and 14.6 in the bottom quartile (2.4 units per 1,000, 28.6% minority): 1.5x and 1.8x, monotone across all four quartiles. County-level correlations are 0.05 (SNC) and 0.14 (water). Oklahoma dominates the extremes: Osage 1,144 health-based violations per 100k with 698 assisted units, Okmulgee 1,003, McCurtain 902.
hunches.hit_means: Subsidized housing is sited where the polluters and the failing water systems already are, so HUD tenants carry the noncompliance load.
hunches.miss_means: The gradient is small-county arithmetic: counties with few residents and many tiny water systems inflate per-capita violations (correlation of log population with violations per 100k is -0.23), and HUD unit density is also higher in small poor counties. Needs a population-band control before it is a story.
hunches.tier_reason: HUD assisted housing is a single quarter (31DEC2025) and ECHO is a snapshot; only the SDWA leg carries dates, so the design is cross-section.
hunches.time_axis: SDWA health-based violations 2020-2024 only; HUD 31DEC2025 quarter; ECHO snapshot
traps: STCTYTRT drops the leading zero on 4,933 of 35,601 rows (10 chars); lpad to 11 before taking the county
TOTAL_OCCUPIED and every PCT_ column read -4 on 4,799 suppressed rows; a bare average goes negative
Public Housing rows repeat CODE: 12,094 rows over 6,047 codes
Oklahoma health-based violation counts look like a state reporting pattern, the same counties surface in H1
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 22 (TRI sites by HOLC grade). This is the first use of FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJECTS against any EPA table, and the first county roll-up of SDWA health-based violations against a housing leg.

traps.trap: Not one trailing-12-month window. PERIOD holds annual rows 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 plus TTM, and INTENT holds Drug_OD, FA_Deaths, FA_Homicide, FA_Suicide alongside All_Suicide and All_Homicide. This corrects the 2026-09-05 trap that said the file is one TTM window with no overdose and that no county overdose series after 2015 is landed. A county overdose series 2019-2024 is landed.
traps.evidence: 22,000 rows per intent = 7 periods x 3,142-3,143 counties; Drug_OD TTM window is Dec 2024-Nov 2025 while the other intents run Feb 2025-Jan 2026

traps.trap: RATE holds -999 as a suppression sentinel; RATE_M is text '0.000000000000000' or '1.000000000000000' so RATE_M='0' matches nothing; COUNT_SUP is a banded string '1-9' on nearly half of counties. A bare average of RATE reads -62 for homicide.
traps.evidence: 6,549 rows at exactly -999, all with RATE_M=1 and COUNT_SUP '1-9'; Drug_OD 2023: 1,424 of 3,143 counties suppressed '1-9', 484 at '0'; three hunch scripts returned zero rows on RATE_M='0'

traps.trap: A constant. Every row is 'N'. Significant noncompliance lives in FAC_PROGRAMS_WITH_SNC (>0), FAC_COMPLIANCE_STATUS ('Significant Violation') and the per-program CWA_SNC_FLAG, RCRA_SNC_FLAG, SDWA_SNC_FLAG, CAA_HPV_FLAG.
traps.evidence: 3,157,891 rows all 'N'; FAC_PROGRAMS_WITH_SNC>0 on 20,836; CWA_SNC_FLAG Y 14,900, SDWA 3,908, RCRA 3,496, CAA_HPV 1,033

traps.trap: A trailing five-year window, not an all-time total. Zero means no penalty since about 2021.
traps.evidence: Of 1,931 SNC facilities with a penalty, 1,907 have FAC_DATE_LAST_PENALTY in 2021-2026; only 24 are dated 1994-2020

traps.trap: County FIPS is an empty string, not null, on a fifth of facilities; RCRA_IDS is space-separated when a site has several RCRA handler IDs, so an equality join misses them.
traps.evidence: 618,136 of 3,157,891 rows have length 0 FIPS; 72,747 rows have a space in RCRA_IDS; exact RCRA join reaches 1,364,246 of 1,613,224 handlers

traps.trap: Every numeric column is TEXT and blanks are empty strings, so count(col) reads full coverage when it is not. Last full-coverage year is 2019; coverage collapses after.
traps.evidence: 2019: count(TOTAL_JAIL_POP)=3,049 but count(nullif(trim(..),''))=2,903; admits 2,832; 2020 has 2,303 counties (admits 1,158), 2023 2,090, 2024 1,633 (admits 137), 2026 597; Washington drops from 39 counties in 2019 to 16 in 2023 and 8 in 2024

traps.trap: One vintage: YEAR 2022, QTR 'A' (annual) only. County rows are AGGLVL_CODE 70-78 (71 = county total by ownership, 74 = county NAICS sector); OWN_CODE 5 is private. Suppressed rows (DISCLOSURE_CODE 'N') carry 0 in every measure, not null, so bare averages pull in zeros.
traps.evidence: 3,619,437 rows, 4,429 areas, 2,159 industry codes, all YEAR 2022 QTR A; manufacturing county rows: 2,886 disclosed with positive employment, 338 'N' rows all at 0

traps.trap: One row per violation x enforcement action, so violation counts inflate 3.5x unless deduped on PWSID+VIOLATION_ID; a million rows are enforcement-only with null violation fields. Dates are MM/DD/YYYY text.
traps.evidence: IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND='Y' on 1,993,255 rows but only 563,944 distinct PWSID||VIOLATION_ID; 1,002,550 rows have null IS_HEALTH_BASED_IND and null VIOLATION_ID

traps.trap: STATE_SERVED is empty on every county row; the state is the first two characters of PWSID. ANSI_ENTITY_CODE is the 3-digit county code; combine with census STUSPS+COUNTYFP to get a GEOID. COUNTY_SERVED is a bare name.
traps.evidence: 0 of 411,651 AREA_TYPE_CODE='CN' rows have STATE_SERVED; the PWSID-prefix join matches 394,358 rows (95.8%) to 3,192 counties; 443 PWSIDs serve 2 to 11 counties

traps.column: BEGIN_DATE_TIME, END_DATE_TIME, STATE_FIPS, CZ_FIPS, CZ_TYPE, DAMAGE_PROPERTY
traps.trap: The typed timestamp columns are null on every row; build dates from BEGIN_YEARMONTH and BEGIN_DAY. STATE_FIPS and CZ_FIPS are unpadded text (1-2 and 1-3 digits). CZ_FIPS is a county code only when CZ_TYPE='C'; 'Z' rows are forecast zones. DAMAGE_PROPERTY is text with K, M, B suffixes. Connecticut counties do not match the 2023 census file.
traps.evidence: BEGIN_DATE_TIME null on 1,780,730 of 1,780,730; CZ_TYPE C 1,058,584 rows, Z 714,633, M 7,513; suffixes K 1,129,418, bare 633,034, M 18,159, B 119; after lpad 3,106 of 3,308 county codes since 2015 match census, misses led by 09005, 09003, 09001 (old CT counties) and 99127, 97002

traps.trap: Format is state abbreviation plus 3-digit county code ('OK063'), not a FIPS, and it is null on 42% of facilities, so county roll-ups of NPDES lose two fifths of permittees.
traps.evidence: 700,160 rows length 5, 513,577 null; 3,206 of 3,232 distinct codes match census; of 616,835 NPDES IDs with QNCR rows since 2015, 367,000 have a county

traps.trap: Two EPA tables, two date formats: RCRA is MM/DD/YYYY, ICIS-AIR is MM-DD-YYYY. left(x,4) returns '01/0' and '01-0' garbage on both; use right(x,4) for the year or try_to_date with the right mask.
traps.evidence: left(DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED,4) grouped into 47 buckets like '01/0','01/1'; left(EARLIEST_FRV_DETERM_DATE,4) into 48 like '01-0'; right(x,4) gives clean years 2003-2017 (17,404-22,275 a year) and 2015-2026 (3,181-5,514)

traps.trap: INCIDENTTYPECODE 'B' is COVID-19 funeral assistance, declared in nearly every county in 2020; it is not housing damage and must be excluded before any disaster analysis. FIPS is null on 11% of rows. DECLARATIONDATE is ISO text with a T00:00:00.000Z suffix.
traps.evidence: 2020 'B': 690,608 rows, 56 declarations, 3,127 counties; 2020 HA $607M vs IHP $4,475M; FIPS null on 2,047,012 of 18,263,336 rows since 2015

traps.column: STCTYTRT, TOTAL_OCCUPIED, PCT_MINORITY and other PCT_ columns, CODE, QUARTER
traps.trap: STCTYTRT loses its leading zero on 14% of rows (10 characters instead of 11), so left(...,5) gives a wrong county unless lpadded. Suppressed rows carry -4 in TOTAL_OCCUPIED and every PCT_ column. Public Housing rows repeat CODE. One quarter only.
traps.evidence: length 10 on 4,933 rows, 11 on 30,572, 0 on 91; 4,799 rows with negative TOTAL_OCCUPIED and negative PCT_MINORITY; Public Housing 12,094 rows over 6,047 codes; QUARTER 31DEC2025

traps.trap: FIPS_CODE changes format by program: RCRAINFO rows are numeric 5-digit FIPS, AIR and NPDES rows are state abbreviation plus 3-digit county ('OH155'), and SFDW, ICIS, E-GGRT rows have no FIPS at all. A numeric join on AIR silently matched zero counties.
traps.evidence: RCRAINFO 1,596,556 rows at length 5 numeric ('01000'-'78030') plus 321 two-digit and 431 three-digit stubs; AIR 279,548 rows 'AK000'-'WY045'; NPDES 697,139 same format; SFDW 0 of 678,040 filled, ICIS 0 of 230,825

traps.trap: Half of facility-quarters carry no status ('U' or blank), and the SNC mapping used here (E, X, T, S, D) is an assumption from ECHO code lists, not verified against the data dictionary; 'W' (10% of rows) is unclassified.
The rate is a banded string, not a number: '0-2', '2.1-4', ... '28.1-30', '>30'. Any average needs a midpoint and the top band is open.
traps.evidence: 16 distinct values on 53,387 rows; '>30' on 551 rows

traps.trap: No FIPS anywhere; COUNTY is a name and sometimes two names joined by '/'. Dates are MM/DD/YY text, some with a '(M)' suffix. Seed 7's NFIP leg needs a name join and was not run.
traps.evidence: 'MACOMB COUNTY/ST. CLAIR COUNTY' on Memphis MI; '08/05/10(M)' on Grand Coteau LA

hubs.notes:
DEAD SEEDS AND WHAT KILLED THEM. Seed 1 (water violations after disasters): general claim dead, declared counties 0.907 vs matched control 0.825 and the gap is entirely the 2015 Oklahoma+Texas flood cohort (154 counties, 1.216); all other declared counties 0.758. The OK/TX 2015 lead survives: Stage 2 disinfection-byproduct MCL violations (rule family 220) 578 to 885 in Oklahoma 2014 to 2016, flood counties up 32% vs 18% for the rest of the state. Seed 2 (sewage noncompliance after storms): dead pooled, Q+1 SNC share 10.8% vs 15.0% in other quarters; Harvey 2017 is the exception (any-noncompliance 47.5% vs 22.0%). Seed 3 (jail x violent death): weak, r=-0.09 suicide, -0.03 homicide; the wage leg holds (1,021 to 888 dollars a week across jail quintiles). Seed 4 (penalty deserts): dead as written, FAC_SNC_FLG is a constant; reframed, 89.2% of SNC facilities are unpenalized everywhere, flat across jail quintiles, and majority-minority tracts are MORE penalized (83.0% unpenalized vs 90.9%), reversing the framing; the deserts are WV coal counties and Washington state. Seed 5 (RCRA x drug poisoning): dead, r=0.007 over 40,827 county-years, every change quintile rose 4.65-5.18. Seed 8 (air violations x manufacturing wage): 1.55x aggregate gradient (14.9 vs 9.6 FRVs per 10k mfg jobs) but per-county r=-0.005 and the top violators are refineries and oil fields. Own idea 2 (FEMA disasters x overdose/suicide change): dead, heavy-hit counties -1.07 overdose, -0.41 suicide 2019-2024. Seed 7 (FEMA dollars vs PHA capacity and NFIP participation) was NOT run: NFIP has no FIPS and a '/'-joined county name; PHA county is STATE2KX||CNTY2KX and FEMA HA dollars are clean, so the PHA half is runnable in an hour.

THE LIVE LEADS. (1) Washington and Oregon 2021 decriminalization: WA 12 counties jail -33.2%, overdose 14.4 to 39.75 per 100k, 12 of 12 up; OR 15 counties jail -20%, overdose +16.0; other 49 states +0.99, median 0.0. National r=-0.011. Caveat: VERA's Washington coverage shrinks to 16 counties by 2023 and the West Coast fentanyl wave arrived late; both stories fit. (2) Oklahoma/Texas 2015 flood cohort and DBP violations, above. (3) Penalty deserts are a state-primacy story: Mingo WV 82 of 82 SNC facilities unpenalized, Boone WV 60 of 60, Lewis WA 72 of 72, Benton WA 57 of 57.

CORRECTION TO THE TRAPS FILE. The 2026-09-05 entry saying FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY is one TTM window with no overdose and that no county overdose series after 2015 is landed is wrong: the table holds annual PERIOD 2019-2024 plus TTM for six intents including Drug_OD. Hunches 8 and 19 in the refined matrix, both marked as ending in 2015, now have a 2019-2024 county overdose leg. Note RATE=-999 sentinel and text RATE_M before using it.

RUN NOTES. All queries through the Python door (connect/db.py); the chat plug-in was not touched. Every query ran under 3 seconds; the 26M FEMA table was hit five times total across scripts, each with a DECLARATIONDATE range and INCIDENTTYPECODE filter. HLRNC SNC mapping (E,X,T,S,D) is my assumption and should be checked against the ECHO QNCR data dictionary before anything is published from H2. County population denominator: LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_COUNTY.POPULATION_2020 (3,222 counties) is the only one in the warehouse; XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY has land area only, VERA has TOTAL_POP_15TO64 by year, CDC poisoning has POPULATION through 2015.

HUB A WISH LIST (top five, what each unlocks). (1) BLS QCEW annual county files 2010-2024 (all years, not just 2022): turns hunches 9 and 21 and seeds 3 and 8 from single-vintage to before/after; the question becomes whether wages fell after plants entered noncompliance, not whether low wages and violations coincide. (2) BJS Census of Jails 2019 and Annual Survey of Jails 2020-2024 county microdata, or a refreshed VERA pull: VERA covers 597 counties by 2026 and Washington falls to 8; this rescues H7 for the 27 Washington counties it cannot see and every decarceration hunch after 2019. (3) EPA ECHO case-level enforcement history (ICIS FE&C case file with penalty assessed dates and amounts, all years): FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES is a five-year snapshot, so seed 4 cannot ask when a facility was last fined or whether penalties fell after an ownership change; case dates make it a timeline. (4) Census ACS 5-year county tables (poverty rate, median household income, race, renter share) and PEP annual county population 2010-2024: every Hub A hunch lacks a demographic control and a per-year denominator; H9's small-county inflation and H3's inverted-U both need them. (5) OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries (v2, county-level with incident begin and end dates and PA/IA flags): the IA registration file has null FIPS on 11% of rows, no incident end date, and misses declarations with public assistance only; the summaries fix the exposure leg for H1, H8 and hunch 5. Also worth landing: EPA SDWIS quarterly snapshots over time (violation counts by begin year jumped 18,287 in 2024 from 11,380 in 2023, which smells like the Lead and Copper Rule Revisions or a reporting change rather than water).

hunches.title: Industry money jumps, Part D does not
