hunches.query_sql:
with y as (select NPI,'2022' yr,sum(try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2)) usd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2022 where NPI is not null and trim(NPI)<>'' and COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE<>'Covered Recipient Teaching Hospital' group by 1 union all select NPI,'2023',sum(try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2)) from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 where NPI is not null and trim(NPI)<>'' and COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE<>'Covered Recipient Teaching Hospital' group by 1 union all select NPI,'2024',sum(try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2)) from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS where NPI is not null and trim(NPI)<>'' and COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE<>'Covered Recipient Teaching Hospital' group by 1),
w as (select NPI,sum(iff(yr='2022',usd,0)) u22,sum(iff(yr='2023',usd,0)) u23,sum(iff(yr='2024',usd,0)) u24 from y group by 1),
g as (select NPI,case when u22<10000 and u23>=100000 then 'grower' when u23>0 or u22>0 then 'field' end grp from w),
q as (select NPI,max(try_to_number(FINAL_SCORE,18,6)) fs,max(try_to_number(PAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_PERCENTAGE,18,6)) adj from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE group by 1),
d as (select NPI,try_to_number(TOT_CLMS,18,6) tc,try_to_number(BRND_TOT_CLMS,18,6) bc,try_to_number(TOT_DRUG_CST,18,6) cost from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS)
select grp,count(*) npis,count(q.NPI) in_qpp,round(avg(fs),2) avg_final_score,round(avg(adj),3) avg_adj,count(d.NPI) in_partd,round(avg(bc/nullif(tc,0)),4) avg_brand_share,round(median(bc/nullif(tc,0)),4) med_brand_share from g left join q using(NPI) left join d using(NPI) where grp is not null group by 1;
-- second leg (p10): drug file DY2022 rolled up per NPI for growers and NPIs ending '00', full outer joined to PART_D_PRESCRIBERS DY2024; median cost24/cost22 by group
hunches.distinct_entities: 169 distinct grower NPIs (110 from under $1k, 59 from $1k-$10k) against 1,325,672 field NPIs paid in any of 2022-2024; 59 growers present in both Part D vintages vs 9,763 sample NPIs
hunches.hit_means: Growers' QPP score or Part D brand share or 2022->2024 Part D growth separates from the field: industry money tracks a change in Medicare behaviour and the top payers deserve a name-by-name look.
hunches.miss_means: Growers match the field: the jumps are device-company buyouts, royalties and consulting deals (Acquisitions $10.8M to 19 NPIs, Royalty $8.7M to 17, Consulting $14.1M to 98) with no Medicare footprint. Result leans miss: QPP 85.11 vs 84.95, avg adjustment +0.307 vs +0.217, brand share DY2024 20.5% vs 15.9% (the only signal), median Part D cost ratio 2024/2022 1.50 for growers vs 1.97 for the sample, only 51 of 169 top 2023 payers had paid the same NPI in 2022.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds and both legs carry dates: Open Payments 2022/2023/2024 payment dates and two Part D vintages (drug file DY2022, summary DY2024). First number found.
hunches.time_axis: Open Payments PY2022, PY2023, PY2024 (DATE_OF_PAYMENT, MM/DD/YYYY text); Part D DY2022 (drug file) vs DY2024 (summary); QPP PY2024 is a single snapshot
traps: FED_CMS_PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG rolls up short: CMS suppresses drug rows under 11 claims, so a per-NPI sum from the drug file is a floor. The 1% sample's median claims ratio DY2024/DY2022 reads 1.53 and cost 1.97, impossible as growth; compare groups against each other, never against 1.0.
NATURE_OF_PAYMENT 'Acquisitions' is a company buyout booked to the physician-owner (Walk Vascular paid one NPI $4,846,659 in 2 rows); it is not marketing money.
Brand share (BRND_TOT_CLMS) exists only in the DY2024 summary; the DY2022 drug file has Brnd_Name/Gnrc_Name and no brand flag.
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest are pharma_paid_excluded (LEIE x OP2022, date-tested) and partd_openpayments_match (one excluded doctor's drugs vs payers). This uses no exclusion list; the mechanism is the year-over-year payment axis across three OP tables plus the two-vintage Part D axis, neither used before.

hunches.title: SAM adds no clinicians
hunches.hunch: Federal-wide SAM debarment would catch clinicians the OIG list misses, and those SAM-only NPIs would still be billing Medicare or taking industry money after their ACTIVE_DATE.
hunches.join_keys: SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2.NPI (7,211 non-sentinel rows = 4,866 distinct NPIs; HHS 4,706, OPM 2,304, reciprocal program) minus LEIE.NPI (8,660 distinct real): 4,687 in both, 179 SAM-only, 3,973 LEIE-only. SAM-only.NPI = QPP.NPI 0/179; = BY_PROVIDER.RNDRNG_NPI 4/179; = PART_D_PRESCRIBERS.NPI 6/179; = OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023.NPI with DATE_OF_PAYMENT > ACTIVE_DATE 4/179; = OPEN_PAYMENTS(2024) 5/179; = FACILITY_AFFILIATION.NPI 0/179; = ORDER_AND_REFERRING.NPI 5/179.
hunches.query_sql:
with samonly as (select NPI,min(ACTIVE_DATE) active_date,max(EXCLUDING_AGENCY) agency from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2 where NPI is not null and NPI<>'0000000000' and trim(NPI)<>'' and NPI not in (select NPI from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE where NPI<>'0000000000') group by 1)
select count(*) sam_only,
(select count(*) from samonly s join (select distinct NPI from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE) q using(NPI)) in_qpp,
(select count(*) from samonly s join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER b on b.RNDRNG_NPI=s.NPI) in_partb,
(select count(*) from samonly s join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS d using(NPI)) in_partd,
(select count(distinct s.NPI) from samonly s join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 o on o.NPI=s.NPI and try_to_date(o.DATE_OF_PAYMENT,'MM/DD/YYYY')>try_to_date(s.active_date,'YYYY-MM-DD')) paid_2023_after_active,
(select count(distinct s.NPI) from samonly s join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_FACILITY_AFFILIATION f using(NPI)) in_affiliation,
(select count(distinct s.NPI) from samonly s join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_ORDER_AND_REFERRING r using(NPI)) in_order_referring
from samonly
hunches.distinct_entities: 179 distinct SAM-only NPIs; 4 of them paid by industry in 2023 after ACTIVE_DATE (7 payments, $312.91, all Food and Beverage); 4 in Part B DY2024 ($136,563 total Medicare paid, Desai NJ cardiology $104,762 excluded 2012 by HHS)
hunches.first_number: 179 SAM-only clinician NPIs after removing the 4,687 that LEIE already carries (SAM snapshot ingested 2026-08-23)
hunches.hit_means: A SAM-only clinician with Medicare or industry money after debarment is a gap between two federal exclusion lists.
hunches.miss_means: SAM's clinician NPIs are a reciprocal copy of LEIE; the SAM remainder is 179 people and 4 lunches. Dead as written. Nearest live version: SAM's UNIQUE_ENTITY_ID side against USAspending contracts (hunch 15, Hub X), and LEIE stays the only clinician exclusion list; the one Part B name (Desai, $104,762 DY2024, HHS active 2012-09-20) is a single lead, not a pattern.
hunches.tier_reason: The SAM-only leg is 179 NPIs and reaches 4 payments worth $312.91 and 4 Part B rows. No pattern is possible on that remainder; the missing piece is a clinician exclusion source beyond LEIE (state Medicaid exclusion lists are not landed).
hunches.time_axis: SAM ACTIVE_DATE (YYYY-MM-DD text, 2009-2026) vs Open Payments DATE_OF_PAYMENT; Part B DY2024 has no date
traps: FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2.NPI: 7,211 non-sentinel rows collapse to 4,866 distinct NPIs and 4,687 of those are already in LEIE; SAM adds 179 clinicians, not 7,211.
UNIQUE_ENTITY_ID is null on every Individual row that carries an NPI in the sample checked; the UEI and NPI legs of SAM are disjoint populations (contractors vs people).
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 15 (SAM UEI x FEMA contracts) and the ghost_npi reports (LEIE x Part B). This is the first SAM-minus-LEIE set difference on NPI; it kills the idea that SAM widens the clinician exclusion net.

hunches.title: Quality bonus, same lunches
hunches.hunch: Clinicians penalized under MIPS PY2024 take more industry money than top-bonus clinicians in the same specialty.
hunches.join_keys: QPP.NPI (503,917 rows, 453,202 distinct; one row per NPI x practice, rolled up with max adjustment) = OPEN_PAYMENTS(PY2024).NPI: 240,329 of 453,202 QPP NPIs paid in 2024 (53.0%). Specialty control on QPP.CLINICIAN_SPECIALTY, top-decile money computed within specialty with ntile(10).
hunches.query_sql:
with q as (select NPI,max(CLINICIAN_SPECIALTY) spec,max(try_to_number(PAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_PERCENTAGE,18,6)) adj from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE group by 1),
o24 as (select NPI,sum(try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2)) usd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS where NPI is not null and trim(NPI)<>'' and COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE<>'Covered Recipient Teaching Hospital' group by 1),
j as (select q.spec,case when adj<0 then '1 penalty' when adj=0 then '2 zero' when adj<0.5 then '3 small bonus' else '4 top bonus' end band,coalesce(o24.usd,0) usd,ntile(10) over (partition by q.spec order by coalesce(o24.usd,0)) dec from q left join o24 using(NPI))
select band,count(*) npis,sum(iff(dec=10,1,0)) in_top_decile_money,round(100*sum(iff(dec=10,1,0))/count(*),1) pct_top_decile from j group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 453,202 distinct QPP NPIs banded: 32,030 penalty, 23,481 zero, 149,302 small bonus, 248,389 top bonus; 240,329 with any 2024 industry payment
hunches.first_number: 10.3% of penalized clinicians sit in their specialty's top money decile vs 10.1% of top-bonus clinicians (PY2024 score, PY2024 payments); the zero-adjustment band is the outlier at 13.0%
hunches.hit_means: A consistent gap by band inside a specialty: quality scoring and industry relationships pull the same people, or opposite people.
hunches.miss_means: Flat: MIPS adjustment does not predict industry money. Result is a miss with one twist. Overall: penalty 57.9% paid, median $33; top bonus 52.9% paid, median $19. Within specialty it flips both ways: Orthopedic Surgery penalty avg $14,116 vs top bonus $21,856; Family Practice penalty avg $2,797 vs top bonus $412 (outlier-driven). The zero band (score exactly 75.00, 26,043 rows) is the most-paid group at 70.0%.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds and the two legs are the same year (QPP PY2024, Open Payments PY2024), but QPP is one snapshot, so no before/after on the score is possible.
hunches.time_axis: Open Payments PY2024 dated per payment; QPP PY2024 single vintage (no year column; dated by MVP roster and adjustment range)
traps: QPP has no performance-year column. PY2024 is inferred: 16 MVP ids including M1366-M1370, which CMS added for PY2024; PAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_PERCENTAGE runs -9.00 to +1.05.

QPP NPI repeats: 503,917 rows / 453,202 NPIs; 41,626 NPIs carry 2 to 13 rows (one per practice) with different scores. PROVIDER_KEY is the row key; roll up per NPI before joining or fan-out inflates every count.
QPP._SOURCE_RUN_ID is unique per row (503,917 distinct); it is a row id, not a run id.
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 19 (QPP x Part D opioid rate). This pairs QPP with Open Payments, a table pair not used before, and controls for specialty with within-specialty deciles.

hunches.title: Opted out, still on the payroll
hunches.hunch: Clinicians who opted out of Medicare keep taking industry money inside their opt-out window, and the money is orthopedic royalties, not lunches, while hundreds of them stay listed on hospital affiliations.
hunches.join_keys: OPT_OUT_AFFIDAVITS.NPI (57,209 rows, 56,455 distinct; OPTOUT_EFFECTIVE_DATE/OPTOUT_END_DATE MM/DD/YYYY text) = OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023.NPI: 11,779 paid at all (20.9%), 8,957 paid with DATE_OF_PAYMENT between effective and end date; 2022 in-window 8,023; 2024 in-window 9,401. = FACILITY_AFFILIATION.NPI 767 (1.4%; 759 hospital, 178 HHA, 35 hospice, 30 nursing home). = BY_PROVIDER.RNDRNG_NPI 1,856 (3.3%), of which only 17 were opted out for all of 2024. = QPP.NPI 68 opted out all of 2024.
hunches.query_sql:
with oo as (select NPI,min(try_to_date(OPTOUT_EFFECTIVE_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) eff,max(try_to_date(OPTOUT_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) endd,max(SPECIALTY) spec from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPT_OUT_AFFIDAVITS group by 1)
select count(*) optout_npis,
(select count(distinct o.NPI) from oo join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 o on o.NPI=oo.NPI and try_to_date(o.DATE_OF_PAYMENT,'MM/DD/YYYY') between oo.eff and oo.endd) paid_2023_in_window,
(select round(sum(try_to_number(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2))) from oo join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 o on o.NPI=oo.NPI and try_to_date(o.DATE_OF_PAYMENT,'MM/DD/YYYY') between oo.eff and oo.endd) usd_2023_in_window,
(select count(distinct f.NPI) from oo join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_FACILITY_AFFILIATION f on f.NPI=oo.NPI) in_affiliation,
(select count(distinct b.RNDRNG_NPI) from oo join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER b on b.RNDRNG_NPI=oo.NPI) in_partb
from oo;
-- nature: select NATURE_OF_PAYMENT_OR_TRANSFER_OF_VALUE, count(distinct NPI), sum(usd) on the same in-window join
hunches.distinct_entities: 8,957 distinct opted-out NPIs paid inside their window in 2023 (8,023 in 2022, 9,401 in 2024); 78 NPIs hold the $43.3M of royalties; 163 of the 8,957 also sit on a facility affiliation, 12 of those took $100k+
hunches.first_number: $70,776,832 paid by industry in 2023 to 8,957 clinicians while they were opted out of Medicare; $43,271,720 of it is Royalty or License to 78 people; Orthopedic Surgery $33,396,098 across 159 NPIs; top recipient Maxwell (TN plastic surgeon, opted out 2017-03-06) $11,600,320 from AbbVie in 7 payments
hunches.hit_means: Opt-out is a way to take device royalties and consulting income outside Medicare's price and sunshine pressure while keeping hospital privileges; the 12 paid $100k+ and still affiliated are the names to pull.
hunches.miss_means: Opted-out clinicians are just the cash-pay psychiatry and dental population and the money is lunches. Miss on the lunches leg: Food and Beverage reaches 8,464 NPIs for only $2.7M. Hit on the money leg: 61% of the dollars are royalties to 78 surgeons. The Part B check is a clean null that validates the data: only 17 clinicians opted out for all of 2024 have a Part B DY2024 row, $64,133 total, none over $10k.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds, first number found, both legs dated: opt-out effective/end dates vs payment dates, tested year by year across 2022, 2023 and 2024.
hunches.time_axis: OPTOUT_EFFECTIVE_DATE 1998-2026 and OPTOUT_END_DATE 2026-2028; Open Payments PY2022/2023/2024 payment dates; Part B DY2024 undated; affiliation snapshot 2026-07-11
traps: FED_CMS_OPT_OUT_AFFIDAVITS: 57,209 rows / 56,455 NPIs; 754 repeat rows, roll up per NPI. _SOURCE_RUN_ID is unique per row (57,209).

The 2024 effective-date surge (15,966 affidavits vs 3,203 in 2023) is Mental Health Counselors (5,431) and Marriage and Family Therapists (5,404), provider types Medicare first enrolled in 2024. It is a rule change, not an exodus of doctors.

The DME-by-referrer table carries RFRG_NPI and no TOT_*PYMT* column at the total level (TOT_SUPLRS, TOT_SUPLR_HCPCS_CDS, TOT_SUPLR_BENES, TOT_SUPLR_CLMS, TOT_SUPLR_SRVCS); a guessed money column throws.
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 7 (opt-out density by ZIP vs HPSA), which never joined opt-out to money. This is the first opt-out x Open Payments x affiliation chain, date-tested inside the opt-out window.

hunches.title: Opioid reps follow the volume
hunches.hunch: Nurse practitioners and physician assistants paid on named opioid products in both 2022 and 2023 write opioids at ten to forty times the rate of unpaid peers in DY2024, but their opioid claims were already that high in DY2022, and rural or HPSA status makes it lower, not higher.
hunches.join_keys: OPEN_PAYMENTS_2022/2023.NPI filtered on NAME_OF_DRUG_OR_BIOLOGICAL_OR_DEVICE_OR_MEDICAL_SUPPLY_1 matching opioid brands/generics (13,529 NPIs 2022, 18,080 NPIs 2023, 6,217 both) = PART_D_PRESCRIBERS.NPI (DY2024, TOT_CLMS>=100) = QPP.NPI for RURAL_STATUS/HPSA (247,558 Part D NPIs with an opioid rate sit in QPP). Time leg: PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG."Prscrbr_NPI" (DY2022) summed on Gnrc_Name opioid match for paid NPIs plus a 10% sample (right(NPI,1)='0'): 58,549 NPIs in both vintages across the four primary-care types.
hunches.query_sql:
with o22 as (select NPI,sum(usd) usd from (select NPI,NAME_OF_DRUG_OR_BIOLOGICAL_OR_DEVICE_OR_MEDICAL_SUPPLY_1 prod,try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2) usd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2022 where NPI is not null and trim(NPI)<>'') where (prod ilike '%xtampza%' or prod ilike '%nucynta%' or prod ilike '%oxycontin%' or prod ilike '%hysingla%' or prod ilike '%belbuca%' or prod ilike '%butrans%' or prod ilike '%percocet%' or prod ilike '%roxicodone%' or prod ilike '%seglentis%' or prod ilike '%olinvyk%' or prod ilike '%oxycodone%' or prod ilike '%hydrocodone%' or prod ilike '%tapentadol%' or prod ilike '%morphine%' or prod ilike '%fentanyl%' or prod ilike '%oxymorphone%' or prod ilike '%hydromorphone%' or prod ilike '%tramadol%') group by 1),
o23 as (/* same on FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 */ select NPI,0 usd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 where 1=0),
q as (select NPI,max(RURAL_STATUS) rural,max(HEALTH_PROFESSIONAL_SHORTAGE_AREA_STATUS) hpsa from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE group by 1),
d as (select NPI,PRSCRBR_TYPE typ,try_to_number(OPIOID_PRSCRBR_RATE,18,6) orate,try_to_number(OPIOID_LA_PRSCRBR_RATE,18,6) larate from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS where try_to_number(TOT_CLMS,18,6)>=100)
select d.typ,iff(q.rural='True' or q.hpsa='True','rural or HPSA','neither') geo,case when o22.NPI is not null and o23.NPI is not null then 'both years' when o22.NPI is not null or o23.NPI is not null then 'one year' else 'never' end grp,count(*) npis,round(median(d.orate),2) med_opioid_rate,round(median(d.larate),2) med_la_rate from q join d using(NPI) left join o22 using(NPI) left join o23 using(NPI) where d.typ in ('Family Practice','Internal Medicine','Nurse Practitioner','Physician Assistant') group by 1,2,3 order by 1,2,3
-- run with o23 as the real 2023 CTE (see script); time leg in query opioid_claims_2022_vs_2024
hunches.distinct_entities: 6,217 distinct NPIs paid on an opioid product in both 2022 and 2023 (5,072 metro, 437 nonmetro among Part D prescribers with a RUCA); primary-care cells: NP 292 metro and 119 rural/HPSA, PA 226 and 58, FP 63 and 31, IM 60 and 25
hunches.first_number: Nurse practitioners paid on opioid products in both 2022 and 2023: median DY2024 opioid prescribing rate 45.1% (n=292, non-rural) vs 0.0% for never-paid NPs (n=32,956); rural/HPSA NPs 52.3% (n=119) vs 1.07% (n=12,539); long-acting rate median 19.7 vs 0
hunches.hit_means: Opioid marketing lands on the highest-volume mid-level prescribers and, if their 2022->2024 opioid claims rose faster than unpaid peers, marketing moved prescribing. The rural question is answered no: nonmetro paid-both-years median 19.1% vs metro 39.1%.
hunches.miss_means: Paid prescribers were already the volume before the payments: DY2022->DY2024 opioid claims ratio for paid NPs 1.028 vs 1.151 for never-paid, PAs 1.017 vs 1.128, FP 0.986 vs 1.011. That is what the data shows: reps target existing volume, the marketing did not create a spike. The story is targeting, not conversion.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds, first number found, both legs dated: payments 2022 and 2023 by date, prescribing at DY2022 (drug file) and DY2024 (summary), so a before/after exists on both sides.
hunches.time_axis: Open Payments PY2022 and PY2023 payment dates; Part D drug file DY2022 vs Part D summary DY2024; QPP PY2024 flags
traps: Payer-name matching for opioid makers is noise: Mallinckrodt Hospital Products Inc. (11,745 NPIs in 2023) sells Acthar and INOmax, Indivior sells Suboxone (buprenorphine for addiction, excluded from CMS's opioid rate), Endo is mostly Xiaflex. Payer-name set is 34,113 NPIs in 2022; product-name set is 13,529. Match NAME_OF_DRUG_OR_BIOLOGICAL_OR_DEVICE_OR_MEDICAL_SUPPLY_1.
SEGLENTIS (Kowa, celecoxib/tramadol) is the biggest opioid-product marketing push by reach in 2023: 11,806 NPIs, $456,716. Purdue Pharma L.P. reached only 69 NPIs ($3.5M, concentrated).
The DY2022 opioid claim count from the drug file is a floor (rows under 11 claims suppressed); use it only to compare groups, both of which carry the same floor.
hunches.script_path: C:/Users/wroge/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Code-Ripple-v6/ee9da5e0-539c-4d14-8f3a-1d0f74fa4423/scratchpad/hubB/p11_opioid_v2.py (payer-name first pass in p5_rural_newnpi.py and p9_opioid_spec_newnpi.py)
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest are hunch 19 (QPP x Part D opioid rate, no money leg) and hunch 4 (buprenorphine share x maker payments, died on OTP). This adds the Open Payments product leg, the specialty control, and the two-vintage Part D time axis; none of those were run before.

hunches.title: Top billers, top payees
hunches.hunch: Clinicians in the top Part B allowed-charge decile of their specialty are nearly twice as likely as their peers to also sit in the top industry-money decile, and in orthopedics the overlap is 487 surgeons holding $100.9M of device money.
hunches.join_keys: BY_PROVIDER.RNDRNG_NPI where RNDRNG_PRVDR_ENT_CD='I' (1,235,757 individuals, DY2024) left join OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023.NPI (933,619 distinct); deciles by ntile(10) within RNDRNG_PRVDR_TYPE on TOT_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT and on OP dollars (zero-filled). Note FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PROVIDER is the same file (hash_agg equal), do not join the two.
hunches.query_sql:
with o23 as (select NPI,sum(try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2)) usd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 where NPI is not null and trim(NPI)<>'' and COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE<>'Covered Recipient Teaching Hospital' group by 1),
b as (select RNDRNG_NPI NPI,RNDRNG_PRVDR_TYPE typ,try_to_number(TOT_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT,18,2) allowed from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER where RNDRNG_PRVDR_ENT_CD='I'),
j as (select b.*,coalesce(o23.usd,0) op_usd,ntile(10) over (partition by typ order by allowed) dec_b,ntile(10) over (partition by typ order by coalesce(o23.usd,0)) dec_o from b left join o23 using(NPI))
select count(*) partb_individuals,sum(iff(dec_b=10,1,0)) top_b,sum(iff(dec_b=10 and dec_o=10,1,0)) both_top,round(100*sum(iff(dec_b=10 and dec_o=10,1,0))/nullif(sum(iff(dec_b=10,1,0)),0),1) pct_of_top_b_also_top_o,round(100*sum(iff(dec_o=10,1,0))/count(*),1) baseline_pct_top_o from j
hunches.distinct_entities: 22,473 distinct NPIs in both top deciles out of 123,529 top-decile Part B billers (1,235,757 individuals scored); Anesthesiology 1,481 (36.1%), Physician Assistant 3,180 (28.3%), Orthopedic Surgery 487 (22.5%)
hunches.first_number: 18.2% of top-decile Part B billers are also top-decile Open Payments recipients in their specialty, against a 10.0% baseline (Part B DY2024, payments PY2023); the 487 both-top orthopedic surgeons hold $100,869,984 of 2023 industry money and $281.9M of Medicare allowed charges
hunches.hit_means: Industry money concentrates on the clinicians who drive Medicare volume; the named both-top list (Booth PA $8.46M, Scuderi NY $5.67M, Frankle FL $4.70M, all orthopedics) is the shortlist for royalty-vs-implant-volume work when an outpatient/inpatient service file with the same year lands.
hunches.miss_means: Overlap at the 10% baseline would mean money and volume are independent. It is not: 1.8x overall, 3.6x in anesthesiology. High allowed charges also mean drug-heavy specialties, so the overlap partly measures who administers expensive drugs.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds and a first number exists, but Part B is a single vintage (DY2024) and the payments are one year, so the claim is cross-sectional; no before/after on billing is possible until a second Part B year lands.
hunches.time_axis: Part B DY2024 (no date column; dated by NPPES enumeration carbon-dating and HCPCS G2211); Open Payments PY2023 dated
traps: FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER is DY2024, not DY2023: 16,978 of its NPIs were enumerated in 2024 (newest 2024-12-30, zero from 2025) and the service file carries G2211 (payable only from 2024-01-01) on 138,770 NPIs, 24.6M services. The registry note reads release code D24 as 'data year 2023'.

FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PROVIDER (1,296,739 rows) is the same file as BY_PROVIDER: hash_agg over NPI, allowed amount and services is identical; the NPI column is named NPI there and RNDRNG_NPI here, and its _INGESTED_AT is a NUMBER.
BY_PROVIDER._SOURCE_RUN_ID and _AND_SERVI._SOURCE_RUN_ID are unique per row (1,296,739 and 9,781,673 distinct); never group by them.
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest are ghost_npi_partb_money (two NPIs' Part B rows) and hunch 18 (royalties vs outpatient hardware, hospital side). This is the first population-wide Part B x Open Payments decile cross, and it re-dates the Part B file.

hunches.title: State malpractice backdrop
hunches.hunch: States with the most NPDB malpractice payments per MIPS physician also carry the most industry money per physician and the lowest MIPS scores, a state-level backdrop that cannot name anyone.
hunches.join_keys: NPDB.WORKSTAT (ORIGYEAR 2022-2024, LICNFELD in ('10','20') = MD/DO, RECTYPE 'P' = malpractice payment) = QPP.PRACTICE_STATE_OR_US_TERRITORY (physician rows, distinct NPI per state) = OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023.RECIPIENT_STATE (physician rows). 49 states with 500+ QPP physicians matched on all three. WORKSTAT is blank on 133,812 of 190,401 NPDB rows in 2022-2024 (70%), so every state rate is a floor.
hunches.query_sql:
with mal as (select WORKSTAT st,sum(iff(RECTYPE='P',1,0)) mal_pay,sum(iff(RECTYPE<>'P',1,0)) adverse from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HRSA_NPDB where ORIGYEAR in ('2022','2023','2024') and LICNFELD in ('10','20') and WORKSTAT is not null group by 1),
q as (select PRACTICE_STATE_OR_US_TERRITORY st,count(distinct NPI) qpp_npis,round(avg(try_to_number(FINAL_SCORE,18,6)),2) avg_fs,round(100*avg(iff(try_to_number(PAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_PERCENTAGE,18,6)<0,1,0)),2) pct_penalized from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE where CLINICIAN_TYPE ilike '%physician%' or CLINICIAN_SPECIALTY like 'Physician/%' group by 1),
o as (select RECIPIENT_STATE st,sum(try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2)) usd from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 where COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE='Covered Recipient Physician' group by 1)
select q.st,q.qpp_npis,q.avg_fs,q.pct_penalized,mal.mal_pay,mal.adverse,round(1000*mal.mal_pay/q.qpp_npis,1) malpay_per_1k,round(1000*mal.adverse/q.qpp_npis,1) adverse_per_1k,round(o.usd/q.qpp_npis) op_usd_per_physician from q join mal using(st) join o using(st) where q.qpp_npis>=500 order by malpay_per_1k desc
hunches.distinct_entities: 49 states; 34,711 NPDB malpractice payment reports 2022-2024 of which the state-attributable share is the 30% with WORKSTAT filled; 366,000-plus QPP physician NPIs summed across states
hunches.first_number: Massachusetts: 117.2 malpractice payments per 1,000 MIPS physicians (2022-2024) and $27,369 of 2023 industry money per physician, MIPS average 81.4; Maine: 3.4 per 1,000, $745 per physician, MIPS average 91.2
hunches.hit_means: The ranking gives a state-level context layer for any named clinician story (this state is a high-payout, high-money state) and flags states where the QPP penalty share and malpractice rate move together (NV 19.7% penalized, 67.9 per 1k; KS 16.5%, 92.2 per 1k).
hunches.miss_means: Rankings driven by tort law, teaching-hospital density and the 70% blank WORKSTAT tell you about states, not doctors. NPDB is de-identified: no NPI, no name, PAYMENT is a midpoint band string like '$97500'. Nothing here names a person and it should be graded as backdrop only.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds and NPDB carries years, but the join key is a state, the entity is a population, QPP is one vintage, and 70% of recent NPDB rows have no state; ecological and cross-sectional in practice.
hunches.time_axis: NPDB ORIGYEAR 1990-2026 (2022-2024 used, 63k-64k reports a year); Open Payments PY2023; QPP PY2024 snapshot
traps: FED_HRSA_NPDB.WORKSTAT is blank on 133,812 of 190,401 rows with ORIGYEAR 2022-2024 (70%); any state rate is a floor over the 30% that carry a state.

NPDB RECTYPE: 'P' = malpractice payment 2004-2026 (282,035 rows), 'M' = malpractice payment 1990-2004 (250,672), 'C' = adverse action 1997-2026 (1,327,847), 'A' = adverse action 1990-2000 (50,631). Filtering RECTYPE='MALPAYMENT' or on PAYMENT text matches nothing useful.
NPDB.PAYMENT is a text midpoint band ('$97500', '$195000', '$22500'); try_to_number gives a band centre, not a settlement.
hunches.overlap_check: No existing hunch or report touches FED_HRSA_NPDB. Nearest in shape is hunch 21 (state/county wage backdrop). This is the first NPDB x QPP x Open Payments state panel.

hunches.title: Newborn NPIs, skin-graft millions
hunches.hunch: Nurse practitioners and physician assistants whose NPIs were created in 2022 or later already sit in Medicare's top 1% of Part B allowed charges for DY2024, three-quarters of their money is skin substitutes, and they bill $21,595 per beneficiary against $3,892 for veteran top-1% billers.
hunches.join_keys: NPPES.NPI where ENTITY_TYPE_CODE='1' and PROVIDER_ENUMERATION_DATE (MM/DD/YYYY) >= 2022-01-01 = BY_PROVIDER.RNDRNG_NPI (88,931 new NPIs in Part B DY2024; 1,232,785 of 1,296,739 Part B NPIs match a type-1 NPPES row) = _AND_SERVI.RNDRNG_NPI for HCPCS mix (all 354 new top-1% NPIs matched) = OPEN_PAYMENTS(2024).NPI 212 of 354 = LEIE.NPI 0 of top 30. Part D leg: new NPIs = PART_D_PRESCRIBERS.NPI (DY2024): 2022 cohort 65,819, 2023 cohort 63,337, 2024 cohort 36,166.
hunches.query_sql:
with n as (select NPI,try_to_date(PROVIDER_ENUMERATION_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') enum from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NPPES where ENTITY_TYPE_CODE='1'),
b as (select RNDRNG_NPI NPI,RNDRNG_PRVDR_TYPE typ,RNDRNG_PRVDR_STATE_ABRVTN st,try_to_number(TOT_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT,18,2) allowed,try_to_number(TOT_BENES,18,0) benes,ntile(100) over (order by try_to_number(TOT_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT,18,2)) pct from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER where RNDRNG_PRVDR_ENT_CD='I'),
top1 as (select b.*,iff(n.enum>='2022-01-01','new 2022+','older') cohort from b join n using(NPI) where pct=100),
s as (select RNDRNG_NPI NPI,sum(iff(HCPCS_CD like 'Q4%',try_to_number(TOT_SRVCS,18,2)*try_to_number(AVG_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT,18,2),0)) q4_allowed,sum(try_to_number(TOT_SRVCS,18,2)*try_to_number(AVG_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT,18,2)) all_allowed from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER_AND_SERVI where RNDRNG_NPI in (select NPI from top1) group by 1)
select top1.cohort,count(*) npis,round(sum(top1.allowed)) allowed,round(sum(s.q4_allowed)) q4_allowed_est,round(100*sum(s.q4_allowed)/nullif(sum(s.all_allowed),0),1) pct_q4,sum(iff(s.q4_allowed>0.5*s.all_allowed,1,0)) npis_majority_q4,round(avg(top1.benes)) avg_benes from top1 left join s using(NPI) group by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 354 distinct NPIs enumerated 2022 or later inside the Part B DY2024 top 1% (12,326 top-1% NPIs total); 94 of them draw over half their allowed from Q4 skin-substitute codes; 36 bill over $100,000 per beneficiary; top cells AZ nurse practitioners 21 NPIs $166.2M (91.6% Q4), CA physician assistants 17 NPIs $139.2M (93.0% Q4)
hunches.first_number: $1,352,392,029 of DY2024 Medicare allowed charges to 354 clinicians whose NPIs did not exist before 2022; 75.1% of it ($443.9M estimated from service rows) is skin substitutes (HCPCS Q4xxx) vs 16.5% for the 11,972 veteran top-1% billers; the single largest, an Arizona NP enumerated 2022-04-05, shows $54,881,402 allowed on 78 beneficiaries
hunches.hit_means: A cohort of brand-new mid-level NPIs is being used as billing vehicles for the skin-substitute wave (Complete FT Q4271 $103.5M across 11 of the top 30 alone), concentrated in AZ, CA, FL, NV, IL; per-beneficiary dollars 5.5x the veteran top 1% is the tell, and Open Payments shows almost none of it (212 of 354 got a total of $90,329 in 2024, lunches), so the manufacturers' money is not in the sunshine file.
hunches.miss_means: New NPIs in the top 1% would be ordinary if their HCPCS mix and per-beneficiary dollars matched the veteran top 1%. They do not. The Part D side is milder but real: a NJ nurse practitioner enumerated 2023-11-15 wrote 26,968 Part D claims and $5,738,366 in DY2024; a Puerto Rico general practitioner enumerated 2022-10-17 wrote 49,024 claims. None of the top 30 Part B names is on LEIE yet, which is what 'before the takedown' looks like.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds, first number found, and the before/after is built in: the enumeration date is a date and the DY2024 volume follows it; the claim is directly testable as written and was tested.
hunches.time_axis: NPPES PROVIDER_ENUMERATION_DATE 2005-2026 (MM/DD/YYYY text); Part B DY2024 and Part D DY2024 (both dated by carbon-dating: newest enumeration 2024-12-30 and 2024-12-06, none from 2025); Open Payments PY2024
traps: FED_CMS_NPPES.ENTITY_TYPE_CODE is '' on 346,179 rows, exactly the count of deactivated-and-never-reactivated NPIs; filtering ENTITY_TYPE_CODE='1' silently drops every deactivated individual.

Part B and Part D summary files are DY2024, not DY2023/DY2022 as the seed brief and the frank report assumed; the newest NPPES enumeration date among NPIs present in a per-NPI file bounds its data year (Part B 2024-12-30, Part D 2024-12-06, QPP 2024-07-17, DME referrer 2024-09-24).
Skin-substitute dollars are estimated as TOT_SRVCS x AVG_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT per service row; the service file suppresses rows under 11 beneficiaries, so the Q4 share is a floor on the service side.
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is hunch 23 (debarred DME suppliers, catheter ring) and hunch 27 (pending applicants). This is the first NPPES-enumeration-date x Part B/Part D volume chain and the first look at skin-substitute (Q4) concentration; no prior report touches Q4 codes or the new-NPI cohort.

hunches.title: Excluded, still cleared to order
hunches.hunch: Clinicians excluded by OIG years ago are still listed in CMS's current Order and Referring file as eligible to order DME, home health and hospice for Medicare patients.
hunches.join_keys: LEIE.NPI (8,660 distinct real NPIs, sentinel '0000000000' excluded, REINDATE='00000000' = never reinstated, EXCLDATE YYYYMMDD text) = ORDER_AND_REFERRING.NPI (2,018,354 rows, 2,018,350 distinct, snapshot ingested 2026-08-05): 38 matched, 26 of them excluded before the snapshot date, 7 excluded before 2025.
hunches.query_sql:
with l as (select NPI,min(EXCLDATE) excl,max(REINDATE) rein,max(EXCLTYPE) typ from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE where NPI<>'0000000000' and trim(NPI)<>'' group by 1),
r as (select NPI,max(PARTB) partb,max(DME) dme,max(HHA) hha,max(HOSPICE) hospice,max(PMD) pmd,max(_INGESTED_AT) ing from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_ORDER_AND_REFERRING group by 1)
select count(*) excluded_still_listed,sum(iff(l.rein='00000000',1,0)) never_reinstated,sum(iff(l.rein='00000000' and l.excl<'20250101',1,0)) never_reinst_excl_before_2025,sum(iff(r.dme='Y',1,0)) dme_y,sum(iff(r.hha='Y',1,0)) hha_y,sum(iff(r.hospice='Y',1,0)) hospice_y,min(l.excl) mn_excl,max(l.excl) mx_excl,max(r.ing) or_ingested from l join r using(NPI)
hunches.distinct_entities: 38 distinct excluded NPIs in the Order and Referring file, all never reinstated, all flagged DME='Y', 26 HHA='Y', 21 HOSPICE='Y'; 26 excluded before the 2026-08-05 snapshot; 7 excluded before 2025 (Miranda TX 2015-06-18, Patel OR 2020-03-19, Fraser NE 2021-08-19, Barker IL 2023-10-02, Sicuro MO 2024-02-20, Gray CA 2024-10-07, Syed CT 2024-12-12)
hunches.first_number: 26 OIG-excluded clinicians remain in CMS's 2026-08-05 Order and Referring file as eligible to order DME; 7 of them were excluded more than 19 months before the snapshot, the oldest in June 2015
hunches.hit_means: The order-and-referring gate that is supposed to block excluded clinicians from driving DME, home health and hospice claims is leaking: a supplier checking the CMS file would see these people as cleared.
hunches.miss_means: A count of zero, or only exclusions dated within weeks of the snapshot, would mean the file is simply lagging a routine update. 19 of the 26 are 2026 exclusions and could be lag; the 7 older ones are not lag. The number is a floor: LEIE holds a real NPI on 8,661 of 83,842 rows.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds, first number found, both legs dated: exclusion date vs the Order and Referring snapshot date, so lag can be separated from failure.
hunches.time_axis: LEIE EXCLDATE 2015-06-18 to 2026-08-20 among the matches; Order and Referring snapshot ingested 2026-08-05 (12 of the 38 were excluded after the snapshot and are not counted)
traps: FED_CMS_ORDER_AND_REFERRING._SOURCE_RUN_ID is unique per row (2,018,354 distinct on 2,018,354 rows); it is a row id. NPI is nearly but not fully unique (2,018,350 distinct).
LEIE joins are floors: 75,001 of 83,842 LEIE rows carry the sentinel NPI '0000000000'.
hunches.overlap_check: ghost_npi_ownership noted one NPI (Miranda) still authorized to order and refer. This runs the same test across the whole LEIE real-NPI set and dates each hit against the snapshot; hunch 27 (LEIE x pending applicants) and hunch 1 (LEIE x hospice affiliation) use different CMS files.

hunches.title: Industry pays dead NPIs
hunches.hunch: Manufacturers report payments to NPIs that NPPES had already deactivated, mostly royalties to retired surgeons but also thousands of meals, while Medicare Part B stops paying the same NPIs the day they die.
hunches.join_keys: NPPES.NPI where NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE non-blank and NPI_REACTIVATION_DATE blank (346,179 NPIs, deactivations 2005-05-23 to 2026-06-07) = OPEN_PAYMENTS(2024).NPI: 3,992 NPIs, 1,325 with DATE_OF_PAYMENT after the deactivation date, 1,224 paid 90+ days after; = OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023.NPI after deactivation 1,156; = BY_PROVIDER.RNDRNG_NPI 3,558 in Part B DY2024 but only 1 deactivated before 2024 ($43,837); = PART_D_PRESCRIBERS.NPI 5,269.
hunches.query_sql:
with n as (select NPI,try_to_date(NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') deact from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NPPES where trim(NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE)<>'' and trim(NPI_REACTIVATION_DATE)='')
select count(distinct n.NPI) npis,count(*) pays,round(sum(try_to_number(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2))) usd,
count(distinct iff(try_to_date(o.DATE_OF_PAYMENT,'MM/DD/YYYY')>n.deact,n.NPI,null)) npis_paid_after_deact,
round(sum(iff(try_to_date(o.DATE_OF_PAYMENT,'MM/DD/YYYY')>n.deact,try_to_number(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2),0))) usd_after_deact,
count(distinct iff(try_to_date(o.DATE_OF_PAYMENT,'MM/DD/YYYY')>dateadd(day,90,n.deact),n.NPI,null)) npis_paid_90d_after
from n join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS o on o.NPI=n.NPI
hunches.distinct_entities: 3,992 distinct deactivated NPIs with 2024 payments (30,370 payment rows); 1,325 paid after deactivation; by nature after deactivation: Royalty or License 14 NPIs $3,368,402, Food and Beverage 1,248 NPIs $82,295, speaking 6 NPIs $457,369, consulting 7 NPIs $105,901; deactivation years 2006-2024, peak 2023 (247 NPIs) and 2024 (215)
hunches.first_number: $4,187,435 reported paid in 2024 to 1,325 NPIs that NPPES had already deactivated, 1,224 of them 90 or more days after deactivation; 2023 shows the same pattern at 1,156 NPIs and $4,680,578; Part B DY2024 pays exactly 1 NPI deactivated before 2024
hunches.hit_means: Two federal systems disagree on who exists: Open Payments keeps attributing money to dead or retired NPIs (Spetzler, neurosurgery, deactivated 2018-11-07, $1,791,118 royalties in 2024), while 1,248 deactivated NPIs 'ate' rep-bought meals in 2024, which means the recipient-matching in Open Payments is stale or the person is practising under a new NPI; either way the sunshine file's per-NPI totals are wrong for that person.
hunches.miss_means: If the after-deactivation money were only royalties it would be legitimate income to retirees booked to an old identifier. It is not only that: 1,248 meal recipients and 7 consultants post-deactivation cannot be retirees. A zero would have meant CMS scrubs Open Payments against NPPES; it does not, while Part B clearly does.
hunches.tier_reason: Chain holds, first number found, both legs dated: NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE vs DATE_OF_PAYMENT, and the same test runs on 2023 and 2024 payments.
hunches.time_axis: NPPES NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE 2005-2026 (MM/DD/YYYY text); Open Payments PY2023 and PY2024 payment dates; Part B DY2024 as a control
traps: FED_CMS_NPPES.NPI_DEACTIVATION_REASON_CODE is empty on all 364,602 deactivated rows; death cannot be separated from retirement or merger in the public file.
FED_CMS_NPPES.ENTITY_TYPE_CODE is blank on exactly the 346,179 deactivated-never-reactivated NPIs; a type-1 filter removes them all.

Open Payments recipient NPIs can post-date the payment year: 40 NPIs in the 2022 file and 367 in the 2023 file were enumerated in 2024 or later (CMS re-matches recipients on refresh); small, but it means NPPES dates and Open Payments dates are not perfectly aligned in either direction.
hunches.overlap_check: ghost_npi_partb_money and ghost_npi_ownership looked at two LEIE NPIs and their NPPES deactivation; pharma_paid_excluded date-tested LEIE against OP2022. This uses NPPES deactivation itself as the trigger across all 346,179 deactivated NPIs, with no exclusion list, and adds the Part B control.

traps.trap: The file is DY2024, not DY2023. The registry note for fed_cms_medicare_provider reads release code 'R26 P05 V10 D24' as data year 2023; D24 is data year 2024. Every earlier report that called Part B 'DY2023' (frank_investigation, ghost_npi_partb_money) is off by one year; Part B, Part D summary, QPP and Open Payments now all align on 2024.
traps.evidence: 16,978 of the file's NPIs have NPPES enumeration dates in 2024 (newest 2024-12-30), zero in 2025; the service file carries HCPCS G2211 (payable only from 2024-01-01) on 138,770 NPIs with 24,627,539 services and G0136 (new 2024) on 2,431 NPIs.

traps.trap: Same file as FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER under a different name; the NPI column is NPI here and RNDRNG_NPI there, and _INGESTED_AT is a NUMBER here. Any chain that walks one into the other is a self-join.
traps.evidence: hash_agg(NPI, TOT_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT, TOT_SRVCS) = -2288124447057648988 on both, 1,296,739 rows each.

traps.trap: DY2024, not DY2022. The seed brief's 'Part D DY2022, no year column' applies only to FED_CMS_PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG (DY22 in the source filename). The two Part D files are two years apart, which gives a Part D time axis nobody had used.
traps.evidence: 36,166 of its NPIs were enumerated in 2024 (newest 2024-12-06), zero in 2025; registry NOTES say 'Data year 2024 (12/2024), release RY26'.

traps.trap: Summing the drug file per NPI under-counts the prescriber's total because CMS suppresses drug rows under 11 claims. A 2022->2024 growth ratio built from it reads as huge growth for everyone. Also the columns are mixed-case ("Prscrbr_NPI", "Tot_Clms", "Gnrc_Name") and must be double-quoted; unquoted throws invalid identifier.
traps.evidence: 1% NPI sample (NPIs ending '00', 9,763 in both vintages): median claims DY2024/DY2022 = 1.531, median cost = 1.972; unquoted Prscrbr_NPI failed with 'invalid identifier' twice.

traps.trap: No performance-year column; PY2024 by inference. NPI is not the row key: one row per NPI x practice, so joins fan out unless rolled up. _SOURCE_RUN_ID is unique per row.
traps.evidence: 503,917 rows, 453,202 distinct NPIs, 503,917 distinct PROVIDER_KEY and 503,917 distinct _SOURCE_RUN_ID; 41,626 NPIs carry 2-13 rows with different FINAL_SCOREs; 16 MVP ids including M1366-M1370 (added PY2024); PAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_PERCENTAGE min -9.00 max +1.05.

traps.trap: The loader stamps a fresh _SOURCE_RUN_ID on every row in these tables, so it is a row id, not a run id (same pattern the DME supplier file showed). count(distinct _SOURCE_RUN_ID) = count(*) says nothing about how many loads happened.
Blank ENTITY_TYPE_CODE means deactivated NPI. Filtering ENTITY_TYPE_CODE='1' silently removes every deactivated individual, which is exactly the population a ghost hunt needs.
traps.evidence: ENTITY_TYPE_CODE='' on 346,179 rows; deactivated-and-never-reactivated NPIs = 346,179 (364,602 deactivated, 18,423 reactivated).

traps.trap: 100% empty. Death, retirement and merger cannot be told apart from the public file.
traps.evidence: '' on all 364,602 rows with a deactivation date.

traps.trap: NPI is blank on every Teaching Hospital row and on some physician rows; filter COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE before any NPI join. Payer ids are stable across years but names drift, so join payers on id. Recipient NPIs can post-date the payment year.
traps.evidence: 2023: blank NPI on 31,400 of 31,400 teaching-hospital rows, 6,801 physician rows, 6,032 NPP rows. Payer ids 1,786 (2022) / 1,817 (2023), 1,579 in both, 98 with a changed name. 40 NPIs in the 2022 file and 367 in the 2023 file were enumerated in 2024+.

traps.trap: Payer-name matching for opioid manufacturers is mostly not opioids: Mallinckrodt Hospital Products sells Acthar/INOmax, Indivior sells Suboxone (MOUD, excluded from the CMS opioid rate), Endo is mostly Xiaflex. Match the product column NAME_OF_DRUG_OR_BIOLOGICAL_OR_DEVICE_OR_MEDICAL_SUPPLY_1 instead.

hunches.title: Material weakness, money keeps flowing
hunches.hunch: Grantees that disclosed an internal-control material weakness in their 2022-23 single audit received HHS assistance in FY2024-25 at the same rate as clean auditees, $15.8B of it.
hunches.join_keys: FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT.AUDITEE_UEI = FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FULL."recipient_uei" (AUDITEE_UEI valid 12-char on 48,115 of 48,116 rows in AUDIT_YEAR 2022, 47,813/47,813 in 2023; only 2 of 36,991 in 2016, so the bridge starts 2022). 1,090 of 8,904 MW-flagged UEIs match an HHS FY24-25 recipient (12.2%) vs 4,943 of 44,310 clean (11.2%).
hunches.query_sql: with f as (select AUDITEE_UEI uei, max(case when IS_INTERNAL_CONTROL_MATERIAL_WEAKNESS_DISCLOSED='Yes' then 1 else 0 end) mw, max(case when IS_GOING_CONCERN_INCLUDED='Yes' then 1 else 0 end) gc from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT where AUDIT_YEAR in ('2022','2023') and regexp_like(AUDITEE_UEI,'^[A-Z0-9]{12}$') group by 1), a as (select "recipient_uei" uei, "assistance_award_unique_key" ak, try_to_number("federal_action_obligation",18,2) obl from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FULL where "awarding_agency_name" ilike '%health and human%' and "action_date_fiscal_year" in ('2024','2025')) select f.mw, f.gc, count(distinct f.uei) auditees, count(distinct a.uei) got_hhs, sum(a.obl) hhs_net_obl, count(distinct a.ak) awards from f left join a on a.uei=f.uei group by 1,2
hunches.distinct_entities: 1,090 distinct UEIs with a material weakness (no going concern) got HHS FY2024-25 money across 8,231 distinct awards; 37 more with both MW and going-concern flags, $603M, 224 awards
hunches.first_number: $15.81B HHS net obligations FY2024-2025 to 1,090 grantees that disclosed a material weakness in their 2022-23 single audit; Southwest Key Programs alone $847.6M (Unaccompanied Children Program 93.676)
hunches.hit_means: HHS grant officers do not use the Federal Audit Clearinghouse flag as a brake; the funding rate is flat (12.2% vs 11.2%) and the dollars are concentrated in child-welfare and refugee programs.
hunches.miss_means: If MW grantees were funded at a much lower rate, the audit flag works as a control and the story is about the exceptions only.
hunches.tier_reason: Both legs dated (AUDIT_YEAR and FY_END_DATE on FAC; action_date on USASpending); the claim is directly testable and was tested.
hunches.time_axis: FAC AUDIT_YEAR 2016-2026 (UEI bridge usable 2022+); assistance action_date 2006-10 to 2026-02, filtered FY2024-2025
traps: FAC flags are 'Yes'/'No' plus 'GSA_MIGRATION' on 312 rows; testing ='Y' returns 0
AUDITEE_UEI is valid on 2 of 36,991 rows in AUDIT_YEAR 2016 and 48,115 of 48,116 in 2022: the UEI bridge does not exist before 2022
A UEI with audits in both years takes max(flag); a 2022 weakness fixed in 2023 still counts
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is ghost_doctors_and_audit_bridge (validated FAC EIN-UEI bridge at 43%). This uses the FAC audit-finding flags against HHS assistance dollars, a pair no report has run.

hunches.title: Revoked nonprofits still funded
hunches.hunch: Nonprofits whose tax exemption the IRS auto-revoked for non-filing, with no reinstatement on file, kept receiving HHS assistance after the revocation date.
hunches.join_keys: FED_IRS_AUTO_REVOCATIONS.EIN = FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT.AUDITEE_EIN (1,006 revoked EINs have a single audit; 917 audited for a fiscal year ending after revocation; 374 with REINSTATEMENT_DATE null; 165 typed non-profit) -> FAC.AUDITEE_UEI = USASpending "recipient_uei" with action_date > REVOCATION_DATE (24 of 165 match).
hunches.query_sql: with r as (select EIN, max(LEGAL_NAME) nm, min(try_to_date(REVOCATION_DATE,'DD-MON-YYYY')) rev, max(try_to_date(REINSTATEMENT_DATE,'DD-MON-YYYY')) reinst from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_IRS_AUTO_REVOCATIONS group by 1), f as (select distinct AUDITEE_EIN ein, AUDITEE_UEI uei from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT where regexp_like(AUDITEE_UEI,'^[A-Z0-9]{12}$') and ENTITY_TYPE ilike '%non-profit%'), x as (select r.EIN, r.rev, f.uei from r join f on f.ein=r.EIN where r.reinst is null), a as (select "recipient_uei" uei, "assistance_award_unique_key" ak, try_to_date("action_date",'YYYY-MM-DD') ad, try_to_number("federal_action_obligation",18,2) obl from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FULL where "awarding_agency_name" ilike '%health and human%' and nullif("recipient_uei",'') is not null) select count(distinct x.EIN), count(distinct a.ak), sum(a.obl), min(a.ad), max(a.ad) from x join a on a.uei=x.uei and a.ad > x.rev
hunches.distinct_entities: 24 distinct revoked nonprofit EINs (24 UEIs) with HHS awards after revocation, 108 distinct awards; 165 revoked nonprofits reported $1.77B of federal expenditures in single audits for years after revocation
hunches.first_number: $50.7M HHS assistance obligated 2011-12 to 2026-02 to 24 nonprofits after the IRS auto-revoked their exemption with no reinstatement recorded; largest Colorado Early Education Network $12.5M Head Start since a 2013-09 revocation, Albuquerque Area Indian Health Board $10.6M since 2022-02
hunches.hit_means: An organization the IRS lists as no longer exempt is being paid as a nonprofit grantee; either the IRS list is stale or nobody at HHS checks it.
hunches.miss_means: A zero would mean the revocation list and the grant rolls never overlap, i.e. the check works or the EINs are different entities.
hunches.tier_reason: Revocation date, audit fiscal year and award action date are all dated; before/after is built into the query.
hunches.time_axis: REVOCATION_DATE 2010-2025 (DD-MON-YYYY text); FAC FY_END_DATE 2016-2026; assistance action_date 2011-2026
traps: FED_IRS_AUTO_REVOCATIONS.REVOCATION_DATE is 'DD-MON-YYYY' text (15-NOV-2017); try_to_date with YYYY-MM-DD returns null on every row
FED_IRS_AUTO_REVOCATIONS._INGESTED_AT is epoch microseconds (1785965067207356), the known 56-million-year trap on a new table
Public bodies (cities, tribes) do not need 501(c)(3); filter ENTITY_TYPE to non-profit or the count inflates
Reinstated orgs may be missing REINSTATEMENT_DATE; treat the 24 as leads, verify each on the IRS TEOS site
hunches.overlap_check: Nearest is graph_hunt_ein (EIN reach across tables) and the FAC bridge report. Neither touches FED_IRS_AUTO_REVOCATIONS; the revocation-date-vs-award-date mechanism is new.

hunches.title: Excluded firms still winning contracts
hunches.hunch: SAM-excluded firms won brand-new federal contracts while their exclusion was active, across every agency, and the post-exclusion contract book is mostly closeouts and deobligations.
hunches.join_keys: distinct trim(UNIQUE_ENTITY_ID) (38,427 UEIs on 168,328 rows) = FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FULL_R2."RECIPIENT_UEI"; per CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY min(ACTION_DATE) > min(ACTIVE_DATE) and <= TERMINATION_DATE ('Indefinite' -> 2099-12-31). 347 excluded UEIs had contracts before exclusion ($4.67B), 134 had any action during exclusion (1,321 contracts, net -$101.6M), 32 won new contracts during exclusion.
hunches.query_sql: with s as (select distinct nullif(trim(UNIQUE_ENTITY_ID),'') u from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2 where nullif(trim(UNIQUE_ENTITY_ID),'') is not null union select UEI_SAM from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_SAM_ENTITY_PUBLIC where PRIMARY_NAICS like '622%' or PRIMARY_NAICS like '623%') select "RECIPIENT_UEI" u, "CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY" ck, min(try_to_date("ACTION_DATE",'YYYY-MM-DD')) first_ad, sum(try_to_number("FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION",18,2)) net_obl, sum(case when try_to_number("FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION",18,2)>0 then try_to_number("FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION",18,2) else 0 end) pos_obl, max(try_to_number("TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED",18,2)) lifetime, max("AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME") agy, max("RECIPIENT_NAME") rn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FULL_R2 where "ACTION_DATE" >= '2010-01-01' and "RECIPIENT_UEI" in (select u from s) group by 1,2  -- then in Python: keep keys whose first_ad falls inside (ACTIVE_DATE, TERMINATION_DATE] with pos_obl > 0
hunches.distinct_entities: 32 distinct excluded UEIs (31 firms, 1 OFAC special entity) won 103 distinct new contracts inside their exclusion window; 134 UEIs had any action inside the window on 1,321 contracts
hunches.first_number: 32 excluded firms won 103 new federal contracts worth $2.22M in positive obligations while excluded, 2010-2026; Bonus Environmental LLC (EPA exclusion 2012-06, indefinite) won 14 Defense contracts, $839k
hunches.hit_means: The exclusion check at award failed 103 times; ten of the 32 are DLA exclusions, four EPA facility restrictions, three HHS.
hunches.miss_means: The aggregate during-window net of -$101.6M says most post-exclusion activity is deobligation and closeout, which is the system working; the story is the 32, not the 134.
hunches.tier_reason: Exclusion ACTIVE_DATE and contract ACTION_DATE both dated; new-award-during-window is a direct test.
hunches.time_axis: SAM ACTIVE_DATE 1989-2026 (157,312 of 168,328 parse); contracts ACTION_DATE filtered 2010-01 to 2026-08
traps: FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FULL_R2 column names are UPPERCASE ("RECIPIENT_UEI") while FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FULL are lowercase ("recipient_uei"); the same quoted SQL fails with 000904 on the other table
SAM ACTIVE_DATE carries sentinels '1908-04-20' and '2099-12-30'; TERMINATION_DATE is the literal 'Indefinite' on most rows
EPA 'Prohibition/Restriction' exclusions are facility-specific Clean Air/Water Act listings, so a DoD award to that firm is not automatically a violation
Net obligation in the exclusion window is negative (-$101.6M): summing without a sign split reads as money clawed back, not paid

hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 15 did SAM x FEMA contracts only, untimed, 26 UEIs, and flagged the timing as not done. This is all agencies, timed to the exclusion window, new awards only.

hunches.title: Jail counties are clinician deserts
hunches.hunch: Counties in the top quartile of 2018 jail incarceration have under half the QPP-participating clinicians per capita of bottom-quartile counties and are almost all whole-county primary-care shortage areas.
hunches.join_keys: QPP.NPI = NPPES.NPI (453,201 of 453,202 distinct QPP NPIs match; 452,088 carry a practice postal code) -> left(PROVIDER_BUSINESS_PRACTICE_LOCATION_ADDRESS_POSTAL_CODE,5) = DIM_ZIP_POINT.ZCTA5 -> PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS = VERA.COUNTY_FIPS (YEAR 2018, 3,042 counties) = DIM_COUNTY.COUNTY_FIPS (POPULATION_2020) = HPSA COMMON_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE (Single County, Designated). 2,290 counties with pop >= 10k and 2018 jail data.
hunches.query_sql: with cl as (select d.PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS fips, count(distinct q.NPI) clinicians from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE q join LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_NPPES n on n.NPI=q.NPI join LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_ZIP_POINT d on d.ZCTA5=left(n.PROVIDER_BUSINESS_PRACTICE_LOCATION_ADDRESS_POSTAL_CODE,5) group by 1), v as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, try_to_number(TOTAL_JAIL_POP,18,2) jail, try_to_number(TOTAL_POP_15TO64,18,0) pop1564 from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.XC_VERA_INCARCERATION_TRENDS where YEAR='2018'), hp as (select COMMON_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE fips, max(try_to_number(HPSA_SCORE,18,2)) score from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HRSA_HPSA_PRIMARY_CARE where HPSA_COMPONENT_TYPE_DESCRIPTION='Single County' and HPSA_STATUS='Designated' group by 1), c as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, POPULATION_2020 pop from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_COUNTY where POPULATION_2020 >= 10000), j as (select c.fips, coalesce(cl.clinicians,0)*10000/c.pop clin_per_10k, v.jail*100000/nullif(v.pop1564,0) jail_per_100k, hp.score from c join v on v.fips=c.fips left join cl on cl.fips=c.fips left join hp on hp.fips=c.fips where v.jail is not null and v.pop1564>0), q as (select *, ntile(4) over (order by jail_per_100k) jq from j) select jq, count(*), median(jail_per_100k), median(clin_per_10k), avg(case when score is not null then 1 else 0 end) from q group by 1 order by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 2,290 distinct counties; 452,088 distinct QPP NPIs placed in a county
hunches.first_number: 2.4 QPP clinicians per 10k residents in top-quartile jail counties (median 820 jailed per 100k adults 15-64, 2018) vs 5.2 in the bottom quartile (189 per 100k); 81% vs 46% are whole-county primary-care HPSAs; r(log clinicians, log jail) = -0.10 across 2,290 counties
hunches.hit_means: Incarceration and clinician absence sit in the same counties; the jail is the biggest health institution left.
hunches.miss_means: A flat gradient would say clinician supply tracks population, not incarceration.
hunches.tier_reason: VERA is a 1970-2026 series and HPSA has designation dates, but the clinician leg (QPP) is one undated snapshot, so this is cross-section only.
hunches.time_axis: VERA YEAR 2010-2019 full (3,042-3,054 counties), 2020+ partial (597 by 2026); HPSA designation dates 1978-2026; QPP vintage unrecorded; NPPES current
traps: FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE has 503,917 rows for 453,202 NPIs; 41,607 NPIs carry 2-8 rows, so count(*) overcounts clinicians 11%
XC_VERA_INCARCERATION_TRENDS has no TOTAL_POP column; the denominator is TOTAL_POP_15TO64 and the published rates are per 100k adults 15-64
NPPES practice postal code is 9 digits on 8,543,679 rows, 5 digits on 715,183, blank on 346,201: always left(,5)
DIM_ZIP_POINT assigns multi-county ZCTAs to the largest-population county; it disagrees with POS's own county on 47% of two-county ZIPs
