hunches.title: Fat margins, thin charity care
hunches.hunch: IRS-registered nonprofit hospitals (NTEE E20-E22) with FY2023 net income over $50M spend under 1% of total costs on charity care.
hunches.join_keys: normalized NAME = normalized HOSPITAL_NAME (generic words stripped, prefix match, both sides >= 6 chars) and upper(CITY) = upper(CITY) and STATE = STATE_CODE, BMF filtered to NTEE E20-E22 and not AUXILIARY/VOLUNTEER/FOUNDATION/GUILD: 1,480 of 5,340 hospital EINs -> 1,146 CCNs (1,601 pairs, 886 exact), 942 CCNs with nonprofit control code 1-2, 41 with for-profit control code 3-6. Sample 10 of 10 real pairs after the guard fix. No EIN column exists in any FED_CMS table except NPPES (redacted), so name is the only bridge.
hunches.query_sql: with b as (select EIN, NAME, CITY, STATE, trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(NAME),'[^A-Z0-9 ]',''),'\\b(INC|LLC|THE|OF|AND|CORP|CORPORATION|CO|LTD|DBA|HOSPITAL|MEDICAL|CENTER|HEALTH|SYSTEM|REGIONAL|COMMUNITY|MEMORIAL)\\b',''),' +',' ')) nn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_IRS_EO_BMF where NTEE_CD like 'E2%' and NTEE_CD < 'E23' and not regexp_like(upper(NAME),'.*(AUXILIARY|VOLUNTEER|FOUNDATION|GUILD|ASSOCIATES|LEAGUE).*')), h as (select PROVIDER_CCN, HOSPITAL_NAME, CITY, STATE_CODE, TYPE_OF_CONTROL, try_to_number(NET_INCOME,18,2) ni, try_to_number(COST_OF_CHARITY_CARE,18,2) cc, try_to_number(TOTAL_COSTS,18,2) tc, trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(HOSPITAL_NAME),'[^A-Z0-9 ]',''),'\\b(INC|LLC|THE|OF|AND|CORP|CORPORATION|CO|LTD|DBA|HOSPITAL|MEDICAL|CENTER|HEALTH|SYSTEM|REGIONAL|COMMUNITY|MEMORIAL)\\b',''),' +',' ')) nn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HCRIS), m as (select h.PROVIDER_CCN, max(h.ni) ni, max(h.cc) cc, max(h.tc) tc from b join h on b.STATE=h.STATE_CODE and upper(b.CITY)=upper(h.CITY) and length(b.nn)>=6 and length(h.nn)>=6 and (b.nn=h.nn or h.nn like b.nn||'%' or b.nn like h.nn||'%') where h.TYPE_OF_CONTROL in ('1','2') group by 1) select count(*), sum(case when ni>0 then 1 else 0 end), sum(case when ni>50000000 and cc/nullif(tc,0)<0.01 then 1 else 0 end), median(cc/nullif(tc,0)), sum(ni), sum(cc) from m
hunches.distinct_entities: 1,480 distinct BMF EINs, 1,146 distinct HCRIS CCNs, 942 of them nonprofit-control
hunches.first_number: 38 IRS-registered nonprofit hospitals with FY2023 net income over $50M and charity care under 1% of total costs; Stanford Health Care $1.05B net income at 0.45% charity, Cedars-Sinai $825M at 0.80%; the 942 matched nonprofits total $29.4B net income against $6.8B charity care (median charity share 1.2%)
hunches.hit_means: The tax exemption is buying very little charity care at the richest hospitals; the IRS leg proves exempt status rather than inferring it from the HCRIS control code.
hunches.miss_means: If charity share rose with margin the exemption would look earned.
hunches.tier_reason: HCRIS is one fiscal year (FY2023) and the BMF is one snapshot; no before/after.
hunches.time_axis: HCRIS FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE 2023-2024 only; BMF snapshot (TAX_PERIOD, RULING year present but not used); none usable as a series
traps: Stripping generic words turns COMMUNITY HOSPITAL into '' and `name like ''||'%'` matches every hospital in the city; the first pass paired HILLTOP HEALTH SERVICES with COMMUNITY HOSPITAL and DIVINE HANDLING & DISTRIBUTION with another; guard both sides with length >= 6
BMF hospital auxiliaries share the hospital's name (HCA HOUSTON HEALTHCARE SOUTHEAST VOLUNTEERS, EIN 510191373, matched the for-profit HCA hospital); exclude AUXILIARY/VOLUNTEER/FOUNDATION/GUILD

FED_CMS_HCRIS.NET_INCOME exceeds TOTAL_COSTS on 148 of 6,103 rows and exceeds 5x on 5 (Holy Family Memorial WI: $2.22B net income, $105M costs, 45 beds); it is not a hospital-level operating margin on those rows
No EIN column in HCRIS, HOSPITAL_GENERAL or POS; information_schema search of FED_CMS% for EIN/TIN returns only the redacted NPPES pair
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 11 (cost-report hypocrisy) uses HCRIS net income and uncompensated care against affiliated doctors' pharma money. This adds the IRS EO BMF EIN leg and asks about the exemption, not the pharma.

hunches.title: Health-center dollars per patient
hunches.hunch: Health Center Program grantees can be ranked on federal dollars per patient because the UDS grant number and the USASpending FAIN are the same key once the activity code is dropped.
hunches.join_keys: left(GRANTNUMBER,3)||right(GRANTNUMBER,5) = "award_id_fain" (H80CS00803 -> H8000803): 1,359 of 1,359 UDS grants match, 1,356 distinct UEIs (100%). UDS INFO.GRANTNUMBER = TABLE3A.GRANTNUMBER (1,356 of 1,357 rows, the odd row is an embedded header). left(HEALTHCENTERZIPCODE,5) = DIM_ZIP_POINT.ZCTA5 -> county -> HPSA Single County flag.
hunches.query_sql: with u as (select GRANTNUMBER, HEALTHCENTERNAME nm, HEALTHCENTERSTATE st, left(GRANTNUMBER,3)||right(GRANTNUMBER,5) fain from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HRSA_UDS_HEALTH_CENTER_INFO where GRANTNUMBER<>''), p as (select GRANTNUMBER, try_to_number(T3A_L39_CA,18,0) m, try_to_number(T3A_L39_CB,18,0) f from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HRSA_UDS_TABLE3A_PATIENTS where GRANTNUMBER<>''), a as (select "award_id_fain" fain, sum(try_to_number("federal_action_obligation",18,2)) obl from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FULL where "cfda_number" in ('93.224','93.527') and "action_date_fiscal_year" in ('2024','2025') group by 1), j as (select u.nm, p.m+p.f patients, a.obl, a.obl/nullif(p.m+p.f,0) dpp from u join p on p.GRANTNUMBER=u.GRANTNUMBER left join a on a.fain=u.fain) select count(*), count(obl), sum(obl), sum(patients), median(dpp), percentile_cont(0.9) within group (order by dpp), max(dpp) from j
hunches.distinct_entities: 1,356 distinct grantees, all with FY2024-25 obligations; 32,746,392 patients (2025 UDS)
hunches.first_number: Median $37 of FY2024-25 Health Center Program obligations (93.224 + 93.527, $1.57B total) per 2025 UDS patient; p90 $220; max $1,349 at Montana Migrant Council (1,714 patients, $2.3M)
hunches.hit_means: The tail is small special-population grantees (migrant, homeless, tribal); high dollars per patient here is program design, not a fraud signal; the real hit is a clean ID bridge from HRSA operations data to USASpending money.
hunches.miss_means: If FAINs had not matched, health-center money and patients could only be joined by name.
hunches.tier_reason: USASpending is dated but UDS is a single reporting year (2025), so dollars per patient is a cross-section.
hunches.time_axis: assistance action_date 2006-2026 (93.224 from 2006-10, 93.527 from 2011-11); UDS REPORTINGYEAR 2025 only
traps: FED_HRSA_UDS_TABLE3A_PATIENTS carries a header row inside the data: BHCMISID='' with the column labels as values ('Total Patients (Sum of Lines 1-38)-Male Patients (a)'); '--' marks suppressed cells
USASpending award_id_fain for HRSA drops the activity code: UDS H80CS00803 is FAIN H8000803; a raw equality join matches 0
FED_HRSA_UDS_HEALTH_CENTER_INFO is REPORTINGYEAR 2025 only, 1,356 rows; no series
hunches.overlap_check: Hunches 7 and 25 use UDS sites and FQHC enrollments for the doctor bridge and terminations. Neither joins UDS to USASpending; the FAIN transform is new.

hunches.title: Post-disaster provider startups
hunches.hunch: New home health agencies and hospices incorporate in a county at a higher rate in the 24 months after a major FEMA individual-assistance declaration than the national trend predicts.
hunches.join_keys: FEMA FIPS (5-digit county) per (DISASTERNUMBER, FIPS) with >= 1,000 registrations, 2017-2023, INCIDENTTYPECODE <> 'B' (626 pairs) = DIM_ZIP_POINT.PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS <- left(enrollment ZIP_CODE,5) (HHA 11,508 rows, 9,211 with INCORPORATION_DATE; hospice 6,066/4,818); INCORPORATION_DATE in [decl, decl+24m) vs [decl-24m, decl), divided by the national ratio for the same calendar windows.
hunches.query_sql: with fema(FIPS, DISASTERNUMBER, decl, regs, itype) as (select * from values ... 626 rows from the p2 receipt ...), enr as (select 'HHA' typ, e.ENROLLMENT_ID, try_to_date(e.INCORPORATION_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') inc, d.PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS fips from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HOME_HEALTH_AGENCY_ENROLLMENTS e join LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_ZIP_POINT d on d.ZCTA5=left(e.ZIP_CODE,5) union all select 'HOSPICE', ... union all select 'SNF', ...), nat as (select typ, inc, count(*) n from enr where inc is not null group by 1,2), per as (select f.FIPS, f.DISASTERNUMBER, e.typ, count(distinct case when e.inc >= f.decl and e.inc < dateadd(month,24,f.decl) then e.ENROLLMENT_ID end) after24, count(distinct case when e.inc < f.decl and e.inc >= dateadd(month,-24,f.decl) then e.ENROLLMENT_ID end) before24 from fema f join enr e on e.fips=f.FIPS and e.inc is not null group by 1,2,3), natw as (select f.FIPS, f.DISASTERNUMBER, n.typ, sum(case when n.inc >= f.decl and n.inc < dateadd(month,24,f.decl) then n.n else 0 end) nat_after, sum(case when n.inc < f.decl and n.inc >= dateadd(month,-24,f.decl) then n.n else 0 end) nat_before from fema f cross join nat n group by 1,2,3) select p.typ, count(*), sum(p.before24), sum(p.after24), sum(p.after24)/sum(p.before24) local_ratio, sum(w.nat_after)/sum(w.nat_before) national_ratio from per p join natw w using (FIPS, DISASTERNUMBER, typ) group by 1
hunches.distinct_entities: 365 disaster-county pairs with HHA activity in 260 distinct counties (334 pairs / 237 counties hospice; 384 / 289 SNF); 663 HHA incorporations before vs 665 after
hunches.first_number: HHA difference-in-differences ratio 1.28 across 365 non-COVID disaster-county pairs 2017-2023 (local 1.003 vs national 0.783) — but Los Angeles County (Oct 2020 fire declaration, 366 -> 464 HHAs) carries it: without LA the ratio is 0.87; hospice 0.94 with LA, 1.50 without; hurricanes only HHA 0.90, hospice 1.34; SNF 0.79
hunches.hit_means: A consistent ratio above 1 would say operators incorporate into disaster counties to catch displaced elderly and FEMA-adjacent demand.
hunches.miss_means: The ratio flips sign depending on one county and one disaster type, so there is no consistent post-disaster startup effect in the enrollment file; LA County's 2020-21 HHA boom is its own story.
hunches.tier_reason: Declaration date and incorporation date are both dated; the before/after was run and returned an inconsistent effect.
hunches.time_axis: FEMA DECLARATIONDATE 2010-2025 in the file, filtered 2017-2023; INCORPORATION_DATE 1900s-2024 (MM/DD/YYYY), national counts 2013-2024 used as control
traps: 143 of 769 large disaster-county pairs 2017-2023 are INCIDENTTYPECODE 'B' (COVID, March-April 2020 declarations in every county) and they swamp any before/after with the national 2020-21 HHA/hospice incorporation boom (HHA 332 in 2018 -> 601 in 2021)
FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS.FIPS is null on Puerto Rico rows (DR-4671: 1,165,086 registrations, no county); DECLARATIONDATE is ISO timestamp text '2010-08-11T00:00:00.000Z'
Enrollment ZIP_CODE is 9 digits with no hyphen ('067704111'); INCORPORATION_DATE is MM/DD/YYYY and blank on 20% of HHAs and hospices
The enrollment file holds only currently-enrolled providers, so older incorporations are under-counted (survivorship); the national same-window ratio is the only control for that
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 5 joins FEMA IA to HMDA by tract; hunch 30 uses INCORPORATION_DATE against penalties. FEMA declarations against enrollment incorporation dates is a new pair.

hunches.title: HPSA designation pulls no clinics
hunches.hunch: Counties newly designated as whole-county primary-care HPSAs gain health-center sites and FQHC incorporations in the following 36 months at a higher rate than before designation.
hunches.join_keys: HPSA COMMON_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE (HPSA_COMPONENT_TYPE_DESCRIPTION 'Single County', geographic designation, min HPSA_DESIGNATION_DATE per county) = UDS sites STATE_AND_COUNTY_FEDERAL_INFORMATION_PROCESSING_STANDARD_CODE (19,038 sites, all dated, 2,301 counties); SITE_ADDED_TO_SCOPE_THIS_DATE within +/-36 months, national same-window control. FQHC orgs: 1,388 ASSOCIATE_IDs with a date, 332 in a whole-county HPSA via DIM_ZIP_POINT.
hunches.query_sql: with hp as (select COMMON_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE fips, min(try_to_date(HPSA_DESIGNATION_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY')) first_desig from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HRSA_HPSA_PRIMARY_CARE where HPSA_COMPONENT_TYPE_DESCRIPTION='Single County' and DESIGNATION_TYPE ilike '%Geographic%' group by 1), s as (select STATE_AND_COUNTY_FEDERAL_INFORMATION_PROCESSING_STANDARD_CODE fips, try_to_date(SITE_ADDED_TO_SCOPE_THIS_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') added from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_HRSA_UDS_SERVICE_DELIVERY_SITES), nat as (select added, count(*) n from s where added is not null group by 1), per as (select hp.fips, hp.first_desig, sum(case when s.added >= hp.first_desig and s.added < dateadd(month,36,hp.first_desig) then 1 else 0 end) after36, sum(case when s.added < hp.first_desig and s.added >= dateadd(month,-36,hp.first_desig) then 1 else 0 end) before36 from hp join s on s.fips=hp.fips where hp.first_desig >= '2005-01-01' group by 1,2), natw as (select hp.fips, sum(case when n.added >= hp.first_desig and n.added < dateadd(month,36,hp.first_desig) then n.n else 0 end) nat_after, sum(case when n.added < hp.first_desig and n.added >= dateadd(month,-36,hp.first_desig) then n.n else 0 end) nat_before from hp cross join nat n where hp.first_desig >= '2005-01-01' group by 1) select count(*), sum(p.before36), sum(p.after36), (sum(p.after36)/sum(p.before36))/(sum(w.nat_after)/sum(w.nat_before)) did from per p join natw w on w.fips=p.fips
hunches.distinct_entities: 374 distinct counties designated 2005 or later; 178 sites added in the 36 months before vs 163 after; 95 counties gained any site after; FQHC orgs 20 incorporated within 36 months after vs 21 before
hunches.first_number: Difference-in-differences ratio 0.90 (local 0.916 vs national 1.014) for health-center sites added after a county's first whole-county HPSA designation, 374 counties, 2005-2026; FQHC incorporations 20 after vs 21 before
hunches.hit_means: A ratio above 1 would show designation working as a magnet (or grant-chasing).
hunches.miss_means: It does not; the designation follows shortage, and sites do not follow the designation. Kill this direction unless the tract-level HPSA components are used.
hunches.tier_reason: Designation date and site-added date are both dated; tested, null result.
hunches.time_axis: HPSA_DESIGNATION_DATE 1978-2026 (waves 1978, 2012, 2017, 2022, 2025); SITE_ADDED_TO_SCOPE_THIS_DATE 1966-2026; FQHC INCORPORATION_DATE
traps: FED_HRSA_HPSA_PRIMARY_CARE is 79,158 rows for 17,697 HPSA_IDs (one row per geographic component: Census Tract 47,840, County Subdivision 18,050, Single County 5,394); count rows and you count tracts
HPSA_DESIGNATION_DATE is MM/DD/YYYY text; max() on the string reads '12/31/2020' while the real latest designation is 2026-03-26
Whole-county designations are 5,394 of 79,158 component rows; most HPSAs are tract or subdivision level and do not map to a county FIPS cleanly
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 8 uses HPSA designation dates as an outcome after jail growth; hunch 25 counts FQHC terminations. Designation date as a cause of new sites is new.

hunches.title: VA pays one-star nursing homes
hunches.hunch: Nursing homes that register in SAM and hold VA community-care contracts are rated no better than the rest, and one-star homes with abuse icons are among them.
hunches.join_keys: normalized PROVIDER_NAME + upper(CITY_TOWN) + STATE = normalized LEGAL_BUSINESS_NAME + upper(PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_CITY) + PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_STATE, SAM PRIMARY_NAICS 623xxx, exact normalized name, length >= 8: 633 of 14,713 homes (4.3%; for-profit 4.5%, nonprofit 3.9%, government 2.9%) -> UEI_SAM = R2 "RECIPIENT_UEI" with AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME like Veterans: 242 of 633 have VA contracts.
hunches.query_sql: with s as (select UEI_SAM uei, upper(PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_CITY) city, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_STATE st, trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(LEGAL_BUSINESS_NAME),'[^A-Z0-9 ]',''),'\\b(INC|LLC|THE|OF|AND|CORP|CORPORATION|CO|LTD|LP|DBA)\\b',''),' +',' ')) nn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_SAM_ENTITY_PUBLIC where PRIMARY_NAICS like '623%'), n as (select CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN ccn, PROVIDER_NAME, upper(CITY_TOWN) city, STATE st, OWNERSHIP_TYPE, try_to_number(TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_FINES_IN_DOLLARS,18,2) fines, try_to_number(OVERALL_RATING,18,2) stars, ABUSE_ICON, SPECIAL_FOCUS_STATUS, trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(upper(PROVIDER_NAME),'[^A-Z0-9 ]',''),'\\b(INC|LLC|THE|OF|AND|CORP|CORPORATION|CO|LTD|LP|DBA)\\b',''),' +',' ')) nn from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_NURSINGHOME411) select s.uei, n.ccn, n.PROVIDER_NAME, n.stars, n.fines, n.ABUSE_ICON, n.SPECIAL_FOCUS_STATUS from s join n on s.st=n.st and s.city=n.city and s.nn=n.nn and length(s.nn)>=8  -- then joined in Python to the r2_combined_pull rows where AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME contains 'Veterans'
hunches.distinct_entities: 633 distinct nursing homes matched to a SAM UEI; 242 distinct homes with VA contracts (4,320 contracts, $960.0M net obligations since 2010)
hunches.first_number: 44 one-star nursing homes (18.2% of 242) hold VA contracts worth part of $960M since 2010; average rating 2.88 stars with VA money vs 2.89 without; Chicago Ridge SNF (1 star, abuse icon, SFF candidate, $588k in CMS fines) holds 4 VA contracts, $346k; Village Place FL (1 star, abuse icon) $2.1M
hunches.hit_means: The VA is buying beds without regard to CMS ratings; the named 1-star, abuse-flagged homes are checkable one by one.
hunches.miss_means: A rating gap in either direction is absent (2.88 vs 2.89), so the VA is neither selecting quality nor selecting junk; the story is the individual homes.
hunches.tier_reason: Contracts are dated but ratings, fines and the SAM match are one snapshot; the SAM name match covers 4.3% of homes, so this is a registered-subset cross-section.
hunches.time_axis: R2 ACTION_DATE 2010-2026; NH411 PROCESSING_DATE snapshot; SAM INITIAL_REGISTRATION_DATE 2000-2026 unused
traps: USASpending 93.498 (Provider Relief Fund) is 2,662 rows, 1 distinct UEI, 1 award, net -$7.96B: an aggregate transfer, not recipient-level; seed 6 (PRF to nursing-home chains) is dead on it
Only 3 of the 633 SAM-registered nursing homes have any HHS assistance ($1.06M); nursing homes do not appear in the assistance file, their federal money is Medicare/Medicaid claims
Exact normalized name+city+state matched 633 homes; loosening to prefix on this table would let 'X HEALTH CARE' variants collide
hunches.seed_source: seed 6 (rescued from PRF to VA contracts)
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 2 ranks chains by fines; hunch 20 pairs nursing homes with dialysis. Neither reaches SAM or USASpending contracts; the VA-contract leg is new.

hunches.title: Nursing-home chains and PRF money
hunches.hunch: Provider Relief Fund recipients in USASpending (93.498) can be name-matched to nursing-home chains and compared on fines (seed 6 as written).
hunches.join_keys: "cfda_number" = '93.498' returns 2,662 rows, 1 distinct "recipient_uei", 1 distinct "assistance_award_unique_key", sum federal_action_obligation -$7,962,159,138; no recipient list exists to match.
hunches.query_sql: select "cfda_number", max("cfda_title"), count(*) n, count(distinct "recipient_uei") d_uei, count(distinct "assistance_award_unique_key") d_awards, min("action_date"), max("action_date"), sum(try_to_number("federal_action_obligation",18,2)) obl from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FULL where "cfda_number" in ('93.498','93.224','93.527','93.129','93.155','93.912','93.301') group by 1 order by 3 desc
hunches.distinct_entities: 1 distinct UEI and 1 distinct award under 93.498; 0 nursing homes matchable
hunches.first_number: 1 recipient UEI carries the entire Provider Relief Fund in USASpending (2,662 action rows, 2020-05 to 2026-01, net -$7.96B)
hunches.hit_means: Would have let PRF dollars per bed be set against fines and deficiencies by chain.
hunches.miss_means: USASpending records PRF as one block transfer; the recipient-level PRF file (HRSA, by provider name/state/TIN) is not landed. Nearest live version: SAM-registered nursing homes with VA contracts (above), 242 homes, $960M.
hunches.tier_reason: Missing leg: HRSA Provider Relief Fund recipient-level payments (provider name, state, payment amount, distribution). Not in the warehouse.
hunches.time_axis: 93.498 action_date 2020-05-18 to 2026-01-06 on one award; no recipient dates
traps: A CFDA with thousands of rows can still be one award; count distinct assistance_award_unique_key and recipient_uei before joining on it
hunches.overlap_check: Hunch 2 (chain fines) is the fines leg; this was to add the money leg and cannot.

hunches.title: Pharma dollars per county head
hunches.hunch: Counties where drug and device makers pay the most per resident have higher Part D opioid claim shares and higher drug-poisoning death rates.
hunches.join_keys: left(RECIPIENT_ZIP_CODE,5) = DIM_ZIP_POINT.ZCTA5 (21,485 distinct recipient ZIPs; teaching hospitals, royalties and ownership excluded) -> PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS; PRSCRBR_ZIP5 = ZCTA5 (20,587 ZIPs, 1,416,883 prescribers) -> county; CDC FIPS YEAR 2015; DIM_COUNTY.POPULATION_2020 >= 20,000. 1,781 counties carry all legs.
hunches.query_sql: with op as (select d.PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS fips, sum(try_to_number(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS,18,2)) op_dollars from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 o join LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_ZIP_POINT d on d.ZCTA5=left(o.RECIPIENT_ZIP_CODE,5) where o.COVERED_RECIPIENT_TYPE not ilike '%teaching hospital%' and o.NATURE_OF_PAYMENT_OR_TRANSFER_OF_VALUE not ilike '%royalty%' and o.NATURE_OF_PAYMENT_OR_TRANSFER_OF_VALUE not ilike '%ownership%' group by 1), pd as (select d.PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS fips, sum(try_to_number(p.OPIOID_TOT_CLMS,18,0)) op_clms, sum(try_to_number(p.TOT_CLMS,18,0)) tot_clms from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS p join LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_ZIP_POINT d on d.ZCTA5=left(p.PRSCRBR_ZIP5,5) group by 1), cdc as (select FIPS, try_to_number(regexp_substr(ESTIMATED_AGE_ADJUSTED_DEATH_RATE_11_CATEGORIES_IN_RANGES,'^[0-9.]+'),18,2) rate_lo from LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY where YEAR='2015'), c as (select COUNTY_FIPS fips, POPULATION_2020 pop from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_COUNTY where POPULATION_2020 >= 20000), j as (select c.fips, op.op_dollars*1000/c.pop op_per_1k, pd.op_clms/nullif(pd.tot_clms,0) opioid_rate, cdc.rate_lo poison_2015 from c join op on op.fips=c.fips join pd on pd.fips=c.fips left join cdc on cdc.FIPS=c.fips) select count(*), corr(ln(op_per_1k), opioid_rate), corr(ln(op_per_1k), poison_2015), corr(opioid_rate, poison_2015) from j
hunches.distinct_entities: 1,781 distinct counties with population >= 20,000 carrying Open Payments, Part D and population; 14,700,786 payment rows aggregated, $3.31B total of which $0.80B to teaching hospitals was excluded
hunches.first_number: r = 0.07 between log pharma dollars per resident (2023) and county opioid claim share; quartile medians run $119 -> $603 -> $1,901 -> $5,500 per 1,000 residents while opioid share runs 2.97% -> 3.20% -> 3.46% -> 3.79% and 2015 poisoning rate 12.1 -> 13.1 -> 12.1 -> 14.1 per 100k
hunches.hit_means: A strong gradient would tie industry spending geography to prescribing and deaths.
hunches.miss_means: The gradient is visible in quartiles but explains under 1% of variance; pharma dollars track where doctors are, not where opioids are; the 8-year vintage gap (OP 2023, CDC 2015) makes the poisoning leg decorative.
hunches.tier_reason: Open Payments 2023 is one program year, the Part D prescriber file carries no year, CDC county poisoning ends 2015; three single vintages 8 years apart.
hunches.time_axis: OP PROGRAM_YEAR 2023; Part D prescriber table undated (hunch matrix labels it DY2024); CDC YEAR 1999-2015, used 2015

hunches.hunch: HUD-assisted housing in counties hit by two or more major FEMA declarations 2017-2023 shows lower occupancy and longer waiting lists than housing in untouched counties.

verdicts.title: Administrator churn, harm rising
verdicts.rerun_number: 0.538 -> 0.825 G-or-worse citations per home, +53.3% (reproduced exactly, all 13 figures). But on the coverage-clean 2024->2025 window it is 0.792 -> 0.825, +4.2%, while zero-churn homes fell 0.411 -> 0.334, -18.7%.
verdicts.reason: Chain, join and entity counts are sound and every claimed number reproduces exactly from my own independently written SQL: directory 14,700 rows / 14,700 distinct 6-char CCN so no fan-out, deficiencies 418,479 rows / 14,632 distinct CCN and all 14,632 land in the directory, groups 7,901 / 3,561 / 1,499 / 1,739. matched_rows 14700 really is the entity count. What breaks the headline is the baseline year. FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_DEFICIENCIES is a rolling ~3-year window off PROCESSING_DATE 2026-06-01 and it cliffs at 2023-06: Jan-May 2023 runs 541, 597, 758, 633, 669 homes per month against 1,748-2,420 every month from June 2023 on. Full-year 2023 covers 10,787 homes, full-year 2025 covers 11,939, and the missing five months sit entirely on the 2023 side. Re-run on windows that do not straddle the cliff and the direction flips: per cited home 2023->2025 gives +38.8% vs +3.8%; Jun-Dec 2023->2025 gives -3.8% vs -28.5%; Jun-Sep 2023->2025 gives +8.8% vs -26.6%; full 2024->2025 gives +4.2% vs -18.7%. The 2023->2024 leg moves both groups together (roughly +47 vs +40, the post-COVID survey catch-up wave), so all the divergence lives in the 2024->2025 leg where coverage is comparable. The relative gap is real and survives every cut at 20-39 points, but "harm rising" is an artifact of a truncated baseline; the honest statement is that harm fell at stable homes and did not fall at churn homes. The stated mechanism is also wrong: measured coverage growth by group is 10.0% / 12.6% / 10.4% / 10.1%, near-identical, so coverage growth cannot produce a 14-vs-53 gap. Confounds cleared: beds are flat across groups (107.7 / 112.3 / 110.2) and per-1,000-beds shows the same pattern; SURVEY_TYPE is 'Health' on all 418,479 rows; try_to_number(x,18,6) on the admin column returns the same integers 0-8 the agent's (18,0) cast did, so no rounding trap fired. Severity: real, not blocker.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 is correct and I could not upgrade or downgrade it. The predictor leg is one undated snapshot: FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.PROCESSING_DATE is '2026-05-01' on all 14,700 rows and the administrator-departure column carries no window start or end anywhere in the file. I LIKE-searched all_landing_tables.txt and marts.json for PBJ, PAYROLL, STAFFING, TURNOVER and ADMINISTRATOR: zero hits in landing and zero in the 1,102 marts, so the dated Payroll-Based Journal staffing file that would make this Tier 1 is genuinely not landed under another name. The only nursing-home tables present are FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME (14,700), _DEFICIENCIES (418,479), _FIRE_DEFICIENCIES (200,030), _PENALTIES (16,180) and FED_NURSINGHOME411 (14,713). The outcome leg is dated and that is what keeps it off Tier 3, but its 2023 slice is truncated, so the trend is weaker than a normal Tier 2 outcome leg.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun only moved denominators and date windows inside the same two tables, so three things are invisible to it by construction. First, I never tested whether SCOPE_SEVERITY_CODE G-L means the same thing in 2023 and 2025 — a CMS severity re-tagging or enforcement-policy shift would look identical to what I measured, and nothing in the warehouse dates the coding rules. Second, the direction of cause is untestable, not just untested: the administrator-departure measure has no start or end date in the file, so I cannot tell whether the churn window sits before, during or after the 2025 harm it is being paired with, and no landed table supplies that window. Third, survivor bias survives every cut I made: the directory is a 2026-05-01 snapshot, so homes that closed between 2023 and 2025 are absent from both my numbers and the agent's, and if churn homes close at a higher rate the surviving churn cohort is the mild end of the distribution. I also did not test whether the 445-rose / 248-fell split is significant against a null of noise; a home whose G+ count moves 0 to 1 counts the same as 3 to 8.
new_traps: FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_DEFICIENCIES is a rolling ~3-year window that CLIFFS at 2023-06, matching PROCESSING_DATE 2026-06-01. Homes surveyed per month: Jan-May 2023 = 541, 597, 758, 633, 669; Jun 2023 onward = 1,748 to 2,420 every month. Full-year 2023 holds 86,418 rows / 10,787 homes against 2025's 107,508 / 11,939, and the whole shortfall is the pre-June-2023 roll-off residue. Any 2023-vs-later trend on this table reads a truncation as a rise. Use 2024 and 2025 as the two comparable full years, or divide by homes actually cited that year.

October 2025 is a hole in the same table: 2,432 rows / 823 homes against 1,748-2,420 homes in every neighbouring month; November 2025 at 5,504 / 1,718 is also low. Any 2025 total off this table is a floor, and any Jun-Dec 2025 window is depressed by roughly 8%.

FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.NUMBER_OF_ADMINISTRATORS_WHO_HAVE_LEFT_THE_NURSING_HOME: the 1,739 blank rows are empty strings, not NULL, AND every one of them is suppression-coded — ADMINISTRATOR_TURNOVER_FOOTNOTE = '26' on 1,455 and '27' on 284, and is null on all 12,961 filled rows. The blanks are not missing at random: those homes average 88.0 certified beds against 107.7 to 112.3 in the three filled groups. Never fold the blank bucket into a comparison group; read the footnote first.

Coverage growth is not a free explanation for a rise on this table. Homes cited grew 10.0% / 12.6% / 10.4% / 10.1% across the four administrator-departure groups — near-identical — so a 14%-vs-53% gap between groups cannot be coverage. Measure coverage growth per group before attributing any floor to it.

FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_DEFICIENCIES.SURVEY_TYPE is the constant 'Health' on all 418,479 rows. It is not a filter. The real split is the STANDARD_DEFICIENCY / COMPLAINT_DEFICIENCY 'Y' flags, and the complaint share jumped from 30.9% of 2023 rows to 39.4% of 2025 rows, which shifts the severity mix on its own.

verdicts.title: REH conversions after the loss
verdicts.rerun_number: 28 of 35 (80.0%) REH predecessors negative, median -12.25% of cost — reproduced exactly; the honest apples-to-apples cut is 21 of 25 (84.0%) and -9.62% on full-year reports only
verdicts.reason: The chain holds and the headline reproduces to the digit. I rebuilt the join independently: REH_CONVERSION_FLAG='Y' gives 48 rows / 48 distinct CCNs / 45 dated; split_part on '|' matches 35 predecessor CCNs in HCRIS (raw value 21, confirming that trap); 28 negative = 80.0%; median -12.25%; 17 CAH / 18 STH; 34 of 35 converted after FY end. I also swapped the tie-break from longest fiscal period to latest fiscal year end — identical numbers. The 3 REHs with a null CAH_OR_HOSPITAL_CCN do not leak into the 35 via the coalesce. Four things are wrong. (1) The comparison is asymmetric: the national benchmark filtered to 350-380 day reports with TOTAL_COSTS>0, the REH side had no filter, and 10 of the 35 REH reports are short periods (4 under 200 days, average 91). Same filter both sides: REH 21 of 25 negative (84.0%), median -9.62%; national full-year 5,714 reports, 34.5% negative, median +5.11%. Add the revenue-filled filter and it is REH 20 of 24 (83.3%), -9.51% of cost, -10.36% of revenue, versus national 5,565, 32.7%, +5.60%. The direction and the size of the gap survive every filter, so the finding is real; -12.25% is just its loosest version. (2) The memorable exemplar is a data artifact. EAMC-Lanier (CCN 010175) has NET_PATIENT_REVENUE and TOTAL_PATIENT_REVENUE = 'nan' and NET_INCOME = -30,412,933 = LESS_TOTAL_OPERATING_EXPENSE exactly; the -138% of cost is the ratio of operating expense to total cost, not a loss. 233 of 6,040 latest HCRIS reports carry blank revenue, 152 with NET_INCOME = -opex, median -112.56% of cost. EAMC is the only one of the 35, so the aggregate holds (27 of 34 clean = 79.4%), but the sentence's headline example must go. Sturgis -55% is clean and survives. (3) The trap 'the new CCN has no cost report, so all history sits under the predecessor CCN' is refuted: 14 of 48 new REH CCNs have a cost report and all 14 are post-conversion; 8 REHs have both a before and an after. Nine of those 14 after-reports show positive margins (+85.3%, +77.0%, +50.7%, +41.5%, +27.5%). The 'watch what happens after' that the hunch files under hit_means is already landed. (4) 'only 8 of 48 appear in Care Compare' measured the predecessor CCN, not the REH CCN: 41 of 48 new REH CCNs sit in FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL, all typed 'Rural Emergency Hospital'. Same unsplit-key error in the POS leg — 43 of 48 predecessors in POS category 01, 40 terminated, not 30 and 25. Not an overlap, not a fabricated join, so not REFUTED; numbers and traps wrong, so CORRECTED.

verdicts.title: E-tags ignore the storms — right conclusion, wrong number, and a FIPS bug that drops seven states
verdicts.rerun_number: 571 E-tag home-event pairs in the 12 months before / 516 after — reproduced exactly with my own SQL. Corrected build: 615 / 591 once STATE_FIPS is zero-padded, and 420 before / 562 after on the symmetric window (direction reverses).
verdicts.reason:
REPRODUCED EXACTLY. My own SQL (left join + max, no correlated exists) returns 4,957 pairs, 3,428 homes, 278 counties, 571 before, 516 after. Cook County 2023-07-02: 76 before, 78 after. Cross-section 43.5% (1,490/3,428) vs 44.4% (4,983/11,235). 6,810 homes with any E-tag. Every published figure matches. The arithmetic is clean.

JOIN KEYS ARE REAL. NURSING_HOME 14,700 rows / 14,700 distinct CCN, no fan-out. FIRE_DEFICIENCIES E-prefix 22,260 rows / 6,810 distinct CCN, 0 unparseable dates, 100% of CCNs present in the directory. Storm big events 447 rows / 447 distinct EVENT_ID, no dupes. The SSA-to-FIPS crosswalk (3,150 pairs, 0 conflicts either direction) I validated independently against XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY: 14,057 of 14,663 mapped homes match the census county NAME exactly; the 407 mismatches are spellings (DU PAGE vs DuPage, MC LENNAN vs McLennan) and the 199 not-in-census are Connecticut. The crosswalk is genuine. DAMAGE_PROPERTY suffixes 2018-2025: K 421,299, blank 116,606, M 2,824, '0' 119, B 26 — no lowercase, the case expression covers them. try_to_number was (18,4), not the banned bare form; rerun at (18,6) gives the same 447 events.

BLOCKER 1 — STATE_FIPS IS NOT ZERO-PADDED. The chain builds county FIPS as STATE_FIPS||lpad(CZ_FIPS,3,'0'). 67,856 of 540,874 storm rows 2018-2025 carry a 1-char STATE_FIPS: CA '6' (19,332), CO '8' (14,606), AL '1' (11,414), AR '5' (10,300), AZ '4' (8,081), AK '2' (2,082), CT '9' (2,041). Those produce a 4-char key that can never match the 5-char home FIPS. 36 of the 447 big county events (8.1%), 16 of them California, are silently dropped. Padded: pairs 4,957 -> 5,434, homes 3,428 -> 3,875, counties 278 -> 302, before 571 -> 615, after 516 -> 591.

BLOCKER 2 — THE HEADLINE DIRECTION IS RIGHT-CENSORING. E-tag SURVEY_DATE ends 2026-05-21; storm days run to 2025-12. A late-2025 storm gets a full before-window inside the data and a truncated after-window. Restrict to storm days whose BOTH 12-month windows sit inside the E-tag range (2019-01-04 to 2025-05-21): 420 before, 562 after. The sign flips — 34% MORE after than before. The published 571 > 516 is an artifact of the window, not a measurement.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION. The agent's own run, at entity level, says the opposite of its headline: 380 distinct homes tagged before vs 435 after. Pairs say "fewer after," homes say "14% more after," from the same query.

THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES — but the test that saves it was never run. Placebo: the same 178 storm days applied to homes in never-hit counties, symmetric window, 1,920,264 pairs — 7.56% before, 9.99% after, lift +32.2%. Hit homes, same window: 9.38% before, 12.55% after, lift +33.8%. Difference-in-differences: 1.6 percentage points. So the entire after-lift is the deficiency file's growth trend, and storms add nothing. "E-tags ignore the storms" is true. 571-vs-516 is not what shows it.

CROSS-SECTION FLIPS TOO. Padded: hit 45.7% (1,771/3,875) vs never-hit 43.6% (4,702/10,788). The claim reports hit 43.5% BELOW never-hit 44.4%. Restore the seven states and the sign reverses. 2.1 points either way is noise, but the published sentence asserts a direction it cannot hold.

SEVERITY. Blocker: the FIPS pad (silent wrong answer, 8% of events). Blocker: the censored window (reverses the headline). Real: the rolling-window trap below. Real: survivorship — FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME is one snapshot of currently-active homes (0 E-tag CCNs missing from it), so a home that closed after a storm is invisible by construction; the strongest possible storm outcome cannot appear.

SMALLEST FIX. lpad(STATE_FIPS,2,'0'), cut storm days to 2019-01-04..2025-05-21, and publish the placebo lift beside the hit lift.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 holds. Both measured legs carry day-level dates — storm events by BEGIN_YEARMONTH+BEGIN_DAY 2018-2025, E-tag by SURVEY_DATE 2018-01-04 to 2026-05-21 — and the chain runs end to end with a real first number. The nursing-home directory is a snapshot but it serves as the spine (county assignment), not as a measured leg, so it does not force tier 2. The stated tier_reason is wrong, though: "the first number is found and it kills the claim as written" is false. The first number does not kill the claim; it reverses sign under the FIPS fix plus a symmetric window. Only the placebo (which the agent did not run) establishes the null.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun uses the same SSA-to-FIPS crosswalk and the same county-level exposure definition, so I cannot see whether a $10M county storm actually touched the block a given home sits on — county exposure is a proxy and I never tested it. I also cannot see closed homes: the directory is current-only, so any home that shut after a storm is absent from both arms of my placebo as well. And the placebo draws both arms from the same deficiency file, so a nationwide change in survey reporting cancels out of the difference-in-differences and stays invisible to me. Finally I only tested the $10M threshold and the 365-day window the agent chose; a different threshold or a 90-day window could read differently and I did not sweep them.
new_traps: ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_STORM_EVENTS.STATE_FIPS is NOT zero-padded: 67,856 of 540,874 rows 2018-2025 hold a 1-char value (CA '6' 19,332; CO '8' 14,606; AL '1' 11,414; AR '5' 10,300; AZ '4' 8,081; AK '2' 2,082; CT '9' 2,041). CZ_FIPS is 1-3 chars too. Build county FIPS as lpad(STATE_FIPS,2,'0')||lpad(CZ_FIPS,3,'0') or seven states drop out of every FIPS join with no error. Measured cost on one join: 36 of 447 big county events and 447 home-storm pairs lost.

FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_FIRE_DEFICIENCIES is a rolling ~3-survey-cycle window, not a history. Homes with any fire survey recorded, out of 14,700: 3.2% in 2018, 13.1% 2019, 4.6% 2020, 12.1% 2021, 26.2% 2022, 52.1% 2023, 63.5% 2024, 54.1% 2025. Median per-home span 833 days, median 3 surveys; 9,860 of 13,914 homes first appear in 2022 or later. For any event before 2022, 'no deficiency before' means 'no survey record kept', not 'no citation'.

The same file ends 2026-05-21 while the storm mart runs to 2025-12: a 12-month after-window is right-censored for every event after 2025-05-21 while the before-window stays whole. That asymmetry alone reversed the sign of an E-tag before/after comparison — 571 before vs 516 after became 420 before vs 562 after once both windows were forced inside the data range. Always clip event dates to [file_min+window, file_max-window] before any before/after count.

FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.COUNTY_PARISH in Connecticut holds council-of-government names, not counties: 'CAPITOL' (51 homes), 'SOUTH CENTRAL CT' (23), 'WESTERN CT' (20), 'GREATER BRIDGEPORT' (15). The POS_OTHER crosswalk maps them onto the retired county FIPS 09001/09003/09009, which are absent from XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY (199 homes total unmatched). CT county geography does not line up between CMS and the 2023+ census file.

verdicts.corrected_claim: E-tags ignore the storms: across 5,434 home-by-storm-day pairs (3,875 homes, 302 counties, $10M-plus county storm events 2018-2025, STATE_FIPS zero-padded), E-tags run 615 pairs in the 12 months before and 591 after — but that gap is right-censoring, not a finding. verdicts.title: Top-paid hospitals, low stars
verdicts.rerun_number: 81 hospitals, $5.8881B — reproduced exactly. But 32.0% / 26.3% / 22.2% at 1-2 stars on the common rated cohort, not the claimed 26.6% / 19.3% / 12.2%; corr(pay-per-discharge, star) = -0.0111 on 2,660 rated hospitals.
verdicts.reason: The count and the money reproduce to the dollar: 81 hospitals, 81 distinct CCNs, $5.8881B, 32 negative and 49 positive net income (stable under two different HCRIS dedup rules; all 81 carry exactly one HCRIS row, so the dedup does not matter for them). The join legs are clean — CCN is a real key on every side, 3,044/3,044 distinct in the inpatient file, 5,432/5,432 in HOSPITAL_GENERAL, 6,103 rows over 6,040 CCNs in HCRIS with 62 dup groups that the row_number handles. No fan-out. Three things are wrong. FIRST, the fiscal year label: the claim says "negative FY2023 net income" but 48 of the 81 sit on cost reports ending in FY2024 and only 33 end in FY2023. Warehouse-wide, FED_CMS_HCRIS is 3,534 FY2023, 2,564 FY2024, 5 FY2022 — the repo's own hunch matrix calls it "HCRIS FY2023" in four places and that is wrong on 42% of rows. SECOND, every percentage in the claim divides by all rows in the decile, counting hospitals with no star rating as "not low-star." HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING is 'Not Available' on 2,250 of 5,432, and the rated share is not flat across deciles — 68.5% in the bottom pay-per-discharge decile, 80.9% in the top. That gap is the claimed gradient. Corrected to the rated denominator: top decile 81/246 = 32.9%, bottom decile 59/209 = 28.2%, risk-adjusted top decile 37/172 = 21.5%. THIRD, and this kills the raw half of the hunch: re-ranked on the 2,660 rated hospitals only, per the project's own rule in traps.md line 70, the bottom decile is 26.3% at 1-2 stars against the top decile's 32.0%, average star 3.24 versus 3.20, and corr(pay_per_discharge, star) is -0.0111. Dead zero. There is no payment-to-star gradient to explain away. The risk-adjustment finding is also mostly an artifact: the agent's risk-adjusted top decile holds 304 hospitals of which 132 have no rating (56.6% rated versus 89-95% in every other decile), 122 of those carry one Care Compare footnote code '16' and have median 145 discharges, and the decile's median discharge count is 511, the lowest of all ten, against 2,967 in decile 9. Dividing pay-per-discharge by BENE_AVG_RISK_SCRE selects small hospitals CMS declines to rate. On the common cohort the lift is real but 22.2%, not 12.2%. The strongest correlate of star in the whole file is not payment at all: corr(risk_score, star) = -0.1907. Finally, "academic and safety-net centers" describes the top 25 by dollars, not the 81: only 18 of 81 have UNIV in the name, 32 are government-owned, 7 are for-profit, and the bottom of the list by dollars is Kona Community (HI), Central Peninsula General (AK), Fairbanks Memorial (AK) and Ed Fraser Memorial (FL, 220 discharges) — remote and rural, not academic.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Top-paid hospitals, low stars: 81 of the 304 hospitals in the top Medicare inpatient pay-per-discharge decile ($20,316 to $130,721 per discharge) carry a 1- or 2-star rating and collect $5.888B (inpatient file undated, ingested 2026-07-26); 32 of the 81 report negative net income and 49 positive on their single latest HCRIS cost report, 33 of which end FY2023 and 48 FY2024. There is no raw payment-to-star gradient: on the 2,660 rated hospitals corr(pay-per-discharge, star) = -0.011, and with deciles recomputed on that common cohort the bottom decile is 26.3% at 1-2 stars against the top decile's 32.0%, average star 3.24 versus 3.20. Dividing payment by BENE_AVG_RISK_SCRE does lift the top decile to 22.2% at 1-2 stars and 3.48 average star, but the headline 12.2% came from counting 132 unrated hospitals inside a 304 denominator — 122 of them carry Care Compare footnote 16 at a median 145 discharges, so the risk-adjusted top decile is mostly hospitals CMS declines to rate, not hospitals CMS rates well. Tier 2: all three legs are single snapshots and the inpatient file has no year column.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 is right. The inpatient file has no year column — I read all 59 columns and there is none, and its companion BY_PROVIDER_AND_SERVICE (145,879 rows) has none either, so no sibling rescues it. Only one vintage exists: one row in all_landing_tables.txt (3,044) and one in marts.json (HEALTH__..._BY_PROVIDER, 3,044). _SOURCE_RUN_ID is unique per row (3,044 distinct on 3,044) so it cannot stand in for a load-vintage either, and _INGESTED_AT is a single instant, 2026-07-26 12:06:20.940. FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL is one snapshot with no date column at all. FED_CMS_HCRIS spans FY2022-2024 but holds one report per CCN for the 81, so it is a cross-section too. No before/after is possible on any leg. Note the tier definition is genuinely ambiguous here — Tier 1 allows "the claim is directly testable as written," and this claim is — but the repo's own matrix puts every HCRIS and one-year-file chain (hunches 11, 18, 21) in Tier 2, so 2 is consistent with house usage.
verdicts.blind_spot: I used the same three landing tables and the same pay-per-discharge metric, so I cannot see whether the inpatient payment snapshot and the Care Compare star snapshot describe the same calendar year. Neither file carries a year column and neither carries a usable ingest date on the star side (HOSPITAL_GENERAL._INGESTED_AT is epoch micros), so if the star file is a 2026 refresh and the payment file is CY2023, the whole cross-section pairs measures two or three years apart and no correlation, positive, negative or zero, means anything. Nothing in the warehouse can settle it, so neither the agent's number nor my refutation of it is safe against that. Second blind spot: I tested the agent's own crude risk proxy (divide by BENE_AVG_RISK_SCRE) rather than a real case-mix adjustment. A proper DRG-weighted or CMS case-mix-index adjustment is not landed, and could move the direction again either way. Third: my rated-only cohort drops the 384 unrated inpatient hospitals entirely, so if unrated hospitals are systematically the worst performers the true low-star rate in every decile is higher than any number I report.
new_traps: FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL.HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING is 'Not Available' on 2,250 of 5,432 rows, and the missingness is NOT random across any volume or payment cut: rated share runs 68.5% in the lowest Medicare pay-per-discharge decile, 80.9% in the highest, 86-93% in the middle. Any 'percent of hospitals at 1-2 stars' computed with count(*) as the denominator understates the true rate by 3 to 10 points and manufactures gradients that do not exist — a decile comparison that read 19.3% vs 26.6% is 28.2% vs 32.9% on the rated denominator, and corr(pay_per_discharge, star) on the 2,660 rated hospitals is -0.0111, i.e. zero. Always divide by count(HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING), and re-rank on the rated cohort.

FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL.HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING_FOOTNOTE tells you WHY a rating is missing and the reason is size: of 132 unrated hospitals in a risk-adjusted top decile, 122 carry footnote code '16' at a median 145 discharges, 3 carry '16, 23', 1 carries '19', and 6 have no row in HOSPITAL_GENERAL at all. Filtering on 'rating is null' silently selects small hospitals. Read the footnote column before treating unrated as a neutral category.

FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL._INGESTED_AT reads 1782339299026347 — epoch MICROSECONDS stamped as seconds, same loader bug as the seven tables already in traps.md (EPA CAMPD, GUDID, GLEIF REPEX, FMCSA census, SAM entity, USCG vessels). year() on it throws. This table is not on that list; add it. It also means the Care Compare star snapshot has NO usable vintage anywhere in the warehouse.

FED_CMS_HCRIS is not one fiscal year: 3,534 reports end in FY2023, 2,564 in FY2024, 5 in FY2022 (year(try_to_date(FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY'))). Calling it 'HCRIS FY2023' is wrong on 42% of rows — reports/hunch_matrix_refined_2026-09-05.md does so on lines 43, 47, 204 and 241. Also 62 CCNs carry two reports (6,103 rows over 6,040 distinct CCNs), and NET_INCOME is text with 89 unparseable non-blank values.

FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL.HOSPITAL_OWNERSHIP mislabels chain hospitals: of 51 facilities whose FACILITY_NAME starts 'HCA', 45 are tagged 'Proprietary' and 6 are not — one 'Government - State', one 'Government - Hospital District or Authority', three 'Voluntary non-profit - Private', one 'Voluntary non-profit - Other'. Never call a hospital government-owned or non-profit from this column alone.

Dividing any per-unit dollar figure by BENE_AVG_RISK_SCRE is not risk adjustment, it is a selection filter for small hospitals. In FED_CMS_MEDICARE_INPATIENT_HOSPITALS_BY_PROVIDER the top decile of (payment per discharge / risk score) has median 511 discharges, the LOWEST of all ten deciles, against 2,967 in decile 9 and 2,364 in the raw top decile — a U shape, because low risk score and low volume travel together. 43% of that decile has no star rating as a direct consequence.

verdicts.title: Chains getting worse, then fined
verdicts.rerun_number: Bria Health Services G-or-worse citations 49 of 228 (21.5%) in 2023 to 76 of 227 (33.5%) in 2025, same 15 homes, all 15 cited both years — exact match to the claim, 0% deviation
verdicts.reason: I rebuilt both legs in my own SQL (v04_mine.py) and every headline figure landed on the digit: Bria 49/76 G+, 228/227 total citations, penalties 30/37/41, fines $1,516,461 then $2,024,466; Crest 12/33 G+, $538,984 then $1,224,496; national G+ share 5.78% then 6.18%; 301 chains at 10+ homes; Bria, Crest, Unlimited Development, Hurlbut are the top four risers in that order. The chain is sound: FED_NURSINGHOME411 is 14,713 rows on 14,713 distinct 6-char CCNs, so no fan-out; deficiency rows are unique on CCN+date+tag+severity+cycle (418,479 of 418,479); 418,408 of 418,479 deficiency rows find a home; CHAIN_ID is a real ID, 617 values mapping 1:1 to 617 names with zero chains carrying two names and zero sentinels ('0','N/A','9999' all absent). FINE_AMOUNT parses on all 13,710 Fine rows; the other 2,470 penalty rows are Payment Denials with a null amount. Three things need fixing. First, the entity sentence is wrong: the 301 chains with 10+ homes hold 8,316 homes, not 10,162. 10,162 is every home carrying any CHAIN_ID across all 617 chains — a reader takes 10,162 as the study denominator and it is 22% too big. Second, the enforcement arrow is cherry-picked. Bria's fines in 2023 H2 alone were $1,768,321, more than the whole of 2024 ($1,516,461). Quoting only "2024 to 2025" hides that the money fell before it rose. Third, the severity rise is partly a survey-mix shift the claim does not mention: Bria's complaint-driven citations went from 62.7% to 79.7% of its total, and complaint deficiencies nationally carry 12.9% G+ against 2.6% for standard. Standardising 2025 to the 2023 mix puts the share at 31.0%, not 33.5% — so the real increase is 9.5 points, not 12.0. The rise survives the adjustment and survives stratification (Bria's complaint G+ rate 24.5% to 36.5%, standard 16.5% to 21.7%, both far over the national 12.9%/13.1% and 2.58%/1.69%) — this is a caveat, not a kill. What almost killed it: the file's rolling window. 7,391 of 14,632 homes (50.5%) have their earliest retained deficiency dated 2023 or later, and 6 of Bria's 15 do, so 2023 is a partial year for half the country and the raw pair 49-to-76 is inflated by truncation. The share pair is the sound number, and truncation drops mostly low-severity standard rows, which biases the 2023 share up and makes the observed rise conservative. Finally, overlap is substantial: this is hunch 2 with a time axis. Same three tables, same two CCN legs, same lead entity Bria.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 holds. SURVEY_DATE parses on 418,479 of 418,479 rows, 2017-03-23 to 2026-05-20; PENALTY_DATE parses on 16,180 of 16,180, 2023-06-17 to 2026-05-13. Two full calendar years are compared on the deficiency leg and the penalty leg runs alongside them, so the before/after is real, not a snapshot. Neither leg is a sample or a capped table: 418,479, 16,180 and 14,713 are all non-round. The one snapshot in the chain is the CHAIN_ID roster (PROCESSING_DATE 2025-12-01, one value), but it is the grouping key, not a measured leg, so it does not push this to Tier 2 — it is a caveat on attribution.

verdicts.title: Hospitals as hazardous-waste violators
verdicts.rerun_number: 33.7% of 243 matched hospitals with 3+ RCRA violation rows since 2015 posted negative net income on their FY2023/FY2024 HCRIS cost report (median margin +5.18% of cost), vs 25.2% of 461 zero-violation matched hospitals (median +7.65%) — claimed 34.5% vs 24.5%
verdicts.reason:
JOIN HOLDS. I rebuilt it with my own normalization (collapse every non-alnum run to one space) and got 835 pairs / 835 RCRA ids / 813 CCNs vs the agent's 832/832/811 — 0.4% apart. RCRA_FACILITIES.ID_NUMBER is a genuine 1:1 key: 1,613,224 rows = 1,613,224 distinct ids = 1,613,224 distinct id+ACTIVITY_LOCATION. Fan-out is clean: zero RCRA ids map to more than one CCN, 20 CCNs map to 2-3 RCRA sites (max 3). Entity count is real, not a row count. Independent corroboration the pairs are the same building: ZIP5 agrees on 777 of 835 pairs (93.1%) — the agent never checked this and it is the strongest evidence in the hunch.

BLOCKER — the control group is "never inspected", not "clean". 348 of 470 zero-violation matched hospitals (74.0%) have ZERO rows in FED_EPA_RCRA_EVALUATIONS since 2015. Restrict both arms to hospitals EPA actually inspected: 33.7% negative income (n=243) vs 30.0% (n=120), z=0.72, p=0.47. As written the gap is z=2.41, p=0.016; conditioned on exposure it is gone. Never-inspected hospitals also run 116 median beds vs 242 in the 3+ group — the gap is small-rural-uninspected vs large-urban-inspected. The dose-response is non-monotone too: among inspected hospitals, high violation-rate 36.4% neg / 4.61% margin, LOW rate 24.6% / 7.85%, inspected-clean 30.0% / 5.48%. "Compliance spending is the first budget cut" is not supported by this cut. Note the effect does survive one fair control — STH hospitals 100-500 beds, full-year report: 38.3% (n=162) vs 26.5% (n=234) — so the finding is alive, just not for the stated reason.

BLOCKER — the named exemplar is from the wrong cohort. "Virginia Hospital Center, Arlington VA: 71 violations" came from p07's top_violators, which ran the LOOSE first-three-words match. RCRA's name is "VIRGINIA HOSPITAL CENTER ARLINGTON", CMS's is "VIRGINIA HOSPITAL CENTER". CCN 490050 appears ZERO times in the exact-match set the claim's statistics are built on. The hunch's own trap #2 says "use exact normalized names" and then the headline cites a loose-match hospital.

REAL — the five "sample exact pairs" are all zero-violation, zero-inspection hospitals. CCNs 010012, 010023, 010040, 010055, 010092: viols 0, evals 0, star 2 on all five. They sit in the sentence directly after the violator statistics and read as violators. They are the first five rows of the match by CCN order, all Alabama.

REAL — "FY2023" is wrong for over a third of the cohort. FED_CMS_HCRIS FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE: 2022 = 5 rows, 2023 = 3,534, 2024 = 2,564. In the 3+ group, 35.2% end in FY2024; two of the five named samples do. Begin dates run 2022-10-01 to 2023-09-28. Say "FY2023/24 cost reports", not "FY2023".

REAL — the violation count is inflated. FED_EPA_RCRA_VIOLATIONS carries no violation key: 708,114 rows, 596,758 distinct (ID, LOC, TYPE, DATE), and 47,048 groups are exact duplicates down to ACTUAL_RTC_DATE (53,831 extra rows, 7.6%). In my matched cohort: 1,837 raw rows vs 1,516 distinct — 17.5% inflation. Dedup and the 3+ group falls 244 to 230.

MINOR — denominator dilution. The agent's pct_neg is avg() over all rows in `per`, so the 9 group-C hospitals with no HCRIS row count as "not negative". 24.5% becomes 25.2% on the HCRIS denominator.

MINOR — "no difference in star rating" compares differently-selected subsets. HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING is 'Not Available' on 2,250 of 5,432 rows; unrated share is 6.6% in the 3+ group and 18.1% in the zero group. 3.26 vs 3.15 is on 228 vs 385 survivors of unequal filters.

MINOR — entity/row slip in join_keys: "61 never returned to compliance" is 60 violation ROWS at 19 hospitals, not 61 facilities.

CORRECTED CLAIM: Among 813 hospitals matched to an EPA RCRA hospital-NAICS site by exact normalized name + city + state (835 pairs, ZIP5 agrees on 93.1%), the 243 with 3+ RCRA violation rows since 2015 posted negative net income on their FY2023/24 HCRIS cost report at 33.7% (median margin +5.18% of cost) versus 25.2% of 461 hospitals with no violation rows (median +7.65%), with no difference in star rating — but 74.0% of that zero-violation group was never inspected since 2015, and among inspected hospitals only the gap falls to 33.7% vs 30.0% (p=0.47), so the headline gap is inspection coverage, not compliance spending. The surviving signal is size-matched: among short-term acute hospitals of 100-500 beds on a full-year report, 38.3% (n=162) vs 26.5% (n=234).
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 holds. RCRA violations are dated (DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED parses 100% as MM/DD/YYYY, 0001-01-01 to 2026-07-24, filtered 2015+), but both outcome legs are single snapshots: HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING is one Care Compare pull, and HCRIS is one cost report per CCN (6,103 rows, 6,040 CCNs, periods beginning 2022-10-01 to 2023-09-28). No before/after on the money side, so it is cross-section only. Not Tier 1. Not Tier 3 — no leg is missing; I LIKE-searched all_landing_tables.txt and every table exists, and the exposure leg the hunch needed (FED_EPA_RCRA_EVALUATIONS, 1,166,410 rows) is landed and was simply not used.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun cannot see whether a name+city+state pair is the same physical building beyond ZIP5 agreement — I never compared street address or LATITUDE83/LONGITUDE83 to the CMS address, so the 58 ZIP-mismatched pairs (6.9%) are unadjudicated and a hospital's separate admin or lab site registered under the hospital's name in the same city would pass my filter too. I also cannot see the 2,505 RCRA hospital sites the exact-name filter drops: if renamed/merged hospitals (systematically the acquired, thin-margin ones) fail the name match, the 14.9% coverage is non-random in exactly the direction of the claim and neither the agent's numbers nor mine would show it. And my inspection-exposure test only sees evaluations reported into RCRAInfo since 2015 — a state inspection never uploaded looks identical to no inspection, so my "74% never inspected" is itself an upper bound. Finally I reused the same string-match mechanism the agent used; if name+city+state is the wrong bridge in principle, my rerun repeats the error rather than catching it.
new_traps: FED_EPA_RCRA_VIOLATIONS has no violation key and repeats rows: 708,114 rows but 596,758 distinct (ID_NUMBER, ACTIVITY_LOCATION, VIOLATION_TYPE, DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED), and 47,048 groups are exact duplicates including ACTUAL_RTC_DATE (53,831 extra rows, 7.6%). count(*) as 'violations' inflated a hospital cohort 17.5% (1,837 raw vs 1,516 distinct) and moved a '3 or more' bucket from 244 hospitals to 230. Count distinct loc+type+date, never count(*).

A zero in FED_EPA_RCRA_VIOLATIONS means NEVER INSPECTED, not clean: 348 of 470 zero-violation hospital sites (74.0%) have zero rows in FED_EPA_RCRA_EVALUATIONS since 2015. Any violator-vs-non-violator comparison must condition on the evaluations table first; here the negative-income gap went from 33.7% vs 25.2% (p=0.016) to 33.7% vs 30.0% (p=0.47) once both arms were inspected. Same shape for any EPA/OSHA/CMS enforcement table.

FED_CMS_HCRIS is not one fiscal year: FISCAL_YEAR_END_DATE lands 2022 on 5 rows, 2023 on 3,534, 2024 on 2,564; FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN_DATE 2022 on 985 and 2023 on 5,118. 6,103 rows cover 6,040 CCNs (61 CCNs have 2 reports, 1 has 3) and 225 rows are periods under 300 days. Labeling the whole table 'FY2023' is wrong for 42% of rows; dedup per CCN and state the period.

FED_CMS_HCRIS.NET_INCOME holds the literal string 'nan' on 89 of 6,103 rows and zero blanks; TOTAL_COSTS fails to parse on 82. try_to_number nulls them silently, so a 'reported' count off count(*) or a not-null test overcounts by 89.

FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL.HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING is the string 'Not Available' on 2,250 of 5,432 rows (41.4%), and the missingness is cohort-dependent: 6.6% unrated among hospitals with 3+ RCRA violations vs 18.1% among zero-violation ones, because unrated hospitals are small. Any 'no difference in star rating' compares two differently-selected subsets, not two cohorts.

verdicts.title: Sold hospitals were already bleeding
verdicts.rerun_number: 60.5% (52 of 86 hospitals) negative net income, median margin -4.69% of cost, HCRIS FY ending 2023-2024
verdicts.reason: Headline reproduces exactly on an independently written query: 86 hospitals, 52 negative, 60.5%, median -4.69%; B group 48 at 52.1%, median -0.22%. Join keys are clean - POS_OTHER cat 01 is 13,540 rows on 13,540 distinct CCN (one row per hospital, samples are real 6-digit CCNs), HCRIS 6,103 rows / 6,040 CCNs deduped to one by qualify with zero ties, Care Compare 5,432/5,432. Matched rows 5,736 equals 5,736 distinct hospitals - no fan-out. CHOW_DT is a real date: 2,532 filled, 0 unparseable, 0 sentinels, range 19730630 to 20260101. Three defects. (1) The 4,401 baseline is labelled never-sold and is not: 1,982 of them carry CHOW_CNT>0 with a blank CHOW_DT, so they were sold and the date is missing. True never-sold is 2,419 at 34.2% negative, median +5.00%. The agent's own p02 receipt already separated this bucket (D_cnt_no_date 3,173) and the load-bearing p10 query dropped the split. Direction survives, the entity count and label do not. (2) The star leg percentages are attached to the wrong denominators: 35.6% is 42/118 including 17 unrated, not 42/101 rated (41.6%); 23.1% is 516/2,237, not 516/1,901 (27.1%). Against the truly-never rated it is 41.6% vs 27.5% of 847, z=2.95. (3) The hunch's interpretive claim, distress precedes the sale rather than following it, dies: A vs B is z=0.94, p=0.35, and the order reverses on short-term hospitals (53.0% vs 55.2%) and on a size-matched STH cut (60.8% vs 63.2%). Group A is 76.7% STH / 3.5% CAH while B is 60.4% / 31.3%, so the pooled 60.5-vs-52.1 gap is facility mix. What holds hard: A vs never is z=5.0, p<0.001, and survives inside every cost quartile (77.3/40.5, 70.0/34.5, 58.6/34.4, 44.0/23.6) and a size-matched STH cut (60.8% vs 32.0%), despite group A hospitals being 2.6x bigger by median total cost. Minor: 70 of the 86 have CHOW_CNT>=2, so CHOW_DT is the latest change and an undated earlier one can sit inside the measured fiscal year; Care Compare _INGESTED_AT decodes to 2026-06-24, not 2026-07.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Sold hospitals were already bleeding: 60.5% of the 86 hospitals whose most recent ownership change post-dates their 12-month HCRIS cost report (FY ends 2023-2024; POS snapshot data-through 2026-03-26) had negative net income on that report, median margin -4.69% of cost, against 34.2% of the 2,419 hospitals with no ownership change on record, median +5.00% - a gap that survives inside every cost quartile and a size-matched short-term-hospital cut (60.8% vs 32.0%). The first pass's 4,401 "never sold" is not never-sold: 1,982 of them carry CHOW_CNT>0 with a blank CHOW_DT. Pre-sale versus post-sale is not separable: the 48 sold within 3 years before their FY end sit at 52.1% (p=0.35 against the 86) and the order reverses on short-term hospitals, so the data says distress travels with a recent ownership change, not that it precedes one. Star leg: 41.6% of the 101 rated short-term hospitals sold since 2021 are 1-2 stars versus 27.5% of the 847 rated with no change on record (Care Compare snapshot loaded 2026-06-24); the first pass's 35.6% and 23.1% were shares of all 118 and all 2,237, rated and unrated together. Matched rows 5,736 = 5,736 distinct hospitals, no fan-out. Tier 1 on the margin leg; the star leg is a single snapshot.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 stands, narrowly. CHOW_DT is a genuine parseable date (2,532 hospitals, 0 unparseable, 0 sentinels) and each HCRIS row carries its own fiscal begin and end date, so sale-before versus sale-after that hospital's own report period is a real per-hospital time test, and the claim as written is directly testable and reproduced to the decimal. Two caveats that stop short of Tier 2: HCRIS holds one cost report per hospital, so no hospital's own post-sale margin is observable anywhere in the warehouse - the "after" is other hospitals, not the same ones - and the Care Compare star leg is a single snapshot, which is Tier 2 shaped and must not ride the Tier 1 label.
verdicts.blind_spot: I reran against the same two snapshots the probe used, so anything wrong inside CMS's own POS file is invisible to both of us: if CMS never backfills CHOW_DT on older changes (the 3,138 count-without-date rows say it sometimes does not), then my "truly never sold" 2,419 is itself contaminated and I cannot measure by how much. I also cannot see any post-sale margin - HCRIS is one cost-report year per hospital, so no within-hospital before/after exists in the warehouse and every causal reading here is between-hospital. And I cannot tell a sale from a lease, a merger or a corporate restructure: CHOW is an administrative event code, no transaction file is landed, so "sold" is an interpretation of the column name, not a verified fact.
new_traps: 2026-09-05 - FED_CMS_POS_OTHER hospital rows (PRVDR_CTGRY_CD='01'): 3,138 of 13,540 carry CHOW_CNT>0 with a BLANK CHOW_DT. A `CHOW_DT is null` bucket is NOT 'never sold' - in the HCRIS-joined cohort 1,982 of the 4,401 'never' hospitals had a change of ownership with no date. Split on CHOW_CNT before labelling any control group; true never-sold is 2,419 at 34.2% negative net income vs the 33.5% the merged bucket reads.

2026-09-05 - FED_CMS_POS_OTHER.CHOW_DT is the MOST RECENT change only, and CHOW_CNT says how many there were: 70 of the 86 hospitals whose CHOW_DT falls after their HCRIS fiscal year end carry CHOW_CNT>=2, so an earlier undated ownership change can sit inside the measured year. verdicts.title: Sprinkler flag yes, inspector says install
verdicts.rerun_number: 1,500 of 14,638 'Yes' homes (10.25%) cited K0351 since 2024-06-01 — reproduced exactly; also exact: 1,605 citation rows, 1,504 homes, 458 F-or-worse, 3 immediate jeopardy, 26 uncorrected, 34 'Partial'. But only 64 of the 1,500 still had an open K0351 when the 2026-05-01 flag was published; 1,436 were already closed.
verdicts.reason: Chain holds and every number reproduces to the digit. Join key is clean: FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME CCN is 14,700 rows / 14,700 distinct, 6 chars, no blanks; the fire table's 13,914 distinct CCNs have ZERO orphans into the directory; no duplicate citation rows; max 3 K0351 cites at one home. K0351 text is verbatim 'Install an approved automatic sprinkler system.' Three defects in the story, not the arithmetic. (1) BLOCKER: the directory flag is a 2026-05-01 snapshot, AFTER the citation window, and 1,436 of the 1,500 'Yes' homes had every K0351 closed with a correction date on or before that snapshot. Only 64 were still open; 26 have no correction date at all. hit_means says 'each of the 1,500 is a public listing contradicted by the home's own survey record' — 95.7% of them were fixed before CMS printed the flag. miss_means says 'the flag cannot read Yes while the tag stands' — it can, 64 times. The hunch contradicts itself: its own first_number already says 26. (2) REAL: selecting on flag='Yes' has zero lift. Base rate Yes = 14,638/14,700 = 99.58%; cited homes Yes = 1,500/1,504 = 99.73%. Random expectation is 1,497.7 homes; observed 1,500, a lift of +2.3. The 1,500 is 'ten percent of all nursing homes,' not a selected set. (3) REAL: 70% of the K0351 citations at 'Yes' homes are scope B-E (B 2, C 38, D 503, E 583) — isolated or pattern, consistent with a sprinklered building missing coverage in spots, not an unsprinklered building. Also the 10.25% mixes denominators: only 11,677 'Yes' homes had any K-tag survey in the window, where the rate is 12.83%.
verdicts.tier_reason: Agree with Tier 2. An information_schema scan of the whole LANDING schema returns exactly ONE table with any sprinkler column: FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.AUTOMATIC_SPRINKLER_SYSTEMS_IN_ALL_REQUIRED_AREAS. That table carries PROCESSING_DATE='2026-05-01' on all 14,700 rows — one snapshot, no history. FED_NURSINGHOME411 (14,713 rows) has no sprinkler field, so the leg is not landed under another name. The citation leg is genuinely dated (SURVEY_DATE 2016-07-28 to 2026-05-21, zero unparsed), but with only one flag vintage no before/after on the flag is possible. Not Tier 1.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun reads the same two landing tables and trusts CORRECTION_DATE as CMS publishes it — there is no revisit-survey record in the warehouse, so I cannot verify a correction actually happened, only that a date was filed. DEFICIENCY_DESCRIPTION is the canned tag label, identical on all 3,781 K0351 rows, so I cannot distinguish a whole unsprinklered building from one missing head; the scope letter is my only proxy and it is a state surveyor's judgment. A home that installed sprinklers between citation and snapshot is indistinguishable in this data from a home that never had a problem. And with only one flag vintage I cannot check whether the flag ever read something other than 'Yes' for these homes.
new_traps: FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME.AUTOMATIC_SPRINKLER_SYSTEMS_IN_ALL_REQUIRED_AREAS has NO 'No' value — three values only on 14,700 rows (2026-05-01 snapshot): Yes 14,638, Partial 34, Data Not Available 28. Filtering flag='Yes' selects 99.58% of the directory; homes cited K0351 are 99.73% Yes. Zero lift over base rate — any 'contradiction' count off this column is the base rate wearing a hat.

FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_FIRE_DEFICIENCIES.DEFICIENCY_CORRECTED never contains the string 'CORRECTED'. Six values, all phrased 'Deficient, Provider has date of correction' (1,528), 'Waiver has been granted' (30), 'Deficient, Provider has plan of correction' (28), 'Deficient, Provider has no plan of correction' (16), 'No revisit needed' (2), 'Past Non-Compliance' (1). upper(x) like '%CORRECTED%' matches 0 of 1,605 rows — dead code. CCN 075387, Autumn Lake Healthcare at Norwalk CT: SURVEY_DATE 2024-07-23, CORRECTION_DATE 2024-07-16 — and that is one of the three headline immediate-jeopardy homes. The pair is not a clean cited-then-fixed timeline.

The nursing home directory snapshot (PROCESSING_DATE 2026-05-01) POSTDATES any recent citation window, so 'flag says X but they were cited' is not a contradiction on its own: 1,436 of 1,500 flagged-Yes cited homes had every K0351 closed before the flag was published. Any flag-vs-citation claim must compare CORRECTION_DATE to the snapshot date, not the citation date to nothing.

verdicts.title: Terminations foreshadowed in cost reports
verdicts.rerun_number: 96 of 142 hospitals (67.6%) terminated 2024-2026 were negative on their FY2023 HCRIS cost report, median -8.14% of total costs — reproduced exactly with an independent rebuild
verdicts.reason:
The load-bearing number is real and robust. My rebuild used a different report-selection rule (latest fiscal-year-end, not longest report), try_to_number(x,18,6) instead of (18,2), and an explicit 'nan' guard, and returned 142 / 96 / 67.6% / -8.14 identically. The join key is clean: FED_CMS_POS_OTHER.CCN is unique in category 01 (13,540 rows, 13,540 distinct), HCRIS PROVIDER_CCN is 6,040 distinct on 6,103 rows and 6,037 of them match POS, so matched_rows 5,736 really is 5,736 hospitals with no fan-out. The gap survives three disproof attempts: within every facility type (STH 64.3% vs 33.1%, CAH 68.8% vs 31.9%, LTCH 86.4% vs 52.2%, PH 62.5% vs 44.8%), on the conventional denominator (median -8.55% vs +5.13% of NET_PATIENT_REVENUE), and after dropping revenue-blank rows (93 of 139, 66.9% vs 1,742 of 5,426, 32.1%). Time order holds: 141 of 142 reports end before the termination date, median lag 366 days, and the negative rate falls monotonically with lag (81.8% at 0-90 days out, 61.7% at 366-730 days).

Three things are wrong and need fixing.

BLOCKER on the named examples. All three "worst" hospitals — EAMC-Lanier AL -138.1%, Hampstead Hospital NH -111.1%, Western Peaks Specialty UT -103.8% — are the only three rows in the 142 with NET_PATIENT_REVENUE null. On each, NET_INCOME equals exactly minus LESS_TOTAL_OPERATING_EXPENSE (EAMC-Lanier: NI -30,412,933, OPEX 30,412,933, NPR null). The revenue side of the cost report is blank, so the "loss" is just the expense line with nothing against it. A margin worse than -100% of cost is the tell. The real worst three with a reported revenue line are Thomasville Regional MC AL -49.9% of cost (terminated 2024-09-21), Colorado West Psychiatric CO -48.1% (2025-03-10), Parkside Behavioral OH -46.3% (2024-04-01).

REAL: the CHOW sub-claim is a floor, not a death. Of the 1,299 terminations 2015-2025, 549 carry CHOW_CNT > 0 but only 294 carry a CHOW_DT. 255 ownership changes have no date at all and can never fall inside a 24-month window. 44 of 1,299 is 3.4%; 44 of the 294 with a dated change is 15.0%. "The sale-then-closure version dies" is not established by this data.

MINOR: the active denominator. 7 of the 5,586 hold the literal string 'nan' in NET_INCOME with a valid TOTAL_COSTS. try_to_number returns null and `case when ni<0 then 1 else 0 end` scores them as profitable. Correct active cohort is 1,889 of 5,579 (33.9%).

Overlap is clean. Hunch 29 pairs HCRIS net income FY2023 with POS terminations but only as county-level counts against TRI density; no report in reports/*_2026-09-05.md joins a termination date to that hospital's own cost report, and none tests CHOW-then-terminate.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 stands, narrowly. Both legs carry per-row dates (POS TRMNTN_EXPRTN_DT parses on 100% of 6,518 non-'00' category-01 rows, blank on all 7,022 active rows — no sentinel; HCRIS FISCAL_YEAR_BEGIN/END_DATE parse clean) and the before/after is real, not assumed: 141 of 142 reports close before the termination, median 366 days ahead. The claim is directly testable as written and was tested. The caveat that stops short of Tier 2: HCRIS is a single landed vintage (one ingest, 6,103 rows, FY ends 2022-12 to 2024-12), so the finding cannot be validated out of sample — 0 of the 862 hospitals terminated 2015-2022 have a 12-month report in this file. You can measure the association once; you cannot yet test whether a bad FY2019 margin predicted a 2020 closure. That is a coverage limit, not a missing date, so it does not demote the tier under the written rule.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun reads the same two landing tables and the same POS snapshot (ingested ~2026-06-25, latest termination 2026-03-05), so it cannot see whether the termination flag is true. A hospital that actually closed but whose POS row still reads PGM_TRMNTN_CD '00' sits silently in my "active" comparison group and drags the 33.9% upward. Nor did I trace CCN successors: PGM_TRMNTN_CD '07' can mean a merge or a CCN renumber rather than a closure, and 1,849 of the 6,518 terminations carry that code — a renumbered hospital would show a termination date and a bad final cost report while still operating. I also never left the two tables: I verified the numbers are internally consistent, not that they match reality outside the warehouse. Finally, both cohorts are the hospitals that filed a full 12-month report; the 50 of 192 terminations 2024-2026 that filed a short report or none are invisible to me, and they are the ones most likely to have collapsed mid-year.
new_traps: FED_CMS_HCRIS.NET_INCOME and TOTAL_COSTS hold the literal string 'nan' — 89 and 82 rows of 6,103. try_to_number returns null silently, and `case when ni<0 then 1 else 0 end` scores those rows as PROFITABLE rather than dropping them. 7 rows carry ni='nan' with a valid TOTAL_COSTS, so a `tc>0` filter does not catch them; they padded an active-hospital denominator from 5,579 to 5,586. Guard with nullif(lower(trim(x)),'nan') before try_to_number.

FED_CMS_HCRIS has a blank-revenue row class: NET_PATIENT_REVENUE is null and NET_INCOME equals exactly minus LESS_TOTAL_OPERATING_EXPENSE. 156 of the 5,732 12-month reports (3 of 142 terminated hospitals, 153 of 5,579 active). Any margin off those rows reads worse than -100% of cost and is an artifact — EAMC-Lanier reads -138.1% of cost purely because its revenue lines are empty. Filter NET_PATIENT_REVENUE > 0 before ranking anything by margin.

FED_CMS_HCRIS.TOTAL_INCOME is not total income: it equals NET_INCOME on 4,059 of 5,732 12-month reports (71%), so median NET_INCOME/TOTAL_INCOME reads exactly 100%. And TOTAL_COSTS is not operating expense — median TOTAL_COSTS $58.9M vs LESS_TOTAL_OPERATING_EXPENSE $69.8M, opex exceeds costs on 5,140 of 5,732 rows (median ratio 1.142). 'Margin as % of cost' is not the standard margin; use NET_PATIENT_REVENUE as the denominator.

FED_CMS_POS_OTHER.CHOW_DT is blank on 55% of hospitals that had an ownership change: of 5,670 category-01 rows with CHOW_CNT >= 1, only 2,532 carry a date, and the gap holds at every CHOW_CNT value (cnt=1: 1,324 of 2,598; cnt=2: 667 of 1,722). There is also only ONE date column for up to 11 changes. Any 'sold then X within N months' rate off this column is a floor — the hospital-termination version reads 3.4% (44 of 1,299) undated and 15.0% (44 of 294) among terminations with a dated change.

Care Compare deletion of terminated hospitals is year-graded, not absolute: FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL holds 0 of 762 hospitals terminated 2019-2023, but 10 of 99 terminated 2024, 36 of 80 in 2025 and 12 of 13 in 2026 — 58 of 192 overall. 'Terminated hospitals vanish from HOSPITAL_GENERAL' is true only for pre-2024; the recent cohort is a partial, decaying sample, which is worse than a clean absence because a count off it looks populated.

FED_CMS_HCRIS.PROVIDER_CCN is not unique: 6,103 rows, 6,040 distinct, 63 CCNs with 2-3 cost reports (one has 3). Any per-hospital measure needs a dedupe. The common tiebreak `row_number() over (order by datediff(days) desc)` picks the LONGEST report, not the latest — here it happened to give the same cohort as `order by fiscal_year_end desc`, but it is the wrong rule and on a fatter HCRIS vintage it would silently return an older year.
