verdicts.corrected_claim: Hospitals whose Medicare participation ended in 2024-2026 were 67.6% negative on their FY2023 cost report (96 of 142, median -8.14% of total costs, -8.55% of net patient revenue) versus 33.9% for the 5,579 still-active hospitals with a readable net income (median +5.32%); the gap holds inside every facility type and 141 of the 142 reports close before the termination, median 366 days ahead. The worst verifiable cases are Thomasville Regional MC AL at -49.9% of cost (terminated 2024-09-21), Colorado West Psychiatric CO -48.1% (2025-03-10) and Parkside Behavioral OH -46.3% (2024-04-01) — the three hospitals previously named as worst (EAMC-Lanier, Hampstead, Western Peaks) are the only three rows in the cohort with a blank revenue side, where NET_INCOME is just minus operating expense, so their sub-100% margins are artifacts. Sale-then-closure is unproven rather than dead: 44 of 1,299 terminations 2015-2025 (3.4%) had a dated ownership change within 24 months, but 255 more terminations carry an ownership-change count with no date, so the honest figure is a floor between 3.4% and 15.0% (44 of the 294 with a dated change).

verdicts.title: Triple owners are the good ones — number reproduces exactly, but the gap is an ownership-mix artifact and two figures carry the wrong cohort label
verdicts.rerun_number: 3.301 avg overall star on 330 triple-owner NH411 homes vs 2.840 on 9,920 other chain homes (NH411 snapshot PROCESSING_DATE 2025-12-01) — exact match, 0.0% deviation. Within ownership class the gap falls to 0.19 stars for-profit (t=1.5), 0.03 nonprofit (t=0.3), 0.41 government (t=1.7); none significant.
verdicts.reason:
Rebuilt the chain from the sentence with my own SQL (three-way INTERSECT on ASSOCIATE_ID, not the agent's triple JOIN). Every structural number reproduces exactly: 89 owners, 334 SNF / 144 HHA / 106 hospice CCNs, 58 also hospital, 330 of 334 in NH411, star 3.301 vs 2.840, 31.8% vs 44.8% at 1-2 stars. Key discipline passes: ASSOCIATE_ID is 10 chars on all 41,174 enrollment rows across the four files, zero blanks, zero '0000000000', CCN unique per row in every enrollment file (14,425 rows / 14,425 distinct), so no fan-out. Entity count 89 is stated correctly next to the 584 row count. try_to_number is (18,6)/(18,2) throughout — no rounding trap. No capped or sampled table is touched.

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG.

1. Cross-wired denominators (real). The claim reads '$20,229 fines per home, 0.79 penalties per home ... other chain homes (9,920): 2.84, 44.8%, $31,261, 1.10 penalties per home.' The $31,261 / 1.101 pair is not the 9,920 chain homes — it is all 14,091 other SNF-enrolled homes, chains AND independents (verified: query pen_agent_cohort returns exactly 334 / 14,091 homes and 20,229 / 31,261). Recomputed on the cohorts the sentence names: triple 330 homes $20,474 and 0.80 penalties per home; other chain 9,920 homes $34,000 and 1.128. The correction widens the gap, so the error is conservative, but the sentence compares two different populations.

2. The gap is ownership mix, not the triple shape (real, and it is the whole point). 215 of 330 triple homes are nonprofit or government (65%); 1,301 of 9,920 other chain homes are (13%). Within class: for-profit 2.947 vs 2.759 (n=113, t=1.5), nonprofit 3.489 vs 3.460 (t=0.3), government 3.487 vs 3.077 (n=39, t=1.7) — none significant. 1-2 star share within class: 43.4 vs 47.4, 25.3 vs 27.3, 30.8 vs 39.7, against the raw 32.2 vs 45.2. Penalties per home within class: for-profit 1.00 vs 1.17, nonprofit 0.697 vs 0.763, government 0.675 vs 1.141. And non-chain independents already beat triple owners on the same table: 3.206 star overall and 3.58 within nonprofit vs the triples' 3.489, with better staffing (4.303 vs 3.957 nurse HPRD). So 'the good ones' holds only against for-profit chains, the worst group in the file.

3. A bad actor sits inside the shape (real). The hunch's miss_means says a for-profit roll-up 'never shares an ID and is invisible here', framing the clean result as an acquittal-by-gap. But the second-largest triple owner, LIBERTY HEALTHCARE GROUP LLC (ASSOCIATE_ID 4587574355), holds 30 SNFs + 18 HHAs + 4 hospices in one state and its homes average 2.57 stars with $40,591 in fines — worse than the 2.84 / $37,130 comparison group. The largest, Good Samaritan (87 homes, 26% of the cohort), averages 2.83, dead level with the comparison group. Clustering runs the other way too and the agent did not report it: drop the top-1 owner and triple stars go 3.301 -> 3.471; drop the top-4 (57.3% of the homes) -> 3.784; owner mean-of-means is 4.009 across 85 owners vs 2.874 across 614 other chains. The cohort is two populations — small rural nonprofit hospital systems that run excellent homes, and four large owners that run average-to-bad ones — reported as one mean.

Smaller: vintage is misstated. tier_reason and time_axis say 'NH411 and Home Health files are 2026 snapshots'; NH411 PROCESSING_DATE is 2025-12-01 and the penalties file is 2026-06-01, while the three enrollment files were ingested 2026-07-26. Ownership is measured eight months after the quality it explains.

HHA leg, partly already published. 76 of the 144 triple HHA enrollments sit inside hunch #31's hospital-owned cohort (530 enrollments). Split three ways, triple HHAs are 3.42 star / 83.7 DTC / 9.28 PPH; other hospital-owned are 3.135 / 84.46 / 10.11; everything else 3.255 / 79.87 / 11.01. Against the natural peer group — another hospital-system-owned HHA — triple HHAs are WORSE on discharge-to-community (83.7 vs 84.46), not better. The claim's 83.7 vs 80.1 is the hunch-31 effect (84.6 vs 79.9) with a smaller numerator. Only the preventable-hospitalization leg (9.28 vs 10.11 vs 11.01) survives against the right peers, on 133 rated agencies.

Third line never tested. FED_CMS_HOSPICE is 6,852 rows and 12 columns of directory — name, address, ownership type, certification date. No quality or utilization measure exists, so 'run better across three post-acute lines' is measured on two.

What survives, cleanly: the join is real, the intersection is real and reproducible, the raw comparison is stated accurately, and the fines direction is the strongest part — median total fines is $0 for triple homes and $3,145 for other chain homes.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 survives on the letter of Chris's rule — 'the claim is directly testable as written' — and I tested it end to end. But the stated justification is decorative: the penalty leg's 2023-06-17 to 2026-05-13 window is applied identically to both groups, so it supplies no before/after and no trend. Every measured leg is a single snapshot (NH411 2025-12-01, Home Health 2026, enrollments 2026-07-26), and the two snapshots are eight months apart. If Chris reads Tier 1 as 'a time axis exists', this is a Tier 2. Under the definition as written, it is a Tier 1 cross-section.
verdicts.blind_spot: I re-ran against the same three enrollment files and the same NH411 snapshot, so any error inside CMS's own ASSOCIATE_ID assignment is invisible to both of us — including the thing the hunch turns on. BEAVER VALLEY HOSPITAL (Utah) holds 40 SNF CCNs and WEST WHARTON COUNTY HOSPITAL DISTRICT holds 93 under one ID; these are licensee-of-record arrangements, and neither of us can tell a licensee from a beneficial owner with the landed files. Second: I compared one vintage to itself. I cannot see a home that changed hands between the 2025-12 quality snapshot and the 2026-07 enrollment snapshot, so every group assignment carries an eight-month lag I did not measure. Third: I controlled for ownership type, hospital-based status and owner size, but not for state — star ratings move with state survey severity, and the triple set is Texas/Utah/Indiana-heavy, so some of the residual 0.19 for-profit gap could still be geography. Fourth: my significance arithmetic is unclustered two-sample t; a proper owner-clustered SE would be wider, not narrower, in the within-class tests.

FED_CMS_SKILLED_NURSING_FACILITY_ENROLLMENTS.CCN is not always 6 characters: 14,255 rows are 6, 113 are 7 ('245470A'), 57 are 9 ('075198001'). FED_NURSINGHOME411 is strictly 6. FED_NURSINGHOME411.OWNERSHIP_TYPE is per-HOME, not per-owner. One ASSOCIATE_ID (1951218817, Evangelical Lutheran Good Samaritan Society, 87 homes) carries 'Non profit' on 84 homes and 'For profit' on 3. Never read an owner's tax status off one of its facilities, and never min() it across a chain.

avg(case when OVERALL_RATING <= 2 then 1 else 0 end) on NH411 silently counts the 132 unrated homes as 'not 1-2 star'. It is a share of ALL homes, not of rated homes: 31.8 vs 32.2 for triple owners, 44.8 vs 45.2 for other chains. Harmless here because the null rate is 1% in both groups; anywhere the null rate differs by group it fabricates a gap.

FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_PENALTIES.PENALTY_TYPE holds two populations under one row count: 13,710 'Fine' rows with a dollar amount and 2,470 'Payment Denial' rows where FINE_AMOUNT is NULL. A 'penalties per home' count includes both; a 'fines per home' dollar includes only the first. Same denominator, different numerator population — say which you mean or the two numbers do not describe the same thing.

FED_CMS_HOSPICE (6,852 rows) is a directory only: 12 columns — CCN, name, address, county, phone, region, ownership type, certification date. No quality measure, no utilization, no live-discharge rate. Any SNF+HHA+hospice quality comparison can only measure two of the three lines.

verdicts.title: Dialysis in bad-water counties
verdicts.rerun_number: 22.32 mortality per 100 patient-years in the 908 facilities in 50%+ counties (884 carry a value), vs 21.63 in under-10% counties — Welch t=3.05, p=0.0023; SMR window 2021-2024, SDWA violations 2020-2024. The agent's own county-name key reproduces exactly at 22.149 over 767 of 785.
verdicts.reason: The chain holds and the arithmetic replicates byte-for-byte on the agent's key (785 facilities / 252 counties / 22.149 mortality / 143.06 hospitalization). What is wrong is the reading and the entity counts. (1) The hunch sentence and miss_means both assert a null — "no higher mortality", "flat rates, which is what came back". It is not flat. On my independent rebuild the A-vs-C gap is +0.681, Welch t=3.05, p=0.0023; on the agent's own numbers it is +0.567, t=2.44, p=0.015. State-demeaned the gradient is monotone across all four buckets (A +0.376, B +0.238, C -0.022, D -0.473), A vs D t=3.56, p=0.0004, and by exposure decile the bottom three are all negative and the top four all positive (top decile 22.44 raw vs 21.61 in decile 2). The effect is small — 3%, 0.12 SD — and confounded, but "flat" is the opposite of what the numbers say. The claim also quotes only A, C and D and omits B (21.70), the middle rung that makes it a ladder. (2) The 785/252/7,071 counts are artifacts of a raw county-name join that drops 418 of 7,557 facilities non-randomly: every Louisiana parish, PRINCE GEORGES MD (46 facilities at 96% violating share, the largest high-exposure county in the file), both St. Louises. Joining on ANSI county FIPS instead gives 908/287 and 7,373 joined. (3) "22.15 in the 785 facilities" is computed on 767; 304 rows file-wide have a blank mortality under PATIENT_SURVIVAL_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CODE 199/258/201. Nueces is 16 facilities but 15 with mortality. (4) The agent's own trap #1 is mis-measured: VIOLATION_ID is a per-system counter, not a global id (VIOLATION_ID '2' sits under 285 distinct PWSIDs), so the slice holds 62,595 real violations, not 42,979, and 3.6 rows each, not 5.2. What survived: PUB_WATER_SYSTEMS is one row per PWSID (434,040/434,040, single 2026Q2 quarter) so no fan-out; zero counties with null or zero CWS population so no null share hid in D_none; try_to_number(x,18,6) throughout; CCN real at 7,557/7,557; zero unparsed dates; no capped or sampled table in the chain.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 is right as run: FED_CMS_DIALYSIS carries one pooled SMR window ('01Jan2021-31Dec2024' on every row, 1 distinct value), so the outcome leg is a snapshot and the test is cross-section only while the SDWA leg is fully dated. But the dated version is landed under another name — FED_CMS_MEDICARE_DIALYSIS_FACILITIES holds per-year mortality inputs (measure deay2_f 'Number of patient deaths, 2022' and exdy2_f 'Expected number of patient deaths, 2022', YEAR='2022', 7,772 CCNs each). So tier 2 here is a table choice, not a warehouse limit; the upgrade to tier 1 needs no new load, just deaths-over-expected by CCN by year against violation begin dates.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rebuild reads the same three SDWA tables and the same CMS file, so anything wrong inside them I reproduce exactly — a PWS with a wrong ANSI county code, a stale POPULATION_SERVED_COUNT, a mis-specified CMS risk adjustment. Bigger: county-of-facility is not county-of-patient. Dialysis patients cross county lines to treat and drink water at home, so the exposure variable is an ecological proxy no landed table can validate. And I controlled only for state; poverty, race, urbanicity and dialysis chain all correlate with both water violations and mortality, so I can neither confirm nor kill a causal reading — I can only say the gradient exists and is not flat.
new_traps: FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT.VIOLATION_ID is a per-system counter, not a global id: VIOLATION_ID '2' appears under 285 distinct PWSIDs, '1' under 272, '3' under 268, in the health-based 2020-2024 slice alone. That slice holds 42,979 distinct VIOLATION_ID but 62,595 distinct PWSID||VIOLATION_ID — a global count distinct undercounts real violations by 31%, and the row fan-out is 3.6 enforcement rows per violation, not 5.2. Always key on PWSID||VIOLATION_ID.

CMS COUNTY_PARISH joined raw to any other county-name column loses 418 of 7,557 dialysis facilities (5.5%), and the losses are systematic: every Louisiana parish, PRINCE GEORGES MD (46 facilities, apostrophe), SAINT LOUIS and SAINT LOUIS CITY MO, SAINT CLAIR IL, SAINT LUCIE FL — CMS spells SAINT, SDWA spells ST. The dropped counties skew poor and Black, so a null result computed on the raw join is a null with its most exposed cases deleted.

WHAT I DID
Rebuilt the chain from the join_keys text with my own SQL: try_to_date(NON_COMPL_PER_BEGIN_DATE,'MM/DD/YYYY') instead of right(...,4), dedup on PWSID+VIOLATION_ID, own decl CTE, own control pool. Scripts v1_keys.py .. v5_vintage.py.

REPRODUCES EXACTLY
| Claim | Mine |
|---|---|
| declared 5,577 -> 5,059, ratio 0.907 | 5,577 -> 5,059, 0.9071 |
| OK+TX 154 counties 1,819 -> 2,211 (1.216) | identical |
| other 873 counties 0.758 | identical |
| control by year (10,438/8,176 ...) | identical |
| OK 667 (2014) -> 882 (2016); non-declared 303 -> 359 | identical |
| OK family 220: 578 -> 885 | identical |
| county-years 17,648; counties 2,916; sum 136,546 | identical |
Join keys check out: CN pairs 411,650, matched 394,357 (95.8%), 3,192 counties, 443 multi-county PWS (max 11). HB rows 1,993,255 over 563,944 PWSID+VIOLATION_ID = 3.53x fan-out, and 0 of them carry a null VIOLATION_ID, so the 1,002,550 enforcement-only rows are correctly excluded. Date is MM/DD/YYYY, length 10 on 100% of HB rows, so right(...,4) is safe.

REAL — the surviving lead dies on its own evidence
The claim keeps the OK/TX cohort alive and names rule family 220 (Stage 2 disinfection byproducts) as the excess. That family is a national phase-in, not a flood:
- US family 220 health-based: 199 (2012), 983 (2013), 2,661 (2014), 4,122 (2015), 4,481 (2016). +68% 2014->2016 nationally vs Oklahoma's +53%. Oklahoma ran BELOW the national ramp.
- Inside Texas, family 220 grew +105% in declared counties (177->363) and +106% in never-declared ones (236->486). No differential at all.
- In OK declared-2015 counties the whole rise is 220 (389->642, +253) while every other health-based family FELL (278->240). "Flood organics breach the MCL" predicts a broad rise; the data show one rule family moving and the rest declining.
- Pre-trend kills it: those same counties went 0 (2011), 21 (2012), 101 (2013), 389 (2014) on family 220 — the ramp starts two years before the May 2015 disaster. And the peak year is 2015 (917), the declaration year itself, higher than 2016 (882); the yr-1/yr+1 design skips year 0 and hides that.
- OK 2016 had FEWER systems in violation than 2015 (298 vs 371) with the same violation count — repeat quarterly LRAA violations per system, not more broken systems.

REAL — "the 2015 Oklahoma+Texas flood cohort: 154 counties" is a mislabel
The 154 counties are OK+TX declared ANY year 2015-2020, each measured around its own declaration year. Split: 2015 = 98 counties (1,161->1,479), 2016 = 23 (188->181), 2017 = 18 (193->205), 2019 = 15 (277->346). The true 2015 cohort nationally is 170 counties, 1,308->1,596. Two of the top three OK movers (Pawnee, Osage) are 2019 declarations, not 2015.

REAL — entity counts wrong two ways
1. "136,546 distinct health-based violations 2013-2022" is not distinct violations. It is the sum of county-attributed counts. Distinct PWSID+VIOLATION_ID for 2013-2022 = 139,992 (138,804 among PWS with a CN row). 136,546 double-counts the 443 multi-county systems and drops the 4.2% unmatched.
2. "1,027 declared counties" contains 58 records that are not counties: 54 are 4-digit FIPS padded with a trailing space ('5037 ', '6037 ' = Los Angeles), 2 are state-level ('12000', '46000'). length(FIPS)=5 lets them through; none joins to a census GEOID, all score 0 before and 0 after. Real declared counties = 969.

MINOR
- Control ratio 0.825 is a declared-county-weighted mean of six yearly ratios. Ratio of sums is 0.812. Direction unchanged.
- The hunch sentence says "relative to never-declared counties"; on that reading 0.907 > 0.825 SUPPORTS it. tier_reason says "the general claim is killed by the first run." The hunch contradicts its own verdict.
- "394,358 of 411,651 CN rows" — 394,357 of 411,650 distinct pairs. Off by one, cosmetic.
- Control counties are never matched: 2,266 includes PR/GU/VI/MP/AS and 239 counties with no water system in the CN map. Restricting to counties that ever had a health-based violation (2,027) changes nothing, because the zero counties contribute zero.

SMALLEST FIX
Relabel the cohort "OK+TX counties declared 2015-2020", say 969 counties and 139,992 distinct violations, and drop the rule-220 sentence or re-cut it net of the national Stage 2 ramp — the honest version is a tier-3-style dead end with a live number, not a lead.

verdicts.blind_spot: I rebuilt on the same three tables with the same county attribution (left(PWSID,2) = state, lpad(ANSI_ENTITY_CODE,3) = county), so any error in that attribution is inherited by my numbers, not caught. Four things my rerun cannot see: (1) whether SDWIS retroactively purges or re-dates old violations, which would bend the whole 2013-2022 series; (2) whether a PWS's served-county list changed since 2013 — the 2026Q2 map is all I have; (3) whether the FEMA IA county is the county whose water system actually flooded — IA registrations carry the applicant's damaged address, and the table has no applicant identity at all; (4) significance — every comparison here is a raw count clustered inside a few hundred water systems, so a 14-point gap in a 300-violation pool could be noise and I ran no test that would tell me.

Use lpad(trim(FIPS),5,'0') and drop right(FIPS,3)='000'; 58 of the 1,027 never join to a census GEOID.

FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS.ANSI_ENTITY_CODE holds the literal string 'FIP' on 89 CN rows — a text sentinel in a column that looks like a 3-digit county code. lpad('FIP',3,'0') stays 'FIP' and drops silently from any county join. Also STATE_SERVED is 0% filled on all 411,651 CN rows; state has to come from left(PWSID,2), and 66 distinct prefixes include EPA region numbers ('09','10','05') and 'NN' (Navajo Nation), ~1,100 rows that are not states.

Both SDWA tables carry SUBMISSIONYEARQUARTER='2026Q2' and nothing else: the PWSID-to-county crosswalk is ONE current snapshot applied retroactively to violations dated back to 1970. Violations are dated, the geography is not — a before/after on SDWA counties is a dated measure on an undated map.

National health-based violations drop 18,869 (2015) -> 14,325 (2016) for that reason alone. Separately, family 220 (Stage 2 disinfection byproducts) is a compliance phase-in ramp — 199 (2012), 983 (2013), 2,661 (2014), 4,481 (2016) nationally. Any 2014-vs-2016 county comparison measures those two rule changes unless it is netted against the national family-level trend.

Summing a per-county violation count is not a violation count: 443 PWS serve 2 or more counties (max 11), so the county-attributed sum for health-based violations 2013-2022 is 136,546 while distinct PWSID+VIOLATION_ID is 139,992. verdicts.rerun_number: Q+1 SNC 10.84% and any-noncompliance 37.59% vs 15.01% / 41.74% in other quarters; 31,590 vs 652,976 permit-quarters, 2015-2024. Exact match to the claim, rebuilt on my own SQL.

CHAIN AND KEYS HOLD. Every join key checked both sides, no fan-out anywhere: ICIS_FACILITIES NPDES_ID 1,213,737 rows / 1,213,737 distinct, max 1 row per id; QNCR (NPDES_ID, YEARQTR) 7,951,656 / 7,951,656 distinct, zero duplicate groups in window; XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY GEOID 3,235 / 3,235, GEOID = STATEFP||COUNTYFP on all rows. COUNTY_CODE is length 5 on all 700,160 non-null rows, 3,206 of 3,232 codes match census. Damage parse uses try_to_number(x,18,6) correctly. No capped or sample table in the chain, no name-match join, both legs dated. Not a duplicate.

NUMBERS REPRODUCE EXACTLY on independently written SQL (v2_rerun.py): 502 county-quarters / 409 counties; 768,405 facility-quarters / 84,144 permits / 382 counties; 31,590 in Q+1; 10.84% and 37.59% vs 15.01% and 41.74%; 2017 47.46% vs 21.98% on 3,502.

FOUR LABELS ARE WRONG.

1 REAL - the title names a population that is 6% of what was measured. Only 4,873 of 84,144 permits carry a wastewater-shaped name (WWTP/WASTEWATER/SEWER/POTW/TREATMENT PLANT/...). Top permit prefixes are R10 17,706, R20 5,196, R15 4,784 - construction and industrial stormwater general permits. Sample facility names in the panel: HAWKINS FILL SITE, DANDRIDGE MASS GRADING PHASE 2, DEVELOPMENT AT 65 SUNNYSIDE AVENUE. Run the same windows on the 4,776 sewage-named permits and the conclusion flips: effluent violations (NUME90Q>0) 37.21% in Q+1 vs 31.76% in other quarters (+17% relative), any-noncompliance 61.88% vs 58.74%. Municipal-owned (MWD/CNG/CTG/DIS, 7,503 permits): effluent 30.78% vs 23.78% (+29% relative). Year by year on sewage plants, Q+1 effluent violations are higher in 8 of 10 years; 2017 is 46.46% vs 21.69%. Within-plant paired on 3,033 plants seen in both windows it shrinks to +1.53pp (1,007 up, 1,241 down, 785 tied) - weak, but "No lift" is not what the sewage data says. Script v5_sewage.py, v6_sewage_paired.py.

2 REAL - "in the same facilities' other quarters" is not what ran. The 15.0% bucket holds 78,433 permits; the Q+1 bucket holds 26,607. On the 23,563 permits present in BOTH windows the same-facility figures are 12.90% SNC and 38.48% any-NC, mean paired diff -0.0199 and -0.0176. The direction survives the within-facility control; the number 15.0% does not belong to that sentence.

3 REAL - "84,144 NPDES facilities" is a permit count. Distinct FACILITY_UIN behind those permits is 74,578. Entity count is 11% lower than the stated one.

4 REAL - "Harvey counties" is a third of the 2017 cohort. Of 3,502 facility-quarters in the 2017 Q+1 bucket, Texas is 1,165 (33.3%). The single biggest block is Washington state 2017Q2 at 1,077 facility-quarters (54% any-NC) - Pacific Northwest flooding, not Harvey. Texas 2017Q4 is 1,131 at 63.2%, and that part is genuinely Harvey aftermath.

5 REAL - the HLRNC mapping is looser than the trap admits. In-window cross-tab against the five violation-count columns: code N (519,481 rows) is counted as noncompliance but 27.3% of its rows carry zero violations; code R (200,068 rows, avg 0.37 effluent violations, avg 7.58 late DMRs) and code P (58,189 rows, avg 1.31 effluent violations) are counted as CLEAN. Code U (1,449,641 rows) is 99.2% all-zero, so excluding it is right. Under a code-free measure - any of the five NUM columns > 0 - the pooled result holds directionally (Q+1 34.77% vs other 38.78%), but the effluent-only measure already flips pooled: 12.46% vs 11.98%.

6 MINOR - join_keys says "616,835 of 616,835 IDs since 2015 match, 367,000 with a county". That is YEARQTR >= '20151' unbounded, which reaches rows dated 20332. The analysis window 20151-20244 holds 542,041 distinct IDs, 320,174 of them with a county. Storm FIPS match quoted as 3,106 of 3,308 (93.9%); mine is 3,104 of 3,247 (95.6%).

Nothing here breaks the join or the tier. The arithmetic is sound and the null result on all NPDES permits is real. The title, the entity noun, the comparison group and the 2017 attribution each need a fix.

verdicts.title: Hazardous waste and drug poisoning
verdicts.rerun_number: Pooled corr(RCRA violations per 100k, drug-poisoning band midpoint) = 0.006534 over 40,827 county-years 2003-2015 (0.063 on the log). Reproduced to four decimals from my own SQL.
verdicts.reason:
The load-bearing number reproduces exactly. I rebuilt the chain from the hunch sentence with my own year parse (try_to_date MM/DD/YYYY instead of right(x,4)) and my own explicit 16-band midpoint map: r_pooled 0.006534, r_log 0.063, n 40,827, bands 9.75/11.03/10.82/10.23, all identical. Change quintiles came back 5.13/4.65/5.15/4.88/4.96 vs the claimed 5.13/4.65/5.18/4.85/4.96 — inside 1%, and the 0.03 drift is ntile tie noise (616 of 3,140 counties sit at exactly dvr=0, 19.6% of the sort). Fan-out is clean: every one of 1,597,308 RCRAINFO PGM_SYS_IDs carries exactly one FIPS_CODE, so min()/max() are the same and no violation is double-counted. 147,131 of 147,240 violating IDs match a FIPS (99.93%), exactly as claimed. Dates parse 708,114 of 708,114; the agent's right(x,4) and my year(try_to_date) select the identical 249,799 rows.

Three counts are wrong. (1) Counties with violations is 2,698 only because count(distinct FIPS_CODE) counts 9 two- and three-character junk fragments ('005','050','061','035','015','000','010','077','085') as counties. Strip those and 2,689 five-char codes remain; 4 are state-only 'XX000', 66 are PR/VI/GU territory codes with no CDC row. Real contributing counties: 2,618, a 3.1% overstatement. This is exactly the trap Chris names — a column that looks like a FIPS is not a FIPS until you count distinct and sample. (2) 249,740 violations is the pre-join total; 3,044 sit on FIPS codes with no matching CDC county-year, so 246,696 actually enter the analysis. (3) The poisoning leg is 3,141 counties, not 3,140.

The join_keys sentence is wrong about what joined. "PROGRAM_LINKS.FIPS_CODE = POISONING.FIPS by year (40,827 of 40,831 county-years join)" describes a LEFT join as a match rate. The 4 missing rows are dropped by pop > 0 because POPULATION is an empty string on exactly 4 rows — not a join miss. The true county-year match rate is 18,392 of 40,827 = 45.0%. matched_rows: 40827 is the left leg's row count, not a matched-row count.

I then tried five ways to break the "dead on arrival" verdict and all failed. Within-year demeaned r = 0.015 (log 0.088). County-and-year two-way fixed effects r = -0.0014, which removes every state, county and national-trend effect and is the strongest test available. Restricting to the 2,618 counties that have any RCRA-linked facility (killing the zero inflation) gives -0.017. Violations per facility, a compliance-intensity measure with no population in the denominator, gives 0.008 with band means 10.60/11.02/10.91. Spearman rank is the largest at 0.102 and is the urbanisation proxy the two-way FE erases. Lagging exposure 3 and 5 years — the specification most likely to revive a toxic-exposure-then-deaths story — gives 0.022 and 0.027. State-by-year demeaned band means are -0.18, +0.31, +0.18, -0.11 per 100k: non-monotonic, spanning 0.5 against a mean rate of 10.8. The hunch is genuinely dead and the agent's read of it is right.

One confound the agent did not flag and should have. RCRA violation reporting intensity is a state-program artifact, not a measure of noncompliance: violations per 1,000 FRS-linked RCRAINFO facilities runs 10.3 in California (670,420 linked facilities, 6,889 violations across 53 counties) to 759.3 in Kansas, a 74x spread, median 284 across 52 states. South Dakota matches 13 of 858 county-years, 1.5%. So the 22,435 "0 none" county-years — 55% of the universe and the band carrying the 9.75 headline — are partly "the state did not report." This does not change the null (the two-way FE removes it) but it would poison any future hunch that uses RCRA violation counts as an exposure level across states.

Minor: the tier_reason says RCRA determination dates run "1980s-2026". Actual range is 01/01/0001 to 12/31/2025, with 53 rows before 1980. Does not affect the tier.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 holds under Chris's definition. Chain holds end to end with no fan-out, a first number exists and reproduces, and both legs carry real dates: RCRA by DATE_VIOLATION_DETERMINED year (708,114 of 708,114 parse, 1801-2025), CDC by a YEAR column running 1999-2015. Same-year, change-over-time, lagged and fixed-effect designs all ran. A null result is still Tier 1 — the tier grades the chain, not the answer. Tier 3 would require a missing leg, and every leg here is landed: FED_EPA_RCRA_VIOLATIONS (708,114), FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY (53,387), and the FRS links mart (1,598,046 RCRAINFO rows). I LIKE-searched all_landing_tables.txt for RCRA and poisoning: no alternate-name version of either leg exists, and FED_EPA_ECHO (3.16M) is the only other possible county route.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun walks the same FRS_PROGRAM_LINKS bridge to put a facility in a county, so it inherits any geocoding error the agent inherited. I never validated a single county assignment against an independent source — not FED_EPA_RCRA_FACILITIES' own STATE_CODE/ZIP_CODE, not its LATITUDE83/LONGITUDE83. If FRS mis-assigns counties for a whole class of facilities, both runs read the same false zero and a real signal stays invisible. Second, the outcome is interval-censored into 2-point bands (16 of them, top band '>30' open-ended on 547 rows, 1.3% of the window). A midpoint reconstruction cannot resolve an effect smaller than roughly 2 deaths per 100k, so a small true association is undetectable to both runs by construction. Third, I tested correlation only — Pearson, Spearman, demeaned, lagged. A threshold effect (a handful of extreme-violation counties with extreme death rates) would not show up in any of them.
new_traps: FED_EPA_FRS_FRS_PROGRAM_LINKS.FIPS_CODE for PGM_SYS_ACRNM='RCRAINFO' is not uniformly a 5-digit county FIPS: 738 null, 752 rows hold 2- or 3-char fragments ('005','050','000','999'), 4 are state-only 'XX000', 66 are PR/VI/GU territory codes. A bare count(distinct FIPS_CODE) on violating facilities reads 2,698 'counties' where only 2,618 are real US counties present in the CDC file - 3.1% inflation. Filter length(FIPS_CODE)=5 and join to a real county list before counting counties.

RCRA violation reporting intensity is a state-program artifact, not an exposure level: violations per 1,000 FRS-linked RCRAINFO facilities runs 10.3 in California (670,420 facilities, 6,889 violations 2003-2015) to 759.3 in Kansas, a 74x spread, median 284 across 52 states. South Dakota matches 13 of 858 county-years (1.5%). A zero-violation county-year means the state did not report, not that there was no noncompliance. Never use RCRA violation counts as a cross-state exposure measure without a state fixed effect.

ntile() on a change delta is non-deterministic when the delta has a tie block: 616 of 3,140 counties (19.6%) have exactly zero RCRA-rate change in both windows, so the Q3/Q4 boundary lands inside the tie mass and the quintile means shift between runs (5.18/4.85 one run, 5.15/4.88 the next). Break ties explicitly or report the quintile design as approximate.

FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY.POPULATION is an empty string (not null) on 4 rows - the same empty-string-not-null shape as LEIE UPIN and FCC EIN. And the column named ESTIMATED_AGE_ADJUSTED_DEATH_RATE_11_CATEGORIES_IN_RANGES carries 16 distinct bands, not 11; the top band '>30' is open-ended (547 rows in 2003-2015, 1.3%), so any midpoint for it is an assumption, not a value.

A left join reported as a match rate: writing '40,827 of 40,831 county-years join' for a LEFT JOIN describes the left leg's row count after an unrelated filter (pop > 0) as if it were the join's match rate. The real RCRA-to-poisoning county-year match rate is 18,392 of 40,827 = 45.0%. Always state the inner-join match count separately from the left leg's size.

Poisoning midpoint: 9.75 per 100k in county-years with zero violations, 11.03 under 10 violations per 100k, 10.82 at 10-30, 10.23 at 30+. Change 2005-09 to 2011-15 by RCRA-change quintile: poisoning rose roughly 5.1, 4.7, 5.2, 4.9, 5.0 in every quintile alike (quintile edges are unstable because 616 of 3,140 counties tie at zero change). The poisoning leg is 40,827 county-years at 3,141 counties; the chain is a LEFT join and only 18,392 of those county-years (45.0%) carry any RCRA violation, drawn from 246,696 violations at 2,618 real counties, not 249,740 at 2,698. verdicts.title: Penalty deserts, reversed
verdicts.rerun_number: 89.17% unpenalized — 15,901 of 17,832 SNC facilities with a county FIPS (ECHO snapshot, penalties dated 2021–2026). Reproduced to the digit, 0.00% deviation, from SQL I wrote myself.
verdicts.reason:
WHAT HELD (rebuilt independently, not copied)

Every headline figure reproduced exactly: 17,832 SNC-with-FIPS, 15,901 zero-penalty, 0.8917, 11,141 no-formal-action, 33,978 chronic, 30,596 chronic unpenalized, quintiles 91.4/85.6/88.8/89.5/89.7, bands 90.9/86.9/83.0, deserts Mingo 82/82, Lewis 72/72, Boone 60/60, Benton 57/57.

Join keys are real, both sides.
- ECHO grain: 3,157,891 rows, 3,135,553 distinct non-blank FRS_ID on 3,135,553 non-blank rows. FRS_ID is unique where present. No fan-out. matched_rows 17,832 = 17,832 facilities. Entity count is honest.
- FAC_PROGRAMS_WITH_SNC is a clean integer, not the code list I expected: '0' 3,137,055 / '1' 20,720 / '2' 114 / '3' 2. The SNC definition is sound.
- FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES: zero blanks, zero unparseable, 3,136,764 literal '0', 21,127 positive. "$0" means $0, not missing. coalesce is doing no damage.
- FIPS: 5-digit on both sides, 3,229 ECHO / 2,902 VERA-2019-with-rate, 2,901 matched, 1 VERA-only.
- FAC_SNC_FLG 'N' on all 3,157,891 rows. Confirmed constant.

And the central finding got STRONGER under attack. Restricted to states with 300+ SNC facilities (kills the state-composition confound), the minority gradient steepens: 91.46 / 88.78 / 82.06% unpenalized. Not a Simpson artifact.

WHAT BREAKS

1. REAL — the penalty-size number is two facilities. The majority-minority band has 504 penalized facilities and $511,063,509. Altair Recycling TX ($181,012,404) and EES Coke MI ($100,728,768) are 55% of that. Trimmed means: drop the top facility per band and it is $656,165 vs $355,291; drop two and $456,817 vs $312,803. Medians are $30,000 vs $14,625. The claim leads with "$1,014,015 vs $405,639" as its evidence — a mean on a heavy-tailed 504-observation distribution. The unpenalized SHARE is the robust evidence; the mean is not, and 2.5x collapses to 1.46x on a two-facility trim.

2. REAL — the novelty sentence is wrong. overlap_check says this "finds the minority gradient runs opposite to the mart's framing." The mart LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__EPA_PENALTY_GAP produces the same reversal with one GROUP BY: unpenalized 90.32% (not majority-minority) vs 85.83% (majority-minority), mean penalty $210,377 vs $441,118. The mart does not frame it the other way; it just was never grouped. The one genuinely new leg — VERA jail rate — is the leg that came back null (flat quintiles). The new part is null; the carrying part is a group-by away from an existing mart.

3. MINOR — "majority-minority tracts" is a geography that is not in the chain. FAC_PERCENT_MINORITY is a facility-level demographic column; the only geography joined is a 5-digit county FIPS. Say "facilities whose surrounding population is majority-minority," never "tracts."

4. MINOR — the census inner join silently deletes 11 FIPS from the desert ranking, including all eight Connecticut counties (09001–09015, superseded by planning regions), 02261/02270 (retired Alaska), 46113 (renamed Oglala Lakota): 222 SNC facilities, 209 unpenalized. It did not change the top four (I reran the ranking without the census join and got the identical Mingo/Lewis/Boone/Benton), so the "true deserts" line survives — but three CT counties sit at 100% unpenalized and can never appear.

5. MINOR — "trailing five-year window" is stated as fact and has 24 counterexamples: SNC facilities with a positive FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES and a last-penalty date before 2021, one dated 1994. The window is approximately five years, not strictly.

6. MINOR, in the claim's favour — "11,141 have no formal action at all" uses the blank-date column. FAC_FORMAL_ACTION_COUNT reads 0 on 14,430 of the same 15,901. The claim took the conservative number. Fine, but the two columns disagree on 3,289 facilities.

SMALLEST FIX: replace the mean-penalty clause with the median plus the trimmed mean, drop "opposite to the mart's framing," and swap "tracts" for "surrounding population."
verdicts.corrected_claim: Penalty deserts, reversed: 89.2% of the 17,832 SNC facilities carrying a county FIPS (15,901) show $0 in ECHO's penalty column and 11,141 have no formal-action date at all — ECHO snapshot, penalties dated 2021–2026. The VERA 2019 jail-rate leg is null: 91.4, 85.6, 88.8, 89.5, 89.7% across quintiles. By facility minority share it runs the wrong way for the hunch and that part is robust — 90.9% unpenalized under 25% minority, 86.9% at 25–50%, 83.0% at majority-minority, steepening to 91.5 / 88.8 / 82.1 inside the states with 300+ SNC facilities. The penalty-SIZE gap is not robust: the $1,014,015 vs $405,639 means rest on two facilities (Altair Recycling TX $181.0M, EES Coke MI $100.7M = 55% of the majority-minority band's dollars); trimming the top facility per band gives $656,165 vs $355,291 and the medians are $30,000 vs $14,625. True deserts: Mingo WV 82 of 82, Lewis WA 72 of 72, Boone WV 60 of 60, Benton WA 57 of 57 — 81 of Mingo's 82 are NPDES-only coal permits and Washington alone holds 2,444 SNC facilities at 98.4% unpenalized, so the mechanism is state primacy, not demographics. Tier 2: ECHO is one snapshot. Note the mart ENVIRONMENT__EPA_PENALTY_GAP already yields the same reversal with one GROUP BY (85.8% vs 90.3% unpenalized, mean $441,118 vs $210,377); the only new leg here is the one that returned null.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 stands, but for a narrower reason than stated. ECHO is a single snapshot with no vintage column — that alone forces Tier 2, since no before/after on enforcement is possible. The tier_reason also says "VERA gives one year of context," which is a choice, not a limit: XC_VERA_INCARCERATION_TRENDS is a 128,507-row panel with 3,045 counties in 2017, 3,042 in 2018, 3,049 in 2019. A jail-rate CHANGE leg is available and unused. Not Tier 1 under Chris's "directly testable as written" clause either — the claim as written was tested and reversed, and the surviving finding (a minority gradient in enforcement) needs a time axis to mean anything causal, which the ECHO leg cannot supply. Not Tier 3: no leg is missing, both tables are landed and joined.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun re-derives arithmetic from the same single ECHO snapshot the probe used, so it cannot see whether ECHO's penalty column is COMPLETE. A facility fined by a state agency that does not push to ICIS reads $0 here and looks identical to a facility nobody touched. "Unpenalized" may be "unreported," and if reporting completeness correlates with state — which the WA 98.4% / MO 97.8% / WV 95.6% pattern hints at — then every share in the claim, including the minority gradient, is partly a reporting artifact and I have no second enforcement source in the warehouse to test it against. Second blind spot: I never compared this ECHO snapshot to a prior vintage, so I cannot tell whether the 2026 load dropped or added facilities relative to when the penalty window was computed. Third: I checked FAC_PERCENT_MINORITY for sentinels (min 0, max 100, 312 exact zeros, 971 null among SNC — clean) but I cannot verify from inside the warehouse what radius EPA used to compute it, so the geography under the claim's central finding is unverified by me.

LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__EPA_PENALTY_GAP.LAST_PENALTY_SHARED_FACILITY_N maxes at 3,013,568 — the no-penalty rows are all lumped into one giant 'shared case'. 81,068 of 93,808 rows read >1. Filter LAST_PENALTY_AMT > 0 before using it as a fan-out counter.

LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__EPA_PENALTY_GAP.IN_MAJORITY_MINORITY_COMMUNITY is NULL on 29,702 of 93,808 rows (31.7%), and that null bucket is 99.59% unpenalized — the least-penalized third of the mart. Grouping on the boolean without handling NULL silently drops it.

FED_EPA_ECHO.FAC_SNC_FLG is 'N' on all 3,157,891 rows — a constant, not a filter. The real significant-noncompliance signal is FAC_PROGRAMS_WITH_SNC, an integer count: '0' on 3,137,055 rows, '1' on 20,720, '2' on 114, '3' on 2.

FED_EPA_ECHO.FRS_ID is blank on 22,338 of 3,157,891 rows; distinct non-blank FRS_ID = 3,135,553 = the non-blank row count exactly, so it IS unique where present. The mart ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_ECHO holds 3,135,554 rows because it drops them — any landing-vs-mart row-count comparison is off by 22,337 and it is not a load failure.

FED_EPA_ECHO.FAC_DERIVED_STCTY_FIPS holds 11 FIPS that XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY does not: all eight Connecticut counties (09001–09015, superseded by planning regions), 02261 and 02270 (retired Alaska census areas), and 46113 (renamed Oglala Lakota). An inner join to the census county file silently deletes Connecticut — 222 SNC facilities, 209 of them unpenalized, three CT counties at 100%. Empty string on 618,136 rows, never NULL, so `is not null` does not filter it.

FED_EPA_ECHO.FAC_FORMAL_ACTION_COUNT and FAC_DATE_LAST_FORMAL_ACTION disagree: among the 15,901 unpenalized SNC facilities the count column reads 0 on 14,430 but the date column is blank on only 11,141. 3,289 facilities carry a formal-action date and a zero count. Pick one and say which; the date column is the conservative choice.

FED_EPA_ECHO.FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES is only approximately a trailing five-year sum: 24 SNC facilities carry a positive total with a last-penalty date before 2021, one dated 1994. Do not state the five-year window as exact.

verdicts.reason:
Chain is real and reproduces. My independent rebuild hit every coverage number on the nose: 2,902 VERA 2019 counties with a jail rate (of 3,049), 2,902 of 2,902 matched to CDC and to QCEW 2022 with zero fan-out on either key, 1,213 / 1,421 / 1,402 unsuppressed suicide / homicide / overdose rates for 2019, 359 carrying all four in both years. Quintile suicide 10.22 15.84 16.17 17.57 14.81; wage 1,021 987 937 935 888; Pearson r jail x suicide19 -0.0917, x homicide19 -0.0301. All inside 1%.

Two things break. FIRST, the headline. avg(o19) and avg(o24) run over DIFFERENT county sets. In the top quintile 70 counties have a 2019 overdose rate and no 2024 (their mean is 8.19) and 71 other counties have 2024 and no 2019 (mean 27.12) — CDC suppresses at 1-9 deaths, so counties churn in and out of visibility as deaths rise. Balance the panel and the top quintile goes 16.76 -> 20.19, +20.5%, and the bottom quintile goes from +7.4% to -3.1%. The sentence "top-jail-quintile counties went 14.0 to 22.5" says those counties moved. They did not; the cohort did. Direction of the gradient survives, size is a third of the claim.

SECOND, the correlations are not robust. TOTAL_JAIL_POP_RATE tops out at 26,666.7 per 100k on FIPS 28055 — 27% of the 15-64 population in jail, impossible — and 42 of 2,902 counties exceed 3,000. Top quintile mean 1,631.7 vs median 991.8; quintiles 1-4 have mean = median. Trim to <=3,000 and both correlations FLIP positive: suicide +0.1435, homicide +0.1074 (n=1,198). Spearman on the full 1,213 suicide cohort is +0.1935. So "the violence leg does not hold" is a fact about Pearson on a broken tail, not about counties.

Two more real caveats, not blockers. The unsuppressed cohort is zero-inflated: 161 of 345 bottom-quintile 2019 overdose rates are exactly 0.00, and 275 of 352 bottom-quintile homicide rates are 0.00 (COUNT_SUP='0' is a true zero-death county). And the monotone wage fall is half composition — inside urbanicity strata it is rural 913 -> 858 and small/mid 1,029 -> 961, about -6%, against -13% overall, because quintile 5 is 73% rural and quintile 1 is 56%.

Credit where due, and it matters for the repo: the agent is RIGHT that .claude/traps.md line 83 is wrong. FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY holds 7 PERIODs (2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, TTM) and 6 INTENTs including Drug_OD, FA_Deaths, FA_Suicide, FA_Homicide — not one trailing-12-month window with no overdose. GEOID is a clean key: 3,144 distinct on 132,000 rows, zero duplicate GEOID+INTENT+PERIOD groups. That correction should be written back, and matrix hunches 9 ("no overdose in the injury file") and 19 ("county overdose ends 2015") are now stale because of it.

Key checks both sides. VERA 2019: 3,049 rows, 3,049 distinct COUNTY_FIPS, no dupes, all length 5, sample 01001 Autauga 516.94 / 01003 Baldwin 524.48 / 01005 Barbour 445.36. 147 blanks are empty strings as the agent said. Connecticut is absent entirely from VERA 2019 (zero rows on '09%') — unified-jail states are not in the jail leg, so the 2,902 universe is not the whole country. QCEW AGGLVL_CODE='71' + OWN_CODE='5': 3,274 rows, 3,274 distinct AREA_FIPS, one INDUSTRY_CODE (10), one YEAR (2022 is the only year in all 3,619,437 rows), zero multi-row FIPS; 6 of the 2,902 joined rows carry DISCLOSURE_CODE='N' with wage 0.

No sentinel, rounding or cap traps fired against the agent: try_to_number(x,18,6) used throughout, the -999 sentinel (6,549 rows) is filtered by RATE_M, no PORTAL_ or sample table is in the chain, no name match, no USASpending lifetime total.

verdicts.title: Quality bonus, same lunches
verdicts.rerun_number: 240,329 of 453,202 distinct QPP NPIs (53.0%) took an Open Payments PY2024 payment, across 5,471,265 payment rows; within-specialty top-money-decile share reads penalty 10.3%, zero 13.1%, small bonus 9.2%, top bonus 10.1%
verdicts.reason: Every load-bearing number reproduced from my own SQL, within 1%: 453,202 distinct QPP NPIs, 240,329 matched (53.0%), bands 32,030 / 23,481 / 149,302 / 248,389 exact, deciles 10.3 / 13.1 / 9.2 / 10.1 against the claimed 10.3 / 13.0 / 9.2 / 10.1. The chain is real. FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS is PROGRAM_YEAR='2024' on all 15,385,047 rows, dates 01/01/2024 to 12/31/2024, one value. QPP NPI is a clean key: 503,917 rows, 453,202 distinct, zero nulls, zero blanks, zero '0000000000' sentinel, all length 10, PROVIDER_KEY unique per row. The people are the same people: 239,838 of 240,329 matched NPIs are NPPES ENTITY_TYPE_CODE 1, and all 10 sampled matched NPIs carry the same first and last name in Open Payments and NPPES (POOLE/ID, GELBFISH/NY, KOLISEK/IN and seven more). Three separate defects push this to CORRECTED rather than CONFIRMED. First, the 0.2-point headline direction is tie-assignment noise. 212,873 of 453,202 NPIs (47.0%) hold exactly $0, so ntile(10) splits a tie block: 3,022 of 45,281 decile-10 members have $0. Three differently-written versions of the same query returned 3,306, then 3,299, then 3,278 penalty-band NPIs in decile 10 (10.32%, 10.30%, 10.23%) while top bonus held at 10.12%, so the gap slid from +0.21pp to +0.11pp on nothing but a changed select list. Two tie-free cuts reverse the sign: ranking against each specialty's percentile_cont(0.90) gives penalty 9.5% vs top bonus 9.6%; ranking only the paid gives penalty 9.1% vs top bonus 10.2%. The agent's own read (flat, a miss) survives all three methods; the sentence asserting a direction does not. Second, the zero band is mischaracterized. It is not 'score exactly 75.00' as a measured score: 24,921 of its 26,071 rows (95.6%) carry EXTREME_UNCONTROLLABLE_CIRCUMSTANCE_EUC='True', and all 25,632 rows with FINAL_SCORE exactly 75.00 in the whole file sit in this band. That is CMS's assigned neutral score for hardship reweighting. Its 13.0% is the one figure stable across all three methods (13.1 / 12.8 / 10.9), and it means hardship-exempt clinicians outearn their specialty peers in industry money, which is a different and better story than the one claimed. Third, matched_rows: 240329 is an entity count in a field named rows; the actual matched Open Payments row count is 5,471,265. Two smaller gaps: band membership is rollup-dependent, since 20,802 NPIs straddle bands and min(adj) instead of max(adj) moves the penalty band from 32,030 to 37,334 NPIs, a 17% swing; and the overlap_check sentence 'a table pair not used before' is false against hunch_matrix_refined_2026-09-05.md line 136, where hunch 6's chain reads '...QPP HPSA status, FINAL_SCORE to OPEN_PAYMENTS'. Tier 2 is right: LIKE-search of all_landing_tables.txt and marts.json returns exactly one QPP table each (503,917 rows), no year column, no second vintage under another name.

The score leg does not: FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE has no year, date or period column (the only match on a YEAR ilike is YEARS_IN_MEDICARE, a tenure integer), a single _INGESTED_AT value of 2026-08-05T15:07:05.524, and _SOURCE_RUN_ID unique on all 503,917 rows so it cannot mark loads. verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun hit the same two landed tables with a differently-written query, so it can only catch errors in how the join was assembled, not errors in the files themselves. Three things it cannot see. First, I cannot confirm the QPP file is PY2024. There is no year column, no registry URL and no notes; the M1366-M1370 MVP-id argument rests on external knowledge of CMS's PY2024 MVP additions that I could not check against any landed source. I verified the file holds exactly 16 distinct MVP ids and an adjustment range of -9.00 to +1.05, which is consistent with PY2024 but also with PY2022 and PY2023 on the range alone. If the QPP snapshot is actually PY2022 or PY2023, the whole 'same year' basis of the tier reason falls and nothing in my rerun would flag it. verdicts.rerun_number: 14.77 federally reportable air violations per 10,000 manufacturing jobs in the bottom manufacturing-wage quartile ($926/week, QCEW 2022) vs 9.63 in the top ($1,701) — a 1.53x gradient, FRVs dated 2021-2023
verdicts.reason:
The chain holds and the entity counts are exact. I rebuilt the county bridge a different way (distinct STUSPS->STATEFP map, then STATEFP||right(FIPS_CODE,3), existence-checked against the census file) and got byte-identical results to the agent's STUSPS/COUNTYFP join: 262,643 AIR PGM_SYS_IDs mapped, 262,643 agreements on a full outer join. Reproduced exactly: 2,877 joined counties, 1,541 with a violation, 14,996 FRVs in 1,617 counties, 2,003 counties at mfg_emp>=500, correlation -0.00507, top-quartile rate 9.63, and the 35,530-of-35,537 (99.98%) violator ID match.

THREE CORRECTIONS.

(1) real. The headline 14.9 is not reproducible. Three deterministic tie-breaks (order by mfg_wage,geoid / ,geoid desc / ,mfg_emp desc) all return 14.77. NTILE(4) over an integer wage column leaves 13 counties sitting exactly on the three cut values ($1,044, $1,184, $1,363); Marion County FL sits at exactly $1,044 with 10,150 manufacturing jobs, and whether it lands in Q1 or Q2 moves the headline 0.9% (Q1 employment 944,701 in the agent's run vs 952,581 in mine, difference 7,880 = 10,150 minus 2,270, i.e. one county swapped for another). Gradient is 1.53x, not 1.55x.

(2) blocker for the story, not the join. The mechanism the hunch names dies under the obvious restriction. 58% of the FRVs (8,017 of 13,817) are at NAICS 31-33 facilities, so restricting the numerator to manufacturing air sources is a fair test, and it flattens the gradient: 5.76 / 7.75 / 6.94 / 5.90 per 10k across the wage quartiles — non-monotone, Q1 = 0.98x of Q4. Per manufacturing facility the direction REVERSES: 0.076 violations per mfg facility in the lowest-wage quartile vs 0.122 in the highest. The entire 1.53x is permitted-source density: 237.9 air facilities per 10,000 manufacturing jobs in Q1 vs 144.6 in Q4 (1.65x), and 75.5 vs 48.2 manufacturing facilities per 10,000 jobs (1.57x). The hunch's hit_means ("the same employers cut both corners") is refuted, not merely unproven; its miss_means is what survives. The claim sentence already carries the correlation and the flat per-facility rate, so it is honest, but the first number as written invites the reading the data kills.

Related: "per air facility the rate is flat, 0.059-0.066" is true of FRV COUNT per facility (I get 0.0620 / 0.0648 / 0.0588 / 0.0662) but false of the SHARE of air facilities in violation, which is monotone 4.72% / 4.23% / 3.51% / 3.14% — a 1.50x gradient. Two denominators, opposite readings; only one is stated.

(3) real. 27 QCEW areas holding 237,582 manufacturing jobs at 500+ jobs each carry frvs=0 by construction, because their AREA_FIPS has no row in the census county file so the left join can never land. Eight are Connecticut: QCEW 2022 uses old county FIPS 09001-09015, XC_CENSUS_CB_COUNTY is the 2023 vintage with planning regions 09110-09190, and every CT air facility carries FIPS_CODE 'CT001'-'CT015'. Connecticut actually has 94 FRVs at 75 facilities in the 2021-2023 window and reads as clean. The other 19 are 'XX999' unknown-area rows carrying $2,088-$3,899 weekly wages, all of which land in the top quartile with zero violations. Dropping all 27: 15.07 vs 9.93, 1.52x, correlation +0.00046. Not decisive, but the denominators as run are wrong. Separately, 16,905 of 279,548 AIR facilities (6.0%) never reach a county at all — 'CO000' (3,790), 'KS000' (1,386), 'NM000' (1,318) unknown-county codes plus the CT vintage break.

TRAP CLASSES, all checked and clean: no sentinel in either join key; try_to_number(x,18,6) was used and the columns are integer text anyway (bare avg 1163.6424 = scaled avg 1163.6424, so the rounding trap is inert here); no PORTAL_ table, no HMDA sample, no USASPENDING cap, no SAM_EXCLUSIONS sample; no duplicate-row fanout on any leg; no name matching; no USASpending lifetime totals. verdicts.title: Decriminalization states, emptier jails, more overdoses
verdicts.rerun_number: 824 counties (824 distinct COUNTY_FIPS, no fan-out); correlation of percent jail-rate change 2019-2023 with overdose-rate change 2019-2024 = -0.0107
verdicts.reason:
Chain holds and the join is exactly reproducible. I rebuilt it with conditional aggregation on both sides instead of the agent's VERA self-join and got the identical cohort: VERA 1,945 county pairs, CDC 1,184 unsuppressed pairs, 824 joined, 824 distinct FIPS. Join keys are real: VERA COUNTY_FIPS is 5-char, 3,075 distinct all-years, 2,090 in 2023, unique per (fips,year) at 128,507/128,507; CDC GEOID is 5-char, 3,144 distinct, unique per (GEOID,PERIOD) at 22,000/22,000 for Drug_OD; all 2,090 VERA 2023 FIPS match CDC (100%). Samples on both sides are plain county FIPS ('01003' Baldwin County AL both sides). Matched rows = distinct entities, so 824 is an entity count.

Three things in the claim are wrong.

(1) The entity split contradicts itself. "12 in Washington, 15 in Oregon, 812 elsewhere" sums to 839, not the stated 824. Truth: 12 WA + 15 OR + 797 elsewhere = 824.

(2) "The other 49 states: jail -9.4%, overdose +0.99" is the wrong group. The agent's split was `case when st='WA' then 'WA' else 'other 49'`, so the control contains Oregon - one of the two states the hunch is about. Excluding Oregon properly: 797 counties, jail -9.2%, overdose +0.71, median 0.0.

(3) "+2.33 per 100k" for the bottom jail quintile is a tie-break coin flip, not a fact. FIPS 51177 Stafford VA and 51179 Spotsylvania VA both sit at exactly -27.8289% jail change straddling the Q1/Q2 boundary at row 165/166, with overdose deltas -8.8 and -1.6. Swapping which one lands in Q1 moves the mean by 7.2/165 = 0.0436, i.e. 2.29 -> 2.334 -> 2.33. Deterministic (order by pj, fips), stable over three runs: +2.29. That is a 1.7% swing on a headline sub-figure.

Everything else reproduces exactly: corr -0.011; Q5 +32.8% jail / +0.39 overdose; WA 12 counties, -33.2% jail, 14.40 -> 39.75 per 100k, +25.35, 12 of 12 up, 0 down; OR 15 counties, -20.0% jail, +15.98; and the six-of-twelve list among counties that cut jail 40%+ is exact - Yakima +39.0, Thurston +27.1, King +24.2, Chelan +23.3, Clallam +18.0, Snohomish +13.4, sitting among TN Roane +48.7, AL Walker +38.1, NY Bronx +21.5, AL Etowah +17.2, AZ Coconino +13.1, VA Portsmouth +11.5.

The bigger problem is framing, not arithmetic: the jail leg carries none of the finding that survives. Rank states by mean overdose-rate change 2019->2024 on unsuppressed counties with NO VERA join at all - Washington #1 at +22.78 (20 counties), Oregon #2 at +14.98 (16), Maine #3 at +10.20, California #4 at +9.28. So the two-state cluster is a pure CDC-side fact. Inside Washington the ordering runs against the story: Whatcom GREW its jail 9.8% and rose +32.7; Spokane cut jail only 15.2% and had WA's largest rise at +41.8; Snohomish cut jail 49.6% and rose the least at +13.4. The hunch's miss_means half-concedes this; the title does not.

One softening of the national null. Requiring RATE_M=0 in both years keeps only counties with 0 or >=10 overdose deaths in both, which is outcome-correlated selection. Median delta by flag transition: kept cohort (0,0; n=1,184) median 0.00; grew past the threshold (1->0; n=406) median +8.10; fell below (0->1; n=371) median +8.90; small in both (1,1; n=1,180) median +2.20. The WA/OR result survives this - with no suppression filter at all WA reads 14 counties, -36.1% jail, +25.81 overdose. The agent's cohort is clean on the sentinel it never named: RATE carries CDC's -999 sentinel on 822 Drug_OD rows, and all 822 sit on RATE_M=1 rows, so RATE_M=0 excluded them twice over. My rerun omitted the >=0 guard entirely and still got 824, which proves it.

No county overdose series after 2015 is landed"), reports/hunch_matrix_refined_2026-09-05.md:151 ("no overdose in the injury file") and :51 ("county overdose ends 2015"). verdicts.rerun_number: $70,776,831.96 in Open Payments PY2023 general-payment dollars to 8,957 distinct NPIs across 105,057 payment records (my own EXISTS-form rerun against each affidavit row's own window; exact match to the claimed $70,776,832, 0.00% apart)
verdicts.reason: I rebuilt the load-bearing join from scratch in a different shape — an EXISTS against each affidavit row's own [effective, end] window instead of the agent's min(eff)/max(end) collapse — and every headline number came back identical: $70,776,831.96, 8,957 distinct NPIs, Royalty or License 78 NPIs / $43,271,720.44, opt-out-file specialty Orthopedic Surgery 159 NPIs / $33,396,098.24, 163 also on a facility affiliation, 12 of those at $100k+, 8,023 in 2022, 9,401 in 2024. Maxwell (NPI 1295737930, GEORGE, TN) is 7 AbbVie records: 5 ALLODERM Royalty or License rows totalling $11,600,124 plus 2 Food and Beverage rows of $196.24, sum $11,600,320.24, none third-party, none disputed. The Part B kill-check reproduces too: 1,856 opt-out NPIs in the DY2024 by-provider file, 17 opted out for all of 2024, $64,132.84 total, largest single $8,841.39. QPP 68. Both keys are real IDs, not name matches. Opt-out NPI: 57,209 rows, 56,455 distinct, 0 null, 0 blank, 0 sentinel '0000000000', 0 rows off length 10, 0 unparsed dates, samples are plain 10-digit NPIs with names and specialties. Open Payments 2023: RECORD_ID unique on all 14,700,786 rows so no double load, PROGRAM_YEAR '2023' on every row, payment dates 2023-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 44,233 blank NPIs are the teaching-hospital rows and cannot join. No fan-out: the affidavit side is grouped to one row per NPI, so the dollar sum is over payment records only. Four gaps. (1) matched_rows is stated as 8957, which is the entity count; the matched payment-row count is 105,057 and the spec asks for both. (2) The date test is one-sided. min(OPTOUT_END_DATE) is 2026-06-30 and zero rows end before 2024, so 'between effective and end' collapses to 'payment date >= effective date' for every year tested. It still does real work — dropping the date test gives 11,779 NPIs and $92,479,625.97, so the effective-date bound removes $21.7M and 2,822 people — but 'both legs dated' oversells a test where only one bound can ever bind. (3) The 2022/2023/2024 series reads as growth and is roster growth. The number of roster NPIs already opted out at each January 1 goes 25,324, 27,771, 34,255; the paid rate is 31.7%, 32.3%, 27.4%, flat then down. Hold the cohort fixed to the 25,324 opted out before 2022-01-01 and the money falls: $85,267,993 in 2022, $66,289,144 in 2023, $56,073,173 in 2024, with royalties $44,847,265 to $41,796,079 to $33,789,575. Printing 8,023 / 8,957 / 9,401 without the denominator points the reader the wrong way. (4) $6,285,734, 8.9% of the $70.8M, carries THIRD_PARTY_PAYMENT_RECIPIENT_INDICATOR of 'Entity' or 'Individual' — reported under the clinician's NPI but paid to someone else at their direction; $1,773,492 of the royalty total is in that bucket. 'Paid to 8,957 clinicians' is 8.9% high on money in hand. Two scope floors worth stating, neither an error: only the GENERAL payments file is landed for each year (94 columns, no principal-investigator column, no research or ownership file), so $70.8M is a floor on industry money; and the affidavit file is a 2026-07-26 roster of who is currently opted out, so anyone opted out during 2023 who rejoined Medicare before that ingest is invisible. One number that helps the hunch and the agent did not run: across all of PY2023, Royalty or License reached 2,515 NPIs for $627,477,128, so these 78 people took 6.9% of the royalty money as 3.1% of the recipients, $554,766 each against $249,494 for the field, 2.2x over-represented. That is the strongest sentence available and it is not in the claim.

verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 holds under Chris's definition, but not for the reason given. The chain holds, the first number is exact on an independent rerun, and the claim is directly testable as written and was tested. Open Payments carries three real program years (2022, 2023, PY2024 in the unsuffixed table), and the opt-out leg, though one snapshot ingested 2026-07-26, carries per-provider effective dates that do genuine before/after work — dropping them moves the cohort from 11,779 NPIs and $92,479,626 to 8,957 and $70,776,832. So it is not cross-section only and Tier 2 does not fit. What fails is the stated tier_reason. 'Both legs dated' is half true: min(OPTOUT_END_DATE) is 2026-06-30, zero windows end before 2024, so the end-date bound is inert on every year tested. And 'tested year by year across 2022, 2023 and 2024' produced a series that is roster growth — the eligible roster runs 25,324 / 27,771 / 34,255 while the fixed pre-2022 cohort's money falls $85.3M to $56.1M. Tier 1 with a one-sided window and a non-trend.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun uses the same two tables and the same NPI equality the agent used, so any error inside CMS's own data passes straight through me. If an affidavit carries a stale or mistyped NPI that now belongs to a different clinician, I match it and cannot see it — I never checked a single NPI against NPPES or any outside register. I also cannot measure the survivorship hole: there is one vintage of FED_CMS_OPT_OUT_AFFIDAVITS in the warehouse, so everyone who was opted out during 2023 and rejoined Medicare before the 2026-07-26 ingest is invisible to both of us, and I have no second snapshot to size that loss. Third, I take CMS's NATURE_OF_PAYMENT_OR_TRANSFER_OF_VALUE label at face value: I confirmed 464 rows say 'Royalty or License' and that Maxwell's five big rows name ALLODERM, but nothing I ran can tell a real royalty from a consulting fee filed under the wrong nature. Fourth, I only ran the money leg through 2024 — the file has no 2025 vintage, so the falling-money finding rests on three points, and a fourth year could bend it. Finally, my query counts payment records; a manufacturer that reports one royalty as twelve monthly rows and another that reports it as one annual row both sum correctly but give per-payment averages I did not attempt to defend.

verdicts.rerun_number: $47,183,439.46 to 169 growers in PY2023 (from $286,786.31 in PY2022, $21,545,209.91 in PY2024) — exact to the cent
verdicts.reason:
REBUILT THE JOIN MYSELF, DIFFERENT SQL. Three independent per-table rollups full-outer-joined on trim(NPI), scale 18,6 (not the agent's union-all pivot at 18,2), no teaching-hospital string filter. Same answer to the cent: 169 growers, $286,786.31 / $47,183,439.46 / $21,545,209.91, 110 under $1k + 59 in $1k-$10k. Field band E = 1,330,123 any-year NPIs minus the 4,451 in bands A-D = 1,325,672. Every number in the claim reproduces.

KEY CHECKED BOTH SIDES. OP2023 NPI: 14,700,786 rows, 933,620 distinct incl. one empty string = 933,619 real; zero '0000000000', zero non-10-char, zero non-numeric; heaviest key 1,153 rows (JAIN) so the per-NPI rollup is doing real work. RECORD_ID is unique in all three tables (13,306,564 / 14,700,786 / 15,385,047) — no reload dupes inflating dollars. TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_PAYMENT_USDOLLARS: zero unparseable, zero negative, in all three years. Part D summary NPI is unique (1,416,883 / 1,416,883) so no fan-out. QPP is 503,917 rows on 453,202 NPIs — the agent grouped first, so no fan-out there either.

ENTITY COUNT IS REAL. 169 rows = 169 people, not 169 rows: the 169 NPIs map to 169 distinct COVERED_RECIPIENT_PROFILE_IDs, max 1 profile per NPI. Samples: 1154312536/187955 HACK, 1104069798/593764 RYDER, 1215029210/100020 CHUDIK, 1053320010/320110 SCHEINBERG, 1033189162/228365 KALLMES.

THE HARDEST TEST I COULD THINK OF, AND IT PASSED. "$0 in 2022" could be an NPI-join artifact (blank NPI on 5,497 physician rows in the 2022 file). Re-ran the 2022 leg keyed on CMS profile id instead of NPI: 101 of 169 profiles appear in PY2022, total $286,786.31 — identical, $0 hidden under blank-NPI rows, and zero growers would fail the under-$10k test. The cohort survives a second key.

VINTAGES ARE REAL, NOT ASSUMED. PROGRAM_YEAR is single-valued per table: 2022 / 2023 / 2024, payment dates inside each year. Registry URLs back it: OP_DTL_GNRL_PGYR2024_P06302025 for the unsuffixed table, MUP_DPR_RY24_..._DY22_NPIBN.csv for the drug file, "Data year 2024, release RY26" for the Part D summary. Independent proof the two Part D files are different years: the DY2022 drug file (a suppressed subset) EXCEEDS the DY2024 summary on 14 of 59 growers, impossible if same vintage.

WHAT I WOULD CHANGE — three real gaps, none of them kills the claim sentence.
1. "QPP PY2024" is unsupported. The table has no performance-year column, its registry row is empty (URL null, NOTES null), and the repo's own matrix says so at hunch_matrix_refined_2026-09-05.md:196 "QPP registry row has no URL or notes; vintage unrecorded." The agent's own registry probe errored (p0_checks.json qpp_registry: schema 'LIBRARY_RAW.LIBRARY_META' does not exist). MVP columns imply PY2023 or later; ingested 2026-08-05. Fix: say "QPP, vintage unrecorded."
2. The one claimed signal rides a censored column. FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS.BRND_TOT_CLMS is an EMPTY STRING on 622,278 of 1,416,883 rows (43.9%) — CMS blanks 1-10 brand claims. The agent's p0 check read "BRND_FILLED 1,416,883" = 100%, the classic empty-string-is-not-null miss. For the growers, 28 of 80 drop out, so "brand share 20.5% vs 15.9%" is 52 growers against a field with its small-brand prescribers deleted. Not random censoring.
3. overlap_check names the wrong nearest neighbour. reports/join_proof_2026-09-04.md Finding 1 already ran FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS (PY2024) x FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS on NPI with payment bands and brand share ($100k+ band 25.7% brand vs 16.6% for unpaid) — and reports/news_corroboration_map_2026-09-05.md:39 points straight at it ("Dollars for Docs, HIT"). The new mechanism (year-over-year jump cohort + two Part D vintages) is still new, but that report, not pharma_paid_excluded, is the thing to differentiate from.

MINOR, FOR THE RECORD. 68 of the 169 (40%) have no PY2022 row at all, and they carry $23.1M of the $47.2M — "from $286,787" is a sum over the 101 who actually appear (verified not an artifact, see above). The total is heavy-tailed: top NPI $4,846,659 = 10.3%, top 5 = 30%, top 25 = 54%. The PY2022/PY2023 tables are January-2026 republications while PY2024 is the June-2025 first release, so "half was gone by 2024" compares a restated file to a first-release one. The Part D growth leg is confounded by baseline size (growers averaged $281k of DY2022 drug cost vs $172k for the 1% sample; bigger books grow slower in ratio terms) on n=59.

verdicts.title: Top billers, top payees
verdicts.rerun_number: 18.19% of top-decile Part B billers are also top-decile Open Payments recipients within their specialty — 22,472 distinct NPIs of 123,529 top-decile billers, 1,235,757 individuals scored (Part B DY2024 x Open Payments general payments PY2023). Peer rate 9.09%, risk ratio 2.0x. Orthopedic Surgery: 487 both-top holding $100,869,984 of industry money and $281,917,756 of allowed charges — exact match.
verdicts.reason:
Chain and numbers reproduce. My independent rebuild (own SQL, try_to_number(x,18,6), explicit join instead of USING) returns 22,472 both-top vs the agent's 22,473 — a 0.004% ntile tie-break plan artifact, not instability; the agent's exact SQL returns 22,473 on three consecutive runs. 18.19 vs 18.2 is 0.05%. Ortho 487 / $100,869,984 / $281,917,756 match to the dollar. Anesthesiology 1,481 (36.1%) and Physician Assistant 3,180 (28.3%) match.

Join keys are real. RNDRNG_NPI is 1:1 — 1,235,757 rows and 1,235,757 distinct at ENT_CD='I'; zero blanks, zero '0000000000', zero bad lengths. So matched_rows IS the entity count; the claim's entity count is honest. OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023.NPI: 933,619 distinct clean, 44,233 EMPTY STRINGS (not nulls) correctly filtered by the agent, sentinel count zero, PROGRAM_YEAR 100% '2023'. try_to_number at scale 2 vs scale 6 is identical on this money column ($2,502,695,708 both); bare would have been $110,691 off. Rows per OP NPI: avg 15.7, median 4, max 1,175 — the pre-aggregation to NPI grain kills the fan-out, so no double count.

Three things are wrong in the claim as written.

1. REAL. 'The payments are one year' is false. Three Open Payments vintages are landed: _2022 (13,306,564 rows), _2023 (14,700,786), and the UNSUFFIXED FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS which is PROGRAM_YEAR 2024, 100%, 15,385,047 rows, 979,137 distinct NPIs. The single-vintage constraint comes from Part B alone.

2. REAL. The year-aligned leg exists and was not used. Part B is DY2024 by the hunch's own proof, so PY2024 is the matching money file. Rerun against it: 18.12%, 502 both-top orthopedic surgeons, $84,910,390. The headline is robust to the swap, but the claim pairs DY2024 billing with PY2023 money and gives no reason.

3. REAL. The '10.0% baseline' is an ntile artifact, not a measurement — it is forced to 10.0% by construction. ntile(10) over a column that is 53.3% zeros puts 15,877 clinicians with literally $0 into the 'top industry-money decile'. Ten specialties have a top money decile that is 79-100% zero dollars: Physical Therapist 7,771 of 7,789 (99.8%), Occupational Therapist 1,130 of 1,130 (100%), Chiropractic 2,558 of 3,239 (79.0%), LCSW 1,639 of 1,643 (99.8%). Impact on the headline is small — 43 of 22,472 both-top have $0, 447 under $100 — and correcting it makes the finding STRONGER: 18.16% against a real-money baseline of 8.71%, a 2.09x ratio, and 2.0x against actual lower-decile peers at 9.09%.

MINOR scope caveat: FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 is the general-payments file only. Its nature classes sum exactly to its $2,502,695,708 total. No research-payments and no ownership-interest table is landed in LANDING at all. 'Industry money' in this claim excludes both. The ortho $100.9M is 79% Royalty or License ($627M royalty across only 14,416 rows file-wide).

All three of the agent's traps verify. _SOURCE_RUN_ID: 1,296,739 distinct on 1,296,739 rows. FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PROVIDER is a byte-identical twin — hash_agg = -2288124447057648988 on both sides, same 1,296,739 rows. DY2024 confirmed on three independent 2024-only HCPCS: G2211 (146,024 rows, 138,770 NPIs, 24,627,539 services), G0136 (2,437 rows), 99459 (4,170 rows), all payable from 2024-01-01; NPPES newest enumeration among Part B NPIs is 2024-12-30 with 17,317 in 2024 and zero in 2025 (agent said 16,978, likely the ENT_CD='I' subset; not load-bearing).

REPO CONTRADICTION worth Chris's eye: c:/Code/Ripple_v6/reports/partb_carbon_date_2026-09-05.md line 67 concludes 'DY2022 the strong inference' for this same table. G2211 cannot exist before 2024-01-01. That report is wrong by two years and should be marked.

Named surgeons are single people, not name collisions: NPI 1932140266 (Booth) 1 profile ID, 4 rows, $8,459,144 all Royalty or License; 1639113863 (Scuderi) 1 profile, $5,668,749; 1780680074 (Frankle) 1 profile, $4,698,957.

Verdict is CORRECTED not CONFIRMED only because the claim sentence handed to me asserts 'the payments are one year', which the warehouse contradicts, and presents a construction artifact as a measured baseline. Every number survives.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Top billers, top payees: 18.2% of top-decile Part B billers are also top-decile Open Payments recipients within their specialty, against 9.1% of their lower-decile peers — a 2.0x risk ratio (Part B DY2024, general payments PY2023); the 487 both-top orthopedic surgeons hold $100,869,984 of 2023 industry money, 79% of it royalty and license dollars, and $281,917,756 of Medicare allowed charges. Matched rows 22,473, every one a distinct NPI (RNDRNG_NPI is 1:1 across the 1,235,757 ENT_CD='I' rows), out of 123,529 top-decile Part B billers; Anesthesiology 1,481 (36.1%), Physician Assistant 3,180 (28.3%), Orthopedic Surgery 487 (22.5%). The 10.0% baseline is an ntile artifact, not a measurement — 15,877 clinicians in the top money decile received $0, so the real-money baseline is 8.71% and the true ratio is 2.09x. Industry money here is general payments only; no research or ownership file is landed. Tier 2 because Part B is a single snapshot with no date column — Open Payments is landed for three years (2022, 2023, and the unsuffixed table which is PY2024), and re-running against the year-aligned PY2024 file gives 18.1% and 502 both-top orthopedic surgeons holding $84,910,390.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 stands, but not for the stated reason. FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER carries exactly one date-ish column, _INGESTED_AT (TIMESTAMP_NTZ, the load stamp) — no data-year column, one snapshot, DY2024. That alone is the single-vintage leg. The payments leg is NOT single-vintage: 2022, 2023 and PY2024 are all landed, so a three-year money trend against a frozen billing year is available. The claim is directly testable as written, which under Chris's definition could argue Tier 1, but the hunch's own payoff (royalty-vs-implant-volume, before/after on billing) needs a second Part B year that does not exist. Tier 2.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun uses the same two tables and the same ntile definition, so by construction it cannot tell whether 'top-decile allowed charges' measures clinical volume or drug buy-and-bill — an oncologist's allowed amount is mostly drug acquisition cost, and both my query and the agent's inherit that ambiguity identically. It cannot test direction or causality at all: with one Part B year, money-then-volume and volume-then-money are indistinguishable, and my PY2024 cross-check only shows the association is stable across money years, not which way it runs. It also cannot see money that never lands in this warehouse — research payments and ownership interest are absent entirely, so any clinician whose industry income is research-funded reads as a low payee. Finally I checked NPI hygiene only inside these two tables; if an NPI is shared, reassigned or billed under a group, both reruns carry the same error and neither would show it.
