verdicts.title: Opioid reps follow the volume — number reproduces, rural conclusion contradicts its own number, control group contaminated
verdicts.rerun_number: 45.12% median DY2024 opioid prescribing rate for paid-both-years non-rural NPs (count(*) 292, but only 277 carry a published rate) vs 0.0% for never-paid NPs (count(*) 32,956, only 25,542 carry a published rate); rural/HPSA 52.31% (119 / 110) vs 1.07% (12,539 / 9,843); long-acting median 19.70 vs 0.00; both-years NPI set 6,217. Claim said 45.1 / 52.3 / 19.7 / 6,217 — reproduced within 0.05%.
verdicts.reason: I rebuilt the chain with my own SQL (own product list, own CTEs, length(trim(NPI))=10 instead of trim<>'') and hit every figure: 6,217 both-years NPIs, 292 / 45.12, 119 / 52.31, 32,956 / 0.0, 12,539 / 1.07, LA 19.7 vs 0. Join keys are real: FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS is 1,416,883 rows / 1,416,883 distinct NPI, all length 10, zero '0000000000'; OPEN_PAYMENTS_2022 has 863,008 distinct NPIs with 51,584 blanks (excluded on both sides); QPP is 503,917 rows / 453,202 distinct NPI, deduped by group-by before the join so nothing fans out. Sampled the 292: real APRN/FNP/DNP people in FL, NJ, NC, WA, IL, KS, VA at 72-89% opioid rates, and QPP calls all 411 of them Nurse Practitioner too. Four things are wrong. (1) SELF-CONTRADICTION, real: the claim reports rural/HPSA NPs at 52.3% vs 45.1% non-rural, then asserts "rural or HPSA status makes it lower, not higher" and "the rural question is answered no." I split the flags — 66 metro-but-HPSA NPs are the highest cell of all at 53.28 median, and on the true rural axis (PRSCRBR_RUCA) nonmetro is lower in every QPP cell (17.84 vs 46.72 among non-rural non-HPSA). QPP's combined flag is not a geography; the claim uses it as one and gets the opposite sign to its own hit_means. (2) N MISLABEL, real: MEDIAN drops nulls and OPIOID_PRSCRBR_RATE is an empty string when CMS suppresses 1-10 opioid claims. 15 of the 292 and 7,414 of the 32,956 have no rate. Coalescing blanks to 0 moves the paid median 45.12 -> 42.52. (3) CONTROL GROUP CONTAMINATED, real: the filter reads only NAME_OF_DRUG..._1. Across all five slots the 2022 set goes 13,529 -> 20,039 (+48%, Kowa files Seglentis in slots 2-5 for 7,506 NPIs) and both-years 6,217 -> 8,229. The therapeutic-area blob the warehouse's own view uses gives 32,865 both-years NPIs, 5.3x. So "never-paid" holds thousands who were paid, and 6,217 is a floor at roughly one fifth. Direction survives: all-five-slots gives 41.72 vs 0.0, Seglentis-removed gives 48.45 vs 0.0. (4) OVERLAP_CHECK IS FALSE, real: the claim says the Open Payments product leg "was not run before." LIBRARY_MARTS.FINDINGS.OPIOID_PRESCRIBER_PAID_HIGH_RX, built 2026-07-27, 6,020 NPIs of which 1,939 are Nurse Practitioners, already unions OPEN_PAYMENTS + _2022 + _2023, filters the five product and five therapeutic-area columns for PAIN / OPIOID ANALGESIC while excluding USE DISORDER and OVERDOSE, and joins FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS on NPI with a within-specialty percentile. Two minors: "NP 292 metro" mixes geography systems — 292 is the QPP not-rural-not-HPSA cell and 17 of them are RUCA-nonmetro; and "ten to forty times" is not a number this chain produces (45.12/0.0 is undefined, 52.31/1.07 is 49x). Smallest fix: swap "rural or HPSA" for PRSCRBR_RUCA, report the with-a-rate n beside every count, and say 6,217 is a slot-1 floor.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 holds, and the dating claim survived the test that could have killed it. verdicts.title: Newborn NPIs, skin-graft millions
verdicts.rerun_number: $1,352,392,029 DY2024 Medicare Part B allowed charges to 354 individual clinicians whose NPIs were enumerated 2022-01-01 or later — reproduced to the dollar. But the skin-substitute cut is $443,922,367 = 32.8% of that headline dollar, not 75.1%.
verdicts.reason:
I rebuilt the chain with row_number()/count() over () instead of the agent's ntile(100), try_to_number(x,18,6) throughout, and my own CTEs. Every number reproduced EXACTLY: 1,235,757 individual Part B rows, top 1% = 12,357 rows, 12,326 after the NPPES type-1 join, 354 new-2022+ / 11,972 veteran, $1,352,392,029, $443,922,367 Q4, 75.1% / 16.5%, 94 majority-Q4, 36 over $100k/bene, AZ NP 1215678495 Allison Charles $54,881,402.34 on 78 benes enumerated 2022-04-05, AZ NP cell 21 NPIs $166,197,494 91.6%, CA PA cell 17 NPIs $139,200,087 93.0%, Open Payments 212 of 354 / $90,329.33, LEIE 0, Part D 65,819 / 63,337 / 36,166.

Keys are clean, no fan-out: BY_PROVIDER 1,296,739 rows = 1,296,739 distinct RNDRNG_NPI; NPPES 9,606,683 rows = 9,606,683 distinct NPI; both 10-char; PROVIDER_ENUMERATION_DATE parses MM/DD/YYYY on 100% of the 7,323,142 type-1 rows, range 2005-05-23 to 2026-06-06. Matched rows 354 = 354 distinct entities. Entity count is honest.

THE DEFECT (real, one sentence, load-bearing). The claim says "$1,352,392,029 ... 75.1% of it ($443.9M ...) is skin substitutes." 75.1% of $1,352,392,029 is $1,015,646,414. The parenthetical contradicts the percentage inside the same sentence. $443.9M is 32.8% of the headline dollar. The 75.1% denominator is a DIFFERENT number: $590,776,865, the service-file reconstruction (sum of TOT_SRVCS x AVG_MDCR_ALOWD_AMT), which recovers only 43.7% of the cohort's provider-file dollars. A reader takes away "~$1B of skin substitutes." Provable is $443.9M. The wrong reading inflates it 2.3x.

Worse, the 75.1 vs 16.5 comparison is on differently-censored bases: the service file recovers 43.7% of the new cohort's dollars but 66.9% of the veterans'. On the common provider-file basis it is 32.8% vs 11.0% — a 3.0x gap, not 4.6x. Direction survives either way; the size does not.

Three attacks that FAILED (the hunch is sound):
1. Q4% overreach. Q4001-Q4051 are casting supplies, not skin substitutes. Tested: in the 354 cohort every Q4 dollar is Q4100+ — 21 codes, all "per square centimeter" grafts, $443,922,367, zero from Q4001-Q4099. Across the veteran cohort Q4100+ vs Q4% differs by $60,795 of $4.07B (0.0015%). The shortcut is safe here.
2. Vintage mismatch between the two legs. Tested by carbon-dating both separately: 17,317 NPIs enumerated in 2024 appear in the provider file, 14,457 in the service file, zero from 2025 in either. Same vintage. The 43.7% gap is suppression, not a year mismatch — median recovery runs 0.810 at <25 benes up to 0.941 at 500+.
3. The AZ outlier being a column shift. Tested: TOT_SBMTD_CHRG $60,357,565 and TOT_MDCR_PYMT_AMT $43,726,452 bracket the $54,881,402 allowed correctly; her top service row is Q4271 Complete FT, 28,625.9 services x $1,656.33 = $47.4M on 36 beneficiaries; NPPES taxonomy 363LF0000X is Nurse Practitioner, Family. Real.

Also confirmed the agent's own ENTITY_TYPE_CODE trap and showed it does not bias the number: the 31 top-1% NPIs dropped by ENTITY_TYPE_CODE='1' hold $115,434,027, 30 of 31 carry a deactivation date, and ZERO are enumerated 2022+.

Provider-type framing checks out: 314 Nurse Practitioner + 35 Physician Assistant = 349 of 354 (98.6%).

Minor, not corrected: "$21,595 per beneficiary against $3,892" are MEDIANS of per-NPI ratios (21594.51 / 3892.17), not cohort rates. Pooled is $19,155.97 vs $2,879.31. Median is the better statistic; the wording just reads like an aggregate.

Tier 1 stands, but on the OTHER clause than the one the agent cited. The agent said "the before/after is built in." It is not. I checked: exactly one Part B vintage exists in the warehouse — LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING BY_PROVIDER 1,296,739 and _AND_SERVI 9,781,673, mirrored 1:1 into LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH, nothing else matching '%PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS%'. The provider file has no year column at all; the only date-ish column is _INGESTED_AT. You cannot show these 354 going from zero to $1.35B, because there is no DY2023 Part B file to show the zero. What is "built in" is a cohort contrast inside one snapshot, which is a cross-section.

Tier 1 survives on Chris's explicit alternative — "or the claim is directly testable as written." The claim is a DY2024 cross-sectional statement, one leg (NPPES enumeration date) is genuinely dated 2005-2026, and I tested the whole thing end to end and it held. verdicts.blind_spot:
I read the same two CMS files, so I cannot see what CMS deleted. 56.3% of the cohort's dollars ($761.6M) have no HCPCS line in the service file at all — suppressed under the 11-beneficiary rule. That missing mix could be anything; 32.8% skin substitutes is a floor and 75.1% is a share of only what CMS chose to publish. Neither I nor the agent can measure the true mix.

Second, "DY2024" is inference by both of us, from the same evidence: no year column exists, only one vintage is landed, and the year is read off NPPES enumeration dates. If CMS shipped a partial year or a different year, every dollar carries that error identically in my rerun and the agent's.

Third, I verified these are 354 distinct NPIs, not 354 distinct humans. NPPES is the only identity source in the chain and it echoes whatever was filed on the application. If a ring enumerated straw clinicians, NPPES says they are 354 people and my rerun agrees. Nothing here distinguishes a busy new NP from a rented NPI — that is the story's whole point and the data cannot settle it.

Fourth, I never checked whether the same physical person holds an older NPI too. The claim "NPIs did not exist before 2022" is about the NPI and is true; "newborn clinicians" would need a name/DOB link I did not build.

The cut used is 1% of the 1,235,757 rows with RNDRNG_PRVDR_ENT_CD='I', not of the 1,296,739-row file — 60,982 organization rows are excluded first. Threshold is $1,129,747.74 allowed. verdicts.title: State malpractice backdrop (Hub B, NPDB x QPP x Open Payments 2023)
verdicts.rerun_number: Massachusetts 117.2 NPDB malpractice payments per 1,000 QPP clinicians, 2022-2024 (reproduced exactly, 0.0% off); 243.8 per 1,000 on the same table's 99.9%-filled LICNSTAT column instead of the 62.6%-filled WORKSTAT
verdicts.reason:
HEADLINE REPRODUCES, THE SUPPORTING COUNTS DO NOT, AND THE HUNCH SENTENCE DIES ON A SHARED DENOMINATOR.

**Rerun, my own SQL** (v2_rerun.py): MA 117.2 / $27,369 / MIPS 81.43; ME 3.4 / $745 / 91.18; 49 rows. Exact match. Join holds: state=state=state, three real legs, no fan-out (each CTE pre-aggregates to one row per state). 49 = all 50 states minus Vermont (234 QPP physicians, under the 500 cutoff); DC/PR/GU/VI/MP also cut. That part is right.

**Wrong number 1 — the report count.** Claim: "34,711 NPDB malpractice payment reports 2022-2024." The panel actually rests on 15,231. 34,711 is every RECTYPE='P' row for those years with no license-field filter and blank states included. The agent's own JSON sums to 15,231.

**Wrong number 2 — the coverage caveat.** Claim: "the state-attributable share is the 30% with WORKSTAT filled." On the payment rows the panel uses, WORKSTAT is filled on 21,459 of 34,711 = **61.8%**, not 30%. The 70%-blank figure is real but belongs to RECTYPE='C' adverse actions (120,560 of 155,690 blank, 77%), which are not the numerator. The caveat is attached to the wrong rows.

**Wrong number 3 — the denominator size.** Claim: "366,000-plus QPP physician NPIs summed across states." Sum over the 49 rows = **333,168** (agent's own rows sum to the same). Distinct nationally under the same filter: 319,096. 366k appears in no query.

**Wrong number 4 — "MIPS physicians."** `CLINICIAN_TYPE ilike '%physician%'` matches **'Physician Assistant'**. There is no CLINICIAN_TYPE value 'Physician' (0 rows); MDs land under 'Doctor of Medicine'. The denominator carries **47,522 PAs, 14.3%** of the 49-state total, while the numerator is MD/DO-only (LICNFELD 10/20). MD/DO-only denominator puts MA at 137.4, not 117.2.

**The hunch sentence fails its own test (real, blocker for the claim as prose).** Both ratios divide by the same QPP count, so a small QPP count lifts a state on both. Swap in an independent physician count (distinct physicians paid by industry in OP 2023):

| Measure | QPP denominator | OP-physician denominator |
|---|---|---|
| MA malpractice rank | **1** (117.2/1k) | **19** (20.4/1k) |
| MA money rank | **1** ($27,369) | **5** ($4,777) |
| malrate vs money, Spearman | +0.30 | **-0.17** |
| malrate vs MIPS score, Pearson | -0.28 | **+0.01** |

The QPP count runs 0.17x to 1.71x the state's industry-paid physician count (MA 2,646 QPP vs 15,160 OP physicians; ME 3,241 vs 1,892). "Also carry the most money and the lowest scores" is induced by the shared denominator, not observed.

**The column choice is the real trap, and the fix is one word.** Same table, same rows: LICNSTAT filled on **24,993 of 25,012** MD/DO payment rows (99.9%) vs WORKSTAT 15,648 (62.6%), HOMESTAT 11,578. Maine: WORKSTAT 11, **LICNSTAT 75**. MA: 310 vs 645. Maine's 3.4 per 1,000 is a redaction artifact, not a safe state — Maine goes to 23.1 per 1,000 on LICNSTAT and sits mid-pack (39.6/1k, rank 18) on the OP-physician denominator.

**And the redaction is not uniform, so the ranking is partly a ranking of redaction.** MD/DO payment rows carrying a work state: 24,765/28,967 (85.5%) in 2010-2012 → 15,648/25,012 (62.6%) in 2022-2024. Per state, the change runs VT 31→4 (-87%) and ME 83→11 (-87%) at one end to NV 128→156 (+22%) and HI 50→61 (+22%) at the other, against a national MD/DO drop of only 14%.

**Smallest fix:** rebuild the panel on LICNSTAT, drop the co-movement sentence, name the denominator "QPP-scored clinicians" not "MIPS physicians," and say 15,231 / 61.8% / 333,168.

**Clean checks (no gap found):** OP_2023 PROGRAM_YEAR is '2023' on all 14,700,786 rows; dollars use try_to_number(x,18,2) on a 2-decimal column, no rounding loss; NPDB SEQNO 1,911,185 rows / 1,911,185 distinct, no dupes; WORKSTAT has zero empty strings so `is not null` is a valid filter; no capped or sample table in the chain.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 stands, for the stated reason. QPP is one snapshot and has no program-year column anywhere in its 198 columns, so the vintage cannot even be confirmed in-warehouse (the agent's "PY2024" is an assertion). The other two legs are dated: NPDB ORIGYEAR 1990-2026, and Open Payments is landed three times (2022 13.3M, 2023 14.7M, 2024 15.4M rows), so only the QPP leg forces cross-section. Not tier 3 — no leg is missing. Not tier 1 — no before/after is possible on the quality leg. I would add one line to the tier reason: the join key is a state whose denominator is not comparable across states, so this is a backdrop, not a rate.
verdicts.blind_spot: My alternative denominator is distinct physicians who received an Open Payments 2023 payment. That is not a physician census — it counts only industry-touched physicians, so it is correlated with the money numerator and undercounts low-marketing states like Maine and New Mexico. My reversal of the correlation therefore proves the original ratio is denominator-driven, but does not establish the true sign; an NPPES active MD/DO count by practice state, or Part B by-provider, would arbitrate and I did not pull one. Second blind spot: no HRSA data dictionary is landed, so WORKSTAT vs LICNSTAT semantics are inferred from fill rates and plausibility, not documented — LICNSTAT is state of licensure and can differ from where a doctor practices, so "use LICNSTAT" is a better-populated column, not a proven-correct one. Third: I checked NPDB row uniqueness on SEQNO but never proved one payment report equals one incident; PRACTNUM repeats up to 22 times in 2023 alone, so a repeat-offender doctor inflates a state count and I did not measure by how much.

verdicts.rerun_number: $4,187,435.11 paid in Open Payments PY2024 to 1,325 NPPES-deactivated NPIs (30,370 matched rows, 3,992 distinct NPIs) — exact match, 0.00% off
verdicts.reason:
Every load-bearing number reproduced exactly on a query I wrote myself (pre-aggregate both sides, then join; the agent joined raw). Rows 30,370 = 30,370. NPIs 3,992 = 3,992. After deactivation 1,325 = 1,325. Dollars $4,187,435.11 vs $4,187,435 with try_to_number(x,18,6) instead of (18,2). 90-day count 1,224 both as >90 and >=90 days. 2023 leg 1,156 NPIs / $4,680,578.44. Nature mix exact to the cent on all four lines. Part B control: 1 NPI, $43,837.40 — Marvin Osman, psychiatry, CA, deactivated 2007-06-21, 12 beneficiaries.

BOTH JOIN KEYS ARE REAL. NPPES.NPI: 9,606,683 rows / 9,606,683 distinct, all ten digits, zero '0000000000'. Deactivated-never-reactivated 346,179 distinct, zero unparseable dates. OP2024.NPI: 979,137 distinct over 15,385,047 rows, RECORD_ID unique so no duplicate rows fan the join, 48,059 blanks (34,391 are teaching hospitals which have no NPI by design). PROGRAM_YEAR is '2024' on 100% of rows, '2023' on 100% of the 2023 file. Fan-out is real (15.66 rows per NPI average, max 1,147) and the claim states both rows and entities, which is the right call.

I ran three attacks and all three failed to break it.
1. Typo-collision: all 1,325 NPIs carry exactly ONE distinct last name across their after-deactivation payments (worst case 1). Not a garbage bucket.
2. Stale-NPI rescue: all 1,325 recipient profile IDs exist in FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_PROFILE_SUPPLEMENT and every single one carries the SAME deactivated NPI. Zero carry a live one. Zero profile IDs in OP2024 carry a second NPI. CMS's own recipient master is stale too, so "the person re-enrolled under a new NPI" is not visible anywhere in the file.
3. Is the deactivation flag real? The 18,423 reactivated NPPES rows all keep their entity type and name; the 346,179 deactivated-never-reactivated rows are blank on entity type, last name, enumeration date, replacement NPI and reason code — 346,179 of 346,179. The strip is real, so the filter is right.

I FOUND A SHARPER CONTROL THAN THE ONE CLAIMED. Of the 264,447 NPIs deactivated before 2024-01-01: 1,110 got 2024 Open Payments money, 1 has a Part B row, 4 have a Part D row. Denominators run the wrong way for the excuse — Part B has 1,296,739 NPIs, Part D 1,416,883, Open Payments only 979,136. The file with the smallest universe carries a thousand times more dead NPIs. And the pattern runs three years, not two: OPEN_PAYMENTS_2022 gives 986 NPIs / $4,921,536 after deactivation. 2023 is royalty-dominated too ($3,623,440 of $4,680,578, 77%), so "same pattern" is fair.

TWO GAPS, both real, neither a number error.

REAL — the word "dead" is not in the data. NPI_DEACTIVATION_REASON_CODE is blank on 346,179 of 346,179 rows, which the agent's own trap #1 says plainly. CMS deactivates for death, retirement, fraud revocation, duplicate NPI and org dissolution, and the public file separates none of them. The title "Industry pays dead NPIs" and the hunch line "Part B stops paying the same NPIs the day they die" assert a cause the warehouse cannot carry. Smallest fix: say "deactivated," not "dead." File: the claim title.

REAL — $4,187,435 reads like a spread and is not one. Top 3 NPIs are $2,865,964 (68.4%), top 10 are $3,935,240 (94.0%). The median dead NPI's after-deactivation total is $28.04, and 1,078 of the 1,325 got under $100 each, $34,972 between them. Same shape as pharma_paid_excluded_2026-09-05.md, where 89% of $338,872 was one Medtronic royalty. Two stories in one number. The claim does disclose the royalty split in distinct_entities, so a careful reader gets there — but the headline number should carry the concentration. Smallest fix: append "94% of it to 10 NPIs."

MINOR — two different 1,248s sit in this hunch. 1,248 NPIs had every payment fall after deactivation; 1,248 NPIs took a Food-and-Beverage payment after deactivation. Overlap is 1,179, not 1,248. Same cardinality, different sets. The claim only uses the food one, so it is correct as written, but anyone re-deriving will trip.

MINOR — the join_keys field says "PART_D_PRESCRIBERS.NPI 5,269" with no vintage, and p12_skin_deact.py names that column in_partd_dy2024. Traps line 13 pins the Part D drug-level file to DY2022. The by-prescriber file's year is untested by me and by the agent. Not load-bearing; the claim sentence Chris reads does not mention Part D.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Industry pays deactivated NPIs: $4,187,435 reported paid in Open Payments PY2024 to 1,325 NPIs that NPPES had already deactivated, 1,224 of them 90 or more days after — but 94% of that money is 10 NPIs and 80% is 14 royalty recipients, while the median deactivated NPI got $28.04 and 1,078 of the 1,325 got under $100. PY2023 shows the same shape at 1,156 NPIs and $4,680,578 (77% royalty); PY2022 at 986 NPIs and $4,921,536. Against 264,447 NPIs deactivated before 2024, Open Payments PY2024 pays 1,110 of them, Part B CY2024 pays 1 and Part D pays 4 — on larger provider universes. NPPES gives no deactivation reason on any of the 346,179 rows, so "deactivated" cannot be read as "dead."
verdicts.tier_reason: Both legs carry real dates and the before/after is the whole test. NPPES.NPI_DEACTIVATION_DATE spans 2005-05-23 to 2026-06-07 (MM/DD/YYYY text, 0 parse failures on 346,179 rows); Open Payments carries DATE_OF_PAYMENT plus a PROGRAM_YEAR that is single-valued per file. The same test ran clean on three vintages — PY2022 986 NPIs, PY2023 1,156, PY2024 1,325 — which is a trend, not a snapshot. The Part B leg is a genuine dated control (1 NPI deactivated before its service year). Chain holds end to end, first number found and reproduced exactly. Tier 1 as claimed.
verdicts.blind_spot: I only proved the two federal files disagree with each other. I read the same single NPPES snapshot the agent read (ingested ~2026-06-08, max deactivation 2026-06-07, one _SOURCE_RUN_ID), so if a deactivation date in that snapshot is itself wrong — a CMS keying error, or a reactivation whose date was never written back — my rerun repeats the error instead of catching it. There is no third source of provider status in this warehouse: no death index, no state licence file, and no landed enrollment file that independently dates when a provider stopped. NPI 1770789471 is exactly that shape — deactivated 2007-06-21 yet billing Medicare $43,837 in CY2024 — and I cannot tell you whether NPPES or Part B is the file that is wrong. I also could not test the "practising under a new NPI" theory at all: REPLACEMENT_NPI is blank on all 346,179 deactivated rows, so the one column that would answer it is empty by construction.
new_traps: FED_CMS_MEDICARE_PHYSICIAN_OTHER_PRACTITIONERS_BY_PROVIDER has NO year column. A search of information_schema for %YEAR%/%YR%/%DT%/%INGEST% returns only RNDRNG_NPI and _INGESTED_AT (2026-08-05). 'DY2024' is a label, not a stamp. It survives an independent test — the deactivation-year mix of its 3,558 deactivated NPIs is 2007:1, 2024:778, 2025:1883, 2026:896 and ZERO for 2008-2023, a shape only a CY2024 service year produces — but state the inference, never quote the year as if the table said it. Same family as the Part D no-year trap.

FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS.DATE_OF_PAYMENT parses to year 2 on 73 of 15,385,047 rows; min(try_to_date(...)) reads 0002-11-30. PROGRAM_YEAR is '2024' on 100% of rows and is the trustworthy vintage column. Never use min(DATE_OF_PAYMENT) to establish a file's start. Harmless in a paid-after-deactivation test (those 73 sort before every deactivation date, so they can only shrink the count), live for anyone charting the year.

FED_CMS_NPPES deactivated-never-reactivated rows are FULLY STRIPPED: ENTITY_TYPE_CODE, PROVIDER_LAST_NAME_LEGAL_NAME, PROVIDER_ENUMERATION_DATE, REPLACEMENT_NPI and NPI_DEACTIVATION_REASON_CODE are all blank on 346,179 of 346,179. The 18,423 reactivated rows are intact (0 blank entity type, 0 blank name), which proves the strip is deliberate. Consequences: any filter on entity type, name, enumeration date or taxonomy silently deletes the entire deactivated cohort; you cannot separate death from retirement, fraud or duplicate-NPI merge; and REPLACEMENT_NPI cannot answer 'did this person get a new NPI.'

FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_PROFILE_SUPPLEMENT does not rescue a stale recipient NPI. All 1,325 COVERED_RECIPIENT_PROFILE_IDs belonging to deactivated-and-paid recipients are present in the supplement, and every one carries the SAME deactivated COVERED_RECIPIENT_NPI — 0 carry a live one, 0 are blank. No profile ID in OP2024 carries a second NPI either. The supplement mirrors the payment file's identity, it does not correct it; do not treat it as an authoritative NPI resolver.

Coincidence trap inside this hunch: 1,248 is two different sets. 1,248 deactivated NPIs had EVERY 2024 payment fall after their deactivation date; 1,248 deactivated NPIs took a Food-and-Beverage payment after deactivation. The overlap is 1,179, not 1,248. Two independently computed counts landing on the same integer is not a cross-check.

verdicts.title: Excluded firms still winning contracts — number reproduces, the label on it does not
verdicts.rerun_number: 103 contracts / 32 UEIs / $2,223,369.51 positive obligations — reproduced to the cent. The defensible subset is 66 contracts / 23 firms / $800,007.26, 2012-11 to 2026-05.
verdicts.reason:
**Verdict: CORRECTED.** The arithmetic is exact. The sentence wrapped around it is not.

**What reproduced (0% deviation)**

| Claim | My rerun | Match |
|---|---|---|
| 103 new contracts | 103 | exact |
| 32 distinct excluded UEIs | 32 | exact |
| $2.22M positive obligations | $2,223,369.51 | exact |
| 134 UEIs / 1,321 contracts / -$101.6M during window | 134 / 1,321 / -$101,618,712.31 | exact |
| 31 firms + 1 special entity | CLASSIFICATION: 31 Firm, 1 Special Entity Designation | exact |
| 10 DLA, 4 EPA, 3 HHS | DLA 10, EPA 4, HHS 3 (+SBA 3, USA 2, DOL 2, None 2, 6 singles) | exact |

I wrote my own SQL (`v3_rerun.py`), pulled the per-award roll-up over **all time** instead of the probe's 2010 floor, and matched against **each exclusion record's own window** instead of the collapsed min/max. Method A (probe's) → 103/32/$2,223,369.51. Method B (mine) → 154/33/$2,096,641.37.

**Join key: real.** `RECIPIENT_UEI` = SAM `UNIQUE_ENTITY_ID`. 168,328 SAM rows, 47,686 with a UEI, 38,427 distinct, 38,426 of them 12 chars (one junk value `'00000'`, 1 row). 384 excluded UEIs appear in R2 across 93,333 award keys / 128,655 action rows. Recipient name agrees with the SAM name on **all 32** — BONUS ENVIRONMENTAL LLC = BONUS ENVIRONMENTAL LLC, MFA INCORPORATED = MFA INCORPORATED, and so on. Not a name collision. Money parses clean: 0 of 128,655 obligations fail `try_to_number(x,18,6)`; I re-ran at scale 6 and got the same cent.

**Real #1 — 2 of the 103 are not new awards. -16.0% of the headline dollar.**
The probe's own `WHERE "ACTION_DATE" >= '2010-01-01'` censors the left edge, so `min(ACTION_DATE)` returns the first *visible* action, not the first action.

| UEI | Firm | Probe's "first" | True first | Money counted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LHKPCBXXLJQ6 | HANFORD NUCLEAR SERVICES INC | 2010-05-03 | **2008-05-02** | $350,690.69 |
| GUVKVVAPBJL3 | MIL-CRAFT MFG., INC. | 2011-11-23 | **2007-04-13** | $5,970.00 |

Both are continuing modifications on pre-existing awards. Strip them: **101 contracts, 30 firms, $1,866,708.82**. That is 16.0% off the claimed dollar — well past the 1% tolerance. (The other feared artefact did not bite: collapsing multiple exclusion windows to min/max invented **zero** hits.)

**Real #2 — 63.7% of the dollars sit under an exclusion type that does not bar a contract.**
8 of the 32 carry `EXCLUSION_TYPE = 'Prohibition/Restriction'`: 36 contracts, $1,417,392.25. The record's own `ADDITIONAL_COMMENTS` field says so in capitals. Verbatim from the Bonus Environmental row:

> "Convicted of Clean Air Act Violation: **INELIGIBLE FOR AWARDS TO BE PERFORMED AT THIS FACILITY ONLY**: Bonus Environmental, LLC, 304 Elizabeth St., Mount Pleasant, MI 48858 (Violating Facility) … **ALL THREE CONDITIONS MUST BE PRESENT** FOR A PERSON TO BE DENIED A CONTRACT, LOAN OR BENEFIT."

**The marquee example in the claim's first sentence is this class.** Bonus Environmental is $839,315 — 37.7% of the whole headline — and its 14 DoD awards are only a violation if performed at that Mount Pleasant address. Nothing in the warehouse establishes that. Same for MFA Incorporated ($127,783, EPA facility-only). Hanford Nuclear ($350,691, HHS `CT_CODE` Z1) is a 42 U.S.C. §1320a-7 **health-care program** exclusion, not a procurement debarment — and it is also left-censored, so it fails twice.

**Defensible core** — only `Ineligible (Proceedings Completed/Complete/Pending)` and `Voluntary Exclusion`, left-censor removed:

| Cut | Contracts | Firms | Positive obligations |
|---|---|---|---|
| As claimed | 103 | 32 | $2,223,369.51 |
| Drop left-censored | 101 | 30 | $1,866,708.82 |
| Hard exclusion types only | 67 | 24 | $805,977.26 |
| **Both filters** | **66** | **23** | **$800,007.26** |

**Real #3 — "won brand-new contracts" overstates the shape.** Parsing `CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY` (last two segments are the parent IDV; `-NONE-` = standalone): **51 of 103** are orders under a pre-existing indefinite-delivery vehicle, holding $1,116,668 — half the money. Inside the defensible core it is worse: 49 of 66 are IDV orders ($756,847); only **17 contracts, 9 firms, $43,160** are standalone new awards. This does not kill the story — FAR 9.405-1(b) bars placing orders beyond the guaranteed minimum on a debarred contractor, and A&S Skill Machinists (DLA Voluntary Exclusion, 16 DLA orders, $130,589) is a clean instance of DLA excluding a firm and then ordering from it. But "won a new contract" and "got an order on an old vehicle" are different sentences.

**Minor — the SAM leg is a current-state snapshot.** `RECORD_STATUS` is `'Active'` on all 168,328 rows: a constant, not a filter. Only 48 rows carry a termination date already past; 159,074 (94.5%) read `'Indefinite'`. Firms excluded in 2013 and reinstated in 2016 are **not in the file at all**. Every count here is a floor, biased toward indefinite exclusions. Tier 1 still holds under Chris's definition — `ACTIVE_DATE`/`TERMINATION_DATE` and `ACTION_DATE` are both real dates and the before/after test runs — but the population is not the historical exclusion list.

**Sentinels checked, clean.** No `'0000000000'`, no `'<UNAVAIL>'`, no `'Not Available'` in the UEI column. `ACTIVE_DATE` does carry the 1908-04-20 / 2099-12-30 sentinels (795 rows pre-1990, 2 future) — none landed on the 32. `try_to_number` at scale 6 changed nothing. `FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2` (not the 10k sample) and `_FULL_R2` on contracts (not the 20M cap) were both used correctly. No PORTAL_ table, no HMDA sample, no lifetime-total summing.

DISAGREE: number reproduces, but 64% of dollars is not a bar.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 holds. SAM carries ACTIVE_DATE and TERMINATION_DATE, USASpending carries ACTION_DATE, and "new award landed inside the window" is a direct before/after test that ran. Caveat the tier does not capture: the SAM leg is a current-active snapshot (RECORD_STATUS 'Active' on 100% of 168,328 rows, only 48 past terminations), so exclusions that ended before Sept 2026 are absent and every count is a floor — a dated snapshot, not an exclusion history.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun cannot see place of performance, so it cannot settle the Clean Air Act three-condition test that decides whether the EPA facility-only listings (37.7% of the headline) are violations at all — I ruled them out on the record's own comment text, not on evidence the work was elsewhere. It also cannot see whether the parent IDVs behind the 51 order-under-IDV hits were themselves awarded before the exclusion, or whether those orders exceeded the guaranteed minimum, which is the actual FAR 9.405-1(b) line. Third: I spent my three R2 queries, so I never tested R2 for duplicate action rows — 32 of the 103 awards carry more than one action row, and a double-loaded action would inflate positive obligations without changing the contract count. Fourth: awards whose true first action predates USASpending coverage (slice floor 2006-10-01) would still read as new even under my all-time method; low risk here since every hit's first action is 2010 or later.
new_traps: FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2.RECORD_STATUS is 'Active' on all 168,328 rows — a constant, and it means the table is the CURRENT active exclusion list, not exclusion history. Only 48 rows carry a termination date already past; 159,074 (94.5%) read 'Indefinite'. A firm excluded in 2013 and reinstated in 2016 is absent entirely, so any 'excluded at time T' count is a floor biased toward indefinite exclusions.

FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2.EXCLUSION_TYPE 'Prohibition/Restriction' is 128,995 of 168,328 rows (33,552 of 38,427 UEIs) and is NOT a bar on winning a contract. The row's own ADDITIONAL_COMMENTS says so: EPA Clean Air Act listings read 'INELIGIBLE FOR AWARDS TO BE PERFORMED AT THIS FACILITY ONLY' with a three-condition test, and HHS CT_CODE Z1 rows bar federal health-care program payment under 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7, not procurement. Only 'Ineligible (Proceedings Completed/Complete/Pending)' and 'Voluntary Exclusion' bar a new award. Filtering this cut a headline from $2,223,370 to $800,007 (-64%).

A WHERE floor on ACTION_DATE turns continuing awards into new awards: min(ACTION_DATE) per CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY computed under "ACTION_DATE" >= '2010-01-01' reported two pre-2010 awards (Hanford Nuclear first action 2008-05-02, Mil-Craft 2007-04-13) as first awarded during an exclusion window — 2 of 103 contracts but $356,661 of $2,223,370, 16.0% of the dollar. Compute the award's first action over all time, then filter the result.

FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FULL_R2.CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY encodes the parent IDV in its last two underscore segments: '-NONE-' means a standalone award, anything else is an order under a pre-existing indefinite-delivery vehicle. 51 of 103 'new contracts' in this pass were IDV orders holding $1,116,668, half the money; in the clean cohort 49 of 66. A distinct award key is not a distinct new contract.

FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2.UNIQUE_ENTITY_ID is clean but not perfect: 47,686 of 168,328 rows populated, 38,427 distinct, 38,426 at 12 characters, one junk value '00000' on 1 row. No '0000000000' sentinel here (unlike the NPI column in the same table). ACTIVE_DATE carries sentinels 1908-04-20 and 2099-12-30 and 11,016 of 168,328 rows do not parse as a date at all.

"REINSTATEMENT_DATE is null" is presented as "the IRS lists this org as no longer exempt." It does not mean that. 15 of the 24 EINs sit in FED_IRS_EO_BMF today with STATUS='01' (unconditional exemption) and in FED_IRS_PUB78_ELIGIBLE_DONEES with DEDUCTIBILITY_STATUS='PC'. verdicts.title: Post-disaster provider startups
verdicts.rerun_number: HHA per-pair-weighted DiD 1.14 across 365 non-COVID disaster-county pairs 2017-2023 (665 actual incorporations vs 583.1 expected from each pair's own national window); the agent's pooled 1.281 reproduced to three decimals
verdicts.reason: Every stated figure reproduced exactly from my own SQL and my own FEMA aggregate off the raw 26M table, with the DiD summed in Python instead of SQL: 365 pairs, 260 counties, 663 before, 665 after, local 1.003, national 0.783, ratio 1.281; no-LA HHA 0.865, no-LA hospice 1.499, hurricane HHA 0.903 and hospice 1.336, SNF 0.788. The chain is clean too - DIM_ZIP_POINT.ZCTA5 is 33,486 rows on 33,486 distinct values with PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS filled on all of them, the enrollment join adds no rows (11,413 joined = 11,413 distinct ENROLLMENT_ID), ENROLLMENT_ID is unique, 11,413 of 11,508 HHA rows match a ZCTA, and the 626 (FIPS, DISASTERNUMBER) pairs carry no duplicates that could fan the natw join. Three things are still wrong with the claim. First, 1.28 is not a difference-in-differences. The query sums local counts across pairs but sums the national counterfactual pair-by-pair unweighted, so LA supplies 70% of the local after-count and one 365th of the national side. Recomputing with each pair against its own national window (expected_after = sum(before x nat_after/nat_before)) gives HHA 1.14, hospice-without-LA 1.27 instead of 1.50, and hurricane-only hospice 1.000 exactly instead of 1.34. Second, the entity count overstates the evidence base 2.6x: 226 of the 365 pairs have zero HHA incorporations in both windows, so the measure rests on 139 pairs in 100 counties, and only 31 of the 113 pairs with any before-activity (27.4%) beat their own national window. Third, LA is not evidence of a disaster effect. LA HHA in rolling 24-month windows runs 118, 160, 366, 464 against national 493, 572, 858, 942 - the step DiD before the declaration is 1.525, the step after it is 1.155, so the excess growth peaked two years before the Oct 2020 fire and decelerated through it. DR-4569 drew 3,234 IA registrations in a 10-million-person county. Separately the 0.783 national ratio is partly file truncation: national HHA incorporations run 601 (2021), 245, 120, 31, max date 2024-08-09, and 90 of the 365 pairs are 2022-23 declarations whose after-windows run past the file's end.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 1 holds by the letter of the rule: FEMA DECLARATIONDATE is a real per-row date and INCORPORATION_DATE parses MM/DD/YYYY on 9,211 of 11,508 HHA rows spanning 1808-2024, so a before/after is possible and was run. The qualification is that the second leg is a current-enrollee snapshot with a retrospective date column - providers that left the file are invisible, and the post-2021 collapse in that column (601, 245, 120, 31) is enrollment lag, not behaviour. That is a Tier 1 with a snapshot-survivorship leg, not a Tier 2, because the trend was computable and computed.
verdicts.blind_spot: I used the same two source tables and the same ZIP-to-ZCTA-to-county hop through DIM_ZIP_POINT, so if a split ZIP is assigned to the wrong primary county my rerun repeats the error identically - I checked the key's uniqueness and fill, not its correctness against a second crosswalk (XWALK_ZCTA_COUNTY, 46,960 rows, would fan). I also cannot see any provider that existed and left: no historical snapshot of the enrollment file is landed, so survivorship is unmeasurable from inside the data, and the national control only cancels it if attrition is geographically uniform, which I did not test. And I tested the DiD's weighting, not its identification - I ran no placebo declarations and no matched control counties.

verdicts.title: HUD housing in repeat-disaster counties
verdicts.rerun_number: 92.6% occupancy in 2+-disaster counties vs 92.3% in no-disaster counties (HUD 31DEC2025 snapshot, 3,232 vs 24,834 projects) — reproduced exactly. But on the 50 states alone, with Puerto Rico and the territories dropped, it is 91.9% vs 92.3% — the sign flips.
verdicts.reason: I rebuilt the chain in my own SQL, reading FEMA live from FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS instead of the agent's hardcoded 626-row VALUES list. Every published figure reproduced to the decimal: 626 disaster-county pairs, 149/264/2,399 counties, 3,232/7,535/24,834 projects, 336,580 units, occupancy 92.6/92.3/92.3, elderly 40.5/46.5/50.2, wait 20.8/27.5/15.6. The join is real and the arithmetic is clean. The reading is not. (1) Puerto Rico is 70 of the 149 treatment counties — 47% of the weight in a county-mean from 24% of the projects. Drop PR/VI/GU and occupancy reverses to 91.9% (2+) vs 92.3% (0), which is the hunch's own hit condition reported as a miss; the elderly gap collapses from 9.7pp to 1.5pp (48.6 vs 50.1); the wait gap doubles from 5.2 to 10.1 months (25.7 vs 15.6). PR's young, high-occupancy public housing stock is doing all three jobs. (2) The 1-disaster bucket is hidden: waiting list runs 15.6 -> 27.5 -> 20.8, non-monotonic. The claim quotes only the ends, so 'repeat disaster' has no dose-response. (3) MONTHS_WAITING is a negative sentinel on 26,611 of 35,601 rows (74.7%): -1 on 21,812, -4 on 4,478, -5 on 321. The headline gap rests on 964 vs 6,466 projects, with coverage differing by bucket (29.8% vs 26.0%). The agent's trap list flags PCT_OCCUPIED's 4,824 negatives and never mentions this larger one. (4) 'Untouched' is false for a third of the control: 8,576 HUD projects across 744 counties had a real non-COVID FEMA IA disaster 2017-2023 that fell under the arbitrary 1,000-registration cut and sit in the '0' bucket; 1,305 counties had a disaster, only 447 cleared the cut. (5) Blank/short STCTYTRT (91 blank, 4 five-char, 1 two-char) lpads into a fabricated county '00000' with 9,221 units that counts as a real control county. (6) join_keys says '2,837 counties' while the buckets sum to 2,812 — 2,837 is the pre-lpad count, the query uses lpad. Robustness checks that passed: PCT_OCCUPIED runs over 100 on 98 rows (max 1334) but capping at 100 moves the weighted figure 0.02pp; TOTAL_UNITS has no negatives; try_to_number(...,18,0) on TOTAL_UNITS does not damage the sum because the values are integers.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 is right and I confirmed the reason directly. FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJECTS has exactly one distinct QUARTER ('31DEC2025') and one distinct SUMLEVEL ('6') across all 35,601 rows. No second vintage exists under another name: landing holds only FED_HUD_MF_SECTION8_CONTRACTS, FED_HUD_PUBLIC_HOUSING_AUTHORITIES, FED_HUD_FHA_SF_PORTFOLIO_SNAPSHOT, FED_HUD_MF_FIRM_COMMITMENTS, FED_HUD_DATA, and marts hold only HOUSING__FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJECTS at the same 35,601 rows. FEMA carries dates, HUD does not, so before/after is impossible — cross-section only. It cannot be Tier 1, and it is not Tier 3 because both legs are landed and the join lands.
verdicts.blind_spot: I rebuilt the same county-FIPS join, with the same 1,000-registration cut and the same 2017-2023 window, from the same two tables — so any defect shared by both runs I reproduce rather than catch. Specifically: FEMA's FIPS is the applicant's damaged-property county, not necessarily the county a HUD project sits in, and I never tested that. FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS.FIPS is NULL on 1,454,111 hurricane registrations in the window (including DR-4671, Fiona in Puerto Rico, 1.17M rows) — both runs silently drop them, so some counties are misclassified into '0' and I cannot say which. I never checked HUD's PCT_OCCUPIED or MONTHS_WAITING against an outside source (PIC/TRACS), so if HUD's own reference date drifts per project, both runs carry that error. And with no earlier HUD snapshot in the warehouse, I cannot test whether any of these gaps moved after the disasters — the whole causal reading is untestable from inside this warehouse, which is exactly why it is Tier 2.
new_traps: FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJECTS.MONTHS_WAITING is a negative missing-code on 26,611 of 35,601 rows (74.7%): -1 on 21,812, -4 on 4,478, -5 on 321. Only 8,990 projects carry a real wait. FED_HUD_ASSISTED_HOUSING_PROJECTS.STCTYTRT is blank on 91 rows, 5 chars on 4 rows and 2 chars on 1 row. lpad(STCTYTRT,11,'0') turns all 96 into county FIPS '00000' — a fabricated county holding 9,221 units that then counts as a real no-disaster control county. FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS.FIPS is NULL on 1,454,111 hurricane (INCIDENTTYPECODE 'H') registrations declared 2017-2023, including DR-4671 Puerto Rico Fiona at 1.17M rows. Any county rollup drops them without warning, so a county can look disaster-free because its biggest disaster had no FIPS.

Puerto Rico dominates any FEMA repeat-disaster county set: 70 of the 152 counties with 2+ non-COVID IA disasters over 1,000 registrations 2017-2023 are PR municipios (77 PR municipios appear across 152 of the 626 pairs). A county-mean over that set is half Puerto Rico; split territories from the 50 states before reading any difference.

A registration-volume threshold on FEMA IA is not a disaster filter: 1,305 counties had a non-COVID IA disaster 2017-2023 but only 447 cleared 1,000 registrations. The other 858 land in the 'no disaster' control, carrying 8,576 HUD projects across 744 counties. Never call the below-threshold group 'untouched'.

And 308 of the 374 (82.4%) already carried an HPSA of some other designation type before their "first" whole-county geographic one — 295 of them by more than 36 months. The event being measured is a change of designation shape, not the arrival of shortage status.

min(PRIMARY_COUNTY_FIPS) per ASSOCIATE_ID. 753 of 1,538 associate IDs sit in more than one county; the max spans 38. Half the orgs get an arbitrary county. verdicts.title: Pharma dollars per county head
verdicts.rerun_number: r = 0.0652 Pearson (log 2023 pharma dollars per 1,000 residents vs county Part D opioid claim share) across 1,781 counties — agent's own receipt reads 0.06519504, exact match. Quartile ladder reproduced digit for digit: $119/$603/$1,901/$5,500 per 1,000 residents; 2.97%/3.20%/3.46%/3.79% opioid share; 12.1/13.1/12.1/14.1 per 100k poisoning.
verdicts.reason:
I rebuilt the chain from the hunch sentence, not the agent's SQL, and it lands on the same 1,781 counties and the same r to four decimals. The join is real and the crosswalk does not fan out (DIM_ZIP_POINT: 33,486 rows = 33,486 distinct ZCTA5). Part D is a clean entity table (1,416,883 rows = 1,416,883 distinct NPIs). Five things in the claim are wrong.

REAL — the dollar and row counts are the whole file, not the analysis universe. $3,314,058,093 and 14,700,786 rows are all of FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023. After the agent's own filters and the ZIP->county join, $1,770,653,601 over 14,071,783 rows feeds the measure — 53.4% of the file. And the exclusions cut $1.54B, not $0.80B: teaching hospitals $797,794,332, then royalties strip a further $629,254,019 from the remainder. The claim's dollar accounting names only the smaller cut. (v3_rerun.json X_headline, v2_keys.json op_recipient_types / op_natures)

REAL — "r = 0.07 ... explains under 1% of variance" is the estimator most damaged by outliers. Spearman is 0.2363. Winsorise opioid share at p99 and Pearson is 0.1823. Twelve counties carry share above 10%, max 31.4%. The robust association is ~3x the headline and the monotone quartile ladder is the honest picture, not the noise. miss_means overstates the kill. (v3_rerun.json X_spearman, v5_adversarial.json winsor_r)

REAL — the 2015 poisoning line is computed with the worst counties deleted. CDC's top category is the literal string '>30'; regexp_substr('^[0-9.]+') returns null on it, silently. 152 counties nationally, 73 inside this cohort. Put them back at 30 and Q2's median moves 13.1 -> 14.1, so the line reads 12.1 / 14.1 / 12.1 / 14.1. One of four headline numbers changes. (v3_rerun.json X_poison_censor, X_poison_with_gt30)

REAL — the tier reason names the wrong leg. Three Open Payments general-payment years are landed under three names: FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2022 (13,306,564, PROGRAM_YEAR 2022), _2023 (14,700,786, 2023), FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS (15,385,047, 2024). County per-capita pharma correlates 0.9385 year over year, so the leg is dated and stable. The actual single vintages are Part D by-provider (registry NOTES: "Data year 2024 (12/2024), release RY26" — one landed year) and CDC poisoning ending 2015. Tier 2 survives; the reason does not. (v4_tier.json op_2024_year / op_2022_year / X_op_2022_vs_2023, v7b.json reg_partd)

OPIOID_TOT_CLMS is an empty string on 350,416 of 1,416,883 rows; the value distribution runs 0, then blank, then jumps straight to 11 — blank is CMS hiding 1-10 claims. sum() puts those prescribers in the denominator with a zero numerator. (v5_adversarial.json q4_composition, v6_suppression.json opioid_clms_low_values)

Part D matches 19,082 of 20,587 ZIPs and 1,372,191 of 1,416,883 rows. (v2_keys.json op_match_rate, partd_match_rate)

Median prescribers per 1,000 runs 1.00 -> 2.16 -> 3.29 -> 5.10 across the same quartiles, median population 34,494 -> 198,253. The top county is Olmsted, Minnesota (Mayo) at $55,765 per 1,000 residents on a population of 162,847 — a workplace, counted against a residence denominator. The agent says this in miss_means; the hunch sentence does not.

ROBUSTNESS — restrict both legs to single-county ZCTAs (COUNTY_SPAN=1, the clean geography) and r falls to 0.0329 on 1,562 counties. The thin Pearson halves. Ten thousand one hundred seventy-four of 33,486 ZCTAs span more than one county, up to six.

Nothing here kills the chain. The join holds, the entities are counties and are counted as counties, no sentinel or capped table touches it, no name match is involved, and the amount column parses on all 14.7M rows. The claim is a real cross-section with a wrong dollar frame, an understated effect size, and a censored third leg.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Pharma dollars per county head: across 1,781 counties with population >= 20,000, Pearson r = 0.065 between log 2023 pharma dollars per 1,000 residents and county Part D opioid claim share — but Spearman is 0.236 and Pearson winsorised at the 99th percentile is 0.182, so the monotone gradient is weak and real, about three times the headline. Quartile medians run $119 -> $603 -> $1,901 -> $5,500 per 1,000 residents, opioid share runs 2.97% -> 3.20% -> 3.46% -> 3.79%, and the 2015 poisoning rate runs 12.1 -> 14.1 -> 12.1 -> 14.1 per 100k once the 73 '>30' counties are restored at 30. The measure rests on $1.77B over 14,071,783 payment rows that actually land in a county — 53% of the file's $3.31B, after cutting $0.80B to teaching hospitals and a further $0.63B of royalties — and pharma dollars per head correlate 0.84 with prescribers per head, so the ladder is largely a clinician-density ladder. verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 stands, for different legs than the claim names. The Open Payments leg is NOT the single vintage — PY2022 (13,306,564), PY2023 (14,700,786) and PY2024 (15,385,047) are all landed as separately named tables, and the county per-capita measure correlates 0.9385 between 2022 and 2023. The single vintages are Part D by-provider, one landed data year (registry NOTES: DY2024, release RY26, no year column in the table), and FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY, which stops at 2015. Two of three legs are one snapshot, so no before/after is possible: cross-section only. Not Tier 1 (no time axis on the outcome legs), not Tier 3 (nothing is missing — every leg is landed and joins).
verdicts.blind_spot: I rebuilt the same aggregation over the same three tables through the same DIM_ZIP_POINT crosswalk, so every version I ran inherits its largest-population-county assignment for the 10,174 multi-county ZCTAs. I did not build a population-weighted ZCTA-to-county allocation from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.XWALK_ZCTA_COUNTY (46,960 rows, the many-to-many version). If that assignment is systematically wrong for suburban ZCTAs, my number and the agent's move together and I cannot see it. Second blind spot: both ZIPs are administrative mailing addresses of record — the payment ZIP and the prescribing ZIP — and no query I can write tells me whether either is where the money or the prescribing actually happened. Third: my robustness checks all use the same 2020 census denominator against 2023 payments and 2015 deaths, so any population drift is invisible to me.

Restoring them at 30 moves a quartile median from 13.1 to 14.1. Coalesce '>30' to 30 (or 31) before any median, mean or corr off this column.

FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS.OPIOID_TOT_CLMS is an empty string on 350,416 of 1,416,883 rows and the value distribution runs 0 (608,000 rows), then blank, then jumps straight to 11 (15,385 rows) — 1 through 10 never appear. Blank is CMS interval suppression, not zero. sum() puts those prescribers in the denominator with a zero numerator, so every opioid claim share off this table is a floor. The suppression share rises with clinician density (21.5% to 25.2% across pharma-per-capita quartiles), so the bias is not flat across a gradient.

Open Payments general payments is landed three times under three names, with the program year in the table name and only one year inside each: FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS (15,385,047 rows, PROGRAM_YEAR 2024), FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023 (14,700,786, 2023), FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2022 (13,306,564, 2022). Calling any one of them 'one program year' as a warehouse limit is wrong — union the three by name to get a time axis.

LIBRARY_MARTS.CORE.DIM_ZIP_POINT.ZCTA5 does not cover every ZIP in the CMS files: 18,894 of 21,472 in-scope Open Payments ZIP5s and 19,082 of 20,587 Part D ZIP5s match. That drops 5.8% of in-scope Open Payments dollars ($110.1M of $1.887B) out of any county. Report the matched ZIP count, never the source file's distinct ZIP count, as the join's reach. Open Payments RECIPIENT_ZIP_CODE is also mixed width — 8,409,896 rows at 5 chars, 6,290,273 at 10 (ZIP+4), 617 empty; left(x,5) is required.

The two CMS Part D files are different data years and the registry is the only place that says so. FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS (by provider, 1,416,883 rows) reads 'Data year 2024 (12/2024), release RY26' in registry NOTES; FED_CMS_PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG (by provider and drug, 25,869,521 rows) is named DY2022 in its registry title. Neither table carries a year column. Do not carry one file's vintage onto the other — the existing traps.md line about 'Part D prescriber-drug is DY22' applies only to the drug-level file.

verdicts.title: Fat margins, thin charity care
verdicts.rerun_number: 38 hospitals (CCNs) — reproduced exactly, twice, with two independently written name normalizers; 37 after dropping the one row where NET_INCOME exceeds TOTAL_COSTS
verdicts.reason: The chain holds and every headline figure reproduces to the digit: 1,601 pairs, 1,480 BMF EINs, 1,146 CCNs, 942 nonprofit-control, 38 hospitals, $29,418,917,765 net income, $6,814,244,073 charity, median charity share 1.2295%. Stanford $1,054,860,529 at 0.447% and Cedars-Sinai $825,005,677 at 0.800% both check out against FED_CMS_HCRIS. Four things need fixing. (1) Vintage: the claim says FY2023 but HCRIS holds fiscal years beginning 2022 (985 rows) and 2023 (5,118), ending 2023 (3,534) and 2024 (2,564) — both named examples end in 2024 (Stanford FYE 08/31/2024, Cedars 06/30/2024). (2) The $29.4B is 7.8% inflated: two of the 942 have NET_INCOME above TOTAL_COSTS and contribute $2,291,312,284; the clean total is $27.1B. One of them, Holy Family Memorial (CCN 520107, WI, $2,224,170,590 net income on $104,653,928 of costs, 45 beds), leads the 38 list even though the agent's own trap flags that row class; guarded, the headline is 37. (3) "1,480 distinct BMF EINs" is a match count, not an entity count: 167 of 1,146 CCNs pull 2+ EINs, Corewell Health Grand Rapids pulls 37, Methodist Houston / Riverside / Northwestern Memorial 18 each, Mayo 16. (4) The IRS leg is looser than "proves exempt status": the city-equality guard rejects the true EIN and admits a relative — Cedars-Sinai Medical Center's own EIN 951644600 sits in BMF at city W HOLLYWOOD against HCRIS LOS ANGELES and never matched, so the hospital was paired with CEDARS-SINAI HEALTH SYSTEM; The Queen's Medical Center's own EIN 990073524 is NTEE E60 and filtered out, so it paired with QUEENS UNIVERSITY MEDICAL GROUP (880820406). 41 of 1,146 matched CCNs carry for-profit control codes while matching a nonprofit E20-22 name — a 3.6% floor on wrong pairs that also applies inside the 942. Separately, the story direction fails at population level: median charity share by net-margin quartile among the matched nonprofits runs 1.151%, 1.113%, 1.210%, 1.597% — the richest quartile gives the most, which is the agent's own stated miss condition. And the IRS leg costs coverage rather than adding it: without it, 91 of 3,035 nonprofit-control hospitals clear the same two bars; with it, 38.

Matched rows 1,601 = 1,146 CCNs against 1,480 BMF rows swept in by stripped-name prefix (167 CCNs pull 2+ EINs, one pulls 37), of which 942 CCNs are nonprofit-control; those 942 hold $27.1B of clean net income against $6.8B of charity care, median charity share 1.23%. Charity share rises with margin quartile (1.15% to 1.60%), so the 38 is a two-threshold tail, not a trend. Tier 2: HCRIS is one cost-report file and the BMF is one snapshot; no before/after.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 stands. Only one HCRIS file is landed — LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CMS_HCRIS at 6,103 rows, and the mart HEALTH__FED_CMS_HCRIS is the same 6,103 rows, so there is no second vintage hiding under another name. A LIKE-search of all_landing_tables.txt for hcris/cost_report/990/sched turns up no cost-report history and no IRS 990 Schedule H (FED_IRS_990 is 200 rows; FED_IRS_990_EFILE_INDEX is a filing index, not financials). The BMF is one snapshot: TAX_PERIOD scatters across filer year-ends (2,226 rows 2024, 2,149 rows 2025, 507 null) and is not a series. No before/after is constructible, so the claim is cross-section only.
verdicts.blind_spot: My rerun reads the same two tables on the same snapshot with the same name-matching recipe, so it can only catch arithmetic and join-shape errors — it cannot tell whether HCRIS S-10 charity care is right at the source, because no second charity-care source is landed (no 990 Schedule H). I scored entity identity by eyeballing 38 name pairs; there is no hospital-to-EIN crosswalk in the warehouse to score the match properly, so a hospital exempt under an EIN that my join never touches is invisible to me, and a wrong-but-plausible pairing inside the other 904 nonprofits would pass unseen. My first attempt also silently failed: bash collapsed the escaping so the SQL regex read '\b' as a backspace character and no stopwords were stripped, giving 1,054 pairs instead of 1,601 — I caught it only because the sanity string came back unchanged. Any rerun of this shape needs that sanity check before its numbers are trusted.

Any fill-rate or coverage check on this table must use try_to_number, never IS NOT NULL. Same class in TOTAL_COSTS (82 unparseable) and NET_INCOME (89).

FED_CMS_HCRIS.NET_INCOME exceeds TOTAL_COSTS on 24 of 6,103 rows, not 148 — 148 is abs(NET_INCOME) > TOTAL_COSTS, which counts big losses too. NET_INCOME > 5x TOTAL_COSTS on 5 rows. Worst: Holy Family Memorial, CCN 520107, Manitowoc WI, NET_INCOME $2,224,170,590 = TOTAL_INCOME, TOTAL_COSTS $104,653,928, NET_PATIENT_REVENUE $2,330,494,373, 45 beds. A city-equality guard on a name join rejects the true entity and admits a relative: CEDARS-SINAI MEDICAL CENTER's own EIN 951644600 (NTEE E220) sits in FED_IRS_EO_BMF under CITY = 'W HOLLYWOOD' while HCRIS says 'LOS ANGELES', so it never matched and the hospital was paired with CEDARS-SINAI HEALTH SYSTEM instead. Same shape at THE QUEENS MEDICAL CENTER: its own EIN 990073524 is NTEE E60 and filtered out by an E20-E22 filter, so it paired with QUEENS UNIVERSITY MEDICAL GROUP (EIN 880820406).

Stripped-name prefix matching fans one hospital to a whole system's EIN list: after generic words are removed, COREWELL HEALTH GRAND RAPIDS matches 37 BMF EINs, METHODIST hospitals in Houston 18, RIVERSIDE REGIONAL 18, NORTHWESTERN MEMORIAL 18, MAYO CLINIC ROCHESTER 16. 167 of 1,146 matched CCNs carry 2+ EINs. count(distinct EIN) off a join like this is a match count, not an entity count.

FED_IRS_EO_BMF NTEE E20-E22 name-matched to FED_CMS_HCRIS on city+state pairs 41 CCNs whose HCRIS TYPE_OF_CONTROL is for-profit (3-6) with a nonprofit charity name — 3.6% of the 1,146 matched CCNs are demonstrably wrong pairs, and that rate carries into the 942 nonprofit-control matches where it cannot be detected by control code.

verdicts.title: VA pays one-star nursing homes
verdicts.rerun_number: 44 one-star nursing homes of 242 with VA contracts = 18.18% — but the national one-star rate is 20.41% (3,003 of 14,713, NH411 snapshot 2025-12-01), so the VA-contracted group is one-star LESS often than the average US nursing home. The 44 hold $137,657,939 (14.3%) of the $960,001,663.73 in VA net obligations, 2010-01-01 to 2026-08-07.
verdicts.reason:
Every number in the claim reproduced exactly on my own rebuild (scripts v1-v6 in the verify dir). 633 join rows / 633 distinct CCN / 633 distinct UEI, no fan-out. 242 homes with VA money. 4,320 distinct CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY over 5,191 action rows. $960,001,663.73 net obligation. 44 one-star = 18.18%. Avg 2.876 vs 2.891 stars. Ownership match rates 4.52 / 3.95 / 2.86 vs the claimed 4.5 / 3.9 / 2.9. Chicago Ridge SNF: 1 star, abuse Y, 'SFF Candidate', $588,187 fines, 4 contracts, $346,163.70. Village Place FL: 1 star, abuse Y, $2,100,000.00 over 3 contracts.

I tried hard to break the name match and could not. It is the strongest name join I have checked: 241 of 242 USASpending RECIPIENT_NAMEs normalise exactly equal to the CMS PROVIDER_NAME; all 242 carry a nursing-home product code (162 'NURSING HOME, LONG-TERM & ADULT DAY CARE SERVICES', 53 'MEDICAL- NURSING HOME CARE CONTRACTS', 17 'NURSING HOME CARE CONTRACTS'); 230 of 242 sit on NAICS 623110. AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME has exactly one value in the slice, 'Department of Veterans Affairs'. This is not a ST LUKES HOSPITAL case. The money is summed net FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION per action, so trap 91 (lifetime TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED repeated per action row) was avoided. I searched all 645 landing tables and all 1,102 marts: no CCN-to-UEI crosswalk is landed, so the name match is the only bridge and 4.3% is a real ceiling, not laziness.

Two real gaps, which is why CORRECTED not CONFIRMED:

1. REAL — the headline number is at or below the base rate and the claim never says so. 18.2% one-star among VA-contracted homes reads as damning. The national rate is 20.41%. The matched non-VA group is 18.67%. The claim's own miss_means admits the 2.88-vs-2.89 gap is absent, but the first number a reader remembers still points the wrong way. The base rate is ownership-driven: for-profit homes are 23.60% one-star, non-profit 11.20%, government 12.51%, and the VA group is 71.9% for-profit against 80.8% in the matched non-VA group — so the VA group is if anything slightly cleaner on mix.

2. REAL — 'worth part of $960M' is vague where an exact figure exists. The 44 one-star homes hold $137,657,939, 14.3% of the total. Median VA net for a one-star home is $1,597,512 against $2,432,340 for all 242. Smallest fix: state the $137.7M.

3. MINOR — 'matched_rows: 4320' labels the contract count. The load-bearing join matched 633 rows.

One near-miss worth recording. My first rebuild returned 216-217 matched homes, a 66% shortfall, with no error. Cause was mine, not the agent's: Snowflake's regexp_replace only honours the \b word boundary when the SQL text carries a DOUBLE backslash, and my file lost one, silently turning the whole INC/LLC/OF strip into a no-op. The agent's escaping is correct; its recorded SQL run verbatim returns 633.
verdicts.tier_reason: Tier 2 is right under Chris's definition — at least one leg is a single snapshot. The contract leg IS dated: 5,191 action rows, ACTION_DATE 2010-01-01 to 2026-08-07. The quality leg is not: FED_NURSINGHOME411 has one PROCESSING_DATE value, 2025-12-01, on all 14,713 rows, and the SAM extract is one pull (matched entities LAST_UPDATE_DATE 2025-08-06 to 2026-08-01). So ratings, fines and the abuse icon cannot move against the contract dates and this is cross-section only. Not Tier 3 — no leg is missing. Smallest path to Tier 1: swap the rating leg for FED_CMS_NURSING_HOME_DEFICIENCIES (dated 2017-2026) or _PENALTIES (2023-2026), both joining NH411 on CCN at 99.9%, and ask whether VA money arrives before or after a home's deficiency history turns.
verdicts.blind_spot:
My rerun walks the same three tables through the same name+city+state key, so it cannot see what that key systematically misses. Two specific holes it is blind to by construction:

1. Parent-level contracting. The 391 homes counted as 'without VA contracts' only lack a VA contract under THEIR OWN UEI. A chain that holds the VA beds under a corporate parent's UEI at a different city is invisible to the agent and equally invisible to me. That is exactly where abuse concentrates, so the 242/391 split — and therefore the whole '2.88 with VA vs 2.89 without' comparison, the load-bearing null result — is untested against parent-level contracting. Neither of us can rule out that the comparison group is contaminated.

2. Entity identity. I confirmed the matched SAM entity has the same name, city, state, NAICS 623110 and nursing-home PSC as the CCN, but there is no CCN-to-UEI crosswalk anywhere in the warehouse to check it against. A same-named sibling operating entity in the same city would pass every test I ran. 4 of the 14,701 NH411 name+city+state keys already carry 2 CCNs, and 52 SAM 623 keys carry up to 5 UEIs, so the failure mode exists at low frequency.

Third, smaller: the whole thing rides a 4.3% slice. 633 of 14,713 homes name-match a SAM registrant. If SAM registration itself correlates with quality, every ratio here is conditioned on that. The 633 are 18.48% one-star against 20.41% nationally, which is a real if small selection signal I could measure but not correct for.
new_traps: 2026-09-05 — Snowflake regexp_replace only honours the \b word boundary when the SQL TEXT carries a double backslash ('\\b(INC|LLC)\\b'). One backslash makes it the backspace char 0x08 and the whole corporate-suffix strip becomes a silent no-op — no error, no warning. Measured on the FED_NURSINGHOME411 to FED_SAM_ENTITY_PUBLIC name+city+state join: 633 matched homes with the correct escaping, 217 with one backslash, a 66% loss that looks like a real answer. Python f-strings, heredocs and JSON round-trips each eat a level. Always test the normaliser on a known pair ('CHICAGO RIDGE SNF LLC' must equal 'CHICAGO RIDGE SNF') before trusting any name-match count.

2026-09-05 — FED_NURSINGHOME411.OVERALL_RATING is an EMPTY STRING, never NULL, on 132 of 14,713 rows (true_null = 0). Same shape as the LEIE UPIN trap. try_to_number returns null so averages are safe, but a share written as count(one-star)/count(*) silently keeps the 132 unrated homes in the denominator.

2026-09-05 — the one-star base rate in FED_NURSINGHOME411 is 20.41% (3,003 of 14,713) and is almost entirely an ownership effect: for-profit 23.60%, non-profit 11.20%, government 12.51%. Any 'N% of cohort X are one-star' headline is meaningless without that comparison — a cohort at 18% is BETTER than average, not worse. Cost a headline its direction this session.

2026-09-05 — FED_SAM_ENTITY_PUBLIC.UEI_SAM is not unique: 895,429 rows, 887,310 distinct. Within PRIMARY_NAICS like '623%' it is 6,593 rows / 6,584 distinct, and 52 of the 6,486 name+city+state keys carry more than one UEI, max 5. Select distinct before joining or a name match fans.

2026-09-05 — FED_SAM_ENTITY_PUBLIC.EXCLUSION_STATUS_FLAG is NULL on 895,346 of 895,429 rows; only 83 rows carry 'D'. It is not a usable debarment filter — it was NULL on all 633 matched nursing homes. Use FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS_FULL_R2 and select distinct UEI instead.

2026-09-05 — FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FULL_R2 CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY behaves as a real key in the VA nursing-home slice: 5,191 action rows collapse to 4,320 distinct keys and 4,320 distinct (RECIPIENT_UEI, key) pairs, so no award switches recipient. Checked, clean — the counterexample to look for elsewhere is d_uei_ck > d_ck.

verdicts.corrected_claim: VA pays one-star nursing homes, but no more often than anyone else: 242 of the 633 nursing homes that name-match a SAM NAICS-623 registrant hold 4,320 Department of Veterans Affairs contracts worth $960,001,663.73 in net obligations, action dates 2010-01-01 to 2026-08-07; 44 of the 242 are one-star (18.2%) and hold $137.7M of that money (14.3%) — but the national one-star rate is 20.41% (3,003 of 14,713, NH411 snapshot 2025-12-01) and the matched non-VA group is 18.7% (avg 2.88 stars with VA money vs 2.89 without), so the VA is neither selecting quality nor selecting junk and the story is the named homes, not the rate: Chicago Ridge SNF, Illinois (1 star, abuse icon, SFF candidate, $588,187 in CMS fines) holds 4 VA contracts worth $346,164, and Village Place Healthcare and Rehabilitation Center, Florida (1 star, abuse icon, $291,005 in fines) holds 3 worth $2,100,000. The join is 633 rows / 633 distinct CCN / 633 distinct UEI with no fan-out, and 241 of the 242 USASpending recipient names normalise exactly equal to the CMS provider name with a nursing-home product code on every contract. Tier 2: the contracts carry dates but the ratings and the SAM extract are single snapshots, and the name match reaches only 4.3% of US nursing homes, so every count here is a floor over a registered subset.

wish_candidates.registry_notes: The registry is LIBRARY_META.REGISTRY.SOURCE_REGISTRY, 2,789 rows (columns SOURCE_ID, NAME, PUBLISHER, URL, DESCRIPTION, TEMPORAL_COVERAGE, INCLUDE, NOTES, GRAIN), joined to REGISTRY.SOURCE_FRESHNESS (102 rows, LANDING_FQN) and REGISTRY.PORTAL_DATASET_INDEX (338,520 rows). Read it with these four cautions. (1) INCLUDE has four states, not two: 'Y', 'N', '' and NULL. Blank rows are catalogued-but-never-queued (fed_fema_openfema, fed_cms_ma_enrollment, fed_cms_medicaid_mc, fed_npdb_puf); NULL rows are auto-registered landed tables with no URL or notes (the eight PECOS enrollment files, nursing home deficiencies/penalties). Python truthiness treats all four as true except NULL. (2) TEMPORAL_COVERAGE is program prose, not the landed slice: fed_bls_qcew says '1990-present' and one year (2022) is landed; fed_cms_hcris says '1996-present' and FY2023 alone is landed. (3) NOTES are last-written status: fed_cms_part_d_prescribers NOTES say 'Data year 2024 (12/2024), release RY26' and that is current and correct, while FED_CMS_PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG's title says DY2022 — so the two landed Part D tables are two data years apart with no year column in either; fed_cdc_wonder NOTES say 'County detail is API-suppressed by CDC policy; state is the floor' (the landed WONDER table is in fact national x ICD chapter x sex, 880 rows, no state column); fed_cms_nursing_home NOTES already advise cross-referencing CHOW records and the SNF affiliated-entity file, and the CHOW file was never queued. (4) LANDING_FQN in SOURCE_FRESHNESS is set on only a handful of landed sources (FED_CMS_HOSPICE, FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY, FED_CDC_OVERDOSE, FED_CMS_HCRIS); most landed tables show fqn=None, so freshness credit proves nothing about landing, in either direction. Two landed catalog tables name the candidates exactly as their publishers do and should be the first stop before any future 'never landed' claim: LANDING.FED_CMS_MAIN (158 rows, the data.cms.gov catalog, with every dated vintage URL per title — All Owners 85-89 quarterly vintages, PBJ 73 quarters, Reassignment List 81 monthly files) and LANDING.FED_CDC_DATA_PORTAL_FULL (1,471 rows, the data.cdc.gov catalog with column lists). PORTAL_DATASET_INDEX also carries the federal titles via the Virginia Open Data Portal's CKAN mirror ('Revalidation Reassignment List', the six 'All Owners', 'Skilled Nursing Facility Change of Ownership', 'VSRR Provisional County-Level Drug Overdose Death Counts', PLACES 2024) with ROW_COUNT null — indexed, never loaded. Candidates checked and dropped: IRS 990 Schedule H — no EIN on any CMS table except NPPES's two redacted columns (regex over all LANDING column names found EIN only on IRS, DOL, OSHA, SEC, FAC, TAGGS tables), FED_IRS_990_EFILE_INDEX (5.5M) is a pointer table and FED_IRS_990 is a 200-row sample, so there is no key to hospitals; HHS Provider Relief Fund — USAspending assistance CFDA 93.498 holds 2,662 rows with ONE recipient, UNITED HEALTHCARE SERVICES, INC. (HRSA's disbursing agent), net obligation -$7.96B, 2020-05-18 to 2026-01-06, so provider-level PRF is not in the warehouse and HRSA's own PRF file has no NPI/TIN key (FED_HHS_TAGGS is 45 rows, INCLUDE='N'); HRSA AHRF county-year workforce file — not landed (AHRF/AREA_HEALTH/AREA_RESOURCE 0/0/0), a strong runner-up for the 7/8/14/25 nearest-live versions. New warehouse traps found during the sweep, for traps.md: (a) ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_STORM_EVENTS.CZ_FIPS is a 3-digit within-state code — 377 distinct values on 1,058,584 CZ_TYPE='C' rows; lpad(STATE_FIPS,2,'0')||lpad(CZ_FIPS,3,'0') yields 3,363 counties; 714,633 'Z' forecast-zone rows and 7,513 'M' marine rows are not counties, and hunch 26 as refined joins on CZ_FIPS alone; (b) FED_CMS_HOSPICE.OWNERSHIP_TYPE is blank on 765 of 6,852 rows, all certified 2023-2024, and CERTIFICATION_DATE is MM/DD/YYYY text so min/max are lexical; (c) FED_CMS_SKILLED_NURSING_FACILITY_ENROLLMENTS.AFFILIATION_ENTITY_ID is a chain id (635 distinct, filled on 10,225 of 14,425), not an owner — Ensign 330, PACS 262, Life Care 194, Genesis 184; (d) FED_CMS_FACILITY_AFFILIATION covers 940,350 NPIs against 1,997,595 practitioner NPIs in the FFS file, so 1,060,336 practitioners (53%) have no org link at all, and the FFS file's 14-xx rows carry 1,997,611 associate IDs for 1,997,595 NPIs (each doctor on his own PAC ID); (e) FED_CDC_DATA_PORTAL (15,000 rows) is a two-dataset sample with one FIPS value, and FED_CDC_DATA_PORTAL_FULL and FED_CMS_MAIN are catalogs, not data; (f) FED_BLS_QCEW is 2022 annual only (QTR='A'), 3,274 county areas at AGGLVL 70-78. wish_final.method: Every candidate was re-run against LIBRARY_RAW and LIBRARY_MARTS information_schema at the column level with keywords the first pass never used (the first pass searched table names only), plus a local grep of all_landing_tables.txt and marts.json and one data probe wherever a candidate could hide under another name, which is how the county overdose series surfaced inside FED_CDC_INJURY_VIOLENCE_COUNTY and the MEDICARE_PROVIDER twin surfaced; receipts are the 01-05 scripts, JSON and logs under scratchpad/wish/final/. Rescue and promotion credit was given only where a file supplies the exact leg the matrix or a skeptic verdict named as missing (the reassignment bridge for 7, 14, 16 and 4; a second vintage for 11, 12, 19, 21, 9 and the four new QCEW and HCRIS tier-2s; the named missing measure for 28), tier-1 hunches earned nothing even when a file deepens them, and candidate 6 was reframed to include the twelve prior-year Hospital Provider Cost Report files because the landed FED_CMS_MAIN catalog lists them and one HCRIS vintage is the sole reason five hospital hunches sit in tier 2. Score is 2 x tier-3 rescues + 1 x tier-2 promotions, no candidate is restricted so nothing was halved, and the 2-2 tie between All Owners and PBJ broke toward All Owners as the smaller file (tens of thousands of rows per snapshot against 1.3M per PBJ quarter).
